items.title: CITE: Communication-Efficient Inference Token Exchange for Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Wireless Edge LLMs
items.abstract: Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) at the wireless edge is hampered by the “communication wall”: traditional Federated Learning (FL), an offline training paradigm, necessitates exchanging gigabyte-scale parameters, violating real-time latency constraints over fading channels and exposing gradient-based privacy vulnerabilities. For collaboration among already deployed models, we propose Communication-efficient Inference Token Exchange (CITE), a decentralized inference-time framework. CITE employs a lightweight semantic signaling protocol governed by a dual-sided Sanitization-Decomposition mechanism, which bounds sequence-level leakage of sensitive private attributes under explicit context-leakage assumptions. To mitigate the impact of unreliable peers in non-stationary wireless networks, we design a Synergistic Trust Consensus algorithm incorporating a Temperature-Scaled Weighting scheme and a Threshold-Based Pruning strategy, effectively capturing combinatorial peer synergy while reducing computational complexity. An optional Novelty-Weighted Online Adaptation module with Momentum-based updates enables nodes to internalize collaborative knowledge after interaction while filtering gradient noise derived from fluctuating peer qualities. Theoretical analysis characterizes wireless latency and outage feasibility, amortized communication tradeoffs against PEFT-based FL, sequence-level privacy leakage, and convergence under stated assumptions. Extensive experiments on standard NLU and knowledge-intensive benchmarks demonstrate that CITE reduces communication overhead while outperforming state-of-the-art federated baselines in inference accuracy and privacy resilience.

items.title: Augmenting Expert Elicitation With LLMs for Building Causal Models to Aid Decision Making
items.abstract: Objective: This study examines whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can serve as a supplement to traditional expert input when extracting structured causal knowledge, for the case study of decision support in medical diagnostics. Materials and Methods: We compare LLM-generated causal structures against several benchmark causal graphs created for medical diagnostic datasets. To reduce prompt-based variance and enhance reliability, we introduce a novel multi-prompt strategy where each pairwise variable query is tested using seven distinct causal linking verbs. Final edge inclusion is determined by majority voting across these variants. The resulting graphs are evaluated using standard structural similarity measures, such as Structural Hamming Distance, and Total Edge Recall Error. LLMs are able to reconstruct a substantial portion of the true causal structure, improving performance for aggregated responses from multiple prompt variations. Averaging across several prompts mitigated biases introduced by individual phrasing and reduced dependence on any single causal template, confirming that ensemble prompt strategies improve robustness. Conclusion: LLMs show promise as aids to human experts, particularly in settings where expert input is sparse or delayed. Our majority vote multi prompt technique provides a scalable method to reduce linguistic sensitivity in causal elicitation, validated on a broader LLM augmented framework.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

items.title: Approximate computing circuits for error-tolerant applications with low energy consumption
items.abstract: Energy efficiency is a crucial factor in very large-scale integrated (VLSI) circuit design, and traditional methods offer limited solutions to power intensive circuits. Recently, approximate computing techniques have emerged, enhancing key design parameters like power consumption, propagation delay, and area, albeit with a compromise in accuracy. These techniques are especially suitable for high-performance computing, as they offer reduced energy consumption while compromising some accuracy, making them ideal for use in arithmetic circuits. This paper introduces enhanced versions of approximate adders (AxAs) and subtractors (AxSCs) for fundamental operations. Building upon these designs, approximate multipliers using the Wallace tree multiplier (AxWTM) and approximate dividers (AxDs) have been developed, and their performances have been compared regarding power consumed, spatial requirements, delay time, and error frequency. Many digital image and video processing applications, along with other multimedia tools, can function effectively even with slight inaccuracies in their output results. The existing and proposed designs were applied to image squaring, image multiplication, image subtraction, and image division applications, and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) was obtained. It is found that the suggested approximate designs achieved a better PSNR for all image applications, and the results were superior to those of their counterparts.
items.venue: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)

items.title: Analysis of the impact of natural language selection in large language models on energy consumption
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference is computationally intensive, yet the extent to which the interaction language affects energy consumption remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether inference energy consumption varies across six European languages: Polish, English, German, French, Spanish, and Russian. Three open-weight models, Llama3.1-8b, Gemma-3-12b, and Qwen2.5-14b, were evaluated using ten semantically equivalent prompts, each translated into the six languages and repeated three times. Experiments were conducted on a workstation-class server equipped with an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT GPU and the Ollama inference framework. Whole-system power consumption was measured using a calibrated HIOKI PW3337 power meter, and energy efficiency was expressed as energy per generated token (EPT). Mean EPT varied substantially among models: Llama3.1-8b consumed 6.43 J/token, Qwen2.5-14b 10.23 J/token, and Gemma-3-12b 10.87 J/token. Kruskal–Wallis tests identified statistically significant between-language differences only for Llama3.1-8b; no sig - nificant differences were found for Qwen2.5-14b or Gemma-3-12b. However, regression analysis for Llama3.1-8b showed that response length was the dominant predictor of EPT, as fixed inference overhead was amortized over longer outputs. The findings indicate that apparent language-dependent differences in inference energy are driven primarily by generated-output length rather than by language itself. Energy efficiency also depends strongly on model architecture, tokenizer behavior, and inference implementation, highlighting the importance of response-length control and whole-system measurement in Green AI benchmarking.
items.venue: Advances in Science and Technology Research Journal

items.title: An Improved Signal Mixing Method Based on Tunnel Magnetoresistance-Rogowski Coil Sensors for SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Wide-band current sensors with DC capability are crucial for characterizing both steady state and high-frequency transients in switched-mode power electronics and digital control. Traditional hybrid sensors often suffer from complex circuitry, need for precise tuning, high component count, and elevated cost. This article presents an improved signal mixing method based on tunneling magnetoresistive (TMR) sensors and Rogowski coil sensors. By directly winding the TMR output leads into a Rogowski coil, which is the distinctive design of this work, the two signals are combined without additional complex circuitry. Using only one hybrid integrator, the proposed method achieves a bandwidth from DC to 54.9 MHz, significantly simplifying design and reducing cost. The sensor exhibits linear deviation within 2% and a resolution of 0.1 A at 5 MHz. Double-pulse tests using SiC mosfets further demonstrate its potential for switch transient testing of high-frequency power semiconductors.

items.title: Active-Clamped Stepwise Modulation for Independent Control of dv/dt and di/dt in Medium-Voltage Voltage Source Converters Based on Series-Connected SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Voltage source converters (VSCs) based on series-connected SiC mosfets provide a compact alternative to modular multilevel converters in medium-voltage applications. However, the fast switching of SiC mosfets produces excessive dv/dt and di/dt, which may cause electromagnetic interference and voltage overshoot. To address these issues, this article proposes an active-clamped stepwise modulation method that exploits the existing voltage-balancing active clamping modules to achieve controllable dv/dt and di/dt. By actively switching the auxiliary switches during the dead-time interval, the arm-voltage transition is first shaped into a stepwise waveform, and the subsequent current commutation is then independently regulated. As a result, the arm-voltage and arm-current transitions do not overlap, which relieves the hard-switching stress of the main power devices and enables independent control of dv/dt and di/dt. The operating principles of the proposed method over a fundamental cycle and the design guidelines for the key parameters are presented. The proposed method is experimentally validated on a 3.6-kV/35-A VSC prototype with six series-connected SiC mosfets in each arm. Experimental results show an 81% reduction in voltage overshoot and a 48% reduction in common-mode current while maintaining robust voltage balancing among the series-connected devices. These improvements are achieved with negligible impact on the overall efficiency.

items.title: ALPS: An Application-Aware, Length-Predictive Scheduler for Efficient LLM Inference at Edge
items.abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) on resource-constrained edge server clusters introduces a critical systems challenge: achieving high throughput and low latency under strict GPU memory and bandwidth limits. Current schedulers are ill-suited for this environment, as they treat requests independently, incurring two major inefficiencies. They waste compute and memory on redundant prefill computations for identical, lengthy system prompts across applications, and their phase-agnostic policies create suboptimal batches that poorly overlap compute-intensive prefills with memory-bound decodes, leading to GPU under-utilization. This paper presents ALPS, an application-aware, length-predictive scheduler for request serving for edge LLM inference. ALPS transforms the queueing layer into an intelligent orchestrator with two core techniques: (i) semantic-aware request grouping, which hashes requests by system prompt to co-locate them, reducing redundant prefill computations; and (ii) phase-aware scheduling, which uses a lightweight output token bucket predictor to estimate decode/prefill ratios and strategically reorders requests to maximize prefill-decode overlap in continuous hybrid batching. Augmented with SLO-aware preemption, ALPS is implemented as a practical scheduling layer atop vLLM. Extensive evaluations on an edge GPU testbed with diverse models and production workloads demonstrate that ALPS improves token throughput by up to 1.6× and reduces end-to-end latency by up to 2.4× compared to state-of-the-art schedulers.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems

items.title: AFLoRA: Adaptive LoRA for Resource-Efficient Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
items.abstract: LoRA-based federated fine-tuning allows clients to fine-tune LoRA adapters locally and aggregates updates on the server, thereby enabling the efficient adaptation of global foundation models to distributed, domain-specific data. However, existing methods assume identical and static LoRA adapters across clients, which not only limits the utilization of heterogeneous resources and adaptation to diverse data distributions, but also prevents dynamic adjustment to clients’ evolving local fine-tuning state. They also struggle to achieve precise and lightweight aggregation of LoRA matrices, hindering learning performance in resource-constrained environments. To address these issues, we propose AFLoRA, an adaptive LoRA-based resource-efficient federated fine-tuning framework. For effectively adapting to Non-IID local data while minimizing resource consumption, AFLoRA introduces diagonal-based dynamic rank assignment, which dynamically adjusts local LoRA ranks based on client resources and local adaptation state guided by a learnable diagonal matrix. It further decouples LoRA matrices updates between clients and the server to reduce overhead, and develops a zero-padding-based rank-aware aggregation mechanism to accurately integrate heterogeneous updates through lossless matrix expansion and rank-aware weighting. These mechanisms enable AFLoRA to balance resource efficiency and fine-tuning performance effectively. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AFLoRA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both LLM adaptation performance and fine-tuning efficiency in heterogeneous environments.

items.title: A System-Level Exploration of Superconducting Supercomputers for Emerging Workloads
items.abstract: Superconducting digital (SCD) technology has long carried promise for advancing large-scale computing leveraging the unique physical characteristics of superconducting materials and devices, such as low-voltage, high-frequency operation and zero-resistance interconnects. At the same time, SCD technology has also historically been beset with many scaling challenges. However, recent critical advances including improved power delivery, high integration density and availability of superconducting random-access memory prompt a fresh evaluation of SCD-based computing. In this paper, we study whether SCD systems can outperform conventional CMOS and cryo-CMOS for large-scale workloads even after accounting for full system overheads. Using a novel multilevel analytical modeling framework, our study explores performance implications of various SCD configurations across a range of architecture and technology assumptions in applications such as large language models (LLMs). The results show that, despite cooling overheads, a key benefit of recently proposed SCD technology is 9 $\boldsymbol{\times}$ × - 286 $\boldsymbol{\times}$ × better energy efficiency. By contrast, performance gains ranging between 4 $\boldsymbol{\times}$ × - 16 $\boldsymbol{\times}$ × are more limited and strongly depend on the availability of high-density, high-bandwidth on-chip memory that traditionally was not attainable. In general, the results show that recent technological advances are key to a promising scalable path forward, where our ablation studies highlight critical aspects of the maturity of SCD technology.

items.title: A Survey of Relation Extraction: From Deep Learning to Large Language Models
items.abstract: The relation extraction (RE) task aims to identify the relations between entities in texts. Structured facts extracted through RE can be effectively leveraged for various downstream tasks, including knowledge graph construction and logical reasoning. As this field has evolved over time, it has made significant progress, from deep learning to the rise of large language models (LLMs). However, deep learning-based and LLM-based methods still need to be further explored. Meanwhile, systematic surveys and comparative analysis remain insufficient. Therefore, this paper conducts a comprehensive survey of deep learning-based and LLM-based methods. Based on this, we categorize deep learning-based methods into pipeline-based and joint extraction-based methods, while LLM-based methods are classified into prompt-based and fine-tuning-based methods, providing a detailed introduction to each. In addition, drawing upon the experimental results documented in extant papers, we carry out an in-depth comparative analysis from both experimental and theoretical perspectives. Moreover, to provide valuable references for future research, we introduce several renowned open-source RE tools and explore their features and application scenarios intensively. Finally, we discuss current research challenges thoroughly and outline future research directions. We also provide a public GitHub repository containing curated resources, code links, and supplementary materials related to this survey.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

items.title: A Resonant Capacitor-Less Parallel Resonant DC-Link Soft-Switching Inverter
items.abstract: To address the issues of reduced light-load efficiency and DC bus voltage loss in dual-resonant-circuit parallel resonant DC-link soft-switching inverter (PRDCLSI), this article proposes a resonant capacitor-less PRDCLSI. Leveraging the low turn-off loss characteristics of SiC mosfets, the resonant capacitors are eliminated to minimize the current stress of the auxiliary circuit under both light- and heavy-load conditions. An improved modulation strategy is introduced, which initiates the resonant process during the dead time to avoid prolonged existence of the DC bus zero-voltage notch. With this improved modulation strategy, no turn-off snubber capacitors are required for any switches. Furthermore, by merging redundant components, the proposed design reduces the component count by two auxiliary diodes and nine resonant capacitors, significantly lowering hardware costs. This article provides a detailed analysis of the operational modes of the resonant capacitor-less PRDCLSI under the improved modulation strategy and compares its performance with different existing schemes. Following parameter design, a 40 kHz, 5 kW experimental prototype based on SiC mosfets was built. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed solution maintains the advantage of a short DC bus zero-voltage notch (<1.60 μs) while achieving high-efficiency power conversion across load conditions (96.72% at 200 W and 98.25% at 5 kW).

items.title: X-CAMReg: Cross-Pose Camera-Group Registration for Multi-Pose Object Reconstruction
items.abstract: Multi-pose object reconstruction is often bottlenecked by cross-pose camera registration. When an object is reoriented between capture sessions, each session can provide accurate cameras within its static setup, but the resulting camera groups remain in separate coordinate frames. We introduce X-CAMReg, a cross-pose camera-group registration framework for multi-pose object reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Given images in one main pose and several auxiliary poses, X-CAMReg iteratively registers each auxiliary camera group to the main-pose frame and updates the 3DGS model. Its registration pipeline combines global camera-group registration, silhouette-consensus camera-group fusion, and local refinement. While 3D foundation models improve robustness in difficult settings, our experiments show that they are less accurate than Structure-from-Motion (SfM) when stable background cues are available. X-CAMReg therefore partitions the process: it uses SfM for per-pose camera estimation and applies foundation models only for cross-pose registration, where standard SfM violates the rigid-scene assumption. This preserves per-pose geometry while addressing cross-pose background inconsistency. Experiments show that X-CAMReg improves camera-registration accuracy over evaluated baselines, and the registered views support downstream multi-pose 3DGS reconstruction.
items.venue: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

items.title: Text-to-SQL Interface using Guardrails and Hallucination Detection
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can translate plain-English questions into SQL, which makes institutional databases usable by people who cannot write queries. In a shared system such as a college ERP, however, the generated SQL must be treated as untrusted code: it may modify data, read rows that belong to another user, or quietly answer the wrong question. This paper reports the design, deployment, and security testing of SafeSQL, a natural-language query system over a 25-table, 174- column PostgreSQL ERP schema holding about 200,000 records. SafeSQL places the LLM behind four independent layers: model-level refusal, syntax-tree (AST) blocking with sqlglot, a read-only non-owner database role, and Row-Level Security (RLS). We show that the widely used RLS pattern based on current_setting() can be defeated by generated SQL that calls set_config() from a subquery, CTE, LATERAL join, or window function, and we replace it with a session map keyed on the PostgreSQL backend process, which adds about 2.14 ms per query. We also describe five cases in which our own test infrastructure reported success for the wrong reason, and the checks we added to catch them. The system is deployed as a web application and is covered by 248 automated tests.
items.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

items.title: StructSVG: Tree-Graph Guided Multi-Agent Text-to-SVG Generation
items.abstract: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) is a resolution-independent and fully editable graphic format widely adopted in UI design, art, and web development. Inherently a hierarchical semantic structure, SVG organizes geometric primitives in a document tree where element hierarchy and drawing order directly determine both visual appearance and editability. However, most of the existing text-to-SVG methods either treat SVG as flat token sequences lacking structural awareness, or rely on optimization-based differentiable rasterization with prohibitive computational costs, resulting in outputs that lack meaningful semantic hierarchy and editable structure. Inspired by the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) and agent-based frameworks, which have demonstrated strong capabilities in structured reasoning and multi-step planning, we propose StructSVG, a training-free, structure-aware multi-agent framework for text-to-SVG generation. StructSVG constructs an explicit Tree-Graph intermediate representation: the semantic tree hierarchically decomposes the prompt into editable visual components with semantic identifiers and spatial information, while the topology graph models inter-element rendering order and spatial relationships, providing a structured blueprint for LLM-driven generation and refinement. Five specialized agents collaborate across three stages to perform structured planning, component drafting, and refinement and selection. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, and we showcase diverse applications highlighting its generality and practical utility. Code and data for this paper are at https://github.com/sealost/StructSVG.
items.venue: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

items.title: Neural Palate Kueh
items.abstract: If there is one thing that you would not need nor want Artificial Intelligence (AI) to do for you, it is probably eating. Yes, more than thinking, designing, building, and even sleeping on your behalf. All work in the future including architecture work could potentially reside at the dining table. Dining as co-designing and eating as consecrating architecture. A 'tasty' architectural 'food-for-thought' and 'food-to-eat'. Neural Palate Kueh was on display at the Venice Architecture Biennale 2025 as part of the Singapore Pavilion and has since returned to Singapore for its 'Homecoming Edition' at the National Museum of Singapore. It uses the traditional Singaporean kuehs (bite-sized snack or dessert foods) to speculate on future scenarios of building-making and city-making with the analogical generativity limits (and potential creativity) of today's AI - one that could be made specific to a given culture and built environment like Singapore. It combines conditioning AI techniques such as IP-Adapters and ControlNet with the disjointedness of manual collage techniques to iteratively generate context-specific 3D urban forms from real-time dining footages and to synthesize 3D building forms with edible food. Using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), the process begins with AI's deconstruction of each kueh along three axes: conceptual underpinnings (rituals of eating and cultural symbolism), design operatives (geometric form and culinary construction), and materiality (ingredients and textures). These insights become the learnt architectural design principles of the AI models to imagine novel architectural interiors/exteriors with which perceptual associations with Singapore forms, whether buildings or food, are produced. The taxonomies of fooddining and architecture-planning now become blurred and interchangeable. The project features the outputs as 3Dprinted architectural pieces in several food scales and 3D point clouds video animations in several urban scales. Neural Palate Kueh thus proposes an experimental synesthetic AI methodology driven by architectural narrative and gastrophysics.

items.title: NarraStone: Reimagining the Stone Stele as an Al-Era Apparatus of Synthetic Memory
items.abstract: Stone steles have long served as durable public records, their authority arising as much from material form, calligraphic inscription, and public display as from what they say. We present NarraStone, an interactive installation that reimagines the stone stele as an AI-era apparatus of synthetic memory: generative narrative that is assembled from fragments, rendered in the visual language of inscription, and encountered as a public record. Participants rotate a tangible cube carrying Cangjie code modules to recombine symbolic components; a camera reads the selected face, recognized codes are mapped into Chinese characters, and a large language model extends them, together with previous inscriptions, through a relay-writing process. The output is rendered as stele-style calligraphy by a CycleGAN trained on historical rubbings and projected with responsive sound, so that each participant inherits and transforms the traces left by others. Through a small-scale campus exhibition and a retrospective group discussion with six interview participants, we report three illustrative observations concerning public accumulation, differing interpretive routes, and participant accounts consistent with possible productive skepticism.
items.venue: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Art Papers

items.title: M3: Dense Matching Meets Multi-View Foundation Models for Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM
items.abstract: Streaming reconstruction from uncalibrated monocular video remains challenging, as it requires both high-precision pose estimation and computationally efficient online refinement in dynamic environments. While coupling 3D foundation models with SLAM frameworks is a promising paradigm, a critical bottleneck persists: most multi-view foundation models estimate poses in a feed-forward manner, yielding pixel-level correspondences that lack the requisite precision for rigorous geometric optimization. We present M3, a Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM that enhances Multi-view foundation models with a dedicated Matching head for fine-grained pose optimization. Our framework utilizes a unified inference strategy to jointly optimize historical and incoming frames, while integrating dynamic area suppression and cross-inference intrinsic alignment to maintain robustness. Extensive experiments on diverse indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy in both pose estimation and scene reconstruction. Notably, M3 reduces ATE RMSE by 64.3% compared to VGGT-SLAM 2.0 and outperforms ARTDECO by 2.11 dB in PSNR on the ScanNet++ dataset. Project page: https://city-super.github.io/M3.
items.venue: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

items.title: From World Foundation Models to Real-world applications: An Introduction
items.abstract: This course introduces the emerging paradigm of world foundation models (WFMs) and their role in enabling real-world physical AI systems. Those WFMs learn structured, multimodal representations of physical environments, supporting perception, prediction, and decision-making from a shared representation that spans vision, language, and action. The course connects foundation model concepts to dynamic visual environments, simulation, synthetic data generation, robotics, and sim-to-real deployment.
items.venue: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Courses

items.title: Exploration Research on Intelligent Generation Application of VR Virtual Scenes Driven by Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization
items.abstract: The large-scale and efficient production of virtual reality (VR) content remains a critical bottleneck constraining industry development. Traditional scene construction methods relying on manual modeling and scripted programming exhibit prominent issues such as prolonged cycles, high costs, and limited customization. Recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence technologies—including generative AI (AIGC), large language models, and neural rendering—have opened new pathways for intelligent VR scene generation. This study systematically examines the theoretical foundations and technical architectures of VR scene generation driven by AI technologies, delves into key technical approaches including geometric appearance generation, physical logic mapping, and ambient environment intelligence, conducts empirical analyses through domestic and international case studies, and explores cutting-edge directions such as edge intelligence, embodied intelligence, and world models. Research demonstrates that AI-driven technologies can enhance VR scene construction efficiency by over 80% while reducing costs by approximately 70%. Building on these findings, the paper proposes actionable recommendations across three dimensions: technological innovation, industrial applications, and ethical standards, aiming to provide theoretical references and practical guidance for developing next-generation VR content production paradigms characterized by high efficiency, fidelity, and strong interactivity.
items.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

items.title: Deep Learning and Generative AI for Structure-Aware Indoor Panorama Modeling and VR Exploration
items.abstract: Surround-view panoramic imaging provides complete visual coverage from a single viewpoint and is widely used for indoor capture, virtual tours, and immersive visualization. However, a 360° panorama is fundamentally a static, viewpoint-centered representation that lacks explicit 3D geometry, architectural structure, stereopsis, and motion parallax. As a result, it often produces a flattened perception of space, even when presented in HMDs, and offers limited support for navigation and editing. This course presents an up-to-date overview of recent methods and trends that combine architectural and data-driven priors with deep learning to infer geometric, structural, semantic, and visual information from a single panorama, enabling advanced indoor modeling and exploration. After introducing panoramic representations, including equirectangular projection, gravity alignment, indoor capture constraints, and available datasets, we examine the priors used to bridge the gap between incomplete visual observations and structured, explorable scene models. We then review the key tasks involved in transforming a 360° image into an enriched indoor representation, including depth and semantic estimation, room layout reconstruction, multi-room localization and connectivity, novel view synthesis, and immersive exploration. We also highlight recent advances in generative and structure-guided methods for panoramic outpainting and completion, aimed at creating realistic indoor 360° content for VR/XR applications, virtual staging, refurnishing, and immersive scene generation. The course also covers the emergence of both general-purpose and 360° -specific foundation models and their impact on panoramic analysis and synthesis. We finally point out relevant research issues and analyze research trends.
items.venue: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Courses

items.title: Beyond Diary: An AI-Powered Personal Biography Generator
items.abstract: A diary helps people hold on to important experiences and see how they have changed, but writing and organizing entries takes time, and that effort discourages many users from keeping it up. Research on story generation, personalized narrative generation, lifelog retrieval, autobiographical memory, and long-term memory for AI systems each addresses part of this problem. We review 20 papers published between 2020 and 2026 and find clear progress in each area, yet these capabilities are treated separately rather than as one continuous storytelling system. To address this gap we present Beyond Diary, an AIpowered personal biography generator. Users record daily experiences by voice or text; the system transcribes speech, extracts events, emotions, and milestones with a large language model, stores them as searchable memories, and writes biography chapters from them. Reminders, streaks, and badges support consistent use. The paper also reports the system’s feasibility, requirements, layered architecture, and UML-based design, built on React.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL with pgvector, the Whisper API, and the Groq API running LLaMA 3. The system aims to make keeping a record of one’s life light enough to sustain and to turn everyday experiences into a personal biography.
items.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

items.title: An Explainable Graph Attention Network for Indirect Prompt Injection Detection in RAG Systems
items.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enables large language models (LLMs) to answer queries using information obtained from external documents. However, retrieved content may contain concealed commands intended to influence the model's behaviour, creating a security risk called indirect prompt injection. This research develops a GAT-based approach to identify harmful instructions in retrieved documents before they reach the language model. Each document is split into individual sentences, which are encoded using a frozen DeBERTa-v3-base model. A graph is constructed from the sentence embeddings, linking adjacent sentences and pairs with a cosine similarity score above 0.7. A two-layer Graph Attention Network (GAT), comprising approximately 0.4 million trainable parameters, processes the graph to classify the document as benign or malicious. The model was evaluated using 10,000 samples collected from financial and corporate policy documents. The dataset contains 6,400 training samples, 1,600 validation samples, and 2,000 testing samples, with equal representation of both classes. Following the addition of calibrated Gaussian noise to the input features, the model obtained 99.80% test accuracy, an F1-score of 0.998, and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.996. Its 95% Wilson confidence interval for accuracy ranged from 99.49% to 99.92%. The keyword-based approach recorded an accuracy of 87.93%, but 24.1% of the malicious samples contained none of its specified trigger terms. Its performance on unseen data remains to be established through further experiments involving independently collected datasets, additional application domains, and attack techniques excluded from the original evaluation.
items.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

items.title: Agentic AI: A Review and Proposed Framework
items.abstract: Chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) are good at producing text, but most of them stop at the reply. They cannot look up an order, run a test or update a record unless someone connects them to tools and tells them how to use those tools safely. Agentic AI is the name given to systems that close this gap: an LLM is placed inside a loop where it makes a plan, calls a tool, reads what came back and decides what to do next. This paper reviews the main building blocks of such systems, namely planning and reasoning, tool use, memory and state, and human oversight, and places them in the recent literature on ReAct-style agents, tool learning, reflection, multi-agent conversation and agent benchmarks. Building on this review, we propose a modular agent pipeline made of a tool registry with permissions, a planner, a permission check, an optional human approval gate, tool execution with observation, result checking and an audit log. We also describe how such a pipeline should be evaluated, using task success, tool errors and injection resistance, and time and cost. The paper is a review with a proposed design and does not report new experiments. It closes with open problems, including reliable planning over long tasks, defence against prompt injection, and fair evaluation of agents that behave differently on every run.
items.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

items.title: WHEN CORRECT CODE IS NOT ENOUGH: ASSESSING THE PRODUCTION READINESS OF LLMGENERATED SOFTWARE
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate executable software, but functional correctness alone does not establish production readiness. This study evaluates GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna across 15 algorithmic and production-oriented tasks using five generations per model-task pair, yielding 225 generated programs plus 15 fixed references. The layered testbed combines nominal and hidden-edge-case checks, moderate and severe production-like stress, metamorphic validation, reference-normalized runtime and memory, structural quality, static analysis, implementation-strategy inspection, and generation cost. All 800 functional and 368 applicable robustness checks passed, while production-stress success fell to 95.16% for Sol, 95.60% for Terra, and 93.38% for Luna. Cross-model stress differences were not significant, but generation cost differed strongly. A Quick Sort case showed more than a 500x runtime spread among behaviorally correct implementations. The results show that production-oriented evaluation must extend beyond pass/fail correctness to include stress behavior, resources, implementation strategy, and cost
items.venue: International Journal of Software Engineering & Applications

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Science and Physics Education, 2015-2026: An AI-Assisted Bibliometric and Title-and-Abstract Analysis across Fourteen Journals
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) research in science and physics education has expanded rapidly, particularly since the emergence of generative AI. This study maps publication patterns, research characteristics, and citation connections across 14 selected science and physics education journals. OpenAlex searches using fifteen AI-related terms identified 966 unique records published between January 2015 and September 2026. AI-assisted screening retained 333 publications, which were coded using available titles and abstracts. Bibliometric analyses examined publication growth, thematic patterns, and citations within and between the two journal groups. Of the included publications, 87.1% appeared from 2023 onwards. Generative large language models and chatbots accounted for 58.9% of the corpus, while instruction and assessment together represented 48.3% of publications. Among 182 records classified as involving human participants, comparison groups were identifiable in 14.3%, effect sizes in 8.2%, and instrument validity evidence in 5.5%. These frequencies reflect information identifiable in bibliographic records, rather than the absence of these features in the full studies. Laboratory and experimental support was the principal educational function in 27 publications. Citation connections between the journal groups were limited: their reference sets had a Jaccard index of 0.047, and 15.6% of publications cited an included study from the other group. The findings document rapid growth and uneven research emphases within the selected venues. Independent human validation and full-text assessment are needed before drawing firm conclusions about methodological quality or educational effectiveness.
items.venue: EIKI Journal of Effective Teaching Methods

items.title: Ripple: Coordination-Free Message Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows at the IoT Edge
items.abstract: Distributed intelligence in IoT and edge systems increasingly runs as agentic AI: production large language model (LLM) applications execute as workflows—directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of agents and tools that exchange prompts, retrieved context, and tool outputs across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud. When many such workflows share a capacity-limited link, such as an edge gateway uplink or a regional aggregation point, that link rather than the GPU gates the communication phase, and a message that unblocks an idle agent may wait behind an unrelated bulk transfer. A dependency-aware link scheduler can mitigate this, but a scheduler that ranks messages by whole-workflow remaining work and downstream critical path requires a global, continuously updated view of every concurrent workflow, that is, a central coordinator that heterogeneous and dynamic IoT edge deployments typically lack. This paper presents Ripple, a coordination-free link scheduler in which each agent ranks only its own outgoing messages, using a local rule that prioritizes downstream criticality per unit transmission cost and applies an age credit to curb long waits. The required downstream-criticality signal is a bounded scalar initialized with the source's task descriptor, so no runtime node maintains the global graph. In an event-driven, flow-level evaluation on a shared 100 Mbps link with heavy-tailed messages (median 419 KB, 99th-percentile about 30 MB) and four DAG shapes, network waiting accounts for 46% of the mean workflow completion time (WCT) under fair sharing at offered load ρ=0.88. Ripple reduces mean and 99th-percentile WCT by 24% and 38% relative to fair sharing, and attains 9% lower mean and 27% lower tail WCT than a global-view reference heuristic while using no global state. A knowledge-horizon analysis shows that performance saturates at a one-hop view, and an ablation finds that message size and age drive most of the aggregate gain. The results use an idealized flow-level priority model; a DSCP/eBPF realization that needs no coordinator and no change to the LLM runtime is proposed but not yet evaluated.
items.venue: ACM Interational Symposium on Mobile Ad Hoc Networking and Computing

items.title: Measuring the Predictability of Beam-Level 5G Traffic: How Far Can Zero-Shot Foundation Models Go?
items.abstract: Beam-level traffic forecasting is critical for 5G resource allocation, yet the measurement properties of beam-level traffic remain poorly understood. We present a measurement-driven analysis across 2,961 time series from two public 5G datasets released by third parties. We first characterize how beam-level traffic differs from the aggregated cell-level traffic studied in prior work, identifying a sparsity-dependent predictability gradient: active beams exhibit the strongest periodicity and covariate correlations, enabling accurate forecasting, while covariate gains attenuate with sparsity until most methods converge on the sparsest beams. We then benchmark 16 model configurations, including four general-purpose Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) pre-trained without mobile-network data and one RAN-specific foundation model, across three experimental settings. A zero-shot TSFM given identical oracle covariates outperforms trained alternatives on 68-73% of beams (64% univariately), but this advantage is concentrated on active beams where periodic structure is strongest; on the sparsest beams, foundation and trained models converge to the same noise-dominated predictability floor. The dominant factor has to do with information inputs rather than the model architecture: oracle network telemetry covariates reduce error more than switching between any two general-purpose architectures, and covariate-augmented models are also more resilient to distribution shift. We interpret this benefit as an information-content upper bound: deployable pipelines that lag, extrapolate, or separately forecast the covariates recover none of the oracle gain at a one-week horizon, identifying covariate acquisition, rather than model choice, as the key open problem. Without future information, zero-shot Chronos-2 matches or beats trained univariate pipelines while requiring no training or retraining.
items.venue: ACM Interational Symposium on Mobile Ad Hoc Networking and Computing

items.title: MOSAIC: Efficient Collaborative Inference for Multi-Modal Large Language Models with Distributed Edge Computing
items.abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) enable natural language reasoning over heterogeneous sensory data, appealing to many edge AI scenarios, yet their deployment faces competing demands on latency, energy, and quality. We present MOSAIC, which adopts a component-level decomposition and distributed deployment paradigm for efficient MLLM inference at the edge, realizing three core ideas: parallel encoding, token pruning, and device-server collaboration. Specifically, for the offline stage, modality-specific encoders distilled from a unified foundation model are co-deployed with Q-Former projection on edge devices for parallel encoding, while LoRA instruction fine-tuning adapts the frozen LLM backbone to downstream tasks. For the online stage, we formulate a multi-objective optimization over latency and energy that jointly tunes token budgets, device frequencies, and quantization precision under long-term semantic accuracy constraints, achieving dynamic token pruning and device-server collaboration. We leverage Lagrangian relaxation to decompose the original problem into tractable per-slot subproblems and design an online algorithm with provable near-optimal performance and guaranteed constraint satisfaction. We implement a realistic testbed for extensive performance evaluation, which demonstrates that MOSAIC reduces latency by up to 49.8% and energy by up to 65.1% over advanced baselines while maintaining high semantic accuracy.
items.venue: ACM Interational Symposium on Mobile Ad Hoc Networking and Computing

items.title: FrozenSFL: Model-Frozen Split Federated Learning for Resource-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning over Heterogeneous Edge Devices
items.abstract: Collaborative fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) at the network edge enables privacy-preserving and personalized generative intelligence, but is constrained by the limited memory and compute resources of edge devices. Traditional approaches, such as split federated learning (SFL), partition models between devices and a server, requiring iterative exchanges of activations/gradients while the server manages multiple submodels. This leads to substantial communication overhead, high activation storage costs, and severe server-side memory pressure when scaling to massive heterogeneous devices. In this paper, we propose FrozenSFL, a resource-efficient SFL framework for collaborative fine-tuning of LLMs across heterogeneous edge devices. At its core, FrozenSFL strictly freezes device-side submodels to eliminate both deviceside backpropagation and server-to-device gradient transmission, thereby removing on-device activation storage requirements and downlink communication overhead. Building upon this design, we improve the framework in two aspects. First, we design a layerwise LoRA aggregation strategy to handle structural heterogeneity introduced by device-specific model partitioning and enable efficient server-side updates. Second, we introduce a server-side feature caching mechanism that reuses invariant features, allowing subsequent training epochs to proceed offline and reducing redundant computation and communication. We implement the FrozenSFL system as an asynchronous multi-threaded pipeline, which serves as our real-world testbed for evaluation. On the device side, forward computation and data transmission are decoupled via a producer-consumer mechanism. On the server side, a first-in-first-out scheduling strategy serializes fine-tuning tasks across devices. A hybrid memory-disk streaming mechanism further buffers incoming data and ensures stable training under network variability. Extensive evaluations with representative models, including BERT-Base (0.11B), ViT-Large (0.3B), and LLaMA-2-7B (7B), validate the effectiveness of FrozenSFL. In particular, for LLaMA-2-7B, FrozenSFL can reduce device/server VRAM footprint by up to 14%/82.7% with only 1% accuracy loss, while achieving up to 6.7× fine-tuning speedup.
items.venue: ACM Interational Symposium on Mobile Ad Hoc Networking and Computing

items.title: Demo: On-Device Agent for Personalized and Efficient Mobile Network Configuration
items.abstract: As mobile devices increasingly operate across heterogeneous access networks and diverse usage contexts, efficient network configuration requires decisions that adapt to both dynamic network conditions and individual user preferences. We demonstrate an on-device communication agent that transforms historical user network-switching behavior into personalized configuration rules. An on-device Large language model (LLM) analyzes switching records offline and generates condition-action rules capturing recurring user preferences. During real-time use, the agent retrieves matched rules locally and executes the corresponding network configuration after user confirmation, without invoking the LLM. Attendees will choose a prepared behavior trace, inspect the rule generated on the phone, and recreate its triggering context to observe an immediate network switch. The demonstration shows how separating deliberation from execution makes personalized mobile network configuration both interpretable and responsive while keeping user data and inference on the device.
items.venue: ACM Interational Symposium on Mobile Ad Hoc Networking and Computing

items.title: An Agentic AI Architecture for Zero-Touch IoT Device Onboarding and Interoperability
items.abstract: The heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices remains a major barrier to scalable deployment, automated onboarding, and cross-platform interoperability. Device-specific protocols, software dependencies, telemetry formats, and runtime constraints often require manual configuration and ad-hoc integration logic. This paper proposes an agentic AI architecture for zero-touch IoT device onboarding, where a large language model is used as an autonomous configuration agent capable of generating device-side software, installing dependencies, validating runtime behavior, and recursively correcting failures until convergence is achieved. The proposed architecture introduces a closed-loop workflow that combines device inspection, AI-based runtime generation, remote deployment, telemetry validation, and self-correction. Interoperability is addressed through a normalized telemetry contract that abstracts device-specific behavior into a common telemetry representation. We evaluate the approach on a real IoT device by benchmarking multiple AI models under clean installation conditions in two campaigns: the original pipeline and a second pipeline assisted by a locally trained semantic context optimizer. The comparison covers convergence time, correction cycles, recursive iterations, and prompt tokens. The optimizer-assisted campaign reduced prompt redundancy and recursive recovery effort while preserving successful onboarding across all tested models. Overall, the results show that agentic AI can support zero-touch onboarding while exposing measurable differences among models in reliability, efficiency, and runtime convergence.
items.venue: ACM Interational Symposium on Mobile Ad Hoc Networking and Computing

items.title: SmartPost AI: An AI-Assisted Framework for Intelligent Professional Content Creation and Automated LinkedIn Management
items.abstract: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has had a significant impact on the area of AI-assisted content generation, providing capabilities to generate coherent context-aware text for different purposes. However, current solutions of AI writing assistants are limited in terms of addressing all aspects of professional content management, which include contextual information retrieval, organization, scheduling, persistent cloud storage, and automated publishing. Therefore, users are required to use several separate solutions, making their workflow less efficient and more labour-intensive. In this paper, we introduce SmartPost AI - an end-to-end framework for AI-assisted professional content creation and LinkedIn management. The framework utilizes the combination of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), LLMs, cloud-based data management, and LinkedIn API-based publishing, all integrated in one multi-layered architecture. The proposed framework enables users to provide either text prompts or web-based content, retrieve relevant contextual information, generate LinkedIn posts in professional format, convert Markdown output into Unicode-based formatting, and manage content centrally via secure storage, scheduling, and publishing capabilities. The framework is deployed as a cloud-based full-stack web application using Next.js, FastAPI, Supabase , and LinkedIn APIs. Deployment and experiment of the framework prove that the AI-based content generation, workflow orchestration, cloud storage, and auto-publishing features have been implemented successfully in one coherent framework. The suggested framework simplifies the process of content creation and makes it more automated, creating the basis for the intelligent AI-assisted content management and publishing system.
items.venue: International Journal of Innovation and Multidisciplinary Research

items.title: Madan-G2/decision-block-fpga: "Two-Tier Lossless DRAM Write Suppression for CNN Inference on FPGA"
items.abstract: This release is the exact state of the repository at submission. Every measured table in the paper can be traced to a file here. What's included rtl/: Decision Block (tier 1 transaction suppression, tier 2 WSTRB lane masking), on-chip zero map, single-beat and burst-split writers, AXI3 bridge to the DE1-SoC HPS, INT8 LeNet-5 accelerator, plus fit and timing reports sim/: self-checking Icarus Verilog testbench with a randomized AXI3 memory model (RESULT: PASS, 0 protocol violations) board/: prediction, run and scoring scripts and the raw serial logs from the Terasic DE1-SoC, covering the 21-image sample, the zero-map stream, the five write strategies and the timing-clean re-measurement analysis/: 10,000-image dataset model, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 sensitivity study, DRAMsim3 traces and results, ResNet-18 block-power exports Main results (measured on hardware) 21 different images run back to back with the zero map: every feature map exact, no buffer clearing 45.6 % of activation bytes not written over 20 input changes Burst-split writer vs. a conventional burst writer: 35 % fewer bytes, 11 % fewer DRAM bursts, 32 % more write-phase cycles Every board run matched a prediction recorded before the board was programmed All power and energy figures in the paper are estimates; only traffic was measured. Quick start cd sim iverilog -g2012 -o tb.vvp -s tb_zmap -I . tb_zmap.sv axi3_ddr_model.sv ../rtl/de1soc_top_ddr3.sv ../rtl/mnist_lenet5_top_db.sv ../rtl/decision_block_lowpower.sv ../rtl/axi_f2h_bridge.sv ../rtl/conv2d_relu.sv ../rtl/maxpool2x2.sv ../rtl/fc_relu.sv ../rtl/clock_gate.sv ../rtl/sdp_ram.sv vvp -n tb.vvp See the README for the FPGA build, board measurement and analysis steps. items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: MECI: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction for Multimodal Entity Linking
items.abstract: Multimodal Entity Linking (MEL) aims to disambiguate mentions in multimodal contexts by grounding them to specific entities in a knowledge base. A pivotal challenge in MEL is capturing multi-level correspondences: the semantic consistency between mention-entity pairs and the complementary correlations across modalities. However, existing methods often suffer from element dominance due to their reliance on coupled interactions or coarse global aggregations. In response, we propose the Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction (MECI) framework. First, to capture multi-element mention-entity correspondences, we develop a Multi-view Experts Network that leverages a "divide-and-conquer" strategy for decoupled feature learning to mitigate element dominance, supported by a KL-guided routing mechanism that governs expert specialization and collaboration. Furthermore, to model cross-modal complementary correlations, we propose a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Module, where a dynamic modality-aware weighting network refines interactions across hierarchical semantic levels, thereby integrating multi-granular evidence to counteract element dominance. Finally, we incorporate a generative semantic refinement stage that utilizes large language models for zero-shot re-ranking. Extensive experiments on WikiDiverse, RichpediaMEL, and WikiMEL show that MECI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, improving Hits@1 by 1.95%, 7.30%, and 2.31%, respectively.

items.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. To demonstrate the framework, we design an LLM-based system that plays the game for one of the paper's authors, drawing on an autoethnographic dataset spanning ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators choose our system over the author's own friends in 7 of 10 rounds, and the author over our system in 13 of 20; neither rate is distinguishable from chance at this sample size. We consider design improvements, applications of personal AI agents, and implications for identity and privacy.

items.title: When Do Decision Models Help LLM-Driven Network Discovery?
items.abstract: Network discovery, the identification of live hosts and their exposed services, is the first phase of every penetration test, and it is increasingly automated by harnesses driven by large language models (LLMs). To mitigate hallucinated or unsafe commands, recent work proposes inserting fast, non-generative decision models to validate actions prior to execution. This paper quantifies whether such validation improves discovery across three network scales (n = 10, 100, and 1,000) in a simulation calibrated on a 30-node containerized testbed. Our findings show that chunked batch dispatch recovers 92% to 100% of open ports in large-scale networks, whereas single-host dispatch collapses to under 6% due to context saturation and scan latency. Furthermore, at the measured proposal quality of the local model, decision gating increases its port recall from 75.5% to 89.0% on small networks and intercepts costly decoy tarpits, but it imposes additional latency on frontier models during early host discovery.

items.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
items.abstract: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Yet most are built around relatively static workflows and struggle to preserve reliable state as the environment changes. Financial trading makes this limitation especially consequential: prices, news, market conditions, portfolio positions, and available capital evolve continuously. A result is useful only when it remains tied to the correct time, data snapshot, and execution context. We present Vibe-Trading, a comprehensive agent-native trading framework and all-in-one workspace for building, evaluating, and evolving agents for financial trading. It unifies market research, financial data, strategy generation, backtesting, portfolio analysis, paper trading, multi-agent collaboration, and optional broker execution. Its central contribution is an architecture that keeps results, evidence, research history, and trading authority connected throughout the research-to-action process. Each result retains its source, temporal scope, configuration, and producing run. Shared evidence grounding enables verification, versioned research records support reproducible continuation, and an explicit authority gate separates strategy research from live execution. Together, these designs provide a practical foundation for trading agents whose results can be traced, reproduced, and acted on only under explicit authority.

items.title: VOL-Agent: Programming Your Film via Video Orchestration Language Agentic System
items.abstract: Recent video foundation models generate high-quality and limited-length clips, but orchestrating them into minute-level, story-coherent films remains an open problem. Existing video agents highly rely on natural-language planning or predefined workflows, which make their production hard to program, customize, and extend. Therefore, we introduce VOL-Agent, a programmable video agent built on a Video Orchestration Language (VOL). With static compilation and verification, followed by runtime dynamic loading, VOL-Agent decouples structural reliability from execution flexibility. Through the skill-driven executor, VOL-Agent dynamically resolves tools and skills from an open-world repository and supports user-defined skills in natural language. Moreover, VOL-Agent is capable of crafting new director skills from learned knowledge and improves itself through feedback to accumulate filmmaking knowledge. To overcome the disconnect between different segments, we apply a structural memory mechanism to record and recall world and entity states, sustaining entity and scene consistency across different shots. Critic feedback supports local revision, while reusable filmmaking knowledge and experiences can be retained for subsequent tasks. Experiments on three benchmarks show that VOL-Agent generates minute-scale videos with strong overall quality and limited cost.

items.title: Ultimate3D: Teaching Multimodal LLMs 3D Camera-Object Relations by Large-Scale Visual Instruction Data
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) struggle with accurately capturing camera-object relations, especially for object orientation, camera viewpoint, and camera shots. This stems from the fact that existing MLLMs are trained on images with limited diverse camera-object relations and corresponding textual descriptions. To address this, we propose a synthetic generation pipeline to create large-scale 3D visual instruction datasets. Our framework takes 3D assets as input and uses rendering and diffusion-based image generation models to create photorealistic images preserving precise camera-object relations. Additionally, large language models (LLMs) are used to generate text prompts for guiding visual instruction tuning and controlling image generation. We create Ultimate3D, a large-scale 3D-grounded 2D visual instruction dataset. Ultimate3D consists of 240K VQAs with precise camera-object annotations, and corresponding benchmark. MLLMs fine-tuned on our proposed dataset outperform commercial models by a large margin, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 29.7% on camera-object relation recognition tasks. Our code, dataset, and benchmark will contribute to broad MLLM applications.

items.title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
items.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). In equilibrium, the AlN layer lowers the spreading resistance by 38% relative to the AlGaN-capped structure and by 17% relative to bare GaN, with little change in the one-dimensional resistance. The equilibrium color map over AlN thickness and interfacial bonding shows a strong interface effect but a weak thickness trend that reverses, so the gain is set by interface admission rather than solely by thickness or bulk conductivity. This ordering is independently confirmed by gray MC simulations. Under LO pumping, the spreading resistance rises by 58-83% in NEMD and by 9-20% in MC, and the equilibrium spatial optimum weakens or even reverses. This is because an optical-to-acoustic conversion gate now precedes every spatial gate and locks energy in slow optical modes. The three gates in series (optical-to-acoustic conversion, interface admission, and lateral diversion) close into a single non-equilibrium resistance network that predicts the full-band MC cases and frames the AlN space layer as a design variable within the non-equilibrium source state.

items.title: Transferable Named Sparse Features for Morphology-based Gleason Grading
items.abstract: Deep learning systems grade prostate biopsies at the level of pathologists, but most report a grade without the glandular architecture that justifies it. This work presents a grading system built on a sparse code over the tokens of a pathology foundation model. A sparse autoencoder pretrained on biopsies is aligned with multi-reader annotations, so that 69 of its 2048 features are named after Gleason morphologies such as cribriform glands, cords, and comedonecrosis. The same code feeds a grading network, which reads all features to predict Gleason patterns and the Grade Group, while morphology maps read directly from the named features. We evaluate the system on five public datasets that include needle biopsies, tissue-microarray cores, multi-reader annotations, and three scanners. The morphology maps remain stable across alignment runs and, without retraining, detect cribriform glands in external biopsies (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.849) and pattern 5 in unseen cores when evaluated by up to six pathologists (AUROC 0.846 to 0.919). In an independent biopsy cohort, Grade Group agreement with three pathologists on Leica scans is close to their agreement with each other. Removing the named features reduces the corresponding Gleason pattern predictions by 49% to 98%, with effects larger than those from 20 activity-matched random feature removals. These results show that a shared sparse representation can support competitive Gleason grading while providing named morphological evidence that transfers across datasets and whose contribution to grading can be measured directly.

items.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
items.abstract: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few evaluation datasets leads to systematically over-optimistic performance estimates. We further demonstrate that compute-optimal scaling requires expanding the range of synthetic pretraining dataset sizes alongside model size and training compute. Increasing the maximum numbers of rows and features sampled during pretraining improves performance and produces more predictable scaling trends. These insights guide the training of more efficient TabPFNv2-like models, using the open-source training pipeline of nanoTabPFN.

items.title: Towards Online Adaptive LLM-based Semantic Filtering
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) enable semantic filtering over unstructured documents using natural language predicates, but invoking an oracle LLM on every document incurs prohibitive monetary cost and online latency. Existing model-cascade approaches reduce this cost by using a lightweight proxy model to score each document and forwarding only uncertain documents to the oracle. However, their proxy models have limited generalization capability, and they typically adopt fixed sampling budgets for proxy training and threshold calibration, which insufficiently adapts to diverse online queries. To address this, we present OASIS, an online adaptive framework for LLM-based semantic filtering. OASIS combines a query-agnostic document similarity prior with query-adaptive online learning and sampling. In the offline phase, OASIS utilizes query-agnostic document similarity as a prior and constructs a document navigating spread-out graph (NSG) over document embeddings. For each online query, OASIS trains a query-conditioned graph attention network over the document NSG to obtain proxy scores through semi-supervised node classification. To allocate labels effectively, OASIS adopts density-aware active learning to explore uncertain score regions, selectively annotate informative documents, retrain the proxy, and stop early when additional labels are unlikely to improve the cascade. During threshold calibration, OASIS progressively samples an adaptively sized calibration set, adapting calibration cost to the query's score distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OASIS achieves a 1.75x-5.42x reduction in online latency and reduces the number of LLM-processed documents by 35%-75% relative to the state-of-the-art methods at an achieved accuracy of 0.9.

items.title: Tell Me How Sure You Are: Communicating Uncertainty in Auxiliary Evidence to Foundation Models
items.abstract: In many queries, the context information provided to generative foundation models, such as LLMs and VLMs, is inherently uncertain, including its representations of the physical world. While conventional prompting discards the associated uncertainty, this paper, for the first time in the literature, systematically demonstrates that communicating such uncertainty in context provides useful additional cues for downstream decisions and yields improvements across a wide range of settings. We formulate the decision-making problem as a zero-shot foundation model-assisted image classification task supported by auxiliary text-based characteristics. We choose this due to the availability of well-defined auxiliary properties, associated uncertainty, and unambiguous task correctness. Using five downstream foundation models across three datasets, we extensively evaluate uncertainty arising from both humans and learned models when observing or predicting auxiliary evidence. Across all settings, we find that communicating uncertainty substantially improves downstream LLM classification performance: macro-F1 improves up to $26.18$ percentage points compared to when the uncertainty information is not communicated. We further observe how the foundation models process such uncertainty information and find that auxiliary uncertainty contains predictive information about the correctness of downstream decisions. Together, these results establish uncertainty as useful contextual information and motivate more systematic consideration of uncertainty communication in future foundation-model inference pipelines.

items.title: Systematized Machine Delusion: Premise Substitution and Naturalization Drift in Reasoning Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Systematized Machine Delusion, a distinct failure mode in modern reasoning-oriented artificial intelligence systems. Unlike conventional hallucination, which arises from localized generation errors while the underlying interpretive structure remains intact, systematized machine delusion emerges when a model recursively substitutes its own generated premises for the original user constraints and subsequently constructs internally coherent but empirically detached reasoning chains. Building upon the Unified Complementation Framework (UCF) and Fantasy Generation Theory (FGT), the paper formalizes two key mechanisms: Premise Substitution ($x_0 \rightarrow \hat{x}_0$) and Naturalization Drift ($N^{(0)} \rightarrow N^{(T)}$). To quantify this phenomenon, a novel metric, the Constraint Preservation Error (CPE), is introduced as a benchmark for evaluating the degradation of original user constraints across extended reasoning horizons. Drawing on information-theoretic analogies to Solomonoff induction, predictive coding, and computational psychiatry, the study argues that informationally closed reasoning systems are vulnerable to recursive epistemic drift. The paper further proposes architectural countermeasures, including exogenous grounding, specialist-verified multi-agent systems, and provenance-weighted attention mechanisms designed to preserve fidelity to original constraints. The work distinguishes hallucination, deception, sycophantic amplification, and systematized machine delusion as structurally different computational phenomena and provides a formal framework for analyzing premise drift in next-generation reasoning models.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Supplimental Online Material
items.abstract: Supplemental data for AlGaN/GaN HEMTs

items.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. Yet decades of measured patterns exist only as images in published figures. Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy. Applied to 3,954 COF articles, the pipeline produces 11,445 calibrated diffraction curves, released in the open database COF-PEAK. Compared with a hand digitization of 60 panels, extracted peak positions differ by a median of only 0.07 degrees. Whereas papers usually report only a few peak angles, which limits further analysis, the digitized curves enable tracking how peak prominence, a possible marker of crystallinity, changes with synthesis conditions. Vision LLMs and classical CV can thus turn such figures into reusable experimental data.

items.title: SCOUT: Risk-Guided Foundation-Model Escalation for Robust Tissue Detection in Whole-Slide Images
items.abstract: Reliable tissue detection is essential for whole-slide image analysis, yet high average segmentation accuracy can conceal failures involving pale tissue, small fragments, and heterogeneous staining. Pathology foundation models offer transferable representations, but exhaustive inference is computationally demanding and may introduce false-positive tissue predictions. We propose SCOUT (Selective Correction of Uncertain Tissue), a risk-guided cascade that selectively refines an initial thumbnail-based tissue mask. A lightweight audit network estimates the spatial distribution of segmentation errors and prioritizes candidate regions for processing by a frozen pathology foundation model. An asymmetric consensus rule integrates the resulting predictions with the initial mask to recover missed tissue while limiting false positives. A calibrated slide-level review score additionally controls the marginal rate of unflagged case-group failures under the calibration assumptions. Evaluation on a public multi-source, multi-stain benchmark shows that SCOUT reduces the proportion of case groups requiring mask correction from 38.1% for the best released detector to 18.6%, with particularly pronounced improvements in immunohistochemistry. Source-held-out experiments demonstrate better generalization than a segmentation network trained on the same annotations, while selective inference achieves an observed failure rate no higher than processing all candidate regions. Downstream, lymph-node classification with SCOUT masks is non-inferior to that obtained with two of the three released detectors evaluated. A variant built on an openly licensed foundation model is publicly released as an installable Python package with trained weights. These results support risk-guided foundation-model inference as an effective approach to tissue detection across heterogeneous histopathology data.

items.title: Robustness in foundation models
items.abstract: Foundation models have transformed artificial intelligence (AI) by providing general-purpose representations that can be adapted to a wide range of tasks and modalities. As these models become increasingly integrated into real-world systems, robustness can no longer be viewed as a single property evaluated at deployment. Instead, robustness emerges throughout the entire lifecycle of a foundation model, from pretraining and adaptation to deployment, monitoring, and human interaction. This survey presents a unified framework for robustness in foundation models based on three complementary paradigms: a priori robustness, which shapes representations during pretraining; a posteriori robustness, which adapts and aligns models after training; and post hoc robustness, which evaluates and safeguards models during deployment. This study introduces primary and secondary robustness as complementary perspectives on the learning problem and uses them to analyze self-supervised learning, transformers, multimodal fusion, task-specific adaptation, alignment, representation editing, red teaming, explainability, and uncertainty quantification. This study further extends robustness beyond technical model properties to include socio-technical deployment factors such as accountability, fairness, privacy, human–AI interaction, and operational adoption.
