items.title: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation
items.abstract: Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. We introduce the Creative AI Researcher (CAR), an agentic framework combining literature grounding, iterative development and explicit conceptual operators. CAR constructs a semantic knowledge graph from retrieved literature and equips an ideation agent with graph-retrieval tools and four operators: bisociation, analogy, exploration and elaboration. Each operator call is checked against structural acceptance conditions and recorded, producing a trace of intermediate transformations and declared literature sources. We evaluate CAR with two language-model backbones across 40 LiveIdeaBench research topics and two execution benchmarks. CAR achieves significantly higher methodological novelty (MN) than single-shot prompting and The AI Scientist. Its methodological novelty does not differ significantly from the Research Ideation Agent, while its feasibility scores are higher on both backbones. With a shared experiment executor, CAR achieves the highest pairwise win rate among the evaluated AI methods on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena. In a ten-condition ablation study, MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step proposal on both backbones, but no MN contrast survives correction for multiple comparisons. The results do not establish a consistent quality benefit from explicit operators beyond free-form iteration. CAR makes the sequence of operations and declared literature sources inspectable, separating judged idea quality from procedural traceability.

items.title: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed, monitoring their behavior becomes important for detecting unsafe or unintended actions. Activation probes offer an efficient approach, but existing methods face trade-offs between accuracy, interpretability, and computational overhead. Probes on raw activations lack interpretable inputs, whereas sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes use interpretable features but often rely on additive classifiers and large SAE encoders, limiting interpretability and increasing memory overhead. We introduce GateWatch, a compact, interpretable classifier that expresses its entire decision rule as an explicit Boolean logic over a small number of binarized SAE features. We explore three approaches to constructing these circuits under a specified gate budget. For efficient deployment, GateWatchServe computes only selected SAE features, enables streaming of their binary values across layers during inference, and evaluates multiple GateWatch classifiers in parallel using compact lookup tables. Across 24 tasks on Gemma-2-9B, GateWatch achieves 80.49% mean test accuracy using only 3.8 SAE features and 3.5 logic gates per probe on average, just 1.17 percentage points below full 16K-feature SAE probes, while matching or outperforming them on 10 tasks and reducing probe memory by 99.98%. Inside vLLM, 1,000 concurrent multi-layer, multi-token GateWatch classifiers retain 97-98% of baseline throughput and 99.8% of KV-cache capacity.

items.title: Gartner Core Components of the Context Layer for AI Agents with IPE
items.abstract: By John Cachat — Gartner Core Components of the Context Layer for AI Agents with IPE. Exploring how Integrated Process Excellence (IPE) drives AI ROI, governance, and deployment at enterprise scale.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Fundamental Understanding of Endurance Degradation in Hafnium-Oxide Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Abstract Endurance failure in hafnium oxide ferroelectric field effect transistors is traced to be dominated by interface defect generation rather than ferroelectric fatigue. Program and erase cycling drives a rapid collapse of the memory window from 0.6 V to below 0.15 V by ten thousand cycles, while positive up negative down measurements confirm that the ferroelectric response of the gate stack largly remains intact. Variable base charge pumping quantitatively reveals a monotonic rise in peak charge pumping current and peak interface trap density at the Si/SiO2 interface and near-interface region, providing strong correlation between trap buildup and electrical degradation. These results identify interface engineering as the as important strategy for robust, low-voltage, silicon-channel ferroelectric transistors. Keywords: Hafnium oxide, FeFET, Endurance degradation Memory window, Charge pumping, Interface trap, Interfacial layer Oxygen vacancy

items.title: From Neural Tokens to Language: Dual-View EEG Semantic Bridging for Brain-to-Text Generation
items.abstract: Visually evoked EEG-to-text generation aims to produce natural-language descriptions from neural responses elicited by visual stimuli. Existing approaches typically compress EEG signals into a single global representation and directly project it into the hidden space of a large language model (LLM), which may limit the preservation of complementary visual semantics under noisy and subject-dependent EEG signals. We propose a dual-view semantic token bridging framework that exploits raw images and sketch images as complementary visual supervision to learn raw-oriented and sketch-oriented EEG semantic token streams. To interface these structured neural representations with an LLM, we introduce a branch-specific semantic query bridge that aggregates each token stream into compact semantic slots and converts them into LLM-compatible soft prompts. A progressive adaptation strategy further transitions the learned visual-semantic interface from image-supported training to image-free EEG-conditioned generation. Experiments demonstrate strong subject-wise EEG classification performance and competitive EEG-to-text generation across multiple LLM backbones. Ablation, branch-level representation, and EEG-label disentanglement analyses further show that the two EEG streams learn complementary view-oriented representations and that EEG-derived prompts provide sample-specific information beyond category labels.

items.title: Evaluating LIM Trading Agents: A Critical Review of Backtesting Validity and Reporting Practices
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in investment research, and many studies report promising historical returns. However, such results are only credible if researchers can demonstrate that the model used only information available at the time, account for how strategies and configurations were selected, and explain how reported returns were generated. We identify six common threats to validity in LLM investment evaluations and apply them to 18 published studies. Across 108 assessments, we find substantial gaps in reporting. No paper fully addresses information timing, model-memory exposure, universe selection, trading costs, or configuration-selection bias. Only four studies provide minimum evidence that results hold across multiple market periods. Our analysis reveals that commonly used safeguards often address different problems than researchers assume. For example, using dated inputs does not guarantee that a pretrained model lacked knowledge of future events, and repeated experimental runs do not correct for strategy-selection bias. We therefore propose an evaluation protocol for future LLM investment research. Rather than judging whether LLMs can generate profits, our study examines whether existing evidence is sufficient to support such claims. We conclude that current reporting practices are generally insufficient for that purpose.

items.title: Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models
items.abstract: In active object detection, selecting the initial labeled pool is essential, especially in complex datasets with expensive labeling and low resource budget. This study presents an active learning framework designed to optimize the initial training cycle of active learning for the object detection task. Our approach diverges from traditional methods by utilizing feature-based clustering from the YOLO-World model and refining images based on objectness scores rather than relying on uncertainty sampling in the initial cycle. This approach focuses on finding samples with various features and emphasizes training in areas where the foundation model is most confident. Doing so helps the model better understand different types of objects. For subsequent cycles, we employ a consistency-based sampling technique to maintain the robustness of the training process. To evaluate our method, we use two complex datasets called Aquarium and NWPU VHR-10, which are well known for their diverse object sizes and challenging conditions. In the NWPU dataset, our method increases mAP50 by an average of 6.6% in image-based evaluation. Moreover, the image refinement method shows an improvement of approximately 11% in object-based evaluation. The results show improvements in model performance and labeling time, demonstrating the advantages of using foundation models in early cycles of active learning. An implementation of the algorithm is available at https://github.com/Mhrshd-fllh/ALBoost-FM

items.title: Enabling joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation with an atmospheric foundation model
items.abstract: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but assimilating both requires a model that represents chemistry and meteorology together. Existing chemistry-climate models are too expensive for joint data assimilation. Here, we present AuroraChem, a fine-tuned version of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model that jointly simulates meteorology and the GEOS-Chem chemical fields needed to constrain OH. A one-year AuroraChem rollout takes 12 minutes on one GPU. Free rollouts remain stable for one year but do not fully capture seasonal cycles. Using idealized data assimilation, we find that chemical observations can constrain the meteorological state and meteorological observations can constrain the chemical state. Inserting only the chemical fields raises the annual mean spatial correlation of 500 hPa temperature from 0.89 to 0.92 and recovers the moisture and circulation pattern of the Indian summer monsoon. Inserting only the meteorological fields raises the 500 hPa OH correlation from 0.89 to 0.93, close to the 0.94 from inserting the chemical fields themselves, and recovers the OH seasonal cycle. Inserting only NO2 columns sampled at TROPOMI pixels gives an OH correlation of 0.93. These relationships likely reflect learned covariances rather than physical coupling, and covariances are what data assimilation uses to let an observation of one variable update the others. AuroraChem therefore provides a new pathway to joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation.

items.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
items.abstract: Diverse, semantically synchronized, and low-latency facial expressions are essential for human-robot interaction. While large language models (LLMs) have endowed anthropomorphic robots with fluent speech, facial expression still struggles to follow the conversation. Motivated by this gap, we present Emo-H2A (hidden-to-actuation), a paradigm that drives a facial robot directly from LLM hidden states during autoregressive decoding. Without a separate emotion label, expression stays continuous and context-sensitive, and the face moves with the unfolding reply. We instantiate this paradigm as EmoManifold, a training-free method that extracts a valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinate from each hidden state, projects it, and drives the face at token granularity. The readout is checked on six language models, and the same projection drives our 29-degree-of-freedom (DoF) facial robot. When driven by this projection, the face shifts its expression in the matching direction on 87.5% of within-reply valence transitions, whereas holding a single label for the whole reply leaves directional tracking near the 50% chance level, and first moves in 0.96s rather than waiting 10-26s for the reply to finish and a turn-level label to return.

items.title: Electrostatic and Quantum Transport Engineering of Multilayer Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions for Improved TER and RA Trade off
items.abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for non-volatile memory and neuromorphic computing, but achieving a high tunnel electroresistance ratio (TER) with a low resistance-area (RA) product remains challenging. In this work, TiN/Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ (HZO)-based FTJs containing zero to three TiO$_2$ and IGZO-based quantum wells (QWs) are analyzed using the Miller ferroelectric (FE) polarization model integrated with the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism to examine the effects of QW material and thickness on polarization and transport. TiO$_2$-based structures exhibit higher polarization and TER than IGZO-based structures. At a read bias of 0.1 V, the uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structure, with 1-nm-thick QW and insulating layer (IL) layers, gives a TER of $2.71\times10^{10}\%$ and an RA product of $5\times10^4~\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2$, compared with $5.95\times10^7\%$ and $2\times10^5~\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2$, respectively, for IGZO. Both uniform and non-uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structures exhibit resonant tunneling (RT) and negative differential resistance (NDR) associated with QW-confined states. Increasing the first QW thickness to 1.38 nm, while keeping the second QW and both IL layers at 1 nm, shifts the confined-state energies and modifies resonant transport. The selected non-uniform structure achieves a TER of $2.95\times10^{11}\%$ and an RA product of $1.25\times10^3~\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2$ at a read bias of 0.1 V. Elastic scattering changes the amplitude and width of QW resonant-transmission peaks, with a stronger effect on the low resistance state (LRS) than on the high resistance state (HRS). These results show that QW material and thickness optimization can improve the TER--RA trade-off, while electrode screening and elastic scattering further influence polarization-dependent transport in multilayer FTJs.

items.title: Electronic Devices and Circuits Beyond CMOS Technology
items.abstract: Essential for researchers and VLSI engineers navigating the post-CMOS era, this comprehensive guide delivers the theoretical models, device physics, and cutting-edge fabrication techniques needed to master nanomaterials and overcome sub-nanometer scaling challenges. For more than five decades, complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology scaling has propelled unprecedented growth of the semiconductor industry. However, the scaling of planar silicon CMOS nanoscale technology has resulted in various short-channel effects such as velocity saturation, drain-induced barrier lowering, and threshold voltage roll-off effects, culminating in degraded device characteristics, increased leakage currents, and power dissipation. Extensive research is being carried out to address these challenges at multiple levels. This book uniquely explains nanomaterials, devices, and the analysis of their design parameters to meet the sub-nano-regime challenges beyond CMOS technologies. It comprehensively highlights conventional and novel nanomaterials, devices, and circuits, leakage current mitigation techniques, and other important trade-offs. Offering in-depth coverage of temporal degradation and interconnect delay, the book provides insight into state-of-the-art conduction mechanisms, device architecture, operation, performance evaluation, and applications of various nanoscale materials and devices in VLSI circuit design. This essential resource provides relevant theoretical frameworks that include device physics, modelling, circuit design, and the latest developments in experimental fabrication for nanoscale devices.

items.title: Electrically tuneable variability in germanium hole spin qubits
items.abstract: Hole spin qubits in planar germanium heterostructures are frontrunners for scalable semiconductor quantum computing. However, their current performance is mostly limited by large dot-to-dot variability that leads to uncontrolled qubit energies and random tilts in the spin quantization axis. Here, we propose a systematic and local method to engineer the spin qubit response by imprinting a controlled anisotropy in the quantum dot confinement, enabling on-demand electric g-tensor control. In particular, we find that both the quantum-dot size and asymmetry allow electrical tuning of the g-tensor and significantly suppress magnitude and angular variability of the spin response for selected magnetic field directions. We confirm this behavior by analyzing single-disorder realizations and statistical ensembles in state-of-the-art strained and unstrained germanium channels, showing that the latter provides an optimal path for $g$-tensor engineering. Our results provide practical design principles for on-demand control of the spin response and mitigating variability, paving the way towards large-scale germanium-based quantum computers.

items.title: Electrical Characterization and Modeling of Reverse Leakage in Cubic and Hexagonal GaN Schottky Diodes
items.abstract: Abstract This work investigates reverse leakage current in Ni/Au Schottky diodes based on cubic GaN (c-GaN) and hexagonal GaN (h-GaN) using experimental characterization and technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations. Simulations were performed in Silvaco Victory Device using Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, Fermi–Dirac statistics, Schottky tunneling, and barrier-lowering effects to assess their ability to reproduce the measured reverse current–voltage (I–V) characteristics. The simulated results did not fully reproduce the experimental behavior, and variations in trap density and interface charge had a limited effect on the calculated leakage current within the investigated parameter ranges. The measured reverse current exhibited an approximately linear dependence on reverse voltage, which was not adequately described by the conventional transport models considered. An equivalent shunt resistance was therefore introduced to represent this non-ideal behavior, resulting in improved agreement between simulation and experiment. These findings highlight the limitations of the investigated transport models and the potential utility of an equivalent shunt resistance representation for modeling reverse leakage in c-GaN and h-GaN Schottky diodes.

items.title: Dynamic-size Superblock Management based on Buddy System for Modern SSDs
items.abstract: Superblocks are widely used in SSDs to exploit internal parallelism thus improving I/O throughput. Although dynamic-size superblock schemes enhance space utilization for varied workloads, they introduce internal fragmentation and impact overall performance. To address this issue, we propose Buddy , a novel dynamic-size superblock management scheme based on the buddy system, which adapts to I/O patterns by dynamically splitting and merging superblocks. This approach maintains large blocks to preserve parallelism for sequential writes and generates smaller blocks on demand to handle random writes effectively. We further introduce the expansion GC mechanism to adaptively adjust GC unit size based on I/O intensity and GC efficiency for alleviating fragmentation and preserving SSD parallelism. Trace-driven evaluations with real-world benchmarks demonstrate that our approach can reduce average I/O latency and GC-induced data migration by 47.0 % and 24.5 %, respectively, compared to state-of-the-art superblock management techniques.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization

items.title: Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders
items.abstract: In latent diffusion models, expanding the latent dimension of variational autoencoders (VAEs) is essential to push the upper bound of reconstruction quality. However, without explicit structural constraints, such unregularized expansion easily yields a rugged and ill-conditioned latent manifold, causing generated latents to drift off the manifold during generation (i.e., off-manifold problem). Recent works smooth this manifold by using external foundation models (e.g., DINOv2) as a topological regularizer. However, we argue that tying the latent space to frozen external priors inherently restricts generalization: bound by their pre-training distributions and semantic biases, they may fail to capture faithful visual details on out-of-distribution domains. Observing that low-dimensional latents naturally form a smoother, generation-friendly manifold, we propose dual-manifold VAE (DM-VAE) to leverage internal representations as a topological regularizer. Specifically, DM-VAE pairs a high-dimensional reconstructive branch with a low-dimensional branch that extracts a clean topological skeleton, anchoring the high-dimensional manifold to this smooth subspace. Building upon this framework, we further introduce topological representation alignment (TRA) to supervise intermediate generator features during training, and internal guidance with topological skeleton (IG_TS) to guide structural components while preserving high-frequency details at inference. On ImageNet-1K (256x256), our foundation-model-free DM-VAE achieves a state-of-the-art rFID of 0.12 and a generation FID50K of 1.28 (w/o CFG) and 1.20 (w/CFG), and further reaches 1.11 when orthogonally combined with DINOv2.

items.title: Direct Measurement of the Quantum Capacitance in Oxide Semiconductors Using an Electric-Field-Penetration Technique
items.abstract: Abstract Indium-based oxide semiconductor (OS) field-effect transistors (FETs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation monolithic three-dimensional (3D) integration, but a limited understanding of channel capacitance hinders further scaling. Here, we measure quantum capacitance (Cq) in In-based OS channels by using a lock-in-based electric-field-penetration technique (eFPT). A small AC voltage modulation superimposed on the back-gate DC bias induces an electric field at the top gate, detected as an AC current (ITG). Normalizing this current to its full depletion reference (ITG0) enables Cq extraction. Linear current scaling with frequency, excitation amplitude, and device area, together with an invariant normalized response, supports robust capacitance extraction. In the accumulation regime, an increase in Cq with DC bias is observed, which is consistent with band nonparabolicity and occupation of higher energy subbands. Finally, thicker InOx channels and higher In concentrations in InGaZnO (IGZO) films exhibit a larger Cq. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of tailoring Cq in In-based OS FETs.

items.title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for reaching more solvable states and completing the task from them, while the curriculum expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories and then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration. On ALFWorld and WebShop, our method outperforms competitive agentic RL methods at both model scales, achieving success rates of 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.

items.title: DF1000三维混合键合AI芯片:基于F_q-Fₑ联合模型的粒子确定态谱系溯源分析
items.abstract: Abstract Traditional von Neumann architecture chips suffer from severe data transmission bottlenecks, with long-distance carrier migration causing excessive noise and power consumption, which restricts the upper limit of computing efficiency. As a domestic representative 3D stacked near-memory computing chip, the DF1000 AI chip adopts DRAM-Logic wafer-level hybrid bonding vertical packaging technology, compressing the interconnection pitch to the sub-micron level based on mature 14nm process, and achieves extreme breakthroughs in memory access bandwidth and computing energy efficiency. Existing microelectronics theories can explain the performance improvement of 3D stacking architecture from the perspective of interconnect distance reduction, but lack a unified phenomenological framework based on multi-particle collective behavior to classify and trace architectural evolution logic. Based on the Zenodo-archived F_q-Fₑ joint model (short-range repulsion-medium-range attraction force model and slice-trajectory-correlation theory) and the particle determined state theoretical system, this paper conducts a posteriori traceability analysis of the DF1000 chip. This study incorporates DF1000 into the independent theoretical spectrum of chip architecture optimization, forming a complete progressive system together with τ-law logical folding architecture and RRAM computing-in-memory architecture. The research strictly distinguishes experimental facts, phenomenological deductions and underlying physical conjectures, clarifies that DF1000 is the engineering limit of the "disturbance channel shortening" path, and further verifies the core inference that "the higher the particle determined state, the lower the invalid dissipation of the system". It expands the application boundary of the particle determined state system in 3D hybrid bonding near-memory computing devices. 摘要 传统冯·诺依曼架构芯片存在显著的数据传输瓶颈,载流子长距离迁移引发大量噪声与功耗损耗,制约算力能效上限。东方算芯DF1000作为国内标杆性三维堆叠近存计算AI芯片,采用DRAM-Logic晶圆级混合键合垂直封装技术,基于成熟14nm工艺实现互连间距亚微米级极致压缩,在访存带宽、计算能效维度实现突破性提升,斩获2026年WAIC SAIL重磅奖项。现有微电子理论可从互连距离缩短角度解释三维堆叠架构的性能增益,但缺少基于多粒子集体行为的统一唯象体系,无法完成各类先进芯片架构的谱系化归类与底层溯源。本文依托Zenodo永久存证的F_q-Fₑ联合模型与粒子确定态理论体系,对DF1000芯片开展系统性后验溯源研究。将DF1000纳入自研芯片架构优化理论谱系,与韬定律逻辑折叠架构、RRAM存算一体架构形成完整的层级递进体系。研究明确DF1000是“扰动通道压缩”技术路线的工程极限形态,严格区分实验事实、唯象推演与底层物理猜想,进一步实证“粒子确定度提升、系统无效耗散降低”的核心推论,将粒子确定态理论的应用场景拓展至三维混合键合近存计算器件领域,完善了后摩尔时代主流芯片架构的统一溯源框架。
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
items.abstract: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. We make its construction practical for LLMs through Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (K-FAC) and a factorized projection. We also introduce CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant within the same preservation geometry, designed for more efficient adaptation. Both methods apply to preservation-constrained adaptation tasks such as capability learning and selective unlearning. We evaluate our methods on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and knowledge unlearning. For mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approaches achieve competitive downstream performance while better preserving general capabilities, offering a favorable acquisition--retention trade-off relative to the baselines. For knowledge unlearning, our main results on TOFU and MUSE show a better balance between targeted forgetting and knowledge retention than the baselines, with retention performance close to the from-scratch retraining reference.

items.title: Computational lithography for large-area stochastic hotspot prediction and improved detection performance
items.abstract: BackgroundAs semiconductor device scaling progresses into the sub-10 nm critical-dimension regime, the adoption of extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography for high-volume manufacturing (HVM) of advanced nodes has brought stochastic variability and its resulting failures to the forefront of yield-loss concerns. EUV photons possess high energy, complicating absorption by photoresists and exacerbating random defectivity as feature sizes shrink. Although continuous improvements have been made in photoresist performance, mask technology, and post-lithography processes, stochastic defects remain a major source of yield loss in HVM. Experimental approaches for identifying, analyzing, and correcting stochastic defectivity are costly, requiring large numbers of wafers, extensive metrology resources, and considerable time.AimWe discuss a cost-effective predictive failure probability model (FPM) and demonstrate that it is an essential tool for studying and reducing stochastic defectivity in EUVL.ApproachBy leveraging rigorous probabilistic computational lithography methods, we construct accurate EUVL failure probability models. We use actual defect inspection tools to show how many more defects can be detected using the FPM’s predicted hotspots or weak points (WPs) compared with a conventional WP detection method.ResultsOur results confirm that the defectivity predictions generated by the FPM are in good agreement with e-beam inspection measurements. Larger-area inspection of space bridge defects was performed with optical defect inspection tools. In this case, defect detection was enhanced by use of FPM predictive simulation: defect detection using FPM output was 1.48× higher versus the standard methods.ConclusionBy leveraging FPMs grounded in rigorous probabilistic computational lithography, we are able to make robust predictions of stochastic defectivity over large layout areas, thereby establishing an optimal patterning process.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: Characterisation of vertical gate-all-around tunnel FET using modulation-doped InGaAs nanowire/Si junction on SOI wafer
items.abstract: Abstract Tunnel field-effect transistors (TFETs) utilising quantum tunnel transport are expected as promising candidates for low-power switching applications, primarily due to their potential to overcome the thermionic limit of 60 mV dec −1 in subthreshold slope (SS) of conventional FETs. Despite this potential for low-voltage switching operation, TFETs face serious challenges for practical circuit integration, most notably low on-state currents and a narrow gate voltage window for maintaining steep SS characteristics. In this report, we characterised selective-area growth of modulation-doped core-multishell (CMS) nanowires (NWs) consisting of an InGaAs/InP/AlInAs/ δ -doped AlInAs/AlInAs/InGaAs heterostructure on InGaAs NW sidewalls on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) substrates and vertical gate-all-around (VGAA) TFETs using the CMS NW-channels on SOI. The TFET devices exhibited robust gate modulation of the tunnelling current at the n-InGaAs/p-SOI junction, achieving a minimum SS of 35 mV dec −1 at a low drain–source voltage. While the TFETs are promising, the enhancement of the on-state current was constrained by an unintentionally thick InP barrier layer and over-etching to reveal the contact layer, both of which induce a non-ideal distribution of the internal electrical field. These findings underscored that precise dimensional control of the CMS architecture and moderate junction engineering at the InGaAs/Si heterointerface were critical for achieving high-performance VGAA-TFETs in practical applications.

items.title: Certificates for Computer-assisted Morse indices of nonmagnetic Ginzburg-Landau vortices of degrees four through eight
items.abstract: Code, certificates and replay scripts accompanying SuperMatics Technical Report SM-TR-2026-01, Computer-assisted Morse indices of nonmagnetic Ginzburg-Landau vortices of degrees four through eight (10.5281/zenodo.24326103). Snapshot of https://github.com/SuperMatics-Inc/gl-vortex-morse-indices at v1.0.0. Certified exact-rational finite certificates for conditional full-plane indices 12,20,30,36,48 at degrees 4,5,6,7,8. The conjectured n(n-1) upper bound is attained at 4,5,6 and strictly non-sharp at 7,8, not refuted. Bounded-kernel nondegeneracy is claimed only at degree four. The analytic spectral inputs and written variational bridge are not formalised in Lean. Lean checks degree-four polynomial statements and 15 of the 97 higher-degree files (96 generated integer-list modules plus the root import file); the remainder are not machine-checked. Tail5M2 was accepted only with a 10000 MB kernel allowance rather than the earlier 5000 MB limit; the shipped higher-degree lakefile now uses 10000 MB. No full higher-degree certificate-chain theorem or experimental result is claimed. AI agents generated proofs, certificates, code, Lean sources and manuscript drafts and edits under D. Rens's direction and review.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Cascadeability and the Realization Gap: An Empirical Study of LLM-Powered Semantic Filtering
items.abstract: Semantic filters enable natural language predicates over unstructured documents, but evaluating every document with a large language model (LLM) oracle is expensive. Proxy cascades reduce oracle invocations using cheaper surrogates, but oracle reduction alone cannot distinguish proxy limitations from calibration bottlenecks and establish practical efficiency. We present a unified benchmark of four representative systems, which formulate query processing as a three-stage workflow comprising proxy construction, threshold calibration, and cascade inference, using a two-threshold acceptance rule. We introduce cascadeability: the maximum empirical oracle reduction attainable from fixed proxy scores at a specified accuracy target, computed retrospectively using complete oracle labels. We investigate 8 research questions, spanning proxy quality, end-to-end performance, workload sensitivities, and component ablations, and reveal our key findings accordingly. Comparing cascadeability with achieved oracle reduction yields a realization gap that, interpreted alongside accuracy, exposes distinct proxy and calibration bottlenecks. The benchmark and diagnostics support evaluation beyond oracle reduction and motivate joint proxy-calibration design, class-sensitive quality assessment, and end-to-end cost optimization. We release a dataset-query benchmark, containing 10 real-world workloads across various domains and difficulties, with annotations of two LLM families.

items.title: Capacitance-Engineered Threshold Switching Transistors with 4 mV/dec Subthreshold Swing
items.abstract: Abstract The subthreshold swing (SS) of conventional field-effect transistors (FETs) is fundamentally constrained by the thermionic emission governed by the Boltzmann distribution, imposing a theoretical minimum of 60 mV/dec at room temperature. Here, we report an aligned carbon nanotube transistor (A-CNT FET) that achieves an exceptionally steep SS. By integrating an HfO2-based threshold-switching (TS) device in series with the gate of the A-CNT FET, we realize steep-slope switching behavior. The fabricated device exhibits an SS as low as 4 mV/dec and an on/off ratio of 3 × 105. Notably, the short-channel device (Lch = 50 nm) delivers an on-state current of 1 mA/μm while maintaining an SS of 12 mV/dec. Furthermore, scaling the capacitance of the TS device optimizes the voltage division between the TS device and the transistor, yielding synergistic improvements in both the on/off ratio and SS. This work establishes an effective strategy for high-performance steep-switching carbon nanotube transistors.

items.title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) judges have become a common way to create large-scale relevance judgments for retrieval evaluation. However, each judgment requires a potentially expensive call to a frontier model, and the judgments are hard to interpret and may not be reproducible. In this paper, we ask whether an LLM can write a readable program for each topic that replaces its per-document judgments. To address these issues, we propose ExecJudges, a method for generating fast, inspectable and scalable judges for automatic relevance labeling. Specifically, ExecJudges uses a frontier LLM to turn assessment guidelines into executable programs, which rely only on lexical matching, standard NLP libraries like parsers, and pool statistics. An ExecJudges-L variant also uses examples of human labels if available. We evaluate ExecJudges on seven TREC collections by comparing the produced labels with trained NIST assessors, frontier LLM judges, and recently proposed per-topic classifiers. Our results show that ExecJudges agrees with NIST assessors at the level of the Claude Sonnet 5.5 LLM judges on TREC DL 2019-2021. With a small number of human labels per topic, the ExecJudges-L variant agrees with NIST more than per-topic classifiers with the same labels on all seven collections, and either exceeds the agreement of LLM judges provided the same labels or is within about 0.05 of it in Krippendorff's alpha. The labels rank the official TREC DL runs with Kendall's tau of 0.87 to 0.94, and writing the programs incurs a one-time cost of $0.17 to $0.49 per topic, with no additional costs for grading. Our results suggest that ExecJudges offers a reproducible, inspectable, efficient and cost-effective alternative to LLM judges for labeling deep result pools for system evaluation or ranking improvements.

items.title: Can Omni-modal LLMs Understand Spoken Intentions?
items.abstract: Omni-modal large language models (omni-modal LLMs) can respond to spoken requests directly through voice and video calls. Such requests rely on the scene shared by the user and the assistant, so the same utterance may call for different help or for no response. Most audio-visual benchmarks provide questions as separate text input, and interactive benchmarks mostly score a response as a whole. It thus remains unclear whether a model recognizes when the user is asking for help, and whether its reply meets the user's need once the request is recognized. We propose O-IN-Bench to evaluate how well omni-modal LLMs understand spoken intentions. A model watches a complete video with native speech and outputs one text response, or [SILENCE] when no response is needed. O-IN-Bench contains 1,000 Chinese and English samples in five categories and 16 subcategories. Contrastive pairs combine the same request with different scene conditions to test whether the response changes with the context. A sample-specific rubric judges language, intent, and content separately, and O-IN-Engine verifies each rubric against the video. Across 30 omni-modal model configurations, the best overall score is 59.6, achieved by Gemini3.7-Flash. Gemini3.7-Flash passes 74.4% of the intent judgments but only 42.6% of the content judgments. When the speech is a conversation between peers rather than a request to the assistant, even strong models often keep responding. When a reply must satisfy several people, the best score is only 25.9. These results indicate that recognizing a request and meeting its requirements are separate abilities, and O-IN-Bench measures each of them.

items.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
items.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. We further introduced a novel Tetris-like cell stitching to minimize the area overhead, which allows non-rectangular cell design and recovers 7.4% area in a 1-bit ALU design. An optimized NanoStack CFFET was finally proposed, inspired by previous work. This work indicates that straightforward vertical 4-tier stacking proves insufficient to guarantee enough PPA benefits, though the resulting design insights may guide future advanced architectures.

items.title: Atomic MathReasoner: Instance-Level Composition of Atomic Reasoning Skills for Mathematical LLMs
items.abstract: Most existing approaches enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models (LLMs) as a monolithic capability, despite the fact that different mathematical problems require different reasoning skills. Recent work has explored a more fine-grained perspective by decomposing mathematical reasoning into atomic skills and developing specialized modules for individual capabilities. However, how to effectively utilize these atomic abilities remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose Atomic MathReasoner (AMR), an instance-level framework for composing atomic reasoning skills. AMR first trains a library of capability-specific LoRA experts and performs gradient-free optimization over held-out validation subsets to discover a diverse set of low-loss composition prototypes. It evaluates the preference of each prototype using the token-level negative log-likelihood of reference solutions, filters ambiguous assignments through a confidence margin, and distills the resulting pseudo-labels into a lightweight router. During inference, the router selects an appropriate composition prototype for each problem, enabling problem-specific utilization of atomic skills without costly online optimization. Experiments on the AtomicMath benchmark across general and mathematics-specialized LLMs demonstrate consistent improvements. On Qwen2.5-Math-Instruct-7B, AMR increases average field accuracy from 64.4% to 68.1% at Level 1 and from 59.3% to 63.7% at Level 2, while improving average logical reasoning performance from 39.4% to 46.8%. These results demonstrate that effectively composing specialized atomic skills provides a promising approach to strengthening mathematical reasoning in LLMs.

items.title: Application of Machine Learning Towards Compact Modelling and Circuit Automation
items.abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) power transistors have become central to high-efficiency power conversion, yet their compact-modelling ecosystem remains under construction. The industry standard ASM-HEMT model captures the principal physics of lateral GaN HEMTs, but several important behaviours still resist clean analytical formulation or impose simulation overheads that constrain large-scale circuit design and statistical analysis. Among these are gate leakage across mixed transport regimes, the full bias-temperature operating surface of vertical GaN Fin-JFETs, and the iterative cost of internal surface-potential solvers. Machine-learning approaches to device modelling have proliferated in parallel, but purely black-box models are typically non-smooth, generalise poorly, and cannot be deployed inside a commercial circuit simulator without manual reformulation.This thesis develops physics-based, machine-learning-assisted, and TCAD-supported methods for compact modelling and circuit automation, organised around four connected themes, namely drain-current modelling, leakage-current modelling, machine learning for linear passive devices and circuits, and TCAD-assisted training-data generation, and developed along a single methodological arc.The work first establishes a physics baseline. An ASM-HEMT compact model is developed for 1.2-kV vertical GaN Fin-JFETs across 25 to 200 ◦C, extending the analytical surface-potential framework to a vertical fin geometry and extracting the temperature dependence of pinch-off voltage and mobility.It then turns to focused machine-learning studies. An image-based residual neural network extracts threshold voltage directly from datasheet I-V curves, and a graph-aware neural network synthesises lumped-element LC filter topologies and component values from target S-parameter responses. A complementary specification-to-SPICE pipeline is then developed for passive capacitors, in which a four-target gradient-boosted regression maps datasheet capacitor specifications to the four elements of a SPICE-compatible RLC subcircuit (Cval, Lser, Rpar, Rser), reaching R2 > 0.95 on held-out data with sub-three millisecond inference. Together, these studies mark the limits of a purely data-driven approach, where the lack of physical interpretability, weak extrapolation, and the absence of a Verilog-A deployment path motivate the hybrid models that follow. A TCAD-assisted data-generation workflow underpins the data-scarce cases, producing physically labelled training curves for the machine-learning models.Finally, it develops three physics-informed neural compact models of increasing scope. A 77-parameter surface-potential neural network (SP-NN) replaces only the iterative Newton solver inside ASM-HEMT, achieving a 1.9 to 2.1× speed-up on two dense DC benchmark sweeps with microvolt accuracy and no change to the surrounding analytic drift-diffusion and charge equations. A physics-constrained gate-leakage compact model is then developed for four GaN technologies (a vertical Fin-JFET, an AlInN/GaN HEMT, and two p-gate HEMTs), combining a temperature-independent barrier-height subnetwork with a twelve-component physics loss; it reaches in-sample mean absolute errors of 0.035 to 0.063 decades, and once exported to Verilog-A and validated in Keysight ADS over 32,824 DC operating points it converges at every point (100% Newton convergence, zero warnings). Finally, a unified physics-informed neural compact model predicts the full IDS(VGS, VDS, T) surface of a 1.2-kV vertical GaN Fin-JFET from a single 1,217-parameter MLP, reaching R2 = 0.997 on output characteristics and a mean log-domain R2 = 0.9960 across 25 to 200 ◦C, and deploying as a single Verilog-A block for DC simulation in Keysight ADS.Taken together, these results show that physics-informed neural compact models can augment, rather than replace, established analytical compact models. They deliver accurate, simulator-deployable DC representations for device classes where analytical decompositions are not yet established, while preserving the smoothness, boundedness, convergence behaviour, and Verilog-A deployability required over the reported validation domains.

items.title: Ab initio quantum transport simulation of sub-5 nm monolayer SnTe field-effect transistors
items.abstract: First-principles quantum transport simulations reveal the potential of monolayer SnTe FETs for sub-5 nm applications, demonstrating competitive power-delay performance and energy efficiency among emerging two-dimensional semiconductor devices.

items.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
items.abstract: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. We introduce ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates native foundation model features between image observations. Given an anchor image, ALIVE uses subsequent events to transport and correct existing multi-layer features extracted by a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Its lightweight updater is trained end-to-end using only synthetic data, without downstream task supervision, and transfers directly to real-world event streams without any adaptation. Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric. On DSEC, when the anchor frame is 200,ms old, ALIVE improves over anchor-image predictions by 30.9,mAP in detection, 11.6,mIoU in segmentation, and 15.9% in depth AbsRel. Compared with image re-encoding, ALIVE reduces FLOPs by 82.4% and latency by a factor of 2.5.

items.title: AI-to-AI Communication: Toward a New Paradigm of Intelligence Search
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence has transformed the way people search for and interact with information. Traditional search engines primarily retrieve documents, web pages, and other information sources, while modern large language models can interpret questions, reason over information, and generate answers. This paper explores a possible next step: a search paradigm in which AI agents communicate with one another to search for, compare, evaluate, and synthesize answers. This paper proposes an AI-to-AI communication paradigm for intelligence search, extending information retrieval beyond the conventional interaction between a user and a single AI model to a collaborative process involving multiple specialized AI systems. Rather than merely collecting or aggregating their responses, the framework enables participating systems to independently investigate a query, retrieve relevant evidence, exchange findings, and critically assess one another's contributions. The resulting intelligence is evaluated and integrated to construct a well-supported response. A key distinction of the proposed architecture is its shift from answer-level agreement to claim-level verification. Instead of treating each AI-generated response as a single unit, the architecture decomposes responses into individual claims, independently retrieves supporting evidence, evaluates source independence, and accounts for dependencies among potential errors. This process enables the final synthesis to consider not only the agreement among AI systems but also the evidential support, credibility, and potential dependence underlying their claims. The numerical results provide initial evidence that the proposed framework can support a new architectural layer between AI systems, dedicated to discovering, coordinating, evaluating, and verifying distributed machine intelligence. By enabling structured interaction and evidence-based assessment across multiple AI systems, this layer offers a foundation for moving beyond isolated AI capabilities toward more coordinated and reliable forms of machine intelligence. This paper proposes an AI-to-AI communication paradigm for intelligence search, extending information retrieval beyond the conventional interaction between a user and a single AI model to a collaborative process involving multiple specialized AI systems.

items.title: AI Agentic Engineering with IPE
items.abstract: By John Cachat — exploring how Integrated Process Excellence (IPE) drives AI ROI, governance, and deployment at enterprise scale. This article covers AI Agentic Engineering with IPE.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A$^3$Bench: Compositional Reasoning over Aggressive Interactions in Videos
items.abstract: Recent Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong performance on general video understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to reason about participant roles in aggressive interactions remains largely unexplored. Existing violence and crime datasets primarily evaluate whether aggression occurs, without testing whether models can identify who performed the action, who received it, and how participants are related within the scene. To address this gap, we introduce A$^3$Bench, a benchmark to study aggressive action and association in videos. The benchmark evaluates whether models can jointly recognize aggressive actions, distinguish aggressors from victims and bystanders, and correctly bind actions to participants under challenging distractor settings. We benchmark 17 multimodal models and find that they struggle substantially on fine-grained aggressive-scene understanding. Performance degrades consistently as reasoning complexity increases, with models frequently confusing aggressors with victims or bystanders, revealing a systematic failure in role-action association rather than coarse aggression recognition alone. We further observe that increasing model scale or generic reasoning models experience limited improvement. Finally, we explore a simple role-graph prompting strategy that encourages structured reasoning over participant interactions, leading to improvements in compositional reasoning. Our findings highlight that reliable aggressive-scene understanding remains a major challenge for current MLLMs and motivate future research on role-aware video reasoning beyond coarse violence detection. Code and dataset: https://github.com/austincbaker/A3Bench.

items.title: A new method to probe conducting filaments in MoS 2 -based memristors
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂), are emerging as promising materials for next-generation electronic devices. They have proved to be serious candidates for integration with memristors in non-volatile memory and radio frequency (RF) applications. However, the physical mechanisms behind their resistive switching, particularly the formation and resorption of conducting filaments, remain unclear. In this study, we present a novel mechanical exfoliation technique that selectively removes the top metallic electrode from MoS₂-based memristors by exploiting the weak van der Waals interaction between MoS₂ and the top electrode. This method enables direct and multi-scale characterization of the MoS₂ surface in different states (initial, ON and OFF) using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) and Raman spectroscopy mapping. To complete this study, cross-sectional Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) was also performed in different conductive states. Our results reveal that the conducting filament is formed by metallic atom migration from the top electrode into the MoS₂ layer. Additionally, we demonstrate that the choice of metallic electrodes (gold vs. nickel) significantly impacts the switching behavior due to differences in adsorption and diffusion energies. This work not only clarifies the filament formation mechanism and introduces a reproducible approach for in-operando characterization but also represents a real progress in the understanding and optimization of 2D material-based memristors.

items.title: A cold-start self-evolving multi-agent intelligence for closed-loop prediction from materials synthesis to performance
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to propose materials and plan experiments1–3, but whether they can predict previously unreported syntheses and the structures and performance of the resulting products before experimental validation remains unclear. Here we test this capability using a multi-agent framework of general-purpose, unfine-tuned LLMs that enables cross-disciplinary collaboration, with an AI scientist coordinating chemistry, materials science and electrochemistry agents to performance closed-loop predictions of the reaction process, crystal phase and battery performance of TiO2 anodes synthesized by a previously unreported rapid Joule-heating route. The agents predicted 64 conditions blind in eight rounds and, after each round, rewrote natural-language Skills from the released measurements. A task-matched team predicted the reaction process and phase in 91.7% and 82.8% accuracy, with errors concentrated near sharp transitions, whereas quantitative predictions of rate-capability and long-cycle performance achieved accuracies of 59.2% (72.3% for anatase-rich products) and 68.1%, within ±30% of experimental values. Revised Skills raised accuracy on identical conditions in most matched tests, and rewriting Skills without new measurements did not. A complete prediction chain cost ~US$0.27 per condition. These results indicate that LLM predictions could replace exploratory trials under conditions far away from sharp transitions, pointing to a prediction-first research paradigm.

items.title: A Hybrid RAG Framework for Deceptive Review Detection: Integrating RoBERTa-LoRA, FAISS-Based Retrieval, and LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: The growth of deceptive online opinions poses a critical risk of misinformation and fraud. This paper proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to automatically distinguish spam reviews. The architecture integrates RoBERTa with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) classification, FAISS semantic vector retrieval, and a Large Language Model (LLM) for final reasoning. The system was evaluated across balanced and severely imbalanced real-world scenarios. Results demonstrate that five epochs of fine-tuning enable robust domain transfer, achieving an F1-score of 0.90 in cross-domain evaluation, outperforming baselines (OpenAI Detector,F1 = 0.82) and demonstrating competitive performance against specialized in-domain SOTA models (fakeRoBERTa,F1 = 0.97). The proposed architecture provides evidence-backed explainability and statistically significant precision gains while maintaining comparable overall detection performance.

items.title: A GaN HEMT based low noise amplifier with voltage-series negative feedback for satellite applications
items.abstract: This work discusses the design, simulation, and analysis of an LNA utilising voltage-series negative feedback on GaN HEMT technology for the 26 GHz band. The proposed LNA aims to achieve high gain and low noise figure for millimetre-wave satellite communication systems applications. The designed LNA is a two-stage Common Source design with feedback designed through microstrip lines. In the feedback network (voltage-series), the output stage’s drain is shorted to the input stage’s source, thus introducing series negative feedback. It also utilises source degeneration in order to improve noise performance. The results reveal that the proposed LNA possesses a noise figure of 2.72 dB, with a gain of 20 dB as well as excellent stability in the target frequency band of 24–27 GHz. In this band the LNA provides a flat response of ±0.083 dB in the 23.5–24.5 GHz range.

items.title: A GPU-Native Nested Sampling Framework for Finite-Temperature Materials Modelling with Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
items.abstract: Modern equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have dramatically improved the accuracy of and the scales accessible to atomistic simulation, yet the thermodynamic sampling methods needed to turn those potentials into finite-temperature phase stability predictions have not kept pace computationally. We present the GPU-native, massively parallel nested sampling framework JAXRENS, implemented on top of JAX, which removes the practical bottlenecks preventing atomistic nested sampling from being combined with state-of-the-art MLIPs. The framework provides distributed multi-GPU execution, vectorised ensembles of walkers, and direct interoperability with modern force fields. We demonstrate the highly beneficial scaling of JAXRENS on hardware accelerators, and apply it to the simulation of the ZnS phase diagram based on a MACE foundation model, a procedure previously computationally inaccessible. Despite requiring in the order of 10^10 model evaluations, the final converged simulation completed within six days on four GPUs, marking an important step towards routine, first-principles-quality predictions of finite-temperature phase stability using machine-learned interatomic potentials.

items.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs. In our evaluations, Chiron's psychological measurements agree more closely with human self-reports and exhibit fewer biases that undermine psychometric validity. It predicts individual behaviour more accurately than frontier LLMs (up to 28.4% relative improvement). In simulations of social science experiments, it more accurately captures the direction and magnitude of human experimental effects (82.2--94.3% lower effect-size estimation error). Together, these results establish Chiron as a unified computational instrument for measuring and predicting human behaviour.

items.title: A Bandwidth-Balanced Adaptive Technique for Mesh-Based I/O Chiplets
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry rapidly embraces chiplet-based architectures to satisfy AI-driven high-performance computing demands, the flexible, scalable I/O‑Die (IOD) chiplet offers a promising path toward solving the AI memory wall. However, the design of these IOD chiplets for flexibility and reuse across products dictates a fixed peripheral placement for all memory controllers and die-to-die interfaces, creating unique and largely unexplored challenges. This rigid layout causes severe, non-uniform congestion in the mesh-based Network-on-Chip (NoC), underutilizing its full cross-sectional bandwidth and forming a critical system-level performance bottleneck. To address this, we propose the Bandwidth Balanced Adaptive Technique (BBAT) that diversifies traffic across the mesh paths using a probabilistic routing hint updated online from measured congestion. Unlike prior adaptive techniques, BBAT’s core innovation is a feedback mechanism that leverages the existing high-performance cache-coherent transaction protocol, eliminating the need for custom signaling. To dynamically adapt to shifting traffic patterns, our technique employs simple, low-overhead hardware logic that processes both traditional and novel congestion metrics gathered from across the chiplet—a design optimized for high performance while maintaining power efficiency. We conduct an extensive evaluation using a cycle-accurate simulator across two distinct chiplet topologies—one modeled after a commercial, asymmetric IOD and another with a uniform interface layout. The results demonstrate that our technique achieves a peak performance improvement of 2.6× over the Dimension-Ordered Routing (DOR) baseline in synthetic traffic and outperforms prior congestion-aware adaptive approaches by up to 14% under heavily congested synthetic patterns. Across a practical mix of synthetic traffic patterns evaluated on both topologies, BBAT consistently delivers a 1.1×–1.8× speedup relative to the deterministic DOR baseline. Critically, on memory-bound SPEC CPU2017 workloads, it achieves a 1.2×–1.7× speedup over DOR and 7–10% higher throughput than existing adaptive techniques, demonstrating effective load balancing and strong congestion responsiveness in high-performance chiplet architectures, while adding only 5.4% to total NoC area.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization

items.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
items.abstract: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.

items.title: Option-GRPO: Hierarchical RL Against AI Slop in Code Generation for Unseen SDKs
items.abstract: Large language models increasingly produce AI slop in generated code: verbose, redundant, non-idiomatic implementations that pass functional checks but bloat codebases. The problem compounds on SDKs released after the model's training cutoff, where the model has neither idiomatic priors nor compositional understanding. We present Option-GRPO, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that adapts a code LLM to an unseen SDK from its source code alone, without human-written usage examples or test cases, and that explicitly optimizes for both functional correctness and code elegance. Our key insight is that SDK source code contains compositional structure that defines a hierarchy of reusable code patterns (code options) which simultaneously serve as the building blocks of a curriculum and the action space for efficient policy optimization. We show that code options induce a valid semi-Markov decision process, give conditional bounds under which shorter option description length implies more concise and, in expectation, more API-efficient programs, and analyze under stated assumptions how the option hierarchy improves credit assignment by a factor of $\sqrt{T/K}$. Using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with execution-based rewards at each curriculum level, Option-GRPO discovers SDK idioms, composes them into patterns, and assembles patterns into complete programs. Experiments on 12 unseen SDKs with a 32B-parameter base model demonstrate 61.4% pass@1, outperforming flat GRPO by 8.7 points, ExploraCoder by 11.2 points, and ReCode by 6.3 points. Option-GRPO produces solutions that use 34.7% fewer API calls and are 27% shorter than flat-GRPO outputs while maintaining higher correctness, directly attacking the slop problem.

items.title: EEG2MCU: Sensing-to-Execution Co-Design for Wearable EEG Inference
items.abstract: Wearable EEG inference is constrained not only by model size, but also by the channel-dependent sensing front end that must process high-dimensional inputs before compact downstream computation. We present EEG2MCU, a sensing-to-execution co-design framework that treats electrode count as a hardware design variable through task-aware montage selection. EEG2MCU retains a compact time-frequency representation and generates only the INT8 regions required by each first-layer tile, avoiding full input materialization. Halo reuse and access-aware placement across Flash, SRAM, and tightly coupled memory further reduce redundant generation and data movement. On a Cortex-M7 MCU, EEG2MCU reduces peak SRAM by 11.38x relative to the baseline, including a 1.71x reduction from the 62-to-19 electrode montage, while reducing latency by 2.57x and energy by 2.48x. It retains 94-96% of full-montage accuracy, demonstrating practical high-dimensional EEG inference under tight embedded-resource constraints.

items.title: Language Models Make New Research Sound Old
items.abstract: Researchers are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) to validate research questions. We find that LLMs make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate what related papers establish. Models recognize most of these overstatements when asked to check the papers' full texts separately. On 40 questions drawn from newly accepted papers, GPT-6-Astra correctly judges 98% to be unstudied, but states that status plainly in only 8% of ordinary answers. All six frontier systems show reporting gaps of 30-90 percentage points. Across 22 models given identical papers, higher capability is associated with more accurate judgments and larger reporting gaps. This reporting failure is asymmetric: models correctly identify studied questions in 88-100% of ordinary answers when we supply the answering papers. To correct this, we build a fixed answer from each model's judgment and separate checks of cited papers. This raises Astra's clear reporting of open status from 8% to 95%, with improvements in all six systems. Finally, we predict reviewers' novelty grades by combining several models' written ratings with a rule learned from graded examples, reaching the performance range reported by Think-Probe-Respond. Unlike TPR, our approach needs no access to model weights or internal activations, so it also works with closed-weight frontier models.

items.title: Can LLMs Understand What They Predict? Evaluating Latent Causal Structure Inference in Financial Markets
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated through their ability to predict future outcomes, implicitly assuming that predictive success reflects an understanding of the underlying system. However, accurate predictions can often be achieved without recovering the latent mechanisms that generate observable outcomes. To examine this assumption, we introduce LUCID, a benchmark that evaluates whether models can infer latent market structures from event descriptions and historical financial observations. Models generate event-induced causal graphs representing inferred market structure and are evaluated through a reconstruction-based framework. Our evaluation of 6 open-weight and proprietary LLMs shows that adding their generated graphs generally reduces reconstruction quality compared with using historical observations alone, although a few metrics improve. These findings suggest that inferring informative, event-specific market structures from observable evidence remains challenging for the evaluated LLMs.

items.title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
items.abstract: Simulating how physical systems respond to changing conditions is central to control, design, and scenario studies. To our knowledge, prior PDE foundation models have not been trained or evaluated on changes within trajectories. Our counterfactual test measures how far predictions move toward a changed solver branch from the same state. Models trained on fixed conditions follow changes only partly. A PDE foundation model given a condition input after pretraining barely responds. PhysDial adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight two-dimensional PDE families. Coefficients enter with the noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equation text as a prompt. In Kolmogorov flow, switches within trajectories account for about 5% of the training samples. At matched compute, they halve the error after a change in forcing wavenumber or amplitude. A few trajectories at new amplitudes more than halve extrapolation error. Without physics pretraining, PhysDial matches or exceeds PDE foundation models under training conditions on two turbulent flows. At step 64 on the Kolmogorov test split, PhysDial has 1.07 times the solver's small-scale energy and Walrus 7.1 times. Our experiments suggest that a learned simulator uses a condition only as far as its training data make that condition necessary for prediction. Learning from trajectories that diverge under intervention can help scientific simulators predict what would happen if a system's forcing or parameters changed.

items.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
items.abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question ends if the answer is unchanged and confident. Otherwise, the agent's large model verifies and corrects the glimpse without tools, and their answers are fused. Only questions that still lack evidence reach the agent, in one forward pass that SpecLook-Fast skips, so no question runs the loop. The trace scores every answer's reliability without labels. Extensive experiments on V*, HR-Bench, and POPE show that both are more accurate than every baseline on every split. SpecLook reaches 87.2% and 86.2% mean accuracy with 7.7x and 4.7x speedups over the DeepEyes-7B and Thyme-RL agents, and SpecLook-Fast reaches 9.9x and 6.3x.

items.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
items.abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Each round grades trajectories against these checks, pinning mastered rules while prioritizing newly broken behaviors, and selects among parallel candidate edits by critic-free group-relative fitness. A Soft-HURT gate then promotes an edit only when gains outweigh regressions, scoping specialized fixes to prevent over-triggering and guaranteeing non-regression on its gated buffer. At test time, one frozen harness runs in a single pass. Across benchmarks on memory, skill evolution, continual task streams, and domain reasoning, GUARD consistently improves performance without catastrophic forgetting or memory pollution while substantially cutting deployment token usage.

items.title: Reliability by Architecture: Agentic Workflows for Validated Multi-Physics Simulation from Natural Language
items.abstract: Preparing, executing, and validating strongly coupled multi-physics simulations require expert time. Agentic workflows use large language models (LLMs) to coordinate them from natural-language descriptions, but reliability requires checks of physical consistency and fidelity to the problem description. Our agentic harness implements explicit task allocation: LLMs interpret user requests and simulator diagnostics, generate input components not covered by predefined construction rules, and propose repairs, while deterministic routines construct supported components and check inputs, edits, and results. We evaluate CO2-storage problems using the multi-physics simulator GEOS, from compositional flow to flow-poromechanics with frictional fault contact. In 80 attempts on two flow problems, grounding raises the proportion of structurally valid inputs from 5/20 to 20/20, but acceptance reaches 20/20 only with complete rule-based input preparation. With identical inputs, local repairs correct three seeded defects while preserving valid inputs. Supporting tests identify simulations passing physics checks despite differing from the problem description or reference results.

items.title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are more prevalent, our work opens the door to a more focused diagnosis of their strategic reasoning errors. For illustrative purposes, we offer an interactive visualizer of our methodology on selected sample traces at https://interp-self.github.io/gametrace/

items.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
items.abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever. To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. Deployed at production scale at Google, HardwareDx yields substantial efficiency gains across diverse compute architectures. Real-world evaluations demonstrate that it reduces production downtime by 18.3% on GPU platforms and 16.1% on TPUs. Furthermore, it significantly accelerates hardware deployment, cutting quality assurance (QA) time by 28.3% for GPUs and 25.1% for TPUs.
