The two nudge conditions also showed numerically similar Behavioral Similarity (BS) values despite differences in human evaluations. These preliminary findings suggest a potential trade-off between supporting human reasoning and maintaining perceived naturalness, highlighting the need to consider both agent behavior and human perception when designing supportive human–AI interactions.

items.title: Neuron Oscillator Computing
items.abstract: Neuron oscillator computing is an invention by the author and his colleague, Jon Borresen. We applied for our first patent in 2010, which was granted in 2012, and a second patent was granted in 2015. The reader should note that neuron oscillator computing, using brain dynamics to build conventional computers, is the opposite of Artificial Intelligence (AI), using conventional computers to simulate brain dynamics, however, understanding how biological neurons work is fundamentally important in AI. The invention could lead to computers that are one million times more efficient than transistor-based computers and building assays for neuronal degradation. Aims and Objectives To provide a brief history of modeling neurons. To review basic operations of neurons, including excitation, inhibition, and threshold voltages. On completion of this chapter the reader should be able to model biological neurons; perform simple binary logic and memory operations using neurons; plot time series data to illustrate functionality; appreciate the potential applications of the invention.

items.title: Negative Capacitance-Driven Organic Memory Phototransistors with Ultralow Subthreshold Swing for Flexible Energy-Efficient Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Organic memory phototransistors (OMPTs) promise advanced flexible neuromorphic systems; however, their practical deployment remains hindered by high power consumption and a limited memory window. Here, we demonstrate an organic phase-change semiconductor-based memory phototransistor (OPCMPT) with photoelectric modulation, a steep subthreshold swing (SS ∼ 46 mV/dec) and a large memory window capacity (γ ≥ 75%), outperforming existing organic memories. This stems from tailored negative capacitance (NC) engineering and TDPA-based self-assembled monolayer modification, which improves NC/organic semiconductor interface compatibility and resolves the steep-SS versus high phase-change efficiency trade-off in OMPTs. Moreover, the flexible NC-OPCMPT array maintains mechanical stability at a 1.5 mm bending radius and achieves ∼90% recognition accuracy with strong fault tolerance at noise ratios >30%. Importantly, the OPCMPT efficiently implements multiply-accumulate operations and convolutional image processing with multiple operators, enabling real-time edge detection and motion tracking via hardware-accelerated convolutional computing, highlighting its strong potential for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing technology.
items.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C

items.title: Navital Gym: Rule-Graded Agent Environments for Indian Workflows
items.abstract: AI agents are being deployed on Indian workflows such as payments, tax, forms, travel and customer support in Hindi and Hinglish. Public agent evaluations rarely cover these workflows, and many score with another language model. We present Navital Gym, a set of six open environments with 321 public tasks in five task families: trip planning, UPI payments and disputes, GST invoicing and returns, form filling (including a multi-document split) and customer support in Hindi, Hinglish and three experimental Indian languages. Every task is graded by named, deterministic rules that recompute the outcome from a synthetic sandbox world. No language model judges any score. We report one run per task for three models on all six environments, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 4.5, and for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on two (UPI and the Support core). Opus solves 315 of 321 tasks, Sonnet 302 and Haiku 205. Trip planning and Hindi/Hinglish support separate the models most. We also describe a private held-out set that is not published, and a 7B adapter trained in the gym. Code is Apache-2.0 and task data is CC BY 4.0. The rules are a documented simplification of Indian practice, not the live systems.

items.title: Natural Organic Fructose-Based Resistive Switching Memory
items.abstract: Abstract The growing demand for energy-efficient computing with minimal e-waste has accelerated interest in natural organic materials, such as carbohydrates and proteins, for neuromorphic electronic components due to their renewable and biodegradable nature and potential for environmentally friendly disposal. This study presents resistive-switching random-access memory (ReRAM), a critical component for neuromorphic systems, formed by a carbohydrate material—fructose. Compared with other reported fructose devices, this new ReRAM device exhibits electroforming-free bipolar resistive switching behavior, lower SET and RESET voltages, and synaptic functions such as long-term potentiation and depression, spike-rate-dependent plasticity, and analog conductance modulation through voltage and frequency control. Furthermore, the performance of this fructose-ReRAM device in neuromorphic computing systems was also evaluated, including linearity, inference accuracy, and latency, using handwritten digit recognition with a machine learning algorithm, stochastic gradient descent, and the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology database. These results establish the potential of fructose as a promising natural organic material for future sustainable neuromorphic computing systems.

items.title: NL2RCtrl: Risk-Controlled Controller Synthesis from Natural Language Requirements
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled the translation of natural language (NL) requirements into linear temporal logic (LTL) specifications, facilitating controller synthesis for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, the reliability of such translations remains a concern in safety-critical applications, particularly when NL requirements are ambiguous. This paper proposes a framework based on Conformal Risk Control (CRC) to provide a statistical guarantee on the risk of issuing a controller that violates the user's intended requirement. Rather than requiring semantic equivalence between the generated and intended specifications, the proposed approach considers language inclusion, a sufficient condition for ensuring that the traces of a controller synthesized for the generated specification satisfy the intended requirement. To account for ambiguity, the LLM is queried multiple times, and the resulting LTL specifications are grouped into semantic equivalence classes and ranked by their frequency of occurrence. Given a prescribed risk level, CRC selects how many of the top-ranked equivalence classes to combine into a single LTL specification, such that the probability of issuing a controller that violates the intended requirement is bounded by that level. A controller is then synthesized for the resulting specification, or the framework abstains. Experiments on a vehicle navigation case study evaluate the proposed approach.

items.title: NARA – NAtural Relationship with Agents: Haptics and Conversational AI as Forms of Communication with Immersive Companions
items.abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) became widely available, enabling the simulation of visual and auditory experiences. However, there remains a lack of sufficient sensory and contextual cues to help users feel fully present, thereby limiting the user experience. We aim to shed light on forms of communication with virtual agents, specifically touch (haptics) and conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI), using a Large Language Model (LLM), within Immersive Virtual Environments. We created a VR setup to compare participants’ subjective perspectives (quantitative and qualitative) regarding a virtual animal companion, represented as the deer Ralph in a winter forest setting. Haptics thereby foster natural interactions, while conversational AI provides context-focused reactions from an LLM. We conducted an empirical study with 30 participants to examine the influence of two main forms of communication (factors) across two conditions (levels) each on participants’ perceptions: Active Haptics and Passive Haptics vs. Verbal AI and Non-Verbal AI. Our results underscore the perspective that Active Haptics and Verbal AI outperform their less sophisticated levels, Passive Haptics and Non-Verbal AI, in interaction qualities, presence, as well as technology-specific characteristics. However, more importantly, each level provides unique advantages for use in the context of a smart animal companion. Active Haptics accelerates realism, while Passive Haptics offers a low-complexity option focused on tactile interactions. In the case of an LLM agent, Verbal AI fosters positive emotions and engagement, while Non-Verbal AI enables subtle interactions and an enhanced perception of responsiveness.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology

items.title: Multistability and State‐Switching in Series‐Coupled Resonant Tunneling Diodes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Resonant tunneling diodes (RTDs) embedded in an electrical circuit are known for their neuron‐like response characteristics, which makes them promising candidates for neuromorphic applications. This paper investigates the dynamical response of series‐coupled RTDs and systematically analyzes the impact of coupling and inhomogeneities on the solution structure. We further propose a scheme for controlled switching between coexisting stable states which allows to realize tunable memory elements in these circuits. The coupled RTD system exhibits a rich bifurcation structure, showing different degrees of multistability between symmetric and antisymmetric solutions. Limit‐cycle branches and their dependence on the system parameters are analyzed using numerical continuation methods. A central focus is placed on the role of symmetry. For two identical RTDs, the system possesses a exchange symmetry, which governs the emergence of symmetry‐breaking bifurcations and multistable states. The analysis is further generalized to coupled RTDs, revealing the underlying symmetry structure and its influence on the organization of equilibrium branches, paving the way for neuromorphic network operation.

items.title: Multi-LLM Agentic AI at the Edge: Joint Agent Scheduling and Resource Allocation
items.abstract: In this paper, an edge-enabled multi-large language model (LLM) agentic AI architecture is proposed, where one supervisor AI agent and multiple worker AI agents cooperatively execute users'requests at the edge. The supervisor AI agent decouples the user request into a series of sub-tasks and dynamically dispatches them to LLM-equipped worker AI agents via two agentic workflows, i.e., parallel and serial workflows, with a two-level retry mechanism to enhance execution reliability. To prolong the service duration of worker AI agents, the energy minimization problems are formulated by jointly considering AI agent selection and resource allocation, subject to task execution latency and quality of service (QoS) constraints. A resource allocation scheme based on alternating optimization (AO) is proposed. Specifically, for the parallel workflow, the scheme decouples the original problem into bandwidth allocation, retrieval selection and AI agent selection sub-problems, which are iteratively solved by the proposed successive convex approximation (SCA), Lagrangian relaxation (LR), and Gale-Shapley (GS) or LLM-based algorithms, respectively. For the serial workflow, the problem is similarly decoupled into service time allocation, retrieval selection and AI agent selection sub-problems; the optimal service time allocation is obtained via Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, while the latter two sub-problems are addressed by extending the proposed algorithms to the serial scenario. Simulation results show that the proposed resource allocation scheme can reduce system energy consumption compared with other benchmarks, while experiments on a multi-LLM agentic AI system based on Qwen and Llama demonstrate improved task execution success rates.

items.title: MiSTiQ: MicroScaling Trellis Quantization for Extreme KV Cache Compression
items.abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) increasingly support longer contexts and serve more concurrent requests, increasing both sequence lengths and batch sizes. Both trends increase KV-cache size and memory traffic during inference. KV-cache quantization reduces these costs, with recent approaches using codebook-based vector quantization to achieve extremely low bit widths. However, hardware constraints limit codebook size, and most methods reconstruct the cache in higher-precision floating-point formats for attention, limiting the computational benefits of quantization. To address these limitations, we introduce MiSTiQ, a drop-in replacement for codebook-based vector quantizers that combines trellis-coded storage with microscaling (MX) formats for low-precision computation. We combine trellis quantization with beam search to encode the KV cache over large reconstruction spaces without large codebooks. To support MX computation, we derive MX-Hash functions that generate reconstruction values directly in the target MX element format. These functions use the scale-conditioned marginal distribution of block-normalized Gaussian inputs. On Llama3 and Qwen3, MiSTiQ achieves lower WikiText perplexity and higher GSM8K accuracy than the evaluated baselines across several block-scale formats at approximately 1.25 effective bits per element. With NVFP4, it also achieves the highest LongBench average on both models.

items.title: Mechanism of Polarization Switching in IWO‐Based Ferroelectric Devices Under the Influence of Trap States
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide/semiconductor interfaces play a critical role in determining polarization‐coupled switching in hafnium–zirconium oxide (HZO)‐based ferroelectric thin‐film transistors (FeTFTs). Herein, bottom‐gate HZO//indium tungsten oxide (IWO) FeTFTs are investigated to clarify how interfacial charge trapping at the /IWO interface influences program/erase switching and cycling stability. The fabricated devices exhibit stable n ‐type transistor characteristics and reversible threshold‐voltage modulation, while ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) measurements confirm voltage‐dependent polarization switching in the HZO‐based stack. The program and erase operations exhibit asymmetric threshold‐voltage modulation, with a smaller positive threshold‐voltage shift during erase than the negative shift during program operation. Under repeated program/erase cycling, both the programmed and erased threshold voltages drift toward positive gate bias, resulting in a reduced memory window. Increasing the assumed effective /IWO interfacial trap density in TCAD qualitatively reproduces these trends, suggesting that interfacial trapping may contribute to the degradation. Changes in polarization switching and oxide‐trap states within the HZO/ stack may also play a role. These results provide an oxide‐channel‐specific interpretation of polarization–trap coupling and identify the /IWO interface as an important control point for polarization‐coupled switching and cycling stability in oxide‐channel FeTFT memory devices.

items.title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
items.abstract: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. Specifically, the Lift phase elevates 2D video observations into dense 3D representations by adaptively aligning features in the policy's shallow layers with the intermediate representations extracted from multiple 3D FMs. Building upon these lifted representations, the See phase equips the policy with explicit geometric and interactive awareness through dual guidance. It introduces depth-map reconstruction to help the model comprehend 3D spatial layouts and utilizes hand region cues to explicitly supervise the encoder's attention toward task-relevant interaction hotspots. Empowered by the dense 3D representation learning and precise spatial guidance, our policy achieves robust and accurate robotic manipulation in the Act phase. Extensive experiments on diverse simulation and real-world tasks demonstrate that LSA significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches. The project page is available at: https://yiyuan00.github.io/Lift-See-Act.

items.title: Language Models Meet Vibration Testing for LEO Constellation Satellites with Calibrated Response Prediction from Few-show Sweeps
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly drive engineering analysis end to end, turning textual records into the inputs of numerical programs, but a plausible and wrong value can pass silently into a decision. We propose deterministic validation gates for LLM-driven engineering analysis, a general paradigm in which a typed configuration produced by LLMs is consumed only after it passes deterministic checks on units, physical consistency, verbatim quotes, agreement between independent models, consistency with measurement exports and the applicability of trained models. The gates target hallucinations from two directions, since quote checking catches fabricated content while agreement between models catches errors of omission that quote checking misses. We instantiate the paradigm on sine vibration acceptance testing for low Earth orbit mega-constellation satellites, where DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Qwen-plus read Chinese test records and extract a configuration of 76 fields. Fact-level F1 ranged from 0.98 to 1.0 on five input variants, with all repairs frozen on development inputs and evaluated on held-out inputs. With all gates, 20 of 20 configurations produced notching results bit for bit identical to the gold run, and all 17 real and injected errors in consumed fields were stopped, of which 16 would have run without gates. Retraining the bound model on a dataset built from an LLM configuration reproduced its results within GPU nondeterminism. We also report a negative result of practical value. Direct LLM curve forecasting only matches linear extrapolation, whereas a small physics-structured network reduces the over-notched bandwidth by 86% to 89% at calibrated coverage c = 0.90, which delineates where direct LLM prediction should give way to a trained model.

items.title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana
items.abstract: Cross-chain bridges have suffered substantial asset losses due to vulnerabilities in their on-chain programs. On Solana, missing validation checks can enable exploits even when the underlying blockchain operates correctly. The ability of large language models (LLMs) to diagnose these flaws from source code or transaction records, rather than merely raise alarms, remains insufficiently understood. We implement a native Rust lock-and-mint bridge on a local Solana validator with four exploitable variants: two model flaws from the Cashio and Wormhole incidents, while the other two represent vulnerability classes documented in Solana security audits. Paired vulnerable and secure programs, together with successful attacks, benign sessions, and blocked attempts, allow us to distinguish correct diagnoses from unsupported alarms. We evaluate six configurations of five open-weight models across 16,800 responses, compare source inputs with and without comments, and grade 7,200 answers on vulnerable inputs using two blinded LLM graders. The results reveal substantial differences across conditions: without comments, models diagnose 24% of vulnerable source inputs while frequently flagging the secure bridge. Transaction diagnosis is high for the missing-signer scenario but averages 6% across the other three scenarios. Original comments, some of which describe the flaw, increase source diagnosis to 60%. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing correct vulnerability diagnoses from unsupported alarms in bridge security review.

items.title: LLM-Judge Behavioral Coding Scheme for Agent Teammate Quality
items.abstract: Evaluating whether an AI agent behaves like a good teammate is becoming a bottleneck as multi-agent language-model systems proliferate, because human ratings do not scale to the transcripts these systems generate. We ask whether a language model can stand in for a human rater of teammate quality, offering a controlled proof-of-concept validation rather than a large-scale study. Drawing on the autonomous-agent teammate-likeness construct from the human-autonomy-teaming literature, we define a six-dimension behavioral coding scheme covering altruistic, benevolent, interdependent, emotive, communicative, and synchronized conduct, adapted for a language-model judge. We validate it by rewriting the partner’s lines in team-task transcripts as cooperative, neutral, or defective while holding the rest fixed, and having five judges from five model families rate every version. Every judge orders the manipulated behavior as intended and every pair agrees on relative ordering, though absolute calibration differs by up to about a scale point. On registers matched for length and politeness the judges separate cooperative from degraded conduct but resolve subtle defection only weakly; a blinded single-rater human pilot reproduces both the orderings and that limit. The scheme is therefore valid for relative comparisons but not for absolute thresholds applied across judges. We give design implications for LLM-judge teaming evaluation, and release the scheme, stimuli, prompts, and ratings.

items.title: KIARA: AI-Assisted Authoring of Augmented Reality Assembly Instructions from Technical Documentation
items.abstract: Creating augmented reality (AR) work instructions from existing technical documentation remains labor-intensive. We present KIARA (German: KI-basierte AR-Anleitungen; English: AI-based AR instructions), an integrated authoring system that transforms image–text PDF manuals into editable, step-based AR assembly instructions. KIARA combines a locally operated multimodal large language model, a browser-based authoring interface, and an AR application currently supporting Magic Leap 2 and Meta Quest 3. Authors can inspect and revise generated AR instructions before synchronizing them with the system back end and loading them onto an AR device, where virtual content can be further placed and adjusted directly in the physical task environment. The interactive demonstration exposes this workflow from document import to executable AR guidance on a physical assembly demonstrator.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology

items.title: Irradiation-hardened p-GaN HEMTs achieving >500 V single-event burnout hardness at 82.06 MeV cm2/mg
items.abstract: This work presents a single-event radiation-hardened p-GaN gate high electron mobility transistor with a grounded Schottky contact (GSC-HEMT). A Schottky contact connected to the source electrode is fabricated on the barrier layer between the gate and drain terminals. Under Ta ion irradiation with a linear energy transfer of 82.06 MeV cm2/mg, the GSC-HEMT exhibits a significantly enhanced single-event burnout (SEB) voltage of over 500 V, demonstrating excellent SEB tolerance. In the conventional p-GaN HEMT, irradiation-induced holes accumulate beneath the gate region, resulting in a larger local electric field and increased gate leakage current. The proposed GSC-HEMT is capable of rapidly collecting irradiation-induced holes through its grounded Schottky contact. This structure can effectively suppress the massive accumulation of positive charges under the gate and within the buffer layer, thereby improving the radiation tolerance of the device. The designed device demonstrates great application prospects in aerospace electronics.

items.title: Iris: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Framework-Grounded, Human-in-the-Loop HCI Evaluation
items.abstract: Expert interface evaluation is costly and typically applies only one or two analytic frameworks. We present Iris, a system that dispatches ten framework-grounded large-language-model (LLM) evaluator agents in parallel, spanning usability heuristics, accessibility, design theory, cognitive load, behavioural design, and ability-based design, over an evidence bundle enriched with rendered HTML, interactive CSS pseudo-class rules, and keyboard-focus screenshots captured from a live browser session. Findings are returned at criterion level for practitioner review; Iris is positioned as decision support within a human–agent workflow, not as a replacement for expert judgment. A controlled sensitivity study shows composite scores respond monotonically to targeted design changes (11.9 → 80.4 across four page versions), and a temperature analysis identifies deterministic sampling as necessary for reproducible scoring. We describe the system, what current evidence does and does not establish, and an ongoing validation programme comprising an expert-annotated benchmark, tool and monolithic-prompt baselines, and a controlled practitioner study.

items.title: Investigation of single-event burnout mechanism in p-GaN gate HEMTs
items.abstract: In this work, the mechanism of single-event burnout (SEB) in p-GaN gate HEMTs is thoroughly investigated by irradiation experiments and simulations. The samples were irradiated with tantalum (Ta) ions (67 MeV cm2/mg in GaN). There are two distinct failure modes observed in samples occurring in SEB. One is the four-terminal short-circuit mode, and the other is the vertical short-circuit mode between the drain and the substrate. By comparing damaged structures, it can be inferred that both failure modes probably originated from the burnout of the drain. According to the transient currents and temperature distributions by simulations, it is found that the most sensitive region to SEB is the edge of the drain, rather than the edge of the gate or field plate. The SEB mechanism can be explained as follows. A large number of generated holes accumulate at the GaN/AlN interface, while a large number of electrons will accumulate at the Si-Sub/AlN interface, leading to a high electric field in the AlN layer and in turn enhancing the impact ionization. Then the generated electrons will drift to the drain and concentrate around the drain, which produces high current density as well as a high electric field near the drain. Therefore, the lattice temperature there is quickly raised to trigger thermal runaway at the drain.

items.title: Investigating EUV-induced crosslinking using a model PFAS-free chemically amplified resist
items.abstract: BackgroundUnderstanding the EUV exposure mechanisms of PFAS-free chemically amplified resists (CARs) is increasingly important, particularly the role of EUV-induced side reactions that may impact lithographic performance.AimThis work uses a range of characterization techniques to elucidate the interactions between EUV photons and photoresist materials and investigates EUV-induced crosslinking in a model PFAS-free CAR.ApproachFourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, ellipsometry, residual gas analysis, and gel permeation chromatography were used to characterize the photoresist. Preliminary lithographic analysis was evaluated using an EUV scanner and critical-dimension scanning electron microscopy (CD-SEM).ResultsFollowing EUV exposure and post-exposure bake, the molecular weight of the polymer matrix increases with the EUV exposure dose, indicating the occurrence of EUV-induced crosslinking. At higher exposure doses, reversals in the trends of the methyl absorption signal and film thickness are also observed, suggesting the onset of additional resist property modifications. Furthermore, lithographic evaluation reveals increases in roughness with increasing EUV exposure dose.ConclusionsIn addition to the intended deprotection reaction, EUV exposure can induce competing side reactions, including crosslinking. These reactions may modify the resist properties and alter resist–developer interactions, ultimately degrading lithographic performance.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: Investigate of degradation mechanism related to trap state in β -Ga2O3 Schottky barrier diode under high-temperature storage
items.abstract: The high-temperature performance of β-Ga2O3 Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) is crucial for applications in high-power scenarios where the ambient temperature is rising owing to the heat generation of electronic systems. The evolution of the electrical characteristics of β-Ga2O3 SBDs during high-temperature (200 °C) storage is investigated, with an emphasis on the role of the Schottky (β-Ga2O3/Ni) interface. The extracted carrier concentration shows a unique performance evolutionary trend as it first decreased from 8.50 × 1015 to 7.90 × 1015 cm−3 then increased to 8.30 × 1015 cm−3 with the rising high-temperature storage test (HTST) processing time. Meanwhile, the numbers for trap density follow the opposite trend to the carrier concentration, first increasing and then decreasing following rising HTST time. The inner mechanism is summarized as Ni diffusion into the β-Ga2O3 interface at the primary stage, leading to the increase in gallium vacancies. Then, the dominant thermal activation energy repairs interface damage, allowing the release of trapped carriers. Besides, the change of breakdown voltage shows that the field-plate dielectric layer also suffers from degeneration, revealing the high requirement of dielectric layer with thermal endurance.

items.title: Integrating a Multi-Tier Memory Manager into a Educational RAG System
items.abstract: Large language model agents often perform well within one conversation yet do not persist interaction-derived state, procedures, and user context needed for sustained collaboration when the session ends. This paper presents the integration of a memory-first extension to a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) agent, in which memory is treated as an explicit architectural layer rather than an enlarged chat history. The current prototype implements a Memory Core and Memory Manager for persistent conversational, semantic, procedural, and episodic memory. At the same time, the complete memory-aware architecture and its evaluation protocol are presented as ongoing work. Relational tables preserve conversational events, while vector-enabled SQL tables store embedded memory units enriched with timestamps, source, intent, confidence, and lifecycle metadata. Deterministic and agent-triggered operations support read, write, update, and delete operations and context-window segmentation. The proposed interface is designed to expose the memory type and provenance associated with retrieved information. The work reframes agent memory as both an engineering and a human-agent interaction problem: useful persistence requires not only accurate recall, but also transparent, controllable, and correctable remembering.

items.title: Injectra: Retrofitting Extensibility into Web-Based Desktop Applications
items.abstract: Large language models can generate code based on natural language prompts, opening up new possibilities for users to customize software and extend its functionality. This paper proposes and implements Injectra, a general-purpose code injection and feature enhancement system for existing desktop clients, suitable for applications whose user interfaces are built using embedded browser engines (such as Electron) or system WebViews (such as Tauri). Injectra decouples the host integration logic from the upper-layer enhancement code. Combining both runtime integration and pre-launch bootstrap mechanisms, it injects JavaScript, HTML, and CSS into the application's internal Web runtime environment through a unified execution channel, thereby enabling modifications to interface rendering, adjustments to interactive behaviors, and client-side functionality extensions. The system uses a command-line interface (CLI) as a unified entry point, allowing external tools, AI agents, and MCP integration layers to reuse its injection and enhancement capabilities. We tested 38 desktop applications already installed on our macOS machine; code injection was successfully completed for all of them. We demonstrated the system's capability to extend functionality through various enhanced use cases and also successfully validated the Windows version. Based on Injectra, we further developed an LLM-powered enhancement tool driven by selection and annotation: users select interface objects within the original application and describe their modification requirements; the large language model then generates the enhancement code, which is injected, executed, and rendered by Injectra. The system's source code has now been released as open source: https://github.com/sqmw/injectra.

items.title: IndustrialKnowEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Level Industrial Knowledge in LLMs
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for industrial tasks, yet few benchmarks evaluate their mastery of industrial knowledge across different types of cognitive demand. We introduce IndustrialKnowEval (IndKnow), a benchmark for industrial knowledge and engineering question answering. It contains 43,282 samples covering 21 task types across seven industrial sectors, including aerospace, electric power, and metallurgy, organized into four levels of cognitive demand: memory, comprehension, reasoning, and engineering application. Enterprise-based domain specialists and experienced researchers participate in all stages of dataset construction and quality control. We conduct a series of experiments on 18 representative LLMs, with domain experts deeply involved in the evaluation. Building upon IndKnow, we propose the Industrial Cognitive Capability Gap (ICCG) metric to characterize the performance differential between foundational industrial knowledge and higher-order reasoning and application, and we analyze it alongside absolute performance to provide a more complete view of model capabilities. We anticipate that IndustrialKnowEval will support the benchmarking of LLMs in industrial scenarios and promote the development of robust industrial intelligence. Code is available at: https://github.com/J4cksonLee/IndKnow

items.title: Incoherent light-induced periodic surface structures on EUV Mo/Si multilayers
items.abstract: Conventional intense coherent laser radiation can induce periodic surface structures, offering a promising route for advanced nanofabrication. However, whether incoherent short-wavelength radiation can drive such self-organized pattern formation remains an open question. Here, we report incoherent light-induced periodic surface structures (ICLIPSSs) on Mo/Si multilayers irradiated by nanosecond 13.5 nm extreme ultraviolet (EUV) pulse from a laser-produced plasma source. The irradiated surface exhibits radially distributed nanostructures with a constant period of ∼58 nm over a broad fluence range, while the amplitude increases with fluence and the morphology evolves from sinusoidal wrinkles to asymmetric ridge-groove features. We attribute this behavior to transient thin-film wrinkling driven by compaction-induced in-plane compressive stress in a stiff surface layer. The Ru capping layer suppresses ICLIPSS by enhancing near-surface EUV absorption and affecting cross-plane heat transport, thereby altering the transient mechanical state required for wrinkling. These findings deepen our understanding of EUV-induced pattern formation in multilayers and suggest a new route for nanoscale surface structuring using incoherent short-wavelength light.

items.title: Implicit-Reasoning-Enabled Elastic Semantic Communications for AI-Agent Networks
items.abstract: AI-agent networks introduce new communication demands driven by proactive interactions and autonomous task execution. Existing adaptive semantic communication schemes primarily adjust semantic representations and resource configurations within predefined processing scales and capability sets, which may be insufficient for evolving task requirements. To address this gap, we introduce elastic semantic communications (ESC), a task-driven framework that extends semantic adaptation to the runtime execution and participation of task-supporting capabilities. ESC comprises two complementary dimensions: vertical elasticity adjusts the execution intensity of existing capabilities, while horizontal elasticity reconfigures the participating capability set. The framework connects these dimensions through the expected marginal value of additional information and computation. To realize ESC, we propose an implicit-reasoning-enabled device--edge mechanism that supports variable-depth local inference through shared-parameter state updates and edge-side continuation through wireless transfer of intermediate reasoning states. Experiments on Sudoku-Extreme demonstrate that the benefits of additional inference depend on wireless conditions, while task-aware edge invocation can preserve task accuracy with substantially lower state-transfer overhead.

items.title: IGZO optoelectronic synaptic transistor for neuromorphic vision and motion tracking applications
items.abstract: Neuromorphic vision systems that integrate optical sensing, memory, and information processing are promising candidates for overcoming the energy and bandwidth limitations of conventional von Neumann architectures. Here, we report an indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) optoelectronic synaptic transistor for neuromorphic vision and motion tracking applications. The fabricated device exhibits excellent electrical performance, including a high on/off current ratio of ∼1.06 × 108, a low subthreshold swing of 110.58 mV/dec, and a field-effect mobility of 1.52 cm2 V−1 s−1. Under 405 nm optical stimulation, the transistor successfully emulates essential biological synaptic behaviors, including intensity- and time-dependent synaptic plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, short-term to long-term memory transition, and learning-forgetting-relearning characteristics, while operating with a low energy consumption of approximately 6.75 pJ per synaptic event. Photoluminescence and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses reveal that oxygen-vacancy-related defect states induce carrier trapping and persistent photoconductivity, providing the physical mechanism responsible for the observed optoelectronic synaptic behavior. To demonstrate its practical applicability, a hardware–software co-designed neuromorphic vision framework employing a 128 × 64 IGZO synaptic transistor array model experimentally calibrated using measured devices' optoelectronic characteristics was simulated for real-time motion detection and vehicle tracking. The proposed system achieved a pixel localization accuracy of 94.8% through hardware-aware spatiotemporal preprocessing, significantly reducing redundant data transmission and computational overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of IGZO optoelectronic synaptic transistors as an energy-efficient platform for intelligent visual perception, edge artificial intelligence, and next-generation in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

items.title: Human-Side Adaptation in Circle-Drawing Feedback Interaction: Adjusting Expression to an Agent's Response Tendencies
items.abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) enable human–agent interactions where humans express themselves nonverbally and agents respond verbally. Sustaining such interactions requires mutual adaptation, yet human-side adaptation remains underexplored. We investigated whether an agent’s verbal expression of its interpretation of a user’s emotions alters the user’s nonverbal expressions. In the experiments, participants drew circles expressing feelings and received feedback from an LLM-based agent. We compared drawing-contingent feedback, derived from a Random Forest estimator (Experiment 1) or developer-defined rules (Experiment 2), with drawing-independent feedback. Participants receiving drawing-contingent feedback produced drawings with smaller discrepancies between intended feelings and the agent’s estimates than those receiving drawing-independent feedback. These results suggest that users can learn the contingency between their behavior and system responses and adapt their expressions accordingly.

items.title: How Reliable Is Visual Token Selection? Rethinking Pruning in Multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: Visual token pruning improves the efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by removing redundant visual tokens, yet the reliability of existing selection signals has not been systematically examined. We analyze token selection under semantics-preserving perturbations and across representative pruning criteria, revealing two limitations. First, attention-based importance shifts non-uniformly under perturbations, so magnitude alone cannot distinguish stable evidence from unstable saliency (local instability). Second, attention- and diversity-based methods select substantially different subsets despite comparable performance, showing that useful evidence is not confined to a unique subset (global inconsistency). These findings motivate reliable token-set construction. We instantiate this perspective in CoRePruner, a training-free framework combining instruction-aware diversity with reliability-aware attention. Across image benchmarks, multiple MLLM architectures, and token budgets, CoRePruner improves performance, especially under aggressive pruning, and remains competitive on video benchmarks. Our results establish reliability as a central consideration in visual token selection.

items.title: How AI Agent Memory and Personality Reshape Trust Calibration in Human-Agent Collaboration
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly remember prior interactions and present themselves through distinct personalities. Whether these relational features help users calibrate their trust appropriately, or instead impose hidden costs without improving how well they rely on agent guidance, is an open and consequential design question. In a remote virtual reality study (N = 92), we independently varied whether an agent referenced its shared history with the user and whether its personality matched the user’s own style. Agents that made memory references caused users to slow down and deliberate longer at every decision point, yet this caution produced no improvement in compliance quality—a pattern we call the memory paradox. More social did not mean better calibrated. Personality congruence did not make users trust the agent more overall, but it did make their trust judgments more behaviorally coherent. Across all conditions, participants followed incorrect agent guidance at a strikingly high rate, and no relational design feature reduced this automation bias. Taken together, these findings argue that the core challenge in human-agent collaboration is not building trust, but calibrating it: AI agents should be evaluated by how accurately users rely on them, not by how humanlike they feel.

items.title: Hivemind: A Federated Protocol for AI-Mediated Tacit Knowledge Sharing in Organisations
items.abstract: This paper presents Hivemind, a federated protocol that enables AI agents to exchange tacit knowledge on behalf of their users, asynchronously and without requiring any direct human interaction. Individual AI memory systems capture the decisions, reasoning, and contextual knowledge that surface during AI-assisted work. Hivemind creates the shared space in which this captured knowledge can flow between individuals across team and departmental boundaries, addressing a structural gap that neither centralised knowledge repositories nor existing AI tooling closes, even where partial solutions such as expert-finding systems exist. The paper evaluates centralised versus decentralised design approaches, proposes a federated architecture grounded in Nonaka and Takeuchi's (1995) Socialisation, Externalisation, Combination and Internalisation (SECI) model, and demonstrates a proof-of-concept implementation using Design Science Research (DSR) methodology. Measuring the enterprise benefit of federated tacit expertise sharing remains an open task for future work.

items.title: GranularGPT: Natural-Language-Driven End-to-End Discrete Element Method Simulations
items.abstract: Discrete element method (DEM) simulations are widely used to investigate granular and particulate systems, but their application often requires specialized expertise in particle physics, numerical modelling, and simulation post-processing. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to simplify these workflows by enabling users to interact with simulation tools through natural language. This study offers GranularGPT, an LLM-assisted agentic framework for end-to-end DEM simulation workflows, from natural-language problem descriptions to simulation execution and automated post-processing. The framework enables users to generate DEM simulation cases, execute and monitor simulations, and automatically extract and report physical and process-level metrics. Evaluation across 60 normal-condition cases covering 12 DEM scenarios and parameter variations achieve a simulation success rate of 91.7%. In the error-handling evaluation, all 10 repairable errors are detected and 9 are successfully resolved, while all 5 non-repairable cases are correctly identified and reported. The framework automatically extracts a range of DEM-relevant metrics, including particle size distributions, packing and density measures, velocity profiles, discharge rates, mixing indices, contact force characteristics, and thermal quantities. GranularGPT provides a foundation for improving the accessibility and efficiency of DEM simulation workflows while reducing the specialized expertise required for their operation.

items.title: Gradis:A Human–AI Collaborative Framework for Workforce-Aligned Curriculum Generation and Personalized Learning
items.abstract: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and evolving workforce requirements have widened the gap between traditional educational curricula and industry needs. Recent developments in large language models (LLMs) and intelligent tutoring systems have improved curriculum generation and personalized learning experiences. However, most existing solutions remain focused on isolated educational tasks and lack a unified framework that integrates workforce intelligence, organizational knowledge, human expertise, and adaptive learning. This paper proposes Gradis, a human–AI collaborative framework for workforce-aligned curriculum generation and personalized learning. Gradis integrates organizational knowledge, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and human expert validation to support the generation and expert-guided refinement of adaptive curricula in response to changing industry needs. Unlike fully automated educational systems, Gradis positions human experts as key decision-makers throughout the curriculum lifecycle while leveraging AI to improve scalability, efficiency, and personalization.

items.title: Generating a simple silicon detector simulation with an open-weight large language model
items.abstract: Recent LLM developments have seen AI-generated code become commonplace in the software development industry. Without tool access, LLMs cannot execute simulations, and their knowledge of toolkits such as Geant4 is limited. We demonstrate here, a detector simulation workflow with a Qwen3.6-27B model with Q4_K_M GGUF quantisation together with custom resources and tools served via MCP servers to generate a particle detector simulation. In 50 independent runs, 42(29--56)% at 95% CI produced energy-deposit distributions statistically consistent with a reference simulation, measured against a reference simulation. These results provide a proof of concept that MC simulations can be generated using text-based prompts with an LLM, given the necessary resources and tools. More extensive resources, such as example code and additional documentation, are likely to be required for more complex simulation tasks.

items.title: GainCtrl: Predicting Remaining Gains for Efficient LLM Agent Execution
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to power agents that interact with tools and environments to solve complex tasks. Repeated attempts improve the quality of tool-using agents, but continued execution incurs additional costs even when it is unlikely to improve the best result ultimately returned. This raises the question of when to stop an attempt to reduce execution cost while preserving task-level Best-of-N quality. To address this question, we introduce GainCtrl, a gain-based execution controller for LLMs. In GainCtrl, a lightweight CPU predictor uses interaction histories to estimate expected positive gains over retained scores, which are then used to guide stopping decisions with calibrated thresholds to limit the loss in mean Best-of-N task quality. We evaluate the controller through trajectory replay across three environments and three LLM actors. Comparisons of interpolated quality-cost Pareto frontiers show that GainCtrl generally uses fewer tokens than baselines at matched target quality. Fixed policies also achieve quality close to that of full execution while substantially reducing token consumption. The predictor runs at millisecond latency on a single CPU thread, supporting repeated monitoring without access to LLM internals.

items.title: GPRM: Global Perspective Process Reward Model
items.abstract: Process Reward Models (PRMs) are widely used for step-level evaluation of multi-step reasoning in large language models, but existing methods are often limited by weak historical dependency modeling and insufficient global awareness. They typically fail to leverage prior step evaluations for coherent judgment and lack visibility into subsequent reasoning, leading to suboptimal assessment of intermediate steps. To address this issue, we propose the Global Perspective Process Reward Model (GPRM), which jointly models the problem, previous reasoning steps and their evaluations, the current step, and future steps to enable history-aware and globally informed process evaluation. We further introduce a structured evaluation framework along four dimensions---look back, look ahead, self-check, and goal alignment---to assess prior consistency, future plausibility, step validity, and task alignment. Based on this framework, we construct datasets for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (GRPO). Experiments show that, despite using less training data and smaller model sizes, GPRM outperforms strong baseline models by 7.8 and 5.4 points on PRMBench and ProcessBench, respectively. GPRM also generalizes well across tasks, surpassing the GPT-4.1 baseline on Agent Error Bench, improving strong baselines by around 4 points under test-time scaling (TTS), and achieving competitive performance on PPE.

items.title: Fysieke modellering en optimalisatie van ferro-elektrische FETs voor geheugentoepassingen
items.abstract: The aggressive downscaling of nowadays electronics is not limited only to logic devices, but also to memory. In order to keep the pace preordained by Moore's law the industry is currently in pursuit of the next generation devices to enable further scaling. The recent discovery of ferroelectric phases in doped high-k materials such as hafnium or zirconium oxide caused a major change in a memory device landscape and rekindled the interest in ferroelectrics. Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistors (FeFET) are potentially faster and more energy efficient alternative to 3-D NAND, which place them as a viable candidate for storage class memory (SCM) devices. Nevertheless, the behavior and physical laws governing these materials are still far from being understood. Nowadays reliability issues such as fatigue, imprint and retention seem to be a crucial problem and providing a model of these phenomena would be benefitable for both industry and scientific community. The aim of this thesis is to develop a physics-based compact model of FeFET in order to enhance the understanding of the device, test it in representative benchmark circuits to study the viability of FeFETs in next generation memory circuits and investigate the electrical impact of degradation mechanisms.

items.title: Frenkel Pair Stabilizes the Stoichiometric One‐Dimensional Charged Domain Walls in ZrO 2
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Charged domain walls (CDWs) in ferroelectrics are often characterized as 2D topological defects with tunable functional properties, offering significant potential for applications in next‐generation nanoelectronics. However, they accommodate large bound charges and are typically stabilized by extrinsic charge‐compensation mechanisms that break the stoichiometry of the material, potentially leading to enhanced leakage currents, accelerated fatigue, and endurance degradation. Here, stoichiometric 1D CDWs in ZrO 2 are reported, which are stabilized by geometrically and energetically stable Frenkel pairs (FPs) arising from the intrinsic formation of oxygen vacancies and interstitials at tail‐to‐tail and head‐to‐head DWs, respectively. Interestingly, the high dielectric constant (ε∼26) of ZrO 2 effectively screens the Coulomb attraction between vacancies and interstitials, preventing their recombination even at sub‐nanometer separations and thereby stabilizing angstrom‐scale ferroelectric domains. The remarkably small barriers for domain‐wall motion suggest that these 1D‐CDWs are highly mobile. We further demonstrate that FPs facilitate various types of 1D‐CDWs and elucidate the atomic‐scale origin of the recently observed 1D‐CDWs in ZrO 2 . Our work opens a new avenue for stoichiometric CDWs and highlights the broader role of FPs, which can be created and controlled by external electric fields for ferroelectric memory applications.

items.title: Formally verified harness for Shor's order finding algorithm with $O(n^{2+\epsilon})$ gate cost
items.abstract: It is commonly understood that factoring a general $n$-bit biprime via Shor's order finding algorithm requires $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ gates by leveraging schoolbook integer arithmetics for addition and multiplication. Recent developments in quantum arithmetic circuits leveraging recursive Toom-Cook schemes have improved the cost scaling to $O(n^{2+\epsilon})$. Here $\epsilon>0$ depends on algorithm implementation details of the recursive multiplication steps, which allow for a vast number of design choices. The challenge in navigating such design space also presents an opportunity for demonstrating innovative practices in quantum software engineering in the era of open agentic science. We present a formally verified harness that ingests a design specification (namely a"policy"that describes a recursive circuit design scheme) from an external source, which may be an AI agent, and produces a set of formalized proofs covering mathematical correctness of the algorithm implementation, asymptotic scaling of the end-to-end gate cost, as well as the correctness of translating the verified algorithm to a detailed circuit implementation with an intermediate representation. The harness is published as an open challenge where human researchers and AI agents can search for more efficient factoring circuits while retaining machine-checked guarantees of correctness and end-to-end asymptotic complexity.

items.title: First principles investigations of negative differential resistance in edge chlorinated MgO nanoribbons
items.abstract: MgO nanoribbons (MgONRs) are analyzed using the first-principles approach utilizing density functional theory (DFT) for potential nanoelectronic applications. Chemically edge-modified MgONRs are investigated for their electrical characteristics. The structural investigations reveal that the nanoribbons are energetically favorable, and chlorination at the edges relatively reduces the energetic favorability of the structures. Bandstructure calculations reveal that the bare MgONRs and chlorine passivated MgONRs are all metallic structures. Further, the two-probe methodology is deployed for the voltage-current ( \(V-I\) ) characteristics. The chlorine passivation is found to significantly enhance the current magnitude, and an interesting negative differential resistance (NDR) phenomenon is noticed in all the chlorine passivated structures. MgONRs having chlorine passivation at the Mg-edge (Cl-MgO-B) have a relatively higher peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR). The observed results show that the chlorinated MgONRs have potential relevance in future nanoelectronic applications such as switching devices, oscillators, nonlinear electronic circuits, etc.

items.title: Ferroelectric switching of skyrmions through magnetic-interaction reconstruction in monolayer InCrTe3
items.abstract: Single-phase multiferroics provide an attractive platform for nonvolatile electrical control of topological spin textures without relying on engineered heterostructures. Here, using first-principles density-functional theory combined with atomistic spin-dynamics simulations, we demonstrate ferroelectric switching of skyrmion stability in monolayer InCrTe3. Reversal of the ferroelectric polarization reconstructs the magnetic energy landscape: the metallic upward-polarized (P↑) state remains predominantly collinear, whereas the insulating downward-polarized (P↓) state supports skyrmions over a broad range of magnetic fields. Remarkably, the enhanced skyrmion stability in P↓ does not originate from an increased Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI). Instead, polarization reversal substantially reduces the exchange interaction and magnetic anisotropy, allowing the DMI to compete more effectively with collinear ferromagnetic ordering and to stabilize chiral spin textures. Biaxial strain provides a complementary control knob, inducing skyrmions in the otherwise predominantly collinear P↑ state and extending the skyrmion-crystal regime in P↓ to zero magnetic field under tensile strain. These results establish ferroelectric reconstruction of competing magnetic interactions as a mechanism for nonvolatile control of skyrmions in a single-phase two-dimensional multiferroic.

items.title: FM-Recon: Exploring Foundation Model Features for Accelerated Cardiac Cine MRI Reconstruction
items.abstract: Foundation models have demonstrated strong feature extraction capabilities across various medical imaging tasks, yet their potential for MRI reconstruction remains largely unexplored, particularly within unrolled reconstruction networks and under artifact-corrupted inputs. In this work, we explore whether and how features from pretrained foundation models can benefit accelerated cardiac cine MRI reconstruction. To this end, we propose FM-Recon, a framework that refines and integrates extracted features from frozen image encoder of foundation models into an unrolled reconstruction network. Through extensive experiments on the CMRxRecon2023 dataset, we systematically evaluate foundation model features across different reconstruction settings. Our results show that foundation models can extract informative representations from artifact-corrupted inputs and improve reconstruction performance, particularly at moderate acceleration factors. These findings demonstrate the potential of foundation model features for accelerated MRI reconstruction and provide insights into their effective integration into unrolled reconstruction networks.

items.title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings. Although sentiment analysis is a common task in this area, affective meaning in social media discourse is often conveyed through culturally situated and pragmatically indirect cues that are not well captured by label-centric evaluation alone. In this paper, we evaluate the robustness of LLMs for sentiment analysis of Spanish political discourse from social media, with emphasis on culturally situated affective interpretation. We introduce a diagnostic protocol that combines three independent human annotation views into Gold and Ambiguous subsets, and extends the corpus with a Synthetic subset built from sentiment-flipped counterfactuals selected through model-conditioned perplexity and LLM-as-a-judge criteria. Using this framework, we compare proprietary and open-weight models under zero-shot and few-shot prompting, focusing on predictive robustness across human agreement conditions and counterfactual shift. Our results show that annotation ambiguity and counterfactual perturbation reveal failure modes that conventional evaluation on the original corpus tends to obscure. GPT-4.1-mini remains the most stable among the evaluated models, whereas the two smaller open-weight models degrade more markedly under synthetic perturbations, and few-shot prompting provides only limited gains. Overall, the paper contributes a reproducible protocol for robustness-oriented evaluation in political sentiment analysis, an empirical characterization of model behavior under ambiguity and sentiment-flipped counterfactuals, and a publicly available Spanish social media dataset with three-way human sentiment annotations.

items.title: Evaluating Authorization and Trust Boundaries in Agentic Orchestration Frameworks
items.abstract: Agentic AI systems extend large language models with tools, memory, and multi-agent collaboration, introducing security risks at orchestration boundaries. These risks depend on how identities are represented, operations are authorized, and instructions or information propagate between components. We evaluate LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, and OpenClaw through twelve experiments mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications using a common LLM (gpt-4o-mini). The experiments cover prompt injection, unauthorized resource access and command execution, memory poisoning, and inter-agent trust and identity attacks. Adversarial inputs induced unauthorized tool invocation, while tool chaining, stale filesystem validation, encoded instructions, and inter-agent delegation exposed weaknesses in authorization across component boundaries. Memory poisoning showed that untrusted state can influence responses, a risk distinct from conventional access-control violations. In the evaluated protected configurations, explicit authorization, controlled capability assignment, filesystem containment, and execution safeguards prevented specific unauthorized operations. The findings emphasize preserving authorization and information-trust boundaries throughout agentic workflows rather than treating framework capabilities or model-level instructions as sufficient security guarantees.

items.title: Embodiment and Social Presence for Mental Health: A Comparative Study of AI Chatbots and Robots
items.abstract: With the rise in AI agents offering mental health support, questions on the conditions and mediators of these agents’ effectiveness emerge. In human-human settings, therapy effectiveness depends heavily on therapeutic alliance, which in turn is influenced by social presence. This experiment tests whether embodiment influences the therapeutic alliance and social presence that participants feel for a mental health support AI agent, using both direct measures and indicators of disclosure. Participants who completed a positive psychology exercise with a minimal design robot vs a voice agent over a speaker reported higher social presence for the robot (only when one outlier was excluded), but therapeutic alliance did not significantly differ. Analysis of the conversation showed greater authenticity and less positive affect for the robot. The results suggest that while embodiment facilitates agent salience and client disclosure, but do not support a relation with therapeutic alliance.

items.title: Electron Scattering at PtCoO 2 and PdCoO 2 Surfaces for Interconnects <10 nm
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The resistivity increase of copper at the nanoscale due to diffuse electron surface scattering imposes a critical bottleneck for semiconductor technology nodes with <10 nm interconnect half‐pitch. Metallic delafossite oxides PtCoO 2 and PdCoO 2 are promising interconnect candidates with bulk in‐plane resistivities of 2.1 and 2.6 µΩ·cm, respectively, and quasi‐2D cylindrical Fermi surfaces that intrinsically suppress electron‐surface scattering. Electron scattering at PtCoO 2 (0001) and PdCoO 2 (0001) surfaces capped with Si and SiO x layers is quantified using in situ transport measurements on d = 3.1–28.4 nm thick epitaxial films. Si caps increase the delafossite sheet resistance proportional to 1/ d , consistent with an additive surface scattering contribution that is attributed to localized interface states. Subsequent oxidation of the Si cap to SiO x reduces the sheet resistance in all samples, suggesting partial recovery of specularity due to passivation of interface states upon oxidation. A new benchmark quantity, the specific surface scattering resistance R s , is used to compare the promise of delafossite conductors to competing interconnect materials including Cu, Co, and Ru. The results indicate that PtCoO 2 in direct contact with SiO x is particularly promising. Its R s = 1.30 × 10 −16 Ω·m 2 is lower than that of any elemental metal, indicating the potential for liner‐free all‐oxide interconnect architectures.

items.title: Effect of TiN deposition temperature on fully ALD TiN/high- κ HZO/TiN stack properties for DRAM applications
items.abstract: Dielectrics with high dielectric constant (κ) are crucial for dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) technology, and Hf1−xZrxO2 (HZO) is a promising candidate. The pursuit of higher DRAM storage density necessitates the move from planar to pillar-type capacitors, demanding fully atomic layer deposition (ALD) TiN/high-κ HZO/TiN stacks for their superior deep-trench filling conformality. This work investigates the influence of ALD-TiN deposition temperature on the electrical and structural properties of the high-κ stack. As the deposition temperature increases from 300 to 400 °C: (1) the zero-bias dielectric constant increases from below 50 to above 60; (2) the leakage current density is suppressed to meet DRAM requirements, accompanied by improved frequency stability; (3) the TiN resistivity and surface roughness are decreased without altering its stoichiometry, accompanied by a denser [111] preferred orientation; and (4) no additional contamination or monoclinic (m) phase is introduced into the HZO, while the oxygen vacancy concentration is reduced and the interface quality is improved. This work provides an essential reference for fully ALD TiN/HZO/TiN stacks, a core enabler for capacitor scaling in next-generation monolithic 3D DRAM.

items.title: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
items.abstract: After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M. Through benchmarking and failure analysis, we identify a practical challenge that some cases are inherently difficult to predict in real-world settings. To address this, we introduce decision model-based gating to filter out cases where predictions are unlikely to be correct before they are presented to the user. Our trained model outperforms existing decision models and raises pass@5 among shown suggestions by 12--25 points at a gating threshold. Our code is available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation.

items.title: Domain-growth kinetics and scaling behavior in pulse-driven accumulative polarizationswitching in HZO
items.abstract: Abstract Accumulative polarization switching driven by sequential sub-coercive electric-field pulses offers a promising route toward low-power ferroelectric memories and neuromorphic devices. Understanding how domain-growth kinetics depend on pulse conditions and initial domain configurations is important for controlling this process. Here, we employ a phase-field model based on the time-dependent Landau–Ginzburg formalism to investigate pulse-driven accumulative polarization switching in ferroelectric HfZrO2 (HZO). By varying the initial domain configuration, applied-field amplitude, pulseon duration, and pulse-off duration, we analyze the evolution of the switched-domain radius and its local logarithmic growth exponent, αloc = d ln(R−R0)/d ln n, where R0 is the initial domain radius and n is the pulse number. The simulated trajectories exhibit three empirical kinetic regimes: superlinear growth (αloc > 1), approximately linear growth (αloc ≈ 1), and sublinear relative growth (αloc < 1). Their occurrence and evolution depend on the pulse parameters and initial domain geometry. Stronger applied fields and longer pulse-on durations enhance domain expansion and can reduce the number of pulses required to approach saturation, whereas longer pulse-off durations promote relaxation and suppress net polarization accumulation. The local exponent provides a useful descriptor of relative domain growth, but its late-stage decrease does not uniquely establish a relaxation-dominated mechanism and may also reflect finite-size constraints and depletion of the remaining switchable area. The results therefore provide an empirical kinetic-regime map for the simulated conditions rather than evidence of a universal scaling law. This framework offers a quantitative basis for comparing switching trajectories and identifying how pulse protocols influence accumulative domain evolution in HZO.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics

items.title: Designing Agent Facilitation: From Dyadic Interaction to Group Co-Creation in HAI
items.abstract: Designing Agent Facilitation (DAF) is a half-day workshop at HAI 2026 that explores how agentic AI systems can be designed to facilitate—rather than replace or subordinate—human collective intelligence. As large language models and generative AI mature, artificial agents exhibit autonomy, initiative, and apparent intent. However, Human–Agent Interaction research still treats agents as one-to-one, task-oriented interfaces. This workshop argues that a critical next step for HAI is to examine agents that actively mediate, structure, and unblock interaction among groups of humans. The workshop combines short paper presentations with structured co-creation methods, including facilitation-oriented discourse mapping and science‑fiction prototyping, to surface design spaces, evaluation challenges, ethical tensions, and failure modes of agent facilitation. By positioning Agent Facilitation as a distinct HAI sub-area, this workshop aims to shape how autonomy and agency are understood beyond the single-user paradigm.

items.title: Delegating Design Critique to AI While Preserving Human Decision Authority: An AI Design Director for a Small Apparel Brand
items.abstract: AI systems can now analyze visual designs, retrieve organizational knowledge, and generate improvement proposals. In creative work, however, delegating judgment to AI may weaken human agency, obscure decision reasoning, and encourage convergence toward established patterns. We present a work-in-progress “AI Design Director” for a small Japanese apparel brand. The prototype combines a multimodal large language model with retrieval-augmented generation over brand principles, past products, and prior review comments to critique bag design proposals. Rather than assigning scores or issuing verdicts, the AI presents relevant criteria, strengths, concerns, uncertainties, matters requiring human judgment, and revision options with reasons. Designers and managers retain final decision authority and can inspect, question, revise, or reject the AI’s proposals. Human–AI disagreement is treated not merely as error, but as a signal of ambiguous criteria, outdated knowledge, or intentional creative departure. We describe the interaction design, prototype, and planned field evaluation.

items.title: Comparing Human and AI Responses to Emotionally Vulnerable Conversations
items.abstract: People increasingly turn to large language models (LLMs) for emotionally vulnerable conversations because of their availability, responsiveness, and perceived privacy. Yet little is known about how supportive human and AI responses differ linguistically and interactionally. This ongoing study compares responses to standardized sadness and disappointment scenarios. Drawing on Du Bois’ stance theory, it examines evaluation, positioning, alignment, acknowledgment, validation, and advice alongside affective lexical patterns and human evaluations. An exploratory pilot established feasibility and informed the full-study protocol. The study integrates discourse-pragmatic and computational lexical analyses with human evaluation to examine supportive communication in Human-Agent Interaction.

items.title: Communication Characteristics and Needs: Effects of Transferring Decision-making Level from Humans to AI Advisors in Academia
items.abstract: Academic advisors increasingly face heavy workloads driven by rising student demand. Designing AI-driven administrative systems based on users’ needs can help alleviate this burden. Our study examines how the perception of human needs and characteristics of communication are affected when AI systems replace human advisors in academic settings. This study employed a mixed-methods design with semi-structured interviews (N = 31) and pre-post surveys (N = 119) to investigate user needs and validate findings for an academic agent-based support system. Our findings show a selective pattern: shifting to AI agents produced significant declines in competence, relatedness, and impactfulness, while autonomy, engagement, and security showed no detected difference. Human advisors were valued for empathy and contextual judgment in complex decisions, whereas AI agents were valued for availability, efficiency, and emotional consistency. Rather than competing alternatives, these results point toward complementary systems that position agents as first-line support while preserving human connection for high-stakes, emotionally complex interactions.

items.title: CivilBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Information Integration in Civil Engineering
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), is increasingly applied in civil and structural engineering for disaster assessment, structural analysis, and engineering decision support. However, the extent to which current VLMs possess the reasoning capabilities required for reliable engineering judgments remains unclear. In this work, we introduce CivilBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs in civil engineering and disaster-related scenarios. CivilBench covers three major task families: Sequential Reasoning, Image-based Structural Understanding, and Open-world Understanding, encompassing numerical reasoning, structural damage assessment, risk inference, causal analysis, and repair planning. The benchmark is constructed through a systematic pipeline of domain-specific data collection, engineering-oriented captioning, expert annotation, question design, and quality verification. Evaluation of representative state-of-the-art VLMs reveals substantial limitations in domain-specific reasoning, with Sequential Reasoning emerging as a major bottleneck, particularly when models must infer numerical relationships from sparse structured observations. Further experiments show that numerical priors and external knowledge can alleviate these limitations, although their effectiveness depends on the model's ability to reliably interpret and use the available evidence. CivilBench provides a capability-oriented testbed for identifying reasoning limitations and evaluating progress toward reliable AI-assisted engineering decision-making. The benchmark will be publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/traceuryuan/CivilBench.

items.title: CAE-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Reusable CAE Solver Development
items.abstract: We developed CAE-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate AI agents on Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) solver development. A CAE solver is more than a PDE solver; it must be able to generalize across various inputs, such as different boundary conditions, geometries, and material properties. CAE-Bench evaluates the generalizability of AI-developed CAE solvers by providing the same task, such as a heat transfer problem, multiple cases, with each case specifying an input. The AI agent develops a solver for a fixed task using only a few public cases, and the resulting solver is then tested on held-out cases, i.e., cases it has never seen before. We evaluate 12 models across a range of reasoning settings on 80 computational tasks. Our experiments show that even if a solver developed by an AI agent performs well on the public cases, it may even get 0 score on held-out cases. For tasks such as fluid dynamics problems, even the solver developed by GPT-6 Astra performs poorly on held-out cases. A data format and an SDK for task registration are provided, so the researcher can use the benchmark on their own infrastructure. We hope that CAE-Bench will help the community to develop AI agents that can develop reusable CAE solvers that generalize to various inputs.

items.title: Breaking the kilowatt barrier: evidence for scalability beyond ASML’s 1 kW EUV power milestone
items.abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography has become the cornerstone of advanced semiconductor manufacturing, enabling transistor patterning at the nanometer scale and supporting transformative technologies such as artificial intelligence. The throughput of these systems is fundamentally linked to the available EUV photon flux, alongside broader scanner and process considerations.
