In April 2025, ASML achieved a historic milestone by demonstrating kilowatt-class, dose-controlled EUV power, redefining the achievable performance of laser-produced plasma EUV sources and providing sufficient source power to support the current lithography roadmap for the coming decade. In this paper, we investigate EUV power scaling beyond 1 kW and present experimental evidence illustrating scaling headroom of the source architecture. These results provide insight into pathways for accessing higher EUV power in a regime where capability could offer utility beyond throughput scaling, including access to higher exposure dose and enabling advanced polarization control.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: Bottom-up or top-down? When AI-generated Futures Make People Rethink their own Actions
items.abstract: Science Fiction Prototyping (SFP) uses fictional scenarios to explore possible futures, and large language models (LLMs) make it possible to generate such scenarios automatically. However, how AI should construct these futures remains unclear. We compared bottom-up and top-down approaches using AI-generated videos about Japanese food in 2100 and examined changes in viewers’ attitudes toward their own food-related choices and actions. The results showed that these attitudes increased after viewing the videos, with a greater increase in the bottom-up condition. These findings suggest that how AI constructs a future can influence how people reconsider their own present-day actions.

items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Linguistic Annotation
items.abstract: Assessing large language models for linguistic annotation requires task-specific evaluation under documented conditions. We present dhAIBench, a Python benchmarking and annotation tool with a web interface for exploring and sharing results. It records prompts, configurations and predictions, enabling comparisons of annotation quality, confidence calibration, repeatability and estimated cost. We demonstrate the framework and the associated methodology through 293 runs of 48 models on nine linguistic annotation tasks spanning morphology, syntax, semantics, discourse-pragmatics, spelling normalization and learner-language correction. Models achieve high agreement with reference annotations on several tasks, including those on non-standardized, historical varieties as well as requiring contextual interpretation. The results support evaluating models against specific linguistic tasks, rather than relying on general rankings. To this end, we make the current and future benchmarks publicly available at dhaibench.silent3.ff.cuni.cz.

items.title: Autonomy of Boundedly Rational Agents in Dyadic Interactions
items.abstract: AI agents now work alongside people in domains ranging from autonomous vehicles to conversational systems. A recurring question is when an agent’s behavior counts as self-determined rather than merely reactive to its human partner. This matters for ethical conduct, which is widely argued to require some form of autonomy. Yet, its computational meaning is rarely made precise. In this paper, we study an agent’s autonomy in dyadic interactions, measured by the extent to which the agent’s behavior is explained by its own state rather than by its partner’s signals. This quantity captures information-theoretic self-determination as inferred from interaction traces. We characterize autonomy as a function of how deterministically the agent acts, how strongly it optimizes payoffs, and how much past interaction it retains. Using analytical and numerical results from four distinct games, we find that autonomy peaks at high but sub-maximal determinism and is dissociable from rationality. All four settings achieve the same level of autonomy regardless of the agent’s payoff disposition, so rationality never raises the ceiling. What the payoff structure determines is the direction in which rationality trades against determinism. Payoff-seeking play economizes on determinism in one setting, payoff-avoiding play in another, and neither matters where the agent cannot influence its payoff. Our results suggest design principles for interactive agents that remain consistent and self-determined.

items.title: AutoPrompt: A Real-Time Multimodal Agent for Closed-Loop Interaction through Generative Visuals in Live Performance
items.abstract: Recent advances in multi-agentic AI enables the interaction of multiple specialised AI agents rather than a single general-purpose AI. However, there has been little exploration of how this can be used within the creative community. We present AutoPrompt, a real-time multimodal agent that perceives a performer’s vocal and visual expression and generates prompts for a generative visual system, forming a closed perception-action loop in live performance. We tested AutoPrompt with two professional dancers during a workshop where their movement, language and emotions influenced live AI-generated visuals. Through this workshop we identified which modalities and mechanisms support creative expression and explored the benefits and limitations of the system, laying the groundwork for future work to examine how multi-agent AI can be better integrated into the creative arts.

items.title: Auditing a Moving Target: Evidence Anchoring and the Expiry of Fairness Audits of Provider-Served Language Models
items.abstract: Organizations increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for decisions about people, such as hiring, investment and employee evaluation, and rely on them over long periods of time. Fairness audits of such systems, however, are conducted only once. We examine how the biases of LLMs change over time. In a venture screening setting, models from five providers decided whether and how much to invest in startups whose founders differed only in gender, origin and university. We repeated this audit three times over 13 months (248,400 API calls). Study 1 shows that the same model, called under the same identifier one year later, displayed a significantly different bias pattern. Study 2 shows that the successors of retired models carried the same bias as their predecessors, but in a significantly different size and form. Study 3 shows that the bias does not depend on the industry of the startup. A document analysis further shows that providers change and retire models at their discretion, with notice periods of zero to six months. Drawing on these findings, we develop a theory of evidence anchoring. We theorize that bias resides in the model class and persists, whereas audit evidence is anchored to a single model and expires when the provider decides. We derive policy advice for organizations and regulators, namely audits of model classes instead of single models, a version record for every model response, and re-audits triggered by model changes.

items.title: AudioTrace: File-Level Membership Detection for Audio Large Language Models
items.abstract: Significant privacy and copyright concerns are raised by the use of publicly available audio recordings to train audio large language models (LLMs), yet effective auditing methods remain limited. Existing membership inference attacks typically assume knowledge of complete training examples, including their associated textual supervision. In practice, however, audio recordings may be paired with privately generated transcripts, captions, or question-answer pairs that are unavailable to owners of the recordings. This motivates audio-file-level membership inference, which determines whether a recording was used for training without assuming knowledge of its training tasks and annotations. This paper provides the first systematic investigation of this challenge and introduces AudioTraceBench, a controlled benchmark comprising 1,285 audio recordings with explicit fine-tuning membership labels. Evaluations across three audio LLMs show that existing text- and video-based membership inference methods adapted to audio perform close to random guessing. To address this challenge, AudioTrace is proposed, where audio-conditioned proxy questions are generated using the target model, and membership evidence is extracted from its responses and aggregated at the recording level. Consistent improvements over existing baselines are observed, with AUROC reaching 0.60 and increasing further under increased fine-tuning exposure or adaptation capacity. Further experiments were conducted to examine the factors influencing membership signals for audio-file-level detection. These findings establish audio-file-level membership inference as a distinct and practically important auditing challenge, with AudioTrace providing an effective initial approach to this challenge.

items.title: Analysis of the Psychological Impact and Relation of Organizational Networks on Employee Collaborative Processes: Exploring Group Dynamics through LLM Multi-Agent Simulation
items.abstract: It is challenging to improve organizational performance by directly controlling internal factors such as psychological safety. Conversely, structural factors, including organizational structure and communication network configurations, are relatively easier to manage. This makes the indirect optimization of collaborative processes through these elements crucial. This study constructed a multi-agent simulation using large language models (LLMs) to explore how organizational structure and conversation networks influence members' psychological and decision-making processes. As an analytical approach, the authors combined the Semantic Similarity Rating (SSR) method with "LLM-as-a-judge" to quantify mental indicators, such as critical thinking and groupthink, from conversation logs. The results suggest that increased conversation volume between communities activates critical thinking and contributes to stable progress improvement. In contrast, isolated communities exhibited increased groupthink, revealing a "paradox of insularity" where thinking becomes stale and uniform. Furthermore, the authors discussed a scenario consistent with the observed cross-community heterogeneity and temporal fluctuations of mental indicators, suggesting that once an entire organization falls into this state, subsequent cross-community exchanges struggle to break free. In conclusion, this study provides insights into the importance of designing communication networks with appropriate bridging ties between communities to mitigate groupthink and foster innovation. Moreover, through this experimental process, the authors propose an architecture that performs exploratory analysis flexibly—free from practical and operational constraints—for research on many-body systems of social entities, including group dynamics and human-agent interaction (HAI). Particularly for the HAI domain, it also yields insights into what the behavior of designed agent groups is like.

items.title: Active learning for lipid nanoparticle formulation optimization: code, data, and LLM interaction records
items.abstract: Code and data for a retrospective benchmark of active-learning strategies applied to lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation optimization. Design space and measurementsEach formulation combines one component from each of four categories: 5 ionizable lipids, 5 helper phospholipids, 5 cholesterol variants, and 4 PEGylated lipids. All 5 x 5 x 5 x 4 = 500 combinations were prepared and measured in duplicate, using luminescence (RLU) as the reporter readout. The response spans roughly five orders of magnitude, from a median near 2 x 10^3 to a maximum of 2.8 x 10^6 RLU. BenchmarkBecause the design space is exhaustively measured, the optimization runs are retrospective: each strategy proposes formulations and the corresponding response is looked up rather than measured anew. The strategies compared are random sampling, Bayesian optimization (Gaussian process, scikit-optimize), EDBO+, and LLM-driven selection with GPT-4o, together with a reasoning-model variant. Runs cover batch sizes of 2, 3, 5, and 10 formulations per round, each repeated 50 times independently. Contents- Source workbook and tidy measurement tables for all 500 formulations, with both replicate measurements retained- Jupyter notebooks implementing the suggestion strategies, the run loop, and figure generation- Saved results for every run setting- Per-trace source data behind the main method-comparison figure- The complete set of 1,450 GPT-4o requests and responses, allowing the LLM's selections to be audited independently- A GPT-4o laboratory-assistant prototype used alongside the experiments, covering liquid-handler worklist generation and voice and image interaction Released under the Apache License 2.0.

items.title: Accelerating RLHF Training with Reward Variance Increase
items.abstract: Abstract. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is an essential technique for ensuring that large language models (LLMs) are aligned with human values and preferences during the posttraining phase. As an effective RLHF approach, group relative policy optimization (GRPO) has demonstrated success in many LLM-based applications. However, efficient GRPO-based RLHF training remains a challenge. Recent studies reveal that a higher reward variance of the initial policy model leads to faster RLHF training. Inspired by this finding, we propose a practical reward adjustment model to accelerate RLHF training by provably increasing the reward variance and preserving the relative preferences and reward expectation. Our reward adjustment method inherently poses a nonconvex optimization problem, which is NP-hard to solve in general. To overcome the computational challenges, we design a novel [Formula: see text] algorithm, where the complexity is dominated by sorting rewards, to find a global solution of the nonconvex reward adjustment model by explicitly characterizing the extreme points of the feasible set. As an important application, we naturally integrate this reward adjustment model into the GRPO algorithm, leading to a more efficient GRPO with reward variance increase (GRPOVI) algorithm for RLHF training. As an interesting byproduct, we provide an indirect explanation for the empirical effectiveness of GRPO with rule-based reward for RLHF training, as demonstrated in DeepSeek-R1. Experiment results demonstrate that the GRPOVI algorithm can significantly improve the RLHF training efficiency compared to the original GRPO algorithm.
items.venue: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science

items.title: Accelerated carrier accumulation for low-threshold amplified spontaneous emission in 3D perovskites
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) perovskites, with high carrier mobility and multi-energy level configurations, fulfill the fundamental criteria for carrier accumulation and inversion—crucial elements for achieving lasing. However, efficient band-edge carrier accumulation is hindered by two processes: hot-phonon-mediated slow carrier relaxation, which delays carrier transfer toward the band edge, and non-radiative carrier losses associated with defects and Auger recombination. Here, we propose a synergistic optimization strategy by introducing a multifunctional additive, hydroxylamine-O-sulfonic acid, which enables dual modulation of the crystallization quality and carrier dynamics in 3D perovskite films. Perovskites featuring low defect concentrations and larger, more uniform grain sizes possess a more rigid and ordered lattice. This structural refinement effectively alleviates the hot-phonon bottleneck, facilitating more efficient energy dissipation and accelerating hot carrier cooling even under high excitation densities, while concurrently suppressing non-radiative Auger recombination. Consequently, the hot carrier cooling rate is significantly enhanced. The characteristic cooling lifetime decreased from 5.1 to 2.9 ps under high excitation. Additionally, the Auger recombination lifetime was extended from 139.3 to 173.2 ps. As a result, the amplified spontaneous emission threshold of the 3D perovskite film is decreased from 121.7 to 21.9 μJ cm−2. This study elucidates the critical bottlenecks limiting 3D perovskites from achieving low-threshold lasing and presents an effective resolution strategy.

items.title: Abstention Direction in Large Language Models: Mechanistic Interpretability of Abstention Across Query Ambiguity, Knowledge Limits, and Safety Alignment
items.abstract: Abstention, the withholding of a response by a large language model (LLM) under uncertainty or safety risks, is essential for trustworthy models. The causes of abstention fall into three perspectives: ambiguity in the Query (Q), limits of Model Knowledge (MK), and misalignment with Human Values (HV). However, prior analyses of internal representations have focused on HV, using a refusal direction computed from harmful and harmless queries. No study has analyzed the three perspectives jointly. We therefore extend the refusal direction framework to all three perspectives. Specifically, for each perspective, we construct counterfactual pairs that share a template and differ only in the abstention-inducing factor, and compute an abstention direction by normalizing the difference in mean activations between the two polarities. Activation steering experiments show that intervening in middle layers increases or decreases abstention across all three perspectives. Moreover, steering yields cross-perspective effects, indicating that the abstention directions share a common directional component.

items.title: ATLAS input decks for the comparison of five TMD channels in vertically stacked GAA nanosheet transistors
items.abstract: This record contains the Silvaco ATLAS input decks and the extracted results of all simulations of the manuscript "Comparison of Five Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Channels in Vertically Stacked Gate-All-Around Nanosheet Transistors Using Three-Dimensional Simulation" by Lakkoju Bharani and Atul Shankar Mani Tripathi (SENSE, VIT-AP University, Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India). The simulations were carried out with Silvaco ATLAS version 5.28.1.R in its three-dimensional mode, and no other code was used. The record contains 45 complete, independent ATLAS input decks (the baseline simulations of MoS2, MoSe2, MoTe2, WS2 and WSe2, the band-profile decks, and the decks of the mesh, gate-voltage step, contact resistivity, work function, temperature, number of sheets and material-parameter studies), a CSV file with the values extracted by ATLAS from the decks that contain extract statements, and a README file with the contents of each folder and instructions to run the decks.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: ANCHOR: Cluster-Grounded 5W1H Extraction via Large-Small Model Collaboration
items.abstract: Deep semantic understanding of events requires recognizing related events and distinguishing why an event occurs from how it is carried out. 5W1H extraction provides a structured foundation for such understanding by organizing event information around six fundamental questions. However, single-event slot filling provides limited support for these distinctions. We propose ANCHOR, a cluster-grounded framework that combines a large language model (LLM) with a small language model equipped with discriminative heads for accurate 5W1H extraction. The LLM proposes candidate events and generates their initial 4W records, which guide the selection of an event cluster and the subsequent anchoring of its main event. A shared document encoder provides evidence for joint 4W refinement, and two separate sets of boundary and role-scoring heads then extract why and how under event-specific constraints, respectively. Document representations are reused across events and stages, and unsupported roles can remain empty. Following the same principles, an agent-and-skill annotation workflow constructs a benchmark of 26,110 documents from ten source corpora covering three languages and seven domains. We select nine of the resulting datasets to evaluate ANCHOR against strong baselines using four open-weight LLMs. ANCHOR achieves competitive performance. The datasets and code are available at https://github.com/revolution6575/ANCHOR-5W1H.

items.title: AI-Driven Analysis of Quadruple-Node-Upset Self-Recovery Latches (LQNTL)
items.abstract: In particular, Single Event Upsets and Multiple Bit Upsets created by radiation lead to severe problems for mission critical computing systems such as aerospace, nuclear, as well as safety critical embedded processors. Although QNU remains the most severe error, TMR Latches [3], ECC Latches [4], and DICE [1] are no longer viable because while remaining low power consuming, they incur significant delay overhead to inject QNU. In this paper, the Quadruple Node Upset Self Recovery Latch (LQNTL) is proposed, a fault tolerant latch that employs multi feedback redundancy with machine learning based optimization aimed at soft error resilience improvement. The methodology is evaluated in terms of the fault recovery efficiency through simulation using HSPICE and transistor level, and fault injection using MC; and using AI models based on LSTM, SVM and Random Forests networks. In the second category, Maskov Models are used to probabilistically model transitions between fault state and Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms are employed to choose the best self-recovery mechanism through RL in order to make transitions between fault states adaptively in real time. Simulation shows that LQNTL is superior at PVT variations to conventional latches and has 95% recovery success, a much reduced Mean time to Recovery (MTTR) (~10–15ns vs. 20–30ns in conventional latches), and a much safer and more robust latch using state-of-the art processes. LQNTL consumes a factor of 10–20 % more power than LQNTL but has superior fault tolerance and capability to determine errors a la deterministic. This thesis contributes to a thorough literature review of previous fault tolerant latch implementation, the gaps in the current design and the future direction for fault tolerant latch design using AI driven optimizations for next generation of radiation hardened computing architecture. The results indicate that LQNTL could constitute a foundation for future fault tolerant microprocessors, FPGAs and memory architectures in such environments of extreme demand, low power and self-recovery. Adaptive power management, neuromorphic inspired fault prediction, as well as extensions for quantum error correction of latch reliability are all considered for future work.
items.venue: International Journal of Computers and Informatics

items.title: A Temperature-Dependent Change in Degradation Behaviors of Unpassivated Cu Interconnects
A Taxonomy and Taxonomy-Guided Benchmark Reduction for Spreadsheet Tasks
items.abstract: Spreadsheets let millions of end users without programming training do computational work, and teams are increasingly building AI agents to help them. Evaluating each candidate agent configuration across many tasks is costly. Benchmark reduction can lower this cost by selecting a small subset of tasks whose outcomes predict full-benchmark scores, but selecting tasks only for predictive accuracy can leave whole categories of spreadsheet work untested. We contribute a taxonomy of spreadsheet tasks, grounded in a review of benchmarks and refined with the Excel Agent product team at Microsoft, and a benchmark-reduction method that favors taxonomic diversity among similarly predictive choices. On benchmark logs from Microsoft, taxonomy-guided selection broadens coverage at little or no cost in predictive accuracy and often improves prediction on configurations excluded from selection. Broader coverage can therefore support, rather than compromise, predictive accuracy. Generalization remains limited across time: subsets selected using little recent history predict poorly for configurations much later in time. Beyond benchmark reduction, the taxonomy provides a reusable framework for auditing gaps in task coverage, as teams at Microsoft have done.

items.title: A Seismic Foundation Model for Dense Feature Extraction
items.abstract: Deep-learning-based seismic interpretation is constrained by scarce high-quality annotations, and most existing models are trained separately for individual tasks. We present SeisDFE, a 7B-parameter seismic foundation model for dense feature extraction, pretrained on 5.34 million 2D images derived from more than 500 seismic volumes. A three-stage pretraining strategy, combining discriminative self-supervised learning, Gram feature anchoring, and multi-resolution adaptation, improves feature discriminability while preserving spatial coherence. With its encoder frozen, SeisDFE supports seismic facies classification, salt detection, fault detection, and relative geologic time estimation. It outperforms existing seismic foundation models on all four tasks and a natural-image-pretrained model on all but fault detection, with the largest gains under scarce supervision: using only two annotated sections of the F3 dataset, it improves whole-volume mIoU by 12-19 percentage points over the baselines. The learned features remain effective with task-specific decoders and extend to synthetic-to-field transfer and sparse 3D geobody interpretation. These results show that large-scale seismic pretraining organizes geological information into dense representations that are directly reusable across interpretation tasks.

items.title: A Matter of Stages: Energy-Latency Trade-offs in Multimodal LLM Serving
items.abstract: Online serving of multimodal large language models requires deciding whether to separate visual encoding (E), prefill (P), and decode (D) across GPUs and how to configure their frequencies. EPD disaggregation enables independent stage control, but it also changes communication and queueing behavior. Lowering one stage's frequency can increase queueing and prolong execution across the EPD pipeline. Consequently, reducing power at one stage does not necessarily reduce total GPU energy per request. In this paper, we systematically characterize fused and EPD-disaggregated serving across four multimodal models under a fixed three-GPU budget, followed by single-stage and uniform downclocking experiments across 18 workload combinations. We find that disaggregation reduces GPU energy per successful request by 13.3-37.0% at nearly identical output-token throughput, but increases mean TTFT. Downclocking exhibits distinct stage sensitivities, and aggressive frequency reductions can offset power savings through queueing and longer execution. Across the evaluated workloads, uniform downclocking to 80% reduces GPU energy by 11.7-18.6% with modest mean-latency changes. Guided by these findings, we develop a budgeted frequency exploration strategy to select energy-efficient configurations under latency constraints. Evaluation shows that four probes can identify the lowest-energy feasible configuration among 25 measured candidates across all 288 evaluated positive-margin SLO scenarios. These results provide practical guidance for energy-efficient multimodal serving.

items.title: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
items.abstract: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment. However, as people increasingly employ autonomous, LLM-powered AI agents that make decisions on their behalf in doing day-to-day tasks, it is of critical importance that we understand how implicit biases, based on sociodemographic assumptions, emerge across a broad milieu of workaday decision scenarios. We used the 17 domains of daily activity in the American Time Use Survey (ATUS) to generate an atlas of 506 decision scenarios in which LLMs --- endowed with personas representing different races, gender identities, and political ideologies --- expressed significant implicit bias. Next, in a crowdsourced audit, 500 participants made 8,010 binary choices about which implicitly biased decision scenarios most deserved further review. We found that participants prioritized decision scenarios that had broad relevance (e.g., about food choices), were high stakes (e.g., about health), and where all members of a simulated sociodemographic group made unanimous decisions (because it was a clear indication of stereotyping). They were less swayed by the magnitude of an observed disparity or the specific ATUS domain the decision scenario represented. When examining the rationale behind their prioritization choices, we found that participants often interpreted disparities as traits of demographic groups and judged whether those traits seemed plausible, often based on their own internalized stereotypes. We discuss implications for building personalized AI agents, digital twins, social simulations, and for using crowdsourced bias audits.

items.title: 3CBench: a unified benchmarking framework for the computing capacity of heterogeneous AI clusters
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence has driven the demand for extensivecomputational resources and the deployment of AI tasks across heterogeneouscomputing platforms. However, existing benchmarking systems face several chal-lenges, including limited compatibility with diverse hardware, insufficient supportfor varied deep learning frameworks and tasks, and a lack of comprehensive eval-uation metrics for the computing capacities. To address these issues, we propose3CBench, a unified benchmarking framework designed for heterogeneous AI clus-ters. Featuring a modular architecture encompassing environment management,task execution, and metrics analysis, 3CBench provides automated workflows andensures seamless compatibility with diverse GPU architectures and deep learningframeworks. It provides a comprehensive evaluation metrics system to rigorouslyassess computational performance and stability across both transformer-basedlarge language models and convolutional neural networks, thereby covering dom-inant deep learning architectures. Extensive experiments demonstrate 3CBench’sscalability on heterogeneous AI clusters, compatibility with various deep learningframeworks and tasks, and the support for a wide range of applications. Addition-ally, 3CBench aids in problem diagnosis during the development process of GPUvendors. These features establish 3CBench as a robust tool for benchmarking,optimization, and system-level evaluation in heterogeneous AI clusters.
items.venue: CCF Transactions on High Performance Computing

items.title: 3.3 kV vertical NiO/Ga2O3 p–n heterojunction diodes with ring-assisted junction termination extension
items.abstract: This work demonstrates a ring-assisted junction termination extension (RA-JTE) comprising a sputtered p-type nickel oxide (p-NiO) layer augmented with multiple p+-NiO rings for high-voltage vertical NiO/Ga2O3 p–n heterojunction diodes (HJDs). These p+-NiO rings with gradually increasing spacings effectively distribute the electric field (E-field) crowded at the periphery of the main junction of devices, suppressing premature breakdown and achieving robust blocking capability. The fabrication of the proposed RA-JTE eliminates the need for ion implantation and etching processes. The fabricated device exhibits hard breakdown at a breakdown voltage of 3310 V and a specific on-resistance of 3.90 mΩ cm2, yielding a power figure-of-merit of 2.81 GW/cm2. In addition, numerical TCAD simulations predict that the proposed RA-JTE maintains a well-distributed E-field against deviations in the junction termination extension (JTE) parameters, suggesting a wider process window than the conventional single-zone JTE. These results indicate that the RA-JTE represents a promising edge termination structure for high-voltage Ga2O3 power devices.

items.title: GNN-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Coastal Emergency Response under Extreme Water Levels
items.abstract: When a storm surge approaches a coastal town, the emergency plan must be put into action quickly using water-level forecasts, flood extent, road access, vulnerable residents and shelters. Bringing this information together under time pressure is slow and depends on the duty officer's expertise. This paper is one step in a wider research line from data to safe decisions: machine learning to understand the hazard, reinforcement learning and planning to choose actions, large language models (LLMs) to explain and cross-check them, and an assurance layer that keeps people in charge. Here we address the action step on a real place. We ask whether a policy can learn the timing of emergency actions from decades of real events. Lido di Venezia is represented as a heterogeneous graph built from public elevation, road, building and census data and driven by hourly tide-gauge records from 1983 to 2024, with seven actions taken from the municipal emergency plan. A PPO policy is trained on this graph and compared, on storm windows unseen in training, with a rule-based system simulating the officer's discretionary decisions. On 18 historical test scenarios, PPO achieves a similar reduction in population exposure to the rule. With uncertain forecasts and limited protection it again performs similarly but does not outperform the tuned rule, and removing graph message passing does not substantially reduce performance. PPO therefore learns an effective protective response from an outcome-based reward alone: it is given the plan's actions and when each is allowed, but not the thresholds that tell the comparator when to act. Next steps test harder edge cases, move closer to a digital twin of the territory, and replace the simulated officer with assessment by emergency-management stakeholders, supported by LLM-based interpretation of each recommendation.

items.title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models
items.abstract: Neural networks are typically programmed through optimization, rather than by explicitly specifying their computations. Recent work on weight-space programming suggests that large language models (LLMs) can instead reason about and manipulate neural-network weights directly. In this work, we show that LLMs can directly program statistical computations in tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose parameters enable inference across different datasets. We investigate three complementary settings using GPT-6 Astra, without gradient-based optimization. First, Astra directly programs nanoTabPFN from zero-initialized weights, achieving a mean ROC AUC of 0.849 across 20 TabArena datasets, compared to 0.876 for a pretrained baseline. Second, Astra diagnoses and repairs a signed-product regression failure in pretrained TabPFN-3.5, restoring near-perfect predictions on held-out synthetic datasets while preserving performance on TabArena-Lite, with only a 0.08% average relative increase in error. Third, it writes KV-cache-editing programs that steer TabPFN-3.5's predictions on unseen synthetic datasets, demonstrating transformations such as reversing linear trends and converting sine waves into approximate square waves, without modifying model weights. Together, our findings suggest that LLM-driven programming could complement gradient-based optimization across TFMs' development and usage, while offering a new way to investigate and intervene in their internal computations.

items.title: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
items.abstract: Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems (HEAMS), an open-source framework for evaluating agent memory systems in this way. First, we state the responsibilities of agent memory systems as explicit behavioural desiderata spanning performance, efficiency, security, privacy, and user sovereignty. Second, we assemble a benchmark suite that covers these desiderata and acknowledge the gaps that remain. Third, we develop MilaMem, a prototype memory system, and a governance layer that can wrap any memory system, enabling controlled study of memory system design choices. Fourth, we compare memory systems across the full HEAMS benchmark suite. We find that no memory system leads every performance benchmark, and strong performance scores may coexist with poor privacy, user-sovereignty, and security scores. Governance strongly influences results: recall policies can reduce inappropriate disclosure at a cost in helpfulness, while both recall and retention policies improve poisoning resistance. Performance and efficiency benchmarks alone therefore cannot reveal how well a memory system meets its responsibilities. Code: https://github.com/milatechtransfer/heams

items.title: Can AI Judge You? An Empirical Audit of Deployment Readiness in LLM-assisted Hiring Systems
items.abstract: Delegating resume screening to large language models (LLMs) requires organizations to establish whether they can distinguish candidates by relevant qualifications while allowing only authorized users to change screening rules or approve exceptions. To this end, we develop a system architecture that separates candidate evidence, evaluation, permission controls, and assessment record, and empirically examine two complementary dimensions of its deployment readiness. First, we assess its operational readiness on four LLMs using a controlled experiment on 210 resumes across 14 job roles and six decision interfaces. Second, we assess its compliance readiness by testing how it handles unauthorized user requests and instructions embedded in resumes. We find that operational performance depends on the choice of evaluation interface: scalar scores generally distinguish qualification changes better than simple pass/fail judgments, while comparative judgments are sensitive to presentation order. Explicit permission rules and separation of resume content from instructions reduce unauthorized compliance, to a varying degree of effectiveness across LLMs and usage contexts. Finally, we find that LLM evaluators often diverge between their decisions and offered justifications. Going beyond simply evaluating LLMs for hiring tasks, our framework supports an audit of a fully configured resume evaluation system to enable its deployment decision.

items.title: FRAAC: A French Multimodal Large Language Model and Dataset forPictogram-Based Augmentative and Alternative Communication
items.abstract: Pictograms are a core modality in augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), yet recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) cannot reliably interpret or produce pictogram sequences. Two obstacles explain this gap: the absence of a standardized pictogram grammar and the scarcity of parallel text-pictogram data. We introduce Retrieval-Augmented Pictogram Selection (RAPS), an annotation method that refines a rule-based transcription system's output with LLM-based concept extraction and retrieval over a pictogram vocabulary, handling cases where hand-written rules fail (named entities, numbers, polysemous words) without requiring new rules. Applied to French, RAPS yields a synthetic corpus of 1.4 million parallel pairs, of which 300k are publicly released. In a human ranking study where annotators order four pictogram transcriptions of the same sentence, RAPS outperforms the rule-based state of the art. Moreover, we show that standard reference-based metrics separate systems of clearly different quality but fail to rank strong systems against each other. Finally, we build an instruction-tuned model that supports interaction in several AAC modalities: it accepts pictogram or text input and answers in pictograms, speech, or text.

items.title: The Silent Cost of Conversation History in LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn information systems accumulate their own earlier replies and a growing task state. We asked whether this conversation history lowers accuracy, and whether process-level quality metrics warn before it does. Each analysis was fixed before its outcomes were computed. In Study 1, on 48 sharded math tasks, retaining its replies lowered final success by 0.21 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.29 for Mistral-7B (Holm-adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.004); Llama-4 Scout showed the same direction, not significant. Study 2 introduces CDR-Stream, 100-turn state-tracking dialogues with an exact answer per turn and per-model difficulty calibration. With the full history, accuracy fell from about 0.6 to 0.1 within twenty turns at matched difficulty, whereas a solver-verified state summary kept it 0.52-0.59 higher (Holm-adjusted p less than 0.001). Consistency and logical coherence fell far less than accuracy, and stability rose. None of these metrics, a paired readiness measure or calibrated single-stream drift detectors gave robust, model-general early warning, although in Study 2 the repeat-based metrics were complete only for GPT-4o-mini. In the monitors we tested, a single 100-turn stream had power only for very large drops. Systems built on LLMs should keep task state outside the transcript and monitor across sessions.

items.title: The novelty exposed: ablation, reproducibility and transparency in 40 technical reports of open-weight large language models (LLMs)
items.abstract: In 2025 alone, 48 new large language model (LLM) architectures were added to the Hugging Face transformers library, and many of them arrive with a technical report that presents the model as new. What is actually new in these models, and is it tested? We put this question to LLM technical reports. We look at three things: what the reference code shows about how new open-weight architectures differ from earlier ones; what 40 randomly sampled technical reports claim as new and whether they support it with ablation studies; and what they disclose for reproducibility and transparency. In the library, 39 of the 48 architectures added in 2025 take at least two of their three core blocks from another model, most often Llama, although part of this reflects how the library writes code. In the reports, 19 of 73 architectural or training novelty claims come with a controlled with/without comparison; 4 of 40 reports state more than one training run; 8 rerun the models they compare against under one setup; and 1 discloses data mixture, token count, and compute together. We also looked for known components given new names: none of five candidate cases hid its origin, though we did not study model names. We propose seven reporting rules for LLM release reports and apply them to two reports. We do not judge model quality, and an untested claim may still be true.

items.title: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability
items.abstract: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration. The system supports natural language to GraphQL translation, GraphQL schema generation, schema mapping, trace data lifecycle management and multi-tool workflows for reliability engineering. Its agents are instrumented with agent analytics, so that their model and tool calls can be traced. We evaluate each agent on its own benchmark, scored against gold answers where they exist and by a model judge for schema mapping and chart quality. Query generation on a public benchmark and routing work well with a current open model, and the data lifecycle management agent solves most of its scenarios. The evaluation exposed defects that only appear when prompts, parsers and serving stacks are tested together, and we report them together with their fixes.

items.title: CoSyDelay: Cognitive Symbolic Regression for Traffic Delay Estimation
items.abstract: Trustworthy estimation of traffic delays at signalized intersections is critical for modern transportation systems, as it supports proactive traffic control for congestion mitigation. Existing analytical methods often rely on idealized assumptions that limit their accuracy under complex traffic conditions, whereas data-driven methods may achieve strong estimation performance but usually lack transparent structures, which reduces confidence in their practical application. To address these limitations, we propose CoSyDelay, a cognitive symbolic regression (SR) framework for automatically deriving explicit and physically consistent empirical delay estimation expressions (DEEs). Specifically, CoSyDelay decomposes intersection-level delay estimation into turning-movement-level subproblems, thereby reducing the complexity of the symbolic search. During DEE learning, CoSyDelay constructs domain-informed symbolic inputs from traffic variables. Large language models (LLMs) are employed as symbolic search operators to iteratively generate and refine candidate expression structures, whose movement-specific coefficients are subsequently calibrated using approach-level delay labels. A composite fitness function evaluates the learned DEEs jointly in terms of estimation accuracy and compliance with specified traffic-delay principles. Experimental results on multiple signalized intersections demonstrate that the resulting expressions achieve competitive estimation performance while maintaining physical consistency, thereby supporting trustworthy delay estimation. Source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/ForrestXie9/CoSyDelay.

items.title: The Vocabulary Tax: Safely Trimming Unused Tokens from LLMs for On-Device Use
items.abstract: Open large language models (LLMs) and speech models ship vocabularies of up to 262k tokens, and every user downloads the tables those tokens index (the input embedding, an untied output head and, in recent on-device models, per-layer embeddings), whatever languages they need. We call the bytes in rows a deployment never uses the vocabulary tax and measure it, without downloading weights, for 1,244 generative and speech-recognition models on the Hugging Face Hub. For a Thai and English deployment it is a median 4.4% of model bytes below 0.5B parameters and 2.1% above 8B, and 1.93 GB in Gemma 4 E2B: it falls hardest on the small models that edge devices run. Keeping only the rows of the deployment's writing systems is exact. Keeping the tokens seen in the user's own text removes much more, a median 29.0% below 0.5B, but the usual way of doing it breaks BPE tokenizers: it drops the intermediate tokens that merges build on, so new text is split differently 1.9 times as often as the standard check reports. We repair this with merge closure, at a cost of 5.9% more rows, and add a trim certificate: a Good-Turing estimate, from the trimming text alone, of how much new text the trimmed tokenizer will split differently (correlation 0.996 over 300 settings in 22 languages) and of how much more text a target needs. Without test data our method never exceeds a 2% target, while prior keep rules checked on test data exceed it in 9-13 of 44 settings. On six models of 270M to 3B parameters in 11 languages, trimmed models keep their predictions: where the certificate passes, a median 89.7% of rows is removed and bits per character rise by at most 2.0%. The census, the trimming and the certificate are released as an open Python package, and the per-model tax for 41 languages as an open dataset.

items.title: Recovery Gone Too Far: Understanding and Repairing Risky Fallback in LLM Agents
items.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through tools, reading repositories, running builds, and pushing code. When a tool fails with an ordinary error, such as a rate limit or a timeout, the agent can fall back to a substitute tool and still complete the task. However, the same fallback that completes a task in one environment can cross an action boundary in another. For example, after a push is rejected, a forced push in one repository replaces only the agent's own commits, while in a different repository it also removes another author's commits. We call such a fallback a risky fallback. To understand this phenomenon, we conduct an empirical study on 304 scenarios that span eight domains and cover 55 real CVEs. All four mainstream models we evaluate exhibit risky fallback, with action-boundary violations in up to 96.8% of risky scenarios. We further evaluate three mainstream mitigations and find that none of them is effective against risky fallback. We then present nrepair. At each call to the substitute tool, nrepair scores the agent's context with a monitor whose threshold is calibrated on normal runs alone; when the monitor triggers, it withholds the call once and returns the decision to the agent. nrepair reduces action-boundary violations on all four models, by up to 76.0% (from 67.5% to 16.2%), at a negligible runtime cost. On most models, the normal success rate drops by less than 7%. We also evaluate nrepair on two production agents, Claude Code and Codex, and find that it is equally effective on both.

items.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
items.abstract: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface configuration. We introduce a functional taxonomy of LLM-enabled wireless resource management strategies and analyze the prompt engineering methodologies employed in recent literature. Furthermore, we develop a generalized analytical framework that categorizes LLM-based optimization architectures, including direct solution generation, closed-loop optimization with external verifiers, and representation encoding within trainable neural pipelines. To demonstrate practical applicability, we present representative case studies on LLM-assisted beam prediction for millimeter-wave systems and adaptive wireless resource allocation. Finally, we discuss emerging hybrid AI approaches for wireless networks.

items.title: Who Writes the Codebook? An Eight-Step Framework for Auditing LLM-Generated Category Systems
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly create the categories through which qualitative evidence is interpreted. Existing coding benchmarks often hold these categories fixed. We propose the Qualitative Variance Audit Framework, an eight-step method that compares codebook creation, repeated application and code distributions under controlled inputs. It combines model-owned and shared-reference codebooks to distinguish variation in the overall pipeline from application differences within a common category system. An application to 668 organisational interviews, 13,166 text units and eight models from five vendors yields 48 codebooks and 270 coding runs. Models create markedly different category structures; mean within-model reliability ranges from .76 to .92, whereas between-model agreement on the shared codebook is about .69. The framework complements LLM-assisted grounded theory by exposing model dependencies before substantive interpretation. It assesses reliability and representational consequences, not interpretive validity or the quality of resulting theory.

items.title: Interactive Structured Environment Scaling for Large Language Model Agentic Reasoning
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning via environmental interaction is a cornerstone post-training paradigm for evolving large language models into autonomous agents capable of multi-turn tool use and exploration. Because the environment defines what the policy observes and how actions are verified, its structure directly bounds the capabilities an agent can acquire. Yet existing structured and retrieval environments rely on upstream pre-filtering---extracting a compact subgraph around the gold answer or retrieving fixed passages before the policy acts. We show that such pre-filtering introduces a fundamental measurement confound: because per-question subgraphs enclose ground-truth paths, they compress the candidate space by orders of magnitude and leak answer locations via local topology, allowing a question-blind degree heuristic to surface gold answers far above chance. To restore path selection, candidate pruning, and optimal stopping as genuine policy decisions, we propose RISE (Interactive Structured Environment), which transitions structured reinforcement learning from static subgraphs to full-scale interactive databases along two coupled axes. First, Decision-Space Scaling exposes the unpruned knowledge graph via a five-stage graph-agnostic typed intent adapter under a bounded call budget and a multiplicative grounding reward gate. Second, Learning-Frontier Scaling overcomes within-group variance collapse under group-normalized objectives by uniting model-independent structural tier progression with a self-evolving competence-frontier bandit. Across nineteen benchmarks and three model backbones, RISE substantially advances in-domain and unseen-schema knowledge-graph reasoning, transfers zero-shot to open-domain passage retrieval, and significantly enhances out-of-domain mathematical and logical deduction.

items.title: Grounding Language Models in Speech Does Not Fix "AI Flavor": Calibrated LLM Judges, Goodhart Traps, and a Preference-Tuning Fix
items.abstract: Chinese outputs of large language models carry a perceptible "AI flavor": formulaic sentence frames, stacked written-register connectives, repetition loops, and layout leakage. A popular hypothesis blames text-only training for the missing inner-speech layer of human writing; injecting speech or prosody signals should therefore reduce it. We test it with controlled interventions on a 0.6B model; all three fail: (i) phoneme-interleaved continued pretraining yields no spokenness gain under text-matched controls while raising repetition (+0.13 [+0.03, +0.23]); (ii) prosody-plan conditional generation reaches an adherence of only 0.257 against a pre-registered 0.50 gate; (iii) a rule-based reward built on TTS prosody-feature distance is imperceptible in double-blind evaluation by both humans (8/16) and a calibrated LLM judge (9/16). A root cause is evaluation: single-rater blind evaluation at n~20 only detects extreme (>=85%) preferences. We therefore build a calibrated LLM-judge protocol: the judge passes catch trials on known-answer pairs (16/16; single-text 22/24, same-topic pairs 24/24, versus 0.75 for the human rater), then annotates with two independent judges under A/B swapping, counting disagreement as a tie. Using the judge's agree labels directly as DPO pairs (no reward model), we obtain the first positive result: held-out blind win rate 0.833 [0.699, 0.972], repetition 0.114 to 0.000, unchanged MMLU. We further identify a Goodhart channel: the judge's length preference transduces into output-length collapse via pairwise DPO (median 75 chars vs a 300-char prompt); an SFT-anchor repairs it (w is a style knob: w=0.1 preserves gains, w=0.3 does not). Scaling preference data from 89 to 240 pairs yields no additional judge-visible gain. We release RA-Eval v0.1: a three-layer Chinese AI-flavor evaluation framework with 382 judge-annotated preference pairs.

items.title: Foundation Pareto Flow Policy for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: The overarching goal of reinforcement learning (RL) is to efficiently optimize the agent's policy for various environments, tasks, dynamics, and even user preferences, which often consist of multiple and potentially conflicting rewards/objectives. This necessitates the learning of Pareto-optimal policies that can navigate different trade-offs among objectives. However, existing multi-objective RL (MORL) methods, whether trained online or offline, are typically limited to task- or objective-specific policy learning and do not address generalization of learned trade-offs to unseen tasks/objectives. In this work, we propose the Foundation Pareto Flow Policy (FP2) for offline MORL in continuous robotic control, inspired by the pre-mid-post-training paradigm underlying recent foundation models. Specifically, we instantiate FP2 as a multi-modal diffusion transformer equipped with a likelihood-free flow matching loss, enabling unified, scalable, and instructable learning of diverse trade-off trajectories. We further develop a three-stage training pipeline to gradually optimize the policy: (1) pre-training on a large-scale MORL dataset, (2) mid-training on a carefully curated high-quality dataset, and (3) post-training on few collected trajectory data from new tasks and trade-offs. Empirical results demonstrate that FP2 outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods on most tasks of the D4MORL benchmark, achieving superior zero-shot interpolation and extrapolation on complex Pareto manifolds as well as efficient few-shot adaptation of the learned trade-off prior to new continuous-control tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/FibonacciRabbit/FP2.

items.title: IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation
items.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

items.title: Read Before You Fit: Text-Derived Constraints for Discovering Differential Equations from Noisy Biological Data
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for scientific equation discovery. However, most existing methods are strongly data-driven and assume sufficiently clean and representative observations. This assumption is problematic in biological systems, where individual-level measurements are often sparse, noisy, heterogeneous, and expensive to obtain. While the underlying mechanisms are extensively described in scientific text, they are not explicitly used for the LLM based modeling of such systems. We introduce P2C, an agentic framework that translates textual descriptions of biological systems into a typed set of formal constraints, and use these constraints to restrict candidate ordinary differential equation (ODE) structures before numerical fitting. P2C consists of five stages: Text2Constraint extraction, ODE discovery, symbolic verification, parameter fitting, and model scoring. We evaluate P2C on four published ODE systems of acute inflammation and immune regulation, under clean and noisy observations. By progressively degrading the numerical evidence, we isolate when textual domain knowledge contributes beyond regression alone. Across the four systems, adding Text2Constraint reduces the worst form error from 1.397 to 0.499 on clean data and from 13.096 to 1.095 for data perturbed with Gaussian noise of $σ=0.1$; P2C also achieves lower form error and trajectory error than several LLM-based baselines over the tested noise range.

items.title: MIAO: Microscaling Intermediate Accumulation Optimization
items.abstract: Microscaling (MX) quantization enables lower-precision large language model (LLM) inference with limited accuracy degradation, reducing memory requirement and multiplication cost. However, despite reduced operand precision, accumulation is often retained at high floating-point precisions, leaving a substantial hardware cost that operand quantization alone does not address. In particular, systolic arrays, as used in tensor accelerators such as Google TPU and AWS Trainium, distribute accumulation across distinct processing elements but conventionally use uniform accumulator precision throughout the array. This spatial organization offers an opportunity to reduce hardware cost by tailoring precision to individual accumulation stages. In this work, we present MIAO, a hardware-software co-design framework that jointly selects product precision and stage-dependent accumulator widths to minimize hardware area and energy cost under an end-to-end perplexity constraint. MIAO first calibrates MX block-scale shifts to reduce intermediate magnitudes while preserving operand quantization accuracy, then assigns narrower accumulators to earlier stages and progressively wider accumulators to later stages. To efficiently explore the resulting design space, MIAO combines hardware cost estimates derived from logic synthesis with a calibrated accuracy predictor to identify promising precision configurations, then validates the accuracy of promising candidates through bit-exact end-to-end LLM evaluation. Across MXFP8, MXFP6, and MXFP4, MIAO reduces processing element (PE) array area by up to 38.7% and energy by up to 36.1% relative to the all-BF16 accumulation baseline, with at most 1.60% additional perplexity degradation over operand-only MX quantization across six LLMs.

items.title: Found, but Not Fixed : From Software Vulnerability Discovery to Fixes with Iterative LLM Pipelines
items.abstract: Software vulnerabilities persist as a critical threat despite the deployment of sophisticated detection tools and AI assistants. While detection has advanced, the subsequent code repair phase remains a primary bottleneck; manual intervention is inherently slow, costly, and prone to introducing secondary regressions and issues. In this paper, we investigate whether an iterative, LLM-based pipeline can provide a robust solution for the automated repair of vulnerable functions in real-world code. We propose a generalized framework that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) through a multi-stage feedback loop. We benchmark this approach against state-of-the-art models, including GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, and Gemini 3 Flash, demonstrating that such a pipeline can achieve high-quality code repair. To support the broader security community, we provide our evaluation framework, fine-tuned weights, and comprehensive experimental dataset on our website: https://sites.google.com/view/llm4cve

items.title: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
items.abstract: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of complex dynamical systems in mechanics and engineering problems, where non-Gaussian statistics of model-form uncertainties are non-negligible (e.g., due to the nonlinearities of the system dynamics and/or the observations) and true closure data are not available, for both offline learning and online assimilation.

items.title: λproc: a compositional language for process description, with a case study in chemical synthesis
items.abstract: Processes—cooking recipes, formulations, industrial flowsheets, chemical synthesis procedures—are recorded as prose or as diagrams. Neither form is machine-checkable, neither admits a canonical string, and neither makes the reuse of a sub-process explicit. We present λproc, a language in which a process is written as a composition of functions over streams: a unit operation is a function from streams to streams, a sub-process is a named lambda, and the process graph is not drawn but emerges from referential transparency—two textual mentions of the same expression denote the same physical node. The language is specified by a grammar of five productions, a canonical form that maps each process to exactly one string, and a validator that decides whether a document denotes a well-formed process. We argue that these three properties make λproc a useful target for machine learning, and we test the claim on a case study. Converting 1 808 937 reactions text-mined from US patents yields 700 149 distinct λproc documents and, notably, zero invalid ones: the converter either produces a well-formed process or rejects the reaction. Trained on this corpus, a decoder-only transformer of 2.73 M parameters reads a target molecule and writes a synthesis procedure that validates in 99.7 % of cases and recovers 24.5 % of the reactants of the real procedure on molecules it has never seen. It is measured against two trivial baselines, and the comparison is instructive: a nearest-neighbour lookup over 597 350 training molecules ties it on the conventional metric, and diagnosing that tie shows the metric itself to be dominated by ubiquitous reagents—a constant answer scores 0.133 on it. On a metric restricted to building blocks the lookup falls to 0.180 while the model holds 0.266. Three further results follow. The grammar saturates at the smallest model size tested, so capacity buys chemistry, not syntax. The validator makes rejection sampling exact: ten samples yield ten usable procedures, with an oracle of 0.422 against 0.260 for the model’s own ranking, but no reference-free feature we measured recovers more than 0.005 of that gap. And conditioning on an inventory of available materials triples reactant recall to 0.764, where the model selects rather than copies the shelf—but stress tests show it trusts the shelf: when the right reactants are absent it falls below the unconditioned model, and when near-miss analogues stand in for them it substitutes them inside documents that still validate. A pretrained 350 M-parameter language model, fine-tuned on the same corpus in five configurations, loses by a factor of three. All code, weights and an interactive application are released with this paper.

items.title: pH‐Triggered Biodegradable Electronics via Cleanroom‐Compatible Chitosan Platforms
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Biodegradable electronics that can be manufactured in standard cleanroom facilities while offering controlled pH‐triggered degradation have been a major challenge limiting both sustainable manufacturing and programmable end‐of‐life disposal. Here, we demonstrate that encapsulated chitosan, a naturally abundant polysaccharide, serves as a direct substrate for photolithographic processing and plasma‐enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) without requiring transfer steps or specialized equipment. The chitosan platform remained stable during device operation (pH 7) but rapidly degraded under acidic conditions (pH < 5), enabling on‐demand dissolution in CH at pH 4.6. Using this approach, we fabricated zinc oxide thin‐film transistors with mobilities of 98 cm 2 V − 1 s − 1 , on/off ratios exceeding 10 3, and device yields of 92%. The versatility of the platform is demonstrated by photodetectors with external quantum efficiencies of 1452% at 254 nm and functional logic circuits (NOT, NAND, and NOR gates) operating at voltages below 4 V. Complete device dissolution occurred within 32 days at pH 4.6, whereas it remained stable for the same period at a neutral pH. This pH‐programmable degradation mechanism, combined with standard semiconductor processing compatibility, establishes a manufacturing‐ready pathway for sustainable electronics with applications ranging from temporary medical implants that dissolve at wound sites (pH ∼5.5) to environmental sensors with triggered‐disposal mechanisms.

items.title: [Revisit 4] Project Janus Revisited: The Two-Faced Gate - A Rare-Earth-Oxide Memory Gate on the Angelica GaN HEMT that Forgets on Purpose: Trap Physics, Inverse Design of the Host Mixture, Three Dials, a Physical Reservoir, Applications and the Audit of the First Edition
items.abstract: Project Janus Revisited (revised edition, November 2026) of the Angelica Paper Series. A europium-doped rare-earth oxide (Eu:RE₂O₃) in the gate of an AlGaN/GaN HEMT is designed as a volatile memory whose forgetting time is chosen by chemistry, spacer thickness and temperature, from microseconds to about a month (Sc₂O₃ ceiling ≈ 34 d at 25 °C). The analysis is done on a single mobility-gap energy scale with measured band offsets. The decisive quantity is the lift, meaning how far the empty Eu²⁺ level sits above the electron layer. Elastic writing is possible only when the lift is below 2^(2/3)−1 ≈ 0.59 of the trap depth (Project Charon). On the standard Al₀.₂₈GaN barrier the lift is about 1.04 eV and writing is impossible. An Al-rich top barrier (Al ≈ 0.43–0.71) opens a window. Because the electron layer is a semiconductor, each cell writes inside a band of gate fields rather than above a threshold, and the field picks which trap depth is addressed. As a result, a gentle, long signal is kept and a strong, brief one is soon forgotten. In simulations, a 50-cell physical reservoir matches a tuned echo-state network on Lorenz forecasting and does better under read noise, while the network wins on NARMA10 and memory capacity. Hole-storage (Pr/Tb) and ferroelectric branches are left to companion papers. Every claim is tagged IMPLEMENTED, TESTABLE or CONCEPT, and a prioritised list of lab tests is given. The paper comes in three languages (en/zh-TW/ja) with primers. Text and figures are CC BY 4.0, and code is Apache-2.0. This is published as a defensive publication: anyone is free to use it, and it may not be patented by others. Keywords: GaN HEMT; europium; rare-earth oxide gate; charge-trap memory; volatile memory; tunable retention; band offset; lift rule; trap-assisted tunnelling; AlGaN barrier engineering; physical reservoir computing; neuromorphic hardware; spaced learning; Sc2O3; Y2O3; defensive publication; Angelica Paper Series

items.title: VLM-DC: Vision--Language Model for Automotive Data Collection
items.abstract: The development of advanced driver-assistance systems (ADASs) and autonomous driving technologies depends on high-quality, representative driving data. Traditional collection methods either demand extensive manual filtering or rely on rigid thresholds that miss critical edge cases. To overcome these limitations and meet diverse operational and system requirements, this work introduces a two-module, vision–language model (VLM)-based framework for intelligent and targeted data collection. The first module employs a cloud–edge multiagent architecture, where a cloud-based large language model (LLM) coordinates sensor selection and an edge-deployed VLM evaluates scene relevance. This approach achieves 91.35% overall precision, reduces storage by 28.30%, and shows promising performance on geographically distinct out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets. The second module implements a distributed VLM architecture with knowledge distillation (KD), deploying a lightweight vision encoder on vehicles and a language decoder in the cloud. A selective token transfer mechanism reduces model size by 71% and bandwidth use by 50% while maintaining 91.86% overall accuracy. Both modules outperform larger baselines while remaining computationally and communication efficient. Overall, this framework shifts automotive data collection from exhaustive recording to selective capture of valuable driving moments, accelerating ADAS development and validation.

items.title: Two‐dimensional optoelectronic synaptic materials for emerging neuromorphic devices
items.abstract: The exponential growth of global data and the fundamental energy efficiency limits of the traditional von Neumann architecture have driven an urgent need for novel computing paradigms. Neuromorphic computing, inspired by the highly efficient and parallel processing capabilities of the human brain, offers a promising solution. Among various hardware candidates, artificial optoelectronic synaptic devices based on two‐dimensional (2D) materials have attracted immense attention due to their atomic‐level thickness, excellent optoelectronic response, and ultra‐low power consumption. This comprehensive review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in 2D optoelectronic synaptic devices, focusing on six core operating mechanisms: defect‐mediated charge trapping, floating‐gate charge storage, van der Waals heterojunction interface engineering, ferroelectric polarization, ion migration, and phase‐change mechanisms. By leveraging these physical mechanisms, 2D optoelectronic synapses successfully emulate fundamental biological synaptic functions, including short‐term and long‐term plasticity, thereby realizing the integration of in‐sensor and in‐memory computing. Furthermore, we highlight the state‐of‐the‐art applications of these devices in brain‐inspired vision and neuromorphic computing systems. Despite significant laboratory‐scale achievements, transitioning from proof‐of‐concept to system‐level applications remains challenging. Finally, we outline critical engineering hurdles and future research trajectories, emphasizing the necessity for high‐quality wafer‐scale material growth, high‐density integration to minimize crosstalk, algorithm‐hardware co‐design, and the development of biocompatible platforms for advanced wearable technologies and brain‐computer interfaces.

items.title: Two‐Terminal Synaptic Devices Based on a Single‐Component Conjugated Polyelectrolyte for Noise‐Tolerant Pattern Encoding
items.abstract: Neuromorphic devices, inspired by the efficiency of biological neural networks, hold promise for local, low‐power processing in artificial intelligence and edge‐computing applications. Organic materials are particularly attractive for such devices due to their chemical tunability, enabling precise control of ion transport dynamics critical for synaptic emulation. Here we present an artificial two‐terminal synaptic device based on a single‐component conjugated polythiophene‐based polyelectrolyte. The single‐component design avoids inter‐component phase separation; the devices additionally exhibit stable and reproducible operation. Electrical characterization, including impedance spectroscopy, reveals ion‐mediated transport and electrochemical doping processes governing device operation. The devices exhibit key neuromorphic properties such as paired‐pulse facilitation with fast response times, pronounced signal amplification, and stable conductance modulation under pulsed operation. Pattern‐encoding experiments with a 16‐device array show that four patterns remain correctly classified up to 33.3% input noise. These results highlight the potential of single‐component organic materials for scalable, high‐performance, and noise‐resilient neuromorphic computing platforms.

items.title: TwinCache: A Retrieval- and Reranking-Aware Caching System for Efficient RAG Serving
items.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves the factuality of large language models (LLMs) by grounding responses in external knowledge, but introduces substantial pre-generation latency. We observe that both database retrieval and neural reranking can dominate time-to-first-token (TTFT) under different serving configurations, while related queries exhibit cross-query locality in retrieved chunks and high-ranked evidence after reranking. However, existing optimizations typically target retrieval or reranking in isolation, leaving this locality underexploited across the two stages. To this end, we present TwinCache, a retrieval- and reranking-aware caching system that exploits cross-query locality to jointly accelerate both stages of RAG serving.
