TwinCache organizes historical queries and retrieved chunks into locality-aware cache regions and constructs a compact, high-utility candidate set for each incoming query using nearest-query evidence, historical reranking feedback, and current-query similarity. This avoids expensive database retrieval on validated cache hits while reducing the number of chunks submitted to the reranker. To further reduce pre-generation latency, TwinCache introduces priority-guided reranking, which processes high-priority chunks first, overlaps subsequent reranking with LLM chunked prefill, and stops once the leading evidence chunks stabilize. TwinCache also mitigates potential false cache hits through online validation and refreshes cache regions during low-load periods using online feedback. Across diverse serving loads, TwinCache achieves up to 2.44 × the serving throughput of a vLLM-based RAG system while maintaining response quality comparable to standard RAG.

items.title: Topological Field & Variational Architecture (TFVA): A Heterogeneous Spintronic-SAW & Thin-Film Photonic Co-Processing Paradigm for Supercomputing & AI
items.abstract: Modern supercomputing and artificial intelligence (AI) data centers face two severe physical bottlenecks: (1) the Von Neumann Memory Wall, where up to 90% of system power is dissipated charging capacitive copper interconnects between High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and digital logic cores, and (2) the Simulation & Sampling Wall, where digital GPUs expend megawatts of clocked Boolean switching to simulate continuous differential equations, combinatorial Ising/QUBO landscapes, and stochastic Boltzmann distributions. While wave-based and spintronic computing have been explored independently, naive attempts to stack acoustic transducers, metallic spintronic films, high-finesse optical cavities, wire-free nanoscale addressing, and high-modulus phase arithmetic into a single unpatterned monolithic slab fail due to five fundamental condensed-matter and information-theoretic limits: (i) the Metallic Cavity Paradox, (ii) High-Order Nonlinearity Limits & CRT Fragility, (iii) the Shannon Space-Bandwidth Limit, (iv) Unpatterned Wafer Drift & Skyrmion Bag Instability, and (v) 2D Acoustoelectric Sheet Thermal Runaway. In TFVA, we resolve all five limits through a heterogeneous 3-chiplet co-processing architecture (TFVA-Node) on a shared Silicon/Organic Interposer: Chiplet 1 (CMOS-Host) handles OS control, HBM3/NVMe storage, exact 64/128-bit ALU math, and Redundant Residue Number System (RRNS) syndrome decoding; Chiplet 2 (TFVA-Spin, Track B) deploys lithographically patterned magnetic micro-corrals (Pt/CoFeB/MgO or compensated GdFeCo) on LiNbO3 lubricated by low-loss 50 MHz Surface Acoustic Waves ( 90% at 300 K, read out electrically via Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (> 200% TMR) with non-volatile "Ultrasonic Freeze" retention; and Chiplet 3 (TFVA-Photonic, Track C) uses etched Thin-Film Lithium Niobate (TFLN) waveguides (1550 nm, < 0.03 dB/cm) for 50-100 GHz MZI linear algebra, native chi^(2) binary (0/pi) DOPO Ising relaxation, and 1-of-p_k spatial-rail low-modulus RRNS arithmetic. Coupled multiphysics simulations verify: (1) 9.58 dB PSLR (71.3% clutter reduction) for M = 64, N_omega = 32 boundary synthesis; (2) a 28,076x improvement in 300 K Boltzmann KL divergence (D_KL = 6.5 x 10^-4 vs. 18.38); (3) 96.41% mean ground-state approximation on frustrated N = 64 Ising benchmarks; and (4) 100.0% single-error correction (0.0 error) in the 8-channel RRNS pipeline.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Tin Halide Perovskite Photonic Synaptic Transistors for Broadband RGB–NIR Color Discrimination and Low‐Light Vision
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photonic synaptic transistors that process wavelength‐dependent optical information are promising building blocks for neuromorphic visual perception, yet most devices operate mainly in the UV or visible region, limiting broadband recognition and low‐light vision. Here, we report thiophene‐engineered mixed‐dimensional 2D/3D tin halide perovskite photonic synaptic transistors for visible‐to‐near‐infrared (NIR) color discrimination. A MA/Cs‐incorporated FASnI 3 composition is used as the 3D bulk channel to combine efficient charge transport with controlled hysteresis, while a surface‐confined 2D phase suppresses dark current and improves operational stability. Compared with phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI), 2‐thiopheneethylammonium iodide (TEAI) more effectively regulates crystallization and passivates surface defects, yielding enhanced charge transport, reduced threshold‐voltage shift during repeated operation, and stable hysteretic photoresponse. The optimized device emulates key synaptic functions, including excitatory postsynaptic current, paired‐pulse facilitation, and long‐term potentiation/depression. Its wavelength‐dependent absorption generates distinguishable conductance states under NIR, red, green, and blue illumination, enabling six‐level RGB–NIR optical encoding. Synaptic‐array‐based neuromorphic preprocessing further enhances low‐light pedestrian detection, demonstrating the potential of 2D/3D Sn perovskite photonic synaptic transistors for multispectral neuromorphic vision.

items.title: Tailoring Ion Exchange Efficiency in Synaptic Electrochemical Memtransistors Through Three‐Dimensional Artificial Crystal Engineering
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Electronic synapses featuring conduction modulation for synaptic weight update play a central role in implementing neuromorphic computing. Though memristors and memtransistors operating via ion exchange for conductance modulation have demonstrated synaptic functionality, their planar architectures suffer from a reduced interfacial area during lateral scaling, limiting their dynamic range of conductance modulation. Here, an electrochemical memtransistor is presented that replaces conventional planar layout with a precisely engineered 3D structure composed of an SU‐8 organic reservoir and ZnO channel, fabricated using proximity‐field nanopatterning. This design increases the effective oxygen ion‐exchange interfacial area available for conductance modulation without enlarging the device footprint. The 3D device achieves a dynamic range nearly 34‐fold larger than a planar counterpart, withstands over 10 4 updating pulses, and exhibits key biological synaptic dynamics. Deep neural network simulations based on the measured weight‐update characteristics show improved classification accuracy over the planar control, and the inherent fading memory of the device supports reservoir computing. These findings establish deterministic 3D structural engineering as a scalable strategy for decoupling device footprint from synaptic modulation capability, thereby addressing a scaling bottleneck in neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Sub-Landauer Optomagnetic Logic: Non-Thermal Floquet–Chern Switching and Pseudoscalar Photonic Gates for Reversible Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Transitioning artificial intelligence from dissipative von Neumann CMOS architectures toward the ultimate physical bounds of non-equilibrium thermodynamics requires hardware substrates capable of non-thermal state reconfiguration, reversible logic execution, and phase-coherent optical routing. Building upon our recent formulations of high-frequency Zeeman-Floquet gauge dynamics, extended topological electrodynamics, and two-century physical bounds on machine intelligence, we construct a rigorous theoretical blueprint for sub-Landauer, in-memory neuromorphic computing in twisted van der Waals moire Chern ferromagnets coupled to nanophotonic and slow-light waveguides. By operating in flat-band regimes where scalar kinetic dispersion is quenched (v0 -> 0) and the dimensionless optomagnetic mixing ratio R_mix(k) = ||H_mixed^(1)(k)|| / ||H_electric^(1)(k)|| is maximized, we demonstrate that structured optical pulses satisfying E_opt . B_opt != 0 drive coherent, bijective topological switching across 0- and pi-quasienergy gaps without carrier thermalization. Using the non-equilibrium Keldysh-Floquet formalism on a regularized two-dimensional lattice, we integrate out electronic degrees of freedom to derive the adiabatic Chern-Simons response alongside explicit upper bounds on dissipative entropy production Delta S_irr per topological gate operation. Finally, we show that coupling these pseudoscalar optomagnetic memory arrays to ultra-cold atomic Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) under Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT) and dispersion-engineered waveguides (m*(q) < 0) resolves relativistic clock-skew and synchronization latency constraints, establishing an actionable experimental pathway toward 10^10 to 10^20 compression in energy per operation.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Scientist Amr Torky LAW 0230: Scientist Amr Torky Law of Non-Volatile Memristive Neuromorphic Synaptic Plasticity Law (Sovereign 100-Gate Live Verification Suite)
items.abstract: Regularizes conductance drift in multi-state analog resistive memory devices. Benchmarked against international formal verification standards (seL4, CompCert, NASA JPL Power of 10, and SV-COMP meta-verifiers). Verified across 100 Live Hardware and Formal Proof Gates, sealed via Merkle-DAG ECDSA P-256.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Scalable In-Memory Computing with N-ary Spintronic Crossbar Arrays
items.abstract: The ever-growing energy and latency demands of AI workloads call for a fundamental shift away from conventional von Neumann architectures. In-memory computing (IMC), which co-locates computation and storage within analog crossbar arrays, is a compelling approach to address the von Neumann bottleneck and the memory wall. Among emerging non-volatile memory technologies, multi-state magnetic tunnel junctions (M2TJs), whose resistance is controlled by the magnetization configuration of crossed ferromagnetic ellipses, stand out for their non-volatility, CMOS compatibility, and intrinsic potential for equidistantly separated resistance levels, making them ideal candidates for n-ary neuromorphic IMC. We present a simulation framework for performing multibit neural network inference on n-ary crossbar architectures, developed for spintronic M2TJs but generalizable to any multistate memristive device. The framework retrieves the matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) result from the measured analog output with minimal assumptions, enabling the crossbar to operate as a standalone AI co-processor. Using simulated 4×4 arrays of 4-state M2TJs, we demonstrate successful inference on the XOR task and on MNIST handwritten digit classification, achieving 94.48% accuracy against a 97.56% software baseline. This gap is further reduced to 2.79% via PCA dimensionality reduction. We provide a systematic error analysis identifying weight quantization as the dominant error source. Systematic nonidealities (shared by all cells) and cell-specific random noise are also studied. Critically, cell-specific noise is less detrimental than systematic nonidealities of equal amplitude, owing to beneficial averaging across the array. The RMSE scales as √n with the number of columns while the SNR grows logarithmically, favoring wide crossbar geometries. Finally, we demonstrate the existence of an optimal number of resistance states Nopt that minimizes total MVM error by trading off quantization error against state resolution, with Nopt decreasing in noisier device environments.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Reliability Study of Tungsten Microheater for Phase Change Material Switch
items.abstract: 5G/6G wireless sensor networks demand high-reliability nonvolatile radio frequency (RF) microactuators for signal routing, and GeTe-based phase-change switches are promising candidates. A tungsten microheater acts as the core electrothermal driving unit, yet conventional W films suffer severe electromigration and thermal fracture under repeated electric pulses, limiting the long-term service of sensing devices. In this work, tungsten thin films with different thicknesses and crystal phases are fabricated via magnetron sputtering and $600~^{\circ }$ C thermal annealing. The coupling failure mechanism induced by Joule heat and electric stress is systematically investigated, and the influences of film thickness (80–150 nm) and $\alpha $ / $\beta $ -W crystal structures on electrical resistance, voltage endurance, and cyclic stability are analyzed. Experimental results demonstrate that the 100–120 nm $\alpha $ -W heater exhibits ultralow resistance of 6– $10~\Omega $ , and stably withstands $10^{6}$ pulses of 10 V/200 ns without open-circuit failure. In contrast, metastable $\beta $ -W films fail at only $6{\,}\times {\,}10 ^{5}$ cycles due to high grain boundary diffusion rate. The integrated phase-change switch maintains stable on / off ratio ( $\sim$ $ 10^{5}$ ) over 1000 switching cycles. This work reveals the electrothermal failure law of W thin films and provides a practical fabrication strategy for high-endurance microheaters, thereby paving the way for reliable phase-change RF switches in next-generation wireless sensor front-ends.

items.title: RS-Infer: A Fast and Secure LLM Inference System for Mobile Devices with Recallable Resource Isolation
items.abstract: The adoption of device-side Large Language Models (LLMs) has grown rapidly, offering stronger privacy and higher availability than their cloud-side counterparts. Attackers may compromise the OS kernel to steal valuable model weights and user data. ARM TrustZone is the de facto hardware-based isolation technology on mobile devices, used to protect sensitive applications from a compromised OS. However, protecting LLM inference with TrustZone incurs significant overhead for both the secure inference and the normal applications, due to two challenges: the inflexible resource isolation and the inefficient secure resource management. To address these challenges, this paper presents RS-Infer, a fast and secure LLM inference system for mobile devices. The key idea is to decouple the access permission from the management permission of secure resources, so that the normal-world OS cannot access them but can still manage them as usual. First, RS-Infer introduces a Recallable Resource Isolation mechanism to construct Recallable Secure Memory (RS-Memory) and a Recallable Secure NPU (RS-NPU). They can only be accessed by the secure world, but can be efficiently allocated and reclaimed by the normal-world OS. Based on them, RS-Infer further introduces the RS-Infer Framework to run secure LLM inference in the secure world. It cooperates with the normal-world OS to manage secure memory. We evaluate an RS-Infer prototype against a TrustZone-based Strawman and its optimized variant. RS-Infer achieves average TTFT speedups of 8.00 × and 2.19 × , respectively, and average response latency speedups of 14.15 × and 2.94 × for multi-model agent workflows.

items.title: RESONA: From Symbolic Knowledge Models to Adaptive Spiking Neural Networks
items.abstract: This paper presents RESONA, a research proposal aimed at extending the existing research on symbolic knowledge representations and inference mechanisms developed within the SENSE project into the fields of neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence and neuromorphic computing systems. The research builds upon executable knowledge models, production rules, and semantic structures developed as part of the research activities at Xolution Research. The proposed research directly builds upon the work of Cotteret et al. (2024, 2025), who demonstrated the feasibility of implementing finite-state automata through distributed symbolic representations in attractor neural networks, as well as their implementation in recurrent spiking neural networks (RSNNs), including on neuromorphic hardware. RESONA seeks to extend these findings by investigating the neural realization of selected symbolic processes derived from the executable knowledge models developed within SENSE. Particular attention is devoted to the incremental adaptation of neural representations, the preservation of functional correctness under repeated modifications, and the identification of the limits of such adaptation. The research proposal envisages experimental validation of the proposed mechanisms through simulations, followed by implementation and evaluation on neuromorphic hardware. The aim of this paper is to formulate the research problem, hypothesis, and methodological foundations for investigating adaptive neuro-symbolic representations that could contribute to the development of more complex cognitive architectures in the future. Keywords: Neuro-Symbolic AI, Spiking Neural Networks (SNN), Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks (RSNN), Neuromorphic Computing, Distributed Symbolic Representations, Incremental Adaptation, Continual Learning, Executable Knowledge Models, Attractor Neural Networks, Symbolic Reasoning, Cognitive Architectures
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Near‐Infrared Persistent Luminescent Synapses of Er 3+ ‐Doped Ca 2 SnO 4 for Photonic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Extending optical synapses beyond the visible spectral region is crucial for realizing bandwidth‐expanded photonic neuromorphic systems compatible with modern optical communication technologies. In this work, we demonstrate a near‐infrared luminescent synaptic device based on Er 3+ doped Ca 2 SnO 4 . Under ultraviolet excitation, the material exhibits stable near‐infrared emission around 1540 nm, corresponding to the telecommunication wavelength band, with pronounced long‐persistent luminescence originating from defect‐related trap states introduced by Er 3+ incorporation. The near‐infrared luminescence shows clear synaptic functionalities, including stimulus‐dependent modulation, paired‐pulse facilitation, and spike‐number‐ and spike‐frequency‐dependent potentiation. These synaptic responses are systematically controlled by pulse amplitude, duration, number, and frequency, closely resembling short‐term and long‐term plasticity in biological synapses. Furthermore, the experimentally measured potentiation curve was used to construct the neuron activation function in an artificial neural network for handwritten digit recognition, while the transient response characteristics were incorporated into reservoir computing for temporal information processing. This work establishes Er 3+ ‐doped Ca 2 SnO 4 as a viable near‐infrared luminescent synaptic platform and provides a pathway toward spectral coincidence with the low‐loss telecommunication C‐band photonic neuromorphic systems operating in the near‐infrared regime, spectrally coinciding with the low‐loss telecommunication C‐band.

items.title: Model-as-a-Service in the Wild: Characterizing Production LLM Inference Clusters at Scale
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference has been widely deployed in modern cloud platforms as Model-as-a-Service (MaaS), serving both online and offline applications on shared, heterogeneous GPU clusters. Recent characterization studies have examined request-level workload patterns, but cluster-wide resource patterns and system-level deployment behaviors remain largely unexplored. This missing view is critical for diagnosing production bottlenecks and for understanding whether and how existing inference techniques should be applied in real MaaS systems. In this paper, we analyze a six-month production LLM inference trace from xMaaS, a large-scale MaaS platform with over 100K GPUs. xMaaS provides a detailed system view of cluster resources and their allocation across 300K applications and 70K model variants, enabling a resource-centric analysis across cluster, application, and model levels. Our study characterizes how heterogeneous GPU resources are supplied and utilized, how application resource demand is distributed and evolves over time, and how model variants and serving modes affect resource allocation on heterogeneous hardware. Based on these observations, we further analyze deployment implications and identify open problems for production MaaS systems, which we hope will motivate future research on resource-efficient LLM inference.

items.title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
items.abstract: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

items.title: MoECatch: Efficient Checkpointing and Consistent Recovery for Mixture-of-Experts Models
items.abstract: Checkpointing is essential for fault-tolerant large language model training, but it increasingly limits persistence frequency and recovery efficiency as training runs become longer and clusters become larger. This problem is especially acute in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) systems, where checkpoint bytes are dominated by expert parameters and optimizer states. Conventional checkpointing persists all experts uniformly at every checkpoint, even though expert updates are highly uneven under skewed token routing. This mismatch wastes checkpointing bandwidth on persisting “barely changed experts”, limits attainable checkpoint frequency, and increases rollback cost after failures. To address this mismatch, we present MoECatch, a sparse checkpointing system for MoE training that treats sparse checkpointing as a coupled checkpoint-and-recovery problem. On the checkpoint path, Aging-then-Greedy Expert Selection (AGES) prioritizes which experts to persist under a fixed budget. On the recovery path, Version Catch-Up (VCU) reconstructs stale experts from mixed-version checkpoints while leaving already aligned state unchanged. MoECatch further accelerates recovery through minimum executable-state restoration and asynchronous optimizer staging. We implement MoECatch in the MindSpeed framework. The results show that MoECatch improves attainable checkpoint frequency by up to 2.5 × and reduces end-to-end wasted time after failures by up to \(22.86\%\). Across both pre-training and fine-tuning workloads, recovery preserves average downstream-task accuracy relative to full-checkpoint recovery. At the state level, the relative L2 parameter deviation between the recovered model and the same-iteration full checkpoint does not exceed \(0.001\%\).

items.title: Mitigating Physical Threats to AI Supernodes with Dynamic Trust Domains
items.abstract: Frontier large-language models (LLMs) have outgrown single accelerator capacity and are increasingly served by AI supernodes: tightly coupled systems of accelerators connected by high-speed scale-up links that carry inter-accelerator traffic. Recent physical attacks on data-center CPU memory buses, which operate at comparable rates, have compromised trusted execution environments, suggesting that similar attacks on scale-up links are within practical reach. Existing protections for accelerator interconnects remain fragmented: some authenticate devices without protecting data in transit, while pairwise secure channels provide cryptographic protection but scale poorly as accelerator domains grow. We present Dynamic Trust Domains (DTDs), a group-key-based mechanism for securing accelerator communication within AI supernodes. DTD's Key Management protocol governs the full domain lifecycle, including creation, key distribution, membership changes, rekeying, and teardown, and runs over SPDM, making the design portable across scale-up interconnects that already adopt this standard. We instantiate DTD on the Huawei Unified Bus (UB) protocol and implement an emulated UB supernode. On Mixture-of-Experts inference with eight cryptographic engines per die, DTD incurs 2.3% throughput loss at a 4096-byte MTU, compared with 57.3% for peer-to-peer encryption at a 10 μs key-swap latency, whose cost is dominated by continuous key swapping in cryptographic engines. These results suggest that group-key trust domains can secure inter-accelerator communication more efficiently than pairwise encryption as AI supernodes scale.

items.title: Logical AI OS: A Training-Free Governance Layer Outside the Model for Instruction Following -- Benefits, Costs, Failures, and the Calibration of the Measuring Instrument Itself
items.abstract: Small language models often fail explicit user requests (length, number of items, format, required or forbidden words, grammatical person, answer language). We measure a training-free governance layer placed outside the model: it reads the requests with rules, checks the answer mechanically, repairs it when a request is not kept, and hands back the original answer when the repair fails. The loop exists in prior work; our contribution is measuring its benefits, costs and failures, and reporting how the measuring instrument itself was calibrated. On four 4-bit Qwen-family models (3B, 7B, 14B, one 7B reasoning model) and 329 Chinese prompts: (1) answers that keep every request the layer read rise significantly (all comparisons p<0.0001), by 34 to 66 of 329 under the corrected checker and 52 to 92 after a length-control fix; a generic redo message brings no significant gain. (2) Exploratory: on 90 repair-triggered prompts, two AI annotators found the layer produced an acceptable answer where the bare model did not more often than the reverse (49:7; 18:12, not significant). (3) Costs: 43-66% more generation time; whole-answer rewriting makes a sizeable share of usable answers unusable. (4) Failures: rule-based reading reaches about 70% and 84% of a two-annotator ceiling on unseen phrasings; unsatisfiable requests make the reasoning model loop; model self-reports are unreliable (18 of 25 "fixed" items were not fixed). (5) Over half of the original checker's "violated" verdicts on structural requests were wrong; after correction the main result holds, and one comparison is downgraded. Conclusions are limited to this Chinese material, the Qwen family and sizes up to 14B. The governance implementation is not released; data, answers, verdicts and the checker are public.

items.title: KVLite: Efficient LLM Agent Scheduling via Head-Aware KV Sharing
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being applied in agentic applications through complex prompting structures, including fixed system prompts and the reuse of historical messages. However, existing service systems suffer from severe inefficiency due to redundant computation caused by shared text segments. Existing KV reuse strategies often fall short due to either stringent application conditions or accuracy degradation resulting from the neglect of the dynamic nature of attention distributions. We propose KVLite, a service framework based on KV sharing for agentic applications. At the algorithm level, KVLite identifies the critical heads in each layer, recomputes the KV cache for these heads to achieve a balance between high accuracy and low recomputation overhead. At the system level, KVLite identifies and shortens the critical path in agentic workflows based on KV sharing. Experimental evaluations across multiple LLM and agent benchmarks show that KVLite can significantly outperform state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a 2.1 × –3.9 × speedup in prefill latency and 2.3 × to 4.6 × improvement in throughput, with negligible accuracy loss compared to the recomputation baseline.

items.title: Intelligent visual perception beyond classification: a survey of deep learning and foundation models
items.abstract: Intelligent visual perception has advanced from traditional image classification to thorough comprehension of objects, scenes, relations, spatial context, and semantic information. This paper surveys the development of intelligent visual perception, particularly focusing on DL and foundation models. This section provides a comprehensive overview of visual recognition, detection, segmentation, and scene understanding, including key methods such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, attention mechanisms, encoder-decoder architectures, generative models, and Vision Transformers. The study also explores feature attribution, visual attention, visual reasoning, and multimodal vision-language models, which combine visual and text information for tasks such as visual question answering, captioning, and visual generation. This study examines recent foundation models incorporating vision-language architectures for their transferability, contextual understanding, and generalized perception capabilities. The study also discusses challenges related to computational efficiency, environmental variability, data requirements, robustness, explainability, and real-time deployment. Finally, it contrasts current developments to identify new approaches to scalable, interpretable, multimodal, and human-centric visual intelligence systems.
items.venue: Future Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence

items.title: InfiniLoRA: Disaggregated Multi-LoRA Serving for Large Language Models
items.abstract: LoRA enables efficient customization of LLMs and is widely used in multi-tenant and multi-task serving. However, emerging model architectures such as MoE significantly increase LoRA memory cost, making existing coupled LoRA serving designs poorly scalable and prone to tail-latency inflation. We present InfiniLoRA, a disaggregated LoRA serving system that decouples LoRA execution from base-model inference. InfiniLoRA introduces a shared LoRA Server with parallelism-aware execution, SLO-driven provisioning, and critical-path optimizations, including GPU-initiated communication and hardware-specialized LoRA kernels. Experiments show that InfiniLoRA can achieve an average 3.05 × increase in serviceable request rate under strict latency SLOs, and improve the percentage of LoRA adapters satisfying the SLO requirement by 54.0%.

items.title: High-Quality EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Dual-Branch Feature Extraction and Cascaded Conditional Diffusion
items.abstract: Reconstructing visual stimuli from electroencephalography (EEG) signals holds significant value for uncovering the underlying mechanisms of the human visual system. However, due to the inherently low signal-to-noise ratio and limited spatiotemporal resolution of EEG, the current reconstruction methods face substantial challenges in achieving precise semantic alignment and high-fidelity image generation. Moreover, some prior EEG reconstruction approaches rely on additional large-scale EEG data for representation pretraining. To address these challenges, we propose MindScryer, a novel end-to-end framework for EEG-based image reconstruction. The proposed framework employs a dual-branch encoder. One branch incorporates a self-supervised transformer to extract temporal features, while the other utilizes a depthwise separable convolutional module to capture frequency-spatial representations. This architecture enhances the EEG signal representation across multiple dimensions. Next, an improved contrastive learning mechanism is introduced to align the EEG embeddings with CLIP embeddings derived from textual descriptions generated by a large language model. This approach highlights key visual semantics and mitigates cross-modal heterogeneity. Finally, a cascaded diffusion model integrates both fine-grained aligned EEG embeddings and coarse-grained categorical information to synthesize high-quality images with improved semantic consistency. Experimental results on the block-design visually-evoked (BDVE) dataset demonstrate that MindScryer significantly enhances the accuracy and visual clarity of EEG-based image reconstruction, while zero-shot evaluation on the external THINGS-EEG dataset confirms its strong cross-dataset generalizability and application potential. These capabilities further enable seamless integration of neural sensing into IoT-driven systems by providing high-level semantic visual representations. The source code associated with our work is available at: https://github.com/FLieWen/MindScryer.

items.title: HBF-EventLab: A Discrete-Event Simulator for Studying Host-Device Coordination in High Bandwidth Flash
items.abstract: High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) combines NAND flash density with high-bandwidth accelerator connectivity, offering additional memory capacity for large language model inference. However, limited hardware availability makes it difficult to evaluate how host behavior and device resource constraints jointly affect HBF request processing. We present HBF-EventLab, an open-source, transaction-level discrete-event simulator based on the Open Compute Project HBF specification. HBF-EventLab connects host request dispatch, command admission, fragmented write assembly, read dispatch, NAND execution, and completion feedback within a shared event loop. It explicitly models distinct resource lifetimes and separates configurable scheduling policies from ordering and resource constraints, enabling controlled exploration of host-device coordination. Experiments show how resource limits, address interleaving, fragment arrival patterns, and scheduling policies affect write completion and request latency. The results highlight the need to consider resource limits and scheduling policies jointly, accounting for their interactions with write assembly and read eligibility. We also integrate HBF-EventLab with real GPU execution of Qwen3-0.6B, combining profiled GPU activity durations with simulated weight-access delays to estimate time to first token and time per output token, with logits and output tokens remaining bitwise identical to those from native GPU execution. HBF-EventLab provides a configurable foundation for studying HBF mechanisms, exploring scheduling policies, and assessing how HBF access delays affect application-level timing. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sjtu-epcc/HBF-EventLab.

items.title: HACK: Homomorphic Acceleration via Compression of the Key-Value Cache for Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Disaggregated Large Language Model (LLM) inference has gained popularity by decoupling the compute-intensive prefill stage from the memory-intensive decode stage, enabling the use of low-end, compute-focused GPUs for prefill and high-end, memory-rich GPUs for decode. This separation reduces cost while maintaining high throughput. However, transmitting Key-Value (KV) data between the two stages can induce high overhead, especially for long prompts. Additionally, the computation time overhead for prefill and decode is key for optimizing Job Completion Time (JCT), and KV data size can become prohibitive for long prompts and sequences. Existing KV quantization methods alleviate transmission and memory overhead by storing KV in low-bit formats, but attention still runs on dequantized BF16 KV in every iteration, incurring substantial recurring dequantization overhead and offering no reduction in attention compute. We propose Homomorphic Acceleration via Compression of the Key-Value cache (HACK) for disaggregated LLM inference. HACK keeps KV in a highly compressed INT2 form for transmission and caching, and it computes attention directly on the quantized KV. A lightweight approximation in the epilogue replaces per-iteration dequantization. HACK thereby reduces KV transmission, decode-time memory access, and attention computation together. Extensive trace-driven experiments show that HACK reduces average JCT by up to 70.9% compared to the disaggregated LLM inference baseline and by up to 53.5% compared to state-of-the-art KV quantization methods.

items.title: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) encode a high-resolution image into thousands of visual tokens, which dominate the cost of the prefill stage. Visual token reduction removes most of these tokens, but two problems remain at extreme budgets. The vision encoder still processes every patch of the image, and the few surviving tokens often miss the small regions that hold the answer. In this paper, we propose Glance-ETD, a two-stage token reduction framework guided by a lightweight question-conditioned scorer. In the first stage, a glance encoder views the image at low resolution and re-encodes only the question-relevant regions at native resolution. In the second stage, Evidence-Tempered Diversity (ETD) selects the final tokens by combining diversity with the evidence predicted by the scorer, so that the kept tokens cover the scene and retain the answer. A single-rollout self-distillation recipe trains the MLLM with the glance encoder. With only 5% of the visual tokens, Glance-ETD retains 91.6% of the full-token performance of Qwen3.5-4B across fourteen benchmarks and outperforms the strongest prior method, LT-OPD, by 17.3 points and the same training recipe with DivPrune by 6.0. It also speeds up the time to first token on 4K images by 3.1x and generalizes to three other MLLMs and to high-resolution document benchmarks, with the largest gains on text-rich tasks.

items.title: GA-LLMSS: Text-Spatio–Temporal Graph-Guided and Cross-Modal Alignment-Enhanced Large Language Model Empowered Soft Sensor
items.abstract: Data-driven soft sensing has gained widespread application in modern industrial processes for real-time, low-cost estimation of key quality variables, but existing models are generally constrained by single-modal numerical inputs and limited representational generalization. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in time-series tasks due to their sequence-pattern generalization, textual reasoning, and cross-modal knowledge transfer abilities, yet their application in soft sensing remains limited. To bridge this gap, this article proposes a text-spatio–temporal graph-guided and cross-modal alignment-enhanced LLM-empowered two-stage soft sensor (GA-LLMSS). Specifically, a scale-adaptive spatio–temporal graph encoder (SASTGE) is developed, which reconstructs raw multivariate time series into dynamic spatio–temporal interaction graphs (STIGs) according to the nonstationary characteristics, injecting structured prior logic to compensate for LLMs’ inherent deficiency in intervariable spatial perception. Building on this, a prompt-enhanced graph construction (PEGC) module enriches input semantics by crafting industrial prior knowledge prompts (IPKPs) with higher-order statistics, while an anchor token then serves as a cross-modal hub to establish logic-guided edges between prompts and graph nodes that explicitly guide LLMs in capturing cross-modal logical relationships and maintaining semantic coherence. To bridge textual and time-series modalities, an improved representation learning, dropout autoregressive alignment stage (DAAS), is proposed to enforce learning of deep spatio–temporal couplings from incomplete observations. Finally, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapts the model to real-world industrial scenarios: air preheaters (APs) and gas turbines (GTs). Experiments show that GA-LLMSS achieves advanced accuracy, superior few-shot representation generalization, and ablation studies validate the independent contributions of each key module.

items.title: Flexible Ultralow‐Power IGZO Multimodal Synaptic Transistors for Thermally Robust Neuromorphic Vision and Wearable Heatstroke Monitoring
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Multimodal synaptic devices are increasingly required to enable more reliable and informed decision‐making in next‐generation neuromorphic systems. A wafer‐scale, energy‐efficient flexible optoelectronic synaptic transistor based on an a‐IGZO channel and ALD‐deposited HfO 2 gate dielectric is demonstrated. The device is fabricated on a rigid silicon substrate and subsequently transformed into a flexible form, maintaining stable electrical characteristics under repeated bending (radius ∼3 cm). The device enables multimodal sensing by responding to optical stimulus and a wide temperature range (10‐75°C), capturing signals such as body temperature, ambient conditions, and sunlight. Under optical stimulation, the transistor emulates key synaptic functions, including EPSC, PPF, and the transition from STM to LTM, as well as learning‐forgetting‐relearning behavior. Reliable synaptic responses are achieved at a low drain voltage of 0.01 V, with an energy consumption of 1.6 fJ per synaptic event. The behavior is governed by defect‐mediated carrier trapping and detrapping in IGZO. System‐level applications include heatstroke risk classification (99.6% accuracy, within the physiological temperature range 37°C–42°C) and neuromorphic vision sensing enabled by persistent photoconductivity. These multimodal capabilities enable both heatstroke monitoring and thermally robust vision processing within a unified platform. The results present a scalable platform for low‐power neuromorphic and wearable healthcare applications.

items.title: Flexible Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Photodetector Based on a Freestanding β-Ga2O3/BTO Semiconductor/Ferroelectric Heterostructure
items.abstract: Abstract Excessive ultraviolet (UV) exposure causes cumulative harm to human health, creating a growing demand for wearable devices that enable real-time UV monitoring. Among various UV-sensitive materials, β-Ga2O3 is particularly attractive because of its wide bandgap, intrinsic solar-blind response, high sensitivity, and excellent stability. However, its intrinsic brittleness and the high temperatures required for growth on rigid substrates limit its use in flexible electronics. Here, we report a flexible solar-blind Ga2O3 photodetector based on a freestanding ferroelectric BaTiO3 (BTO)/Ga2O3 heterostructure fabricated using a nondestructive, water-soluble transfer strategy. Spontaneous polarization in the BTO layer generates a built-in electric field that promotes the separation of photogenerated carriers. In addition, polarization rotation and domain evolution provide ferroelastic strain accommodation, enabling effective stress relaxation and improving the mechanical stability of the flexible device. The device retained more than 90% of its initial photocurrent after 1000 bending cycles at a bending radius of 7.5 mm. It was further integrated into wearable devices, including a wristband, smart sunglasses, and a ring, demonstrating its mechanical conformability and integration capability on wearable platforms. This work offers an effective strategy for integrating brittle wide-bandgap semiconductors into flexible devices and advances wearable solar-blind UV sensing technologies.

items.title: FlashCodec: Unleash All Decoding Resources for Low-Latency Video Decoding in MLLM Inference
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly support video understanding workloads, where video decoding constitutes a substantial portion of end-to-end inference latency, as raw video streams must be decoded into pixel frames before model processing. However, existing frameworks fail to effectively leverage abundant decoding resources (e.g., CPUs and NVDECs) to minimize per-video decoding latency while maintaining high throughput. As a result, video decoding becomes a dominant contributor to the Time-To-First-Token (TTFT). This inefficiency arises from inter-frame dependency constraints in video decoding, device-level heterogeneity between CPU and GPU, and intrinsic limitations of decoding resources themselves, along with GPU resource contention with co-located MLLM inference, collectively limiting effective resource utilization. In this paper, we present FlashCodec, a video decoding framework designed to effectively utilize heterogeneous decoding resources for low-latency, high-throughput video decoding. FlashCodec introduces: (1) a dependency-isolated GOP-level scheduling scheme that enables parallelism without redundant decoding; (2) a runtime adaptive scheduler that dynamically assigns GOPs to heterogeneous decoders without pre-allocation, guided by device characteristics to maximize utilization; and (3) an SM-light decoding pipeline that minimizes reliance on GPU SMs, reducing interference under co-located inference. Together, these techniques enable efficient and low-latency video decoding for latency-critical online MLLM inference. Experiments across a wide range of codecs and GPU servers show that FlashCodec achieves 6.8–25.7 × decoding speedup over out-of-the-box implementations with over 90% peak efficiency, surpasses static chunking parallelization strategies 2.7-7.0 × in latency and 2.6-9.8 × in throughput, incurs minimal overhead when co-located with MLLM services, and enables up to 7.1 × stricter TTFT SLOs in end-to-end inference.

items.title: Ferroelectric Polarization Dynamics of HZO FeCAPs at a Verified Subnanosecond Time Scale
items.abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM) based on the ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) offers a promising solution for next-generation embedded memory. In this Letter, we demonstrate subnanosecond ferroelectric polarization dynamics in HZO FeCAPs using an RF-compatible structure. By simultaneously measuring the electrode voltage and transient current under subnanosecond pulsing, we directly observe polarization dynamics with a temporal resolution below 100 ps. Our results demonstrate subnanosecond switching under directly monitored TE pulses with voltage amplitudes of 5 V in 8 nm-thick HZO capacitors with an area of 16 μm2. We also map switching kinetics for sub-10 ns pulse widths using this methodology. We further correlate polarization obtained from the dynamic current transient with the results from the postpulse readout scheme. Motivated by dynamic random-access-memory (DRAM) latency targets, these results establish a device-level benchmark for delivered subnanosecond switching in HZO FeCAPs and, together with a simplified nucleation-limited switching (NLS) analysis, define an effective ultrafast switching window for FeCAP evaluation.

items.title: Evaluating generative AI for dimensionally correct and manufacturable CAD models
items.abstract: Generative AI now writes Computer-Aided Design (CAD) programs and boundary representations; however, the output that executes or resembles a target need not be dimensionally correct, constrained, or manufacturable. This review asks what evidence supports the engineering validity of generated parametric CAD. Journal articles from 2022 to 2026 were retrieved from OpenAIRE and Crossref, and records outside design geometry were removed. A bibliometric map of 60 articles was combined with manual coding of 19 core studies against a six-rung validation ladder, technical appraisal of ten full texts, and a structured synthesis of 14 matched contrasts. Output rose from three articles in 2022 to 2023 to 50 in 2025 and the partial year 2026, and mentions of feedback loops more than tripled in 2026. Of the coded studies, 14 reported shape fidelity and 10 execution success, but only 3 checked dimensions or explicit constraints, none reported functional analysis, and one measured a manufactured part. Three of six appraised studies with shape metrics normalized scale away. Feedback from interpreters, kernels, or a rule monitor raised execution or validity by 3.9 to 19.4 percentage points, but none was compared with resampling under an equal budget, and shape fidelity fell in four of five contrasts. The highest correction rates, 32.6 to 36.9 points, came from runs two thirds of which carried author-injected defects, certified by the monitor supplying the feedback. No study held out part families. Generative CAD has learned to produce valid programs; evidence that it satisfies engineering requirements remains thin.
items.venue: Journal of Engineering and High Technology

items.title: Energy-Efficient In-Memory Computing with Non-Volatile N-ary Spintronic Crossbar Arrays for Sustainable AI
items.abstract: The electricity consumed by artificial-intelligence (AI) workloads is becoming a major sustainability concern, and a large share of it is wasted not on computation itself but on the constant shuttling of data between the physically separated processing and memory units of conventional von Neumann computers, the so-called memory wall. In-memory computing (IMC), which performs the computation directly inside an analog memory array where the data already reside, removes this energy bottleneck and is one of the most promising routes to sustainable AI hardware. Its energy efficiency, however, hinges critically on the memory device. The ideal cell would be non-volatile, so that the stored neural-network weights consume zero static power and survive power-down with no need for refresh, while also being CMOS-compatible for cheap integration and offering many evenly spaced conductance levels for dense, high-precision analog encoding. Here we show that spintronics, the branch of electronics that exploits the electron’s intrinsic magnetic moment (its spin) rather than only its charge, supplies exactly such a device. Our cell is a multi-state magnetic tunnel junction (M2TJ): two ferromagnetic layers shaped as crossing ellipses are separated by a thin insulating barrier, and the relative orientation of their magnetizations sets the quantum-mechanical tunneling resistance. Because magnetic shape anisotropy pins each ellipse’s magnetization along its long axis, the junction settles into several discrete, well-defined, and naturally equidistant resistance states that persist without power. This combination of non-volatility, CMOS compatibility, and intrinsically equidistant levels makes M2TJs ideal n-ary (multi-level) building blocks for neuromorphic IMC, in which each cell stores a multibit synaptic weight, complementing other emerging multilevel routes such as ferroelectric-FET crossbars. We present a simulation framework for multibit neural-network inference on n-ary crossbar arrays, developed for spintronic M2TJs but generalizable to any multistate memristive device. The framework retrieves the matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) result from the measured analog output with minimal assumptions, letting the crossbar act as a standalone AI co-processor placed where the data are generated: analog data from a camera or sensor enter the array directly as row voltages, cell currents sum along the columns by Ohm’s law, and threshold-sensing circuitry reads the outputs and feeds the next inference layer. Using simulated 4×4 arrays of 4-state M2TJs, we demonstrate successful inference on the XOR task and on MNIST handwritten-digit classification, reaching 94.48% accuracy against a 97.56% software baseline; principal-component-analysis (PCA) dimensionality reduction narrows this gap to 2.79%. A systematic error analysis identifies weight quantization as the dominant error source. We further study systematic nonidealities shared by all cells and cell-specific random noise. Critically, cell-specific noise is less detrimental than systematic nonidealities of equal amplitude, thanks to beneficial averaging across the array: the root-mean-square error scales as the square root of the number of columns while the signal-to-noise ratio grows only logarithmically, favoring wide crossbar geometries. Finally, we show that an optimal number of resistance states Nopt minimizes the total MVM error by trading quantization error against state resolution, with Nopt decreasing in noisier device environments, a direct design rule linking magnetic-device quality to achievable system accuracy. By turning the unique magnetic, non-volatile, and multilevel character of crossed-ellipse junctions into accurate analog computation, this work positions n-ary spintronic crossbars as a concrete, energy-efficient hardware substrate for the sustainable AI that future materials-for-sustainability applications, from autonomous edge sensors to renewable-energy management, will demand.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Emerging opportunities in layered transition metal dichalcogenides for chemiresistive gas sensing via structural and surface chemistry modulation
items.abstract: Abstract Among two-dimensional (2D) layered materials, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) constitute a versatile class exhibiting rich electronic diversity beyond the semi-metallic nature of carbon materials. Depending on their composition and polymorphs, TMDs span semiconductors, metals, semimetals, and superconductors. Their properties can be precisely tailored by engineering a layered structure, stacking sequence control, and surface modifications, making them highly attractive for chemiresistive gas sensing. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of TMD materials, with strong emphasis on correlating sensing behavior with their structural features, synthesis strategies, and morphology control. Further, various advances in synthesis methods, including exfoliation, chemical vapor deposition, wet-chemical techniques, and physical vapor deposition, are discussed. Structural engineering strategies are addressed systematically through defect creation, heterostructure formation, doping, surface functionalization, porosity, and photoactivation, which enhance gas adsorption and charge transfer processes, thereby amplifying the sensing response. Finally, the current technological challenges remain for 2D TMDs-based chemiresistive devices regarding stability, large-scale synthesis, and integration with practical platforms. Emerging opportunities for combining TMDs with flexible electronics, advanced nanostructures, and intelligent signal processing frameworks are also discussed, paving the way toward their deployment in next-generation, energy-efficient gas sensors.

items.title: Dasheng: LLM-powered Reliability Engineering Assistant for Cloud Overlay Networks
items.abstract: Amid mounting incidents of network failures, cloud service providers are placing increasing emphasis on reliability engineering. Leveraging their capabilities in text understanding and reasoning, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated to assist conventional cloud network reliability tools. However, deploying an LLM-powered reliability engineering assistant to cloud overlay networks is significantly challenging due to the scale, complexity, and intricate couplings of cloud overlay network components. In this work, we present Dasheng, an LLM-powered reliability engineering assistant for cloud overlay networks. Dasheng extends the standard assistant paradigm with an iterative, multi-step tool interaction mechanism to fit the characteristics of cloud overlay networks. Dasheng has been deployed on a production cloud for two years. To date, it has been used by 1,450 engineers for approximately 70k invocations. Most Dasheng invocations complete within 3-100 seconds, and reduce case resolution time by up to 97%. In 92% of evaluated cases, Dasheng produces useful outputs that materially assist engineers.

items.title: Client-side brute force attack detection leveraging large language models
items.abstract: For email authentication systems, the last mile of authentication poses a critical security challenge, as attackers leverage known, real logins to bypass established server-side protections against brute-force attacks and credential stuffing. Traditional methods like rate limiting and threshold anomaly detection are ineffective against distributed, stealthy attacks that mimic normal user activity. This paper proposes a novel framework for detecting authentication sequences on the client side by leveraging lightweight Large Language Models (LLMs) in real time. Unlike signature-based approaches, the proposed framework can "explain" the temporal and contextual characteristics of login behavior and detect anomalous sequences, such as high-frequency bursts and low-and-slow last-mile reassembly attacks, without the need for predefined signatures or centralized log aggregation. The framework was tested with 2.5 million authentication sessions, 1 million of which were marked as attacks, and achieved 98.4% attack-detection accuracy with a false-positive rate of 1.2%. With an average response time of 180 ms, it achieves near real-time inference without impacting the user experience. The system was live-deployed for six months and succeeded in blocking more than 1.2 million malicious logon attempts and safeguarding more than 850,000 user accounts against traditional baselines in both scale and precision. The results demonstrate the promise of lightweight, client-side LLMs as a privacy-safe, low-resource, and robust solution for last-mile email authentication security against current and future brute force attack vectors.

items.title: CacheSched: Efficient LLM Request Scheduling for Hierarchical Prefix Caching
items.abstract: Stateful Large Language Model (LLM) applications heavily rely on prefix caching to eliminate redundant prefill computations. To support massive concurrency, modern serving engines deploy hierarchical, multi-tier caches that offload less-active prefixes from limited GPU memory to spacious host DRAM. However, existing multi-worker request schedulers typically route traffic based solely on the longest prefix match, ignoring the highly heterogeneous data transfer costs between cache tiers. This oversight causes severe cluster-level load imbalance and triggers frequent GPU pipeline stalls as workers wait for slow host-to-device data transfers. To resolve these inefficiencies, we propose CacheSched, a scheduling system tailored for multi-worker LLM serving with hierarchical prefix caching. CacheSched is driven by a lightweight analytic performance model that estimates batch execution and data transfer times. Building on this model, CacheSched introduces two key mechanisms: (1) a heterogeneity-adaptive routing algorithm that dispatches requests based on predicted prefill costs, successfully balancing cache tier locality with cluster-wide worker load, and (2) a dynamic batch-matching algorithm at the worker level, which restricts host-memory prefix loads to the predicted compute window of the active batch, reducing GPU pipeline stalls. Evaluations demonstrate that CacheSched increases overall serving throughput by up to 2.58 × compared to state-of-the-art systems while satisfying strict Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) Service-Level Objectives (SLOs).

items.title: Brain Cognition-Inspired Adaptable LLM Agents for Continuous Knowledge Reuse Across Tasks in IoT
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are promising in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, existing agent systems suffer from an ephemeral limitation: agents are instantiated for individual tasks and terminated upon completion, losing valuable execution experiences across different tasks where past knowledge reuse is impossible. Inspired by dual-process theory in cognitive science, we propose a brain cognition-inspired dual-system agent framework for continuous knowledge reuse across heterogeneous task streams, termed the cognition-inspired dual-system agent framework for continuous knowledge reuse (CIA-CKR). The CIA-CKR framework separates fast (reactive execution) from slow (deliberative planning) cognition phases by maintaining a persistent knowledge base throughout the operational lifetime of agents. Two synergistic mechanisms are designed that mirror bidirectional knowledge flow in human cognition: a personalized agent generation mechanism that retrieves task-relevant knowledge and configures context-specific agent capabilities through top-down adaptation, and a knowledge accumulation mechanism that extracts experiential insights from execution traces through bottom-up feedback. Extensive experiments on HomeBench (smart home control) and OmniEAR (embodied multiagent collaboration) datasets demonstrate that CIA-CKR consistently outperforms both vanilla LLMs and recent memory-augmented methods, achieving 10.82% and 4.23% average accuracy improvements on HomeBench and OmniEAR, respectively, over the best baselines.

items.title: Axon: Asynchronous Global KV-Aware Scheduling Across Distributed Instances for Agentic Workloads
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) applications are increasingly moving toward agentic workflows, where models interact with users and tools over many turns, causing context lengths to dominate sequence composition and accumulate across dozens of turns. Existing serving systems fail to address this setting because they often overlook the reuse of KV caches across distributed instances within a cluster. We present Axon, an asynchronous global serving architecture that treats distributed GPU HBM as a unified KV cache resource pool for multi-turn agentic workloads. Axon introduces Asymmetric Query Context Parallelism to distribute attention over context shards across instances by communicating only query tensors, eliminating the synchronization bubbles and heavy KV traffic of conventional sequence-parallel designs. Its fully asynchronous scheduler decouples new-request allocation, KV cache restoration, and batch preparation from GPU execution, leveraging aggregated PCIe bandwidth to restore missing fragments in parallel, while a context-locality-aware scheduling policy jointly optimizes cache hit ratio and per-instance load. Evaluation on production agent traces shows that Axon reduces prefill latency by up to 4.14 × , decode latency by 1.87 × , and end-to-end latency by 2.27 × compared to existing systems.

items.title: Aqua Llama: Enhancing Operational Technology System Reliability Through Semantic-Aware Early Threat Detection
items.abstract: Maintaining the reliability and availability of operational technology (OT) systems is critical, as anomalous behaviors (protocol violations, abnormal command patterns, and timing deviations) can propagate into safety hazards, equipment damage, or unplanned shutdowns. From a reliability engineering perspective, this study proposes a semantics-first, edge-deployable anomaly detection framework that significantly enhances OT operational safety and failure prevention capabilities. The framework addresses OT-specific constraints (heterogeneous protocols, limited labeled data, strict auditability, and resource-constrained hardware) through three synergistic components: 1) traffic compression into concise, human-readable tokens capturing operational semantics; 2) domain knowledge encoded as editable plain-language rules enabling rapid site-specific adaptation; and 3) a four-step large language model (LLM) reasoning chain that remains short and auditable on CPU-only edges. Using an open-weight, LoRA-adapted 7B LLM without cloud dependencies, Aqua Llama separates a real-time symbolic alert path (CPS-Stream tokenization and natural semantic protocol analysis (NSPA) rule evaluation, operating at millisecond-level latency) from an LLM-assisted explanation path driven by the summarisation-aided logic chain (SALC), whose prompt-construction, prefill, and decoding costs are reported explicitly rather than folded into a single end-to-end figure. Validation across secure water treatment, Modbus, and ToN-IoT datasets yields a macro $F1$ of 0.928, with the strongest gains on subtle multicue anomalies that traditional threshold-based methods miss. Longitudinal evaluation shows an early detection rate (EDR) of 98.5% and a trace-based preventive action effectiveness (PAE) of 91.9%, while the auditable reasoning chain provides operators with traceable explanations, reducing diagnostic time and supporting risk-informed decisions essential for safety-critical OT reliability management.

items.title: A highly reliable, self-healing photovoltaic cell-level dynamic reconfigurable architecture based on software-defined energy flow management
items.abstract: Traditional crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules employ irreversible laminated packaging. Once individual cells fail or become obstructed, the entire string’s output power declines significantly, and repairs cannot be made without damaging the module—this constitutes a fundamental limitation of “static packaging.” This paper proposes a cell-level dynamic reconfigurable photovoltaic architecture that encapsulates each cell as a standardized “power generation cell,” integrating chip-level power optimizers, microfluidic active cooling systems, and high-speed industrial communication networks. Through a matrix backplate, the system enables online hot-swapping of cells and millisecond-scale electrical reconfiguration. This architecture redefines photovoltaic systems from static “power panels” into self-healing energy networks with physically maintainable components and software-defined energy pathways. A joint electrical-informatics-reliability simulation model was developed, comparing the proposed architecture with traditional modules under local failures, non-uniform shading, and long-term degradation conditions using Python simulations. Results demonstrate that during single-cell failure, the proposed architecture isolates the faulty cell and switches to backup cells within 5 ms, achieving power loss below 2%; over a 25-year lifecycle, the system’s rated output availability approaches 100%, whereas traditional modules show annual declines to approximately 82%. Active liquid cooling maintains cell temperatures at 45 ± 2 °C, thereby substantially reducing thermal hotspot risks under the simulated conditions. This study establishes a novel system paradigm and quantitative benchmark for next-generation high-reliability, intelligent photovoltaic power systems. The reported performance metrics are derived from numerical simulation; experimental validation through hardware-in-the-loop testing and outdoor prototyping remains necessary and is outlined as future work.

items.title: A bibliometric review, systematic evidence synthesis, and structured quantitative synthesis of retrieval-augmented and agentic large language models for software repair
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) now generate patches, call tools, retrieve context, and iterate on test feedback, yet published gains are usually reported as counts of patches that pass a test suite on public benchmarks. This review asks whether retrieval-augmented and agentic designs yield more independently correct repairs at comparable cost. Journal articles issued from 2022 to 2026 were retrieved from the OpenAIRE Graph and Crossref with the full Boolean string, supplemented by title screening where abstracts were unavailable. A three-layer design combined a bibliometric map of 151 articles, an abstract-level evidence map and technical appraisal of 67 core empirical studies (11 in full text), and a structured synthesis of matched within-study contrasts. Output grew from 19 articles in 2024 to 83 in 2026, concentrated in five software engineering venues. Coupling analysis separated learning-based repair, agentic repository-level repair, and patch-validity research, with weak modularity indicating a shared intellectual base dominated by Defects4J. Agents, retrieval, and repository-level tasks rose sharply between 2024-2025 and 2026, whereas attention to contamination and patch correctness stayed flat. Only 11% of core abstracts mentioned the plausible versus correct distinction and 11% addressed contamination. Seven studies yielded ten matched contrasts; the nine with magnitudes showed relative gains of 6% to 56%, but none reported paired discordant outcomes or variances, so no pooled estimate was defensible. Memorization and production evidence indicate that benchmark gains overstate deployable correctness. The review proposes a minimum reporting set built on paired per-bug outcomes, budget parity, independent oracles, and contamination audits.
items.venue: Journal of Engineering and High Technology

items.title: A Verified Guess Is Not a Reversed Fact: What Test-Time Thinking Repairs in the Latent Generalization of Fine-Tuned Knowledge, Why Its Gains Follow the Forward Paths a Query Leaves Open, and the Candidate-Pool Controls That Would Separate Inversion From Search
items.abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research A language model fine-tuned on new facts often cannot use them the way it uses the same facts placed in its context: it fails to answer reversed questions and to chain two trained facts into a conclusion. A 2026 study trained a reasoning model with reinforcement learning to think over its own fine-tuned knowledge, reported that thinking repairs many of these failures and transfers to knowledge on which no reinforcement learning was run, and found one exception: pure reversals, where thinking does not invert a stored fact but reaches above-chance accuracy by proposing candidates and checking each in the trained direction. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the exception is the rule seen from its other side. Test-time thinking can traverse an association only in the direction in which it was stored, so its gains track whether the query leaves a forward path to the answer. On the author's arithmetic from the study's own figure, thinking closes 56 to 88 percent of the gap between fine-tuning and in-context learning on the three holdouts where such a path exists, and 10 to 31 percent on the two where the answer can be reached only through a reverse key. Where no path exists, a reasoning model can still turn inversion into search, but search succeeds only as far as three things allow: a candidate pool small and salient enough to enumerate, coverage of that pool within the trace, and a verifier that does not accept wrong candidates. The published record bears on each: verification of facts is learned before generation, yet it can affirm both an old and a new answer, and longer reasoning raises hallucination when it raises the attempt rate. The paper consolidates the measured values in Table 1 and Figure 1, states the decision structure as Algorithm 1, and specifies the pool-size, direction-swap and oracle-verifier controls that would separate inversion from search.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A Resistive Random‐Access Memory With Reduced Current–Voltage Nonlinearity for Reliable Analog Vector–Matrix Multiplication
items.abstract: Suppressing current–voltage ( I – V ) nonlinearity in resistive random‐access memory (RRAM) is essential for minimizing computational errors in hardware neural networks. In this study, we propose a Pt/Al/TiO x /Al 2 O 3 /AlN/Pt RRAM with reduced nonlinearity in both high‐ and low‐resistance states (HRS and LRS). While the fabricated device maintains reliable multilevel memory characteristics, including pulse endurance over 6 × 10 5 individual programming pulses and multilevel retention for 10 5 s at 120 °C, it exhibits enhanced linearity within the analog read voltage range owing to trap‐assisted tunneling in the HRS and ohmic behavior in the LRS. Extended to the array level, the impact of the proposed device on analog vector–matrix multiplication (VMM) operations was experimentally measured. By incorporating the measurement data into system‐level simulations of fully‐connected network and VGGNet‐11 architectures, the hardware system achieved performance close to the ideal software baseline. Furthermore, comparative simulations based on different conduction mechanisms demonstrate the importance of device I – V linearity for accurate VMM operations. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed device for reliable hardware neural‐network implementation.

items.title: A High-Robustness Surrogate Modeling Method for On-Chip Microwave Passive Components in Chiplet-Based IoT Integrated Microsystem
items.abstract: In this article, a novel surrogate modeling method applied to 3-D on-chip microwave passive devices for Internet of Things (IoT) applications, which is based on barycentric form transfer functions combined with artificial neural networks (ANNs), is proposed. Among them, this work presents a transfer function parameter extraction algorithm named the set support point adaptive Antoulas–Anderson (SSP-AAA) algorithm, which avoids the problem of ill-conditioned matrices by optimizing the sequence of support points using a dual criterion based on error and condition number. At the same time, the dimension of the training data was reduced through the set-value strategy. During the model training process, the EM behavior was initially approximated into a transfer function representation through the SSP-AAA algorithm, followed by employing the ANN to establish the mapping relationship between geometric variations and transfer function coefficients. Compared with surrogate modeling based on vector fitting, this method effectively improves the stability of parameter extraction by imposing constraints on the condition number of the Loewner matrix. The test results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves training errors of 2.86%, 1.49%, and 2.98% and test errors of 3.54%, 2.06%, and 3.36% on three different microwave components, respectively, while maintaining stable coefficient extraction even under wide geometric sampling ranges.

items.title: When AI Agents Should Repair, Replan, or Abandon: A Threshold Theory of Plan Commitment
items.abstract: AI agents often discover mid-execution that their plan is broken, for example when an action fails or a tool is withdrawn. Deployed systems use conventions such as retry loops or "always replan," and a recent benchmark finds no fixed strategy dominates. This paper derives the optimal policy. In the model, a disruption destroys the causal support of part of a plan; repair is a partial reset that preserves the plan's structure, replanning is a full reset, and changing a plan is costly because others have conditioned on it. The optimal policy is a threshold in effective disruption depth: repair shallow damage, replan after deep damage, and abandon the goal when even a fresh plan is not worth its cost. Depth depends on plan structure. In expectation, a single broken action forces 1+R(G)/n actions to be revalidated, where R(G) counts the pairs of actions joined by a dependency path; to first order, a fully serial plan switches to replanning at raw damage about w times smaller than a plan of w parallel chains. A closed-form stability-price threshold determines when a worse repaired plan should be kept over a better fresh one. As language-model planners push replanning costs toward zero, the stability price becomes the only force sustaining plan commitment. Under repeated disruptions, revision frictions make commitment hysteresis optimal: the agent keeps executing a plan it would never choose fresh, and each repair adds patch debt until the debt outweighs repair's cost advantage and the agent rebuilds. A value-of-diagnosis result states when measuring damage is worth its compute and shows that "always replan" is optimal when damage is predictably deep and replanning is the better fallback. A separately implemented numerical checker tests each proposition (zero violations; 1.6 million static-model evaluations), and the model's regime map reproduces that benchmark's regime flips qualitatively.

items.title: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
items.abstract: Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. On the Norwegian North Sea benchmark, GeoLog-Agent achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.9307 and a peak $R^2$ of 0.9713. It exceeds the nine-baseline average $R^2$ of 0.8387 by 0.0920, with a 30.97% average RMSE reduction, and exceeds the strongest baseline by 0.0274--0.0498 in $R^2$, with 16.25%--24.05% lower RMSE. Ablations confirm the effectiveness and synergy of geological prior reasoning, multi-scale dilated generation, and conditional adversarial modules. Transferring the coupling mechanism to six conventional deep learning models improves their $R^2$ by 0.0162--0.0789 with cross-well stability. These results demonstrate how foundation-model domain reasoning can constrain deep generative reconstruction of missing petrophysical measurements.

items.title: Data-Driven Heuristic-Guided Business Process Redesign
items.abstract: Business process redesign (BPR) has a long-standing catalog of best-practice redesign heuristics, yet, applying them remains a mostly manual task that requires extensive domain knowledge. Despite recent advances using Large Language Models (LLMs) for conversational process model redesign, limitations remain. For example, redesign is user-driven instead of data-driven and is not guided by best practices such as the redesign heuristics. Moreover, only one change can be handled at a time. To address these limitations, given an event log and a BPMN model, we present the DH-BPR framework to realize data-driven heuristic-guided BPR using LLMs. To design DH-BPR, we first conducted an analysis of which redesign heuristics can be automatically detected and applied given information contained in an event log such as the fraction of cases that bypass an activity. Based on this, DH-BPR detects and validates heuristic candidates through a combination of rule-based techniques and an LLM. After that, DH-BPR jointly designs and records an application plan for valid candidates, before finally yielding a redesigned BPMN model and an updated resource model (the way resources execute the process). Evaluation based on simulation using a synthetic benchmark and two real-world event logs shows that the framework's redesign reduces the mean case completion time by up to 61.5%.

items.title: Learning from Mutants: Teaching Small Language Models to Synthesise Loop Invariants
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have proven promising for synthesising loop invariants, a long-standing obstacle to automated program verification. Yet, frontier LLMs are typically accessible only through third-party APIs, hampering reproducibility and local deployment. Small language models (SLMs) sidestep these obstacles but require task-specific fine-tuning, for which high-quality training data is needed.
