Finally, we demonstrate that the same representation-level insights also enable a lightweight defense that mitigates pretrain-to-finetune jailbreak transfer while preserving downstream utility.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Not Just for Tech Giants: The Economic Payoff of LLM‐Measured AI Adoption in Nontechnology Firms
items.abstract: Technology firms dominate AI narratives, but the economic implications of AI in traditional industries remain underexplored. We develop a firm‐level AI adoption indicator using ERNIE, a Chinese large language model. Using this measure, we find that AI adoption significantly enhances the value of nontechnology firms. Mechanism analyses show that AI adoption improves productivity, innovation performance and financing conditions. The effects are stronger for firms with greater dynamic capability, favourable information environments, competitive positions, larger size, private ownership and eastern regional locations. Our study provides evidence on the economic consequences of AI and a novel AI adoption measure for future research.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements to Hyperparameter Translation for Quantum Software via LLMs
items.abstract: Quantum software engineering (QSE) lacks validated approaches for translating natural-language non-functional requirements (NFRs) into execution parameters such as shots and transpiler optimization levels. Existing methods emphasize semantic similarity rather than execution outcomes. We evaluate seven large language models (LLMs) against a deterministic heuristic baseline using 540 synthetic and 18 real-world user stories. We assess semantic accuracy and execution outcomes, including time, cost, top-state probability, and two-qubit gate exposure, through Qiskit/Aer simulations. All LLMs significantly outperformed the heuristic in semantic accuracy, achieving 55.6 to 83.3 percent on real-world stories compared to 16.7 percent for the heuristic. However, no LLM demonstrated statistically significant superiority over others on the real-world dataset. Speed- and cost-oriented configurations reduced execution time and cost, but fidelity improvements were not supported. Some failures resulted from provider safety refusals rather than translation errors. Our findings demonstrate the potential of LLMs as middleware for NFR-to-configuration translation in QSE, while emphasizing execution-based validation, human oversight, and careful interpretation of model differences.

items.title: Noise-Adaptive Analog-Digital Preconditioning
items.abstract: Analog in-memory computing offers the potential to accelerate approximate inverse preconditioning, but hardware errors can degrade preconditioners designed in digital arithmetic. We develop an analog-digital preconditioner for symmetric positive-definite linear systems that combines analog block Jacobi with a small digital low-rank residual correction. The correction space is constructed by probing the same programmed analog arrays used in the solve, targeting errors from both the coupling omitted by block Jacobi and persistent hardware perturbations. Under a random linear-operator model, we separate the programmed-mean error from fresh read fluctuations, distinguish the effects of copy averaging and repeated reads, and quantify the sampling accuracy of columnwise probing. Under a centered additive write-noise model, we also derive a computable regularization threshold and identify the approximation error introduced by the regularization shift. Experiments with an analog hardware simulator show that programming errors can change the directions that block Jacobi reduces poorly. In the tested comparisons with significant programming errors, learning the correction space from the programmed copies reduces FGMRES iteration counts relative to construction from digital block Jacobi.

items.title: Negative Capacitance Gate‐All‐Around Nanosheet FET for Low Power Application
items.abstract: Real-world silicon-based field-effect transistors (FETs) are severely constrained by short-channel effects, leakage currents, and scaling voltage at sub-10-nm technology nodes due to the growing demand of small, powerful, and energy-efficient electronic devices. This paper is based on the consideration that the assumption of gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet FETs to deal with these limitations results in the development of a negative capacitance gate-all-around nanosheet FET (NC-GAA NS-FET). Such gadgets show subthreshold swings (SS) beneath the thermionic limit of 60 mV/dec with the internal voltage-enhancement offered by ferroelectric materials such as lead zirconate titanate (PZT). This will make it possible to switch faster and consume less power. GAA nanosheet architecture has more electrostatic control of the channel than FinFETs and nanowire FETs, which significantly diminishes short-channel effects and increases current drivability. Simulation studies through Landau–Khalatnikov (L-K) modelling and technology-computeraided design (TCAD) confirm that NC-GAA NS-FETs present excellent scaling to sub-5-nm nodes, greater drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL), or improved on/ off current ratios. Neural network-based and compact designs are also known as circuit-level integration. The metal work, dielectric characteristics, gate length, and nanosheet thickness are critical factors of design whose optimization is required to optimize performance and reliability. The study indicates that NC-GAA NS-FETs are a concrete approach to sustaining Moore's law and to enable next-generation low-power VLSI circuits. However, material stability, hysteresis, and proper matching capacitance must be fixed. The only way out of these limitations is to further develop materials engineering and device modelling studies to maximize the potential of NC-based nanoscale transistors.

items.title: Nb2O5 Interlayer Engineering for Switchable Polarization and Tunneling Electroresistance in HZO-Based Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions
items.abstract: Abstract Hf1–xZrxO2 (HZO)-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) enable polarization-controlled resistance switching at nanometer-scale thicknesses, offering potential for nonvolatile memory and multilevel conductance operation. In metal–ferroelectric–insulator–ferroelectric–metal (MFIFM) structures, highly insulating interlayers such as Al2O3 can suppress leakage at the expense of switchable polarization and low-resistance-state (LRS) transport. Here, Nb2O5 is explored as an alternative interlayer with a relatively low electron-transport barrier, and Al2O3- and Nb2O5-inserted MFIFM FTJs with identical HZO layer thicknesses and total dielectric-stack thicknesses are directly compared. Replacing Al2O3 with Nb2O5 increases the positive-up–negative-down (PUND)-derived 2Pr from 17.2 to 27.4 μC/cm2, accompanied by a higher fitted orthorhombic-phase contribution and a higher out-of-plane texture index. The Nb2O5-inserted device also exhibits a higher tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio than its Al2O3-inserted counterpart (60 vs 36 at a read voltage of 1.2 V), accompanied by a larger relative increase in LRS current than in high-resistance-state (HRS) current. The Nb2O5-inserted device further exhibits a higher breakdown voltage than the Al2O3-inserted counterpart, maintains distinguishable polarization states up to approximately 107 switching cycles, and demonstrates repeatable overall multilevel conductance-update behavior over 20 consecutive cycles, despite variations in individual intermediate conductance levels. These results establish interlayer selection as an effective strategy for modulating switchable polarization, resistance-state transport, and electrical reliability in HZO-based MFIFM FTJs.

items.title: NVBleed: Covert and Side-Channel Attacks on NVIDIA Multi-GPU Interconnect
items.abstract: Multi-GPU systems are becoming increasingly important in high-performance computing (HPC) and cloud infrastructure, providing acceleration for data-intensive applications, including machine learning workloads. These systems consist of multiple GPUs interconnected through high-speed networking links such as NVIDIA's NVLink. In this work, we explore whether the interconnect on such systems presents a source of leakage, enabling new forms of covert and side-channel attacks. Specifically, we reverse-engineer the operations of NVLink-V1, V2, and V3 and identify two primary leakage sources: timing variations caused by contention and performance counters that reveal communication patterns. The leakage sources are visible from a remote GPU, enabling potentially dangerous attacks. We further validate their presence across three generations of NVLink, as well as on AMD and NVIDIA multi-GPU configurations connected via PCIe. Building on these observations, we develop contention-based covert-channel attacks across two GPUs, achieving a bandwidth of over 70 kbps with an error rate of 4.78% for the contention channel. We also develop two end-to-end side-channel attacks: application fingerprinting (including 18 high-performance computing and deep learning applications) and 3D graphics character identification within Blender, a multi-GPU rendering application. These attacks are highly effective, achieving F1 scores of up to 96.77% and 86.86%, respectively. We also discover that leakage surprisingly occurs across virtual machines on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and demonstrate a side-channel attack on Blender, achieving F1 scores exceeding 88%. We also explore defenses against cross-VM attacks by adding differential privacy noise to obscure side-channel leakage.

items.title: Monolayer MoSe2 as an Attenuator of Spintronic Terahertz Emission
items.abstract: Understanding ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion at ferromagnetic/2D interfaces is critical for developing THz-frequency spintronic devices such as ultrafast memories, sensors, and compact THz sources. We investigate this by studying spintronic THz emission (STE) from Py/Au heterostructures capped with transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayer MoSe2 using time-domain THz spectroscopy. We observe a pronounced reduction in emitted THz amplitude when a monolayer MoSe2 flake covers Py/Au or Py/Pt emitters compared with uncovered regions. A consistent, approximately fourfold attenuation occurs for both systems, despite an order-of-magnitude larger THz radiation from the bare Py/Pt emitter. These results indicate that the suppression is independent of emitter strength. We attribute the attenuation to THz absorption by free charge carriers and trions that are either present due to charge transfer from the metallic layer or photoexcited by the laser pulse, which can significantly diminish the detectable STE signal. This finding provides an explanation for the discrepancy between weak STE signals from FM/TMD heterostructures and magnetotransport reports of sizable spin-orbit torques in similar systems, and highlights the need to account for photoinduced THz attenuation when interpreting ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion measurements in 2D TMD heterostructures.

items.title: Mo/Multilayer graphene/SiN composite membranes with high EUV transmittance and mechanical robustness for EUV pellicles
items.abstract: Multilayer graphene (MLG) is a promising membrane material for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) pellicles because it combines high optical transparency with outstanding mechanical properties. However, practical implementation requires precise control of graphene thickness and uniformity while maintaining sufficient mechanical robustness. In this work, we demonstrate the controlled synthesis of few-layer MLG by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) using Ni and NiCu alloy catalysts and its integration into freestanding Mo/MLG/SiN composite membranes for EUV pellicle applications. The graphene thickness and uniformity were systematically tailored through catalyst composition and growth-condition optimization. Increasing the Cu content reduced the average graphene thickness from approximately eight to four layers while improving large-area thickness uniformity to below 5%, as confirmed by optical-contrast mapping and Raman spectroscopy. Transfer-matrix modeling predicted that a multilayer structure comprising an approximately 5 nm-thick MLG layer with ultrathin Mo and SiN capping layers can achieve an EUV transmittance exceeding 90% at a wavelength of 13.5 nm.Based on this design, freestanding Mo/MLG/SiN composite membranes were fabricated and evaluated by bulge testing. Increasing the MLG thickness enhanced the rupture pressure, rupture deflection, and ultimate tensile strength, while the Mo capping layer further improved fracture tolerance and overall mechanical reliability. These findings establish a practical design strategy for realizing mechanically robust and highly transparent EUV pellicles through precise control of graphene growth and multilayer membrane architecture.

items.title: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
items.abstract: Large foundation models are integrated into Computer Use Agents (CUAs), enabling autonomous interaction with operating systems through graphical user interfaces (GUIs) to perform complex tasks. This autonomy introduces serious security risks: malicious instructions or visual prompt injections can trigger unsafe reasoning and cause harmful system-level actions. Existing defenses, such as detection-based blocking, prevent damage but often abort tasks prematurely, reducing agent utility. In this paper, we present MirrorGuard, a plug-and-play defense framework that uses simulation-based training to improve CUA security in the real world. To reduce the cost of large-scale training in operating systems, we propose a novel neural-symbolic simulation pipeline, which generates realistic, high-risk GUI interaction trajectories entirely in a text-based simulated environment, which captures unsafe reasoning patterns and potential system hazards without executing real operations. In the simulation environment, MirrorGuard learns to intercept and rectify insecure reasoning chains of CUAs before they produce and execute unsafe actions. In real-world testing, extensive evaluations across diverse benchmarks and CUA architectures show that MirrorGuard significantly mitigates security risks. For instance, on the ByteDance UI-TARS system, it reduces the unsafe rate from 66.5% to 13.0% while maintaining a marginal false refusal rate (FRR). In contrast, the state-of-the-art GuardAgent only achieves a reduction to 53.9% and suffers from a 15.4% higher FRR. Our work proves that simulation-derived defenses can provide robust, real-world protection while maintaining the fundamental utility of the agent. Our code and model are publicly available at https://bmz-q-q.github.io/MirrorGuard/.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Meta-predictive ensembles of LLM pipelines for automated named entity recognition in aerospace software requirements
items.abstract: In safety-critical aerospace systems, errors in requirements engineering can lead to significant operational risks, which makes accurate information extraction essential. Named Entity Recognition (NER) plays a crucial role in this process by supporting tasks such as requirements classification and automated test case generation. Despite the emergence of diverse language model–based predictive pipelines across multiple domains for NER, the aerospace software development field has so far witnessed only limited exploration of the capabilities of foundational large language models (LLMs). This study investigates the effectiveness of foundational LLMs, recurrent architecture–enhanced LLMs, and generative models under domain-specific constraints. However, single-model approaches struggle with stability, domain shifts, and difficulty in capturing long-context dependencies, which motivates the need for more robust solutions. To address this, the study proposes a novel meta-predictive pipeline that integrates heterogeneous models for improved robustness. To develop a robust and precise meta predictor, it benchmarks the performance of 15 foundational LLMs, 30 recurrently enhanced LLMs, and 4 generative language models, including DeepSeek, ChatGPT, LLaMA, and Gemini. Finally, 12 distinct meta-predictors were developed based on foundational LLMs and recurrent architectures. The best performing meta predictor on the public AeroBERT-NER benchmark dataset achieved 94.73%, 93.59%, and 94.17% precision, recall, and F1-score, respectively. The key findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach to improve reliability and scalability in aerospace requirements engineering workflows.
items.venue: International Conference on Automated Software Engineering

items.title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
items.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance LLMs with external knowledge but introduce a critical attack surface: corpus poisoning. While recent studies have demonstrated the potential of such attacks, they typically rely on impractical assumptions, such as white-box access or known user queries, thereby underestimating the difficulty of real-world exploitation. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proposing MIRAGE, a novel multi-stage poisoning pipeline designed for strict black-box and query-agnostic environments. Operating on surrogate model feedback, MIRAGE functions as an automated optimization framework that integrates three key mechanisms: it utilizes persona-driven query synthesis to approximate latent user search distributions, employs semantic anchoring to imperceptibly embed these intents for high retrieval visibility, and leverages an adversarial variant of Test-Time Preference Optimization (TPO) to maximize persuasion. To rigorously evaluate this threat, we construct a new benchmark derived from three long-form, domain-specific datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIRAGE significantly outperforms existing baselines in both attack efficacy and stealthiness, exhibiting remarkable transferability across diverse retriever-LLM configurations and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense strategies.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs
items.abstract: Memory decides which LLMs an edge device runs, and how fast: capacity on a 4 GB Jetson Nano, bandwidth on an 8 GB Jetson Orin Nano Super. Deployed formats (GPTQ, AWQ, llama.cpp's K- and I-quants) spend equal bits on every integer code of a matrix, although the codes are far from uniform. LazyWeights keeps these formats but tunes GPTQ so the codes compress, Huffman-codes them losslessly in interleaved lanes, and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged and DRAM moves only coded bytes. At 1% and 3.5% perplexity budgets, coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B and SmolLM-1.7B are 5.7-31.4% smaller than the best llama.cpp format. A bit-exact 0.21 mm^2 ASIC decoder unit (1 GHz, 7 nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to 36% and 38% (54% and 44% with prompt-lookup speculation). On the Nano, LazyWeights needs 58-64% less time and 53-57% less energy per token than CPU llama.cpp, and runs a streamed Mistral-7B 6.6x faster at 3.89 bits per weight. A Huffman decoder beats an rANS decoder in rate and area at equal throughput; the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).

items.title: Kosmo-GFM: A Production-Ready Geometry Foundation Model
items.abstract: We present Kosmo-GFM, a scene reconstruction system that integrates a geometry foundation model (GFM), a pose optimization engine (PoseEngine), and reconstruction-derived supervision from KosmoWorld. GFM predicts camera parameters, depth, cross-view correspondences, and dynamic 3D points from images and videos. PoseEngine combines these predictions with geometric optimization to recover scene-level camera poses and geometry for downstream 3D and 4D Gaussian Splatting. KosmoWorld generates images and geometric supervision from reconstructed real-world scenes to improve GFM's geometric predictions. On the Sparse and Medium subsets of SpatialBench, GFM achieves the lowest absolute relative depth error and the highest relative-pose AUC at 5 degrees among the compared methods. It also achieves the lowest mean endpoint errors for dynamic points and scene flow across the five evaluated datasets. Across 34 scenes completed by all compared reconstruction systems, PoseEngine achieves the highest scene-averaged pose AUC at thresholds of 1, 3, and 5 degrees, with a cumulative runtime of 14.07 hours, approximately 20% of GLUEMAP's 69.67 hours. PoseEngine Flash provides a further accuracy-efficiency trade-off, with a measured mixed-precision runtime of 2.62 hours, approximately 4% of GLUEMAP's runtime. Separate scaling experiments show generally favorable trends with increased data, model computation, and training budgets. These results support the use of learned geometric priors within a scene-level reconstruction pipeline.

items.title: Input Serialization in Zero-Shot LLM Fault Diagnosis of Rooftop Units: A Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Nine Models
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for building fault diagnosis, but input representation is often changed alongside model adaptation or added knowledge. This study isolates serialization effects using matched rooftop unit measurements rendered as deterministic prose, fixed schema JSON, and JSON with a fixed evidence card covering all classes. Nine API models evaluated 240 windows from 39 source files in the public ORNL_RTU dataset across four diagnostic classes. Prompt development was separated from evaluation by season, and uncertainty was assessed at the source file level. Observed macro F1 differences between JSON and prose ranged from −0.082 to 0.029, and no model-specific contrast remained significant after Holm adjustment, which does not establish equivalence. Output validity nevertheless varied: JSON reduced the MiniMax invalid schema rate by 0.333, the evidence card increased Kimi diagnostic coverage by 0.508, and larger macro F1 changes coincided with changes in schema validity or abstention. Model condition macro F1 ranged from zero to 0.182, compared with 0.543 for a supervised Random Forest reference under seasonal holdout, so no evaluated zero-shot configuration is suitable for unattended fault classification. Diagnostic accuracy, schema validity, abstention, and name-level evidence grounding should therefore be evaluated jointly when selecting input representations.

items.title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
items.abstract: Users of artificial intelligence services, including those powered by large language models and other transformer-based models, need assurance that inference and training follow the declared computation without exposing private models or data. Zero-knowledge proofs can provide this assurance, but proof generation remains expensive. Hardware acceleration research often reports gains for individual cryptographic operations, leaving their effect on the full cost of proving neural-network workloads, particularly large transformer models, unclear. We introduce a four-layer framework linking verifiable AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels and hardware platforms, use it to review the literature, and add original measurements of six provers and seven kernels to identify which costs matter in practice. Our measurements show that the dominant cost changes with the proof system and input length. In low-rank fine-tuning, the cost of opening commitments to fixed model weights remains nearly constant across input lengths from 64 to 2048, while the work associated with intermediate values grows. A 13-billion-parameter fine-tuning configuration exceeds the capacity of a 40-gigabyte graphics processor but completes on an 80-gigabyte device, showing why capacity must be assessed alongside execution time. Our kernel profiling further identifies instruction issue and synchronization limits that a bandwidth-only model misses. We use these findings to assess graphics processors, reconfigurable logic, custom chips and existing artificial intelligence accelerators. The resulting research agenda connects proof-friendly numeric formats, reuse of fixed-weight commitments, heterogeneous execution and shared benchmarks to the measured bottlenecks. Effective acceleration requires selecting hardware and proof-system optimizations around the cost profile of the target workload.

items.title: Identification automatique de domaines de connaissances dans un dictionnaire universel du XVIIIe s.
items.abstract: On se propose de présenter les résultats d’une recherche visant à l’identification et à la classification automatique de domaines de connaissances dans un dictionnaire universel du XVIIIe siècle.L’œuvre support des analyses est l’édition de 1743 du Dictionnaire Universel François & Latin (désormais, DUFLT) dit de Trévoux. Environ 20 % des articles héberge un ou plusieurs paragraphes associés à une marque de domaine (Pétrequin 2009, Turcan 2024) qui stipule de quelle science (astronomie ...), art (poësie ... forge...) ou métier (charron ...) relève le contenu. On est loin de la systématicité de l’Encyclopédie de Diderot et d’Alembert (1751-1772) où 83% environ des articles est pourvu d’une marque de domaine (données tirées de l’ARTFL et de l’ENCCRE). Notre objectif est de parvenir à une classification complète de l’ensemble des paragraphes du dictionnaire en leur affectant un ou plusieurs domaines de connaissance. Pour ce faire, nous développons une approche combinant grands modèles de langage (LLMs) et modèles de classification supervisée. On soulignera que la classification en domaines de connaissances a déjà fait l’objet de plusieurs études computationnelles sur l’Encyclopédie de Diderot & d’Alembert (Horton et al. 2009, Roe et al. 2016, Brenon et al. 2022), mais qu’aucune n’a été conduite à ce jour sur le DUFLT.Dans une première partie, nous présenterons les choix méthodologiques qui structurent notre démarche. Nous justifierons le choix du paragraphe comme unité de base de nos analyses, le regroupement des marques de domaine (simples : en termes de géographie ...; complexes : Terme de Botanique & de Pharmacie) en un nombre restreint de « macro-domaines ». Nous aborderons également les difficultés liées à l’hétérogénéité de ces marques et à la nature parfois pluri-/inter-disciplinaire de leurs contenus.Dans une seconde partie, nous décrirons le protocole expérimental mis en œuvre. À partir d’un ensemble de paragraphes initialement pourvus d’une ou plusieurs marques de domaine (que l’on aura retirées), nous sollicitons différents LLMs dans un cadre de classification few-shot afin de leur faire associer un ou plusieurs macro-domaines. Les prédictions sont ensuite évaluées par comparaison avec les annotations existantes. Cette phase permet d’identifier les configurations de prompts et les modèles les plus performants, et d’affiner progressivement les instructions fournies aux modèles. Les résultats préliminaires montrent qu’un des modèles testés (Gemini 3.5 Flash) atteint un F-score proche de 70 % sur un jeu d’évaluation encore limité à une cinquantaine de paragraphes. L’extension de ce jeu de test constitue une étape importante afin d’obtenir une mesure plus robuste des performances.Le meilleur modèle sera ensuite appliqué à un ensemble de paragraphes dépourvus de marque de domaine. Les annotations produites feront l’objet d’une validation et d’une correction manuelle, permettant la constitution d’un corpus de référence (gold standard). Ce corpus servira à l’entraînement d’un modèle de classification supervisée fondé sur une architecture Transformer de type encodeur, mieux adaptée à un déploiement à grande échelle sur l’ensemble du dictionnaire.Nous montrerons que cette approche progressive, associant annotation assistée par LLM et apprentissage supervisé, permet non seulement d’améliorer la couverture de l’annotation thématique du DUFLT, mais aussi d’ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives pour l’étude de l’organisation des savoirs dans les dictionnaires encyclopédiques du XVIIIe siècle.

items.title: Hoss: Fast Oblivious Semantic Search with Heterogeneous GPU-CPU-TEE Architecture
items.abstract: Semantic search is widely deployed in modern AI systems, but protecting both data contents and access patterns remains challenging. The current state-of-the-art system, Compass, achieves oblivious semantic search by building an optimized ORAM over HNSW graphs. However, even with aggressive optimizations, it still incurs large overheads. Closing this performance gap is fundamentally difficult: Compass has already removed most cryptographic overheads, leaving ORAM accesses as the dominant cost, which are constrained by well-known Ω(log N ) bandwidth lower bounds. Our key insight is that traditional ORAM overhead stems from the assumption of limited private memory, whereas modern GPU TEEs provide large private memory (Pmem) that blinds internal access patterns ( Hunt et al., NSDI'23 ). This shift opens a new design space. We therefore propose Hoss, a first-of-its-kind oblivious semantic search system with a heterogeneous CPU–GPU TEE architecture that supports fast, scalable search with low cost of ownership. In Hoss, the GPU TEE's large Pmem hosts the hot-path HNSW traversal, while the lower layers of the graph, if exceeds GPU capacity, are offloaded to CPU TEEs. The system invokes oblivious primitives only when accessing these lower layers. The availability of large Pmem also enables new optimization opportunities. For example, Hoss features a host-access ORAM mechanism that goes beyond traditional performance constraints, and incorporates several data-dependent optimizations that are not possible in prior designs. We implement a prototype of Hoss and benchmark it against Compass. Our result shows that Hoss achieves up to 99× speedup while maintaining high recall, with larger gains at scale.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Heterogeneous Memristive Neuromorphic Computing with Physics-Aware Cross-Modal Attention for Energy-Efficient Multimodal Emotion Recognition
items.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) is a crucial technology for achieving emotional intelligence in human–computer interaction. However, the substantial computational demands of MER models currently overwhelm the capacities of resource-constrained edge devices. To address this problem, this paper proposes a Heterogeneous Memristive Neural Network for Multimodal Emotion Recognition. The proposed network adopts a hardware–algorithm co-design approach, in which different memristive devices are assigned to different modal processing tasks according to their physical characteristics. Specifically, highly stable filamentary memristors are utilized to construct deterministic feature extraction pathways for text and video, whereas highly plastic Phase-Change Memory (PCM) crossbar arrays are designed for audio encoding. Based on the high plasticity of PCM, a memristive cross-modal attention network is further designed to achieve dynamic and adaptive multimodal feature fusion. Furthermore, a collaborative weight update method is proposed. During weight updates, the inherent writing noise and conductance drift of PCM are utilized as hardware-level regularization and automatic sparse learning strategies. Simulation experiments conducted on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets using the MemTorch framework demonstrate that the proposed neural network maintains recognition accuracy comparable to GPU baseline models, even when accounting for device non-idealities. Overall, the proposed neural network effectively resolves the “performance–power” conflict when deploying high-performance MER models on resource-constrained edge devices, providing an efficient and stable neuromorphic computing solution for edge applications.

items.title: GaAs semiconductor opening switches grown by halide vapor phase epitaxy
items.abstract: Semiconductor opening switches (SOSs) are pulsed power components that enable high-power, high repetition rate switching with ns switching times, but require deep junctions that can be onerous to manufacture using diffusion methods. We demonstrate an 80 μm GaAs SOS diode with a ∼38 μm deep junction grown under 1 h by halide vapor phase epitaxy. Graded p-type doping was achieved using dimethylzinc, while the n-type background doping was utilized for the n-type side of the junction. The diode doping profile was characterized using electrochemical capacitance-voltage, and scanning Kelvin probe force microscopy was used to identify the shape and depth of the junction. Single and multiple diode stacks were processed and then characterized with a pulser circuit to evaluate their SOS performance. A six-diode stack generated a 2.5 kV pulse cutting off a peak current density of 6.8 kA/cm2. Circuit gain ranged from 6 to 11, decreasing with input bias. Rise time as low as 900 ps and repetition rates of 4 MHz were achieved. The choice of GaAs opens a new application space for SOS devices with narrow pulses and high repetition rates.

items.title: From Prompting to Multi-Agent AI: Controlled Generation of CEFR-Specific Language Learning Content
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to support content creation in digital language-learning environments; however, generating educational materials that consistently reflect different proficiency levels remains a challenge. This study investigates an orchestrated multi-agent AI architecture for generating language-learning content targeting different CEFR proficiency levels. The proposed architecture employs an orchestrator that routes content-generation requests to independently configured, level-specialized agents operating under predefined lexical, structural, and instructional requirements, without inter-agent collaboration or deliberation. To distinguish the effects of explicit level-specific constraints from those associated with agent-based orchestration, a controlled experiment compared three generation conditions using the same underlying large language model: conventional prompt-based (PB) generation, constrained prompting (CP), and multi-agent (MA) generation. CP incorporated the same core level-specific requirements and vocabulary resources as MA without employing agent-based orchestration. The three conditions were evaluated using 100 matched tasks across five intended CEFR levels (A1–C1), resulting in 300 generated stories. The outputs were assessed in terms of text length, lexical diversity, syntactic characteristics, and adherence to predefined generation constraints. Within MA, all six continuous linguistic measures showed significant differences across intended proficiency levels, although adjacent-level differentiation varied across linguistic dimensions. Across the three conditions, PB differed from CP and MA on several linguistic measures, whereas CP and MA exhibited greater similarity, with statistically significant differences in 12 of 30 planned comparisons. Both CP and MA achieved 100% adherence to the evaluated story-length, target-vocabulary-count, and comprehension-question-count requirements in the analyzed outputs. Overall, the findings suggest that explicit constraints and vocabulary resources contribute substantially to controlled proficiency-targeted generation, while the orchestrated multi-agent architecture provides modular organization and is associated with selected level-dependent linguistic differences rather than consistent superiority over CP. The study therefore focuses on controlled linguistic differentiation and operational constraint adherence, rather than independent validation of CEFR proficiency levels.

items.title: Flexible Low-Voltage Thin-Film Transistors for Logic Circuits and Neuromorphic Computing Applications
items.abstract: Flexible thin-film transistors (TFTs) operating at low voltage are key building blocks for next-generation wearable electronics and brain-inspired systems, yet simultaneously achieving low-voltage operation, environmental robustness and multifunctionality remains a great challenge. In this work, flexible indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) TFTs based on a solution-processed nanocomposite gate dielectric were fabricated, in which the introduced nanofiller effectively enhanced the capacitance, mechanical strength and moisture resistance of the polymer dielectric. The resulting devices exhibit an on/off ratio over 106 and can be fully turned on at a gate voltage below 1 V. After 2000 bending cycles, 90-day ambient aging and 3600 s continuous gate-bias stress, the threshold voltage and subthreshold swing show only slight drifts and the on/off ratio remains above 106, demonstrating outstanding mechanical durability, anti-aging capability and bias stability. On this basis, a logic inverter was constructed, which delivers a peak voltage gain of ~9 at a supply voltage of 2.5 V and realizes stable dynamic inversion for low-frequency square-wave signals. Owing to the tunable ion migration and electric double-layer polarization of the gate dielectric, the TFTs emulate typical biological synaptic behaviors, including pulse-dependent potentiation, long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). Neural network simulations based on device conductance states achieve accuracy of ~90% on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset and 88.1% on the challenging Stanford Cars vehicle dataset. This work verifies that the developed flexible TFTs possess dual functions of logic operation and neuromorphic computing, providing a feasible solution for the development of high-performance flexible low-power electronic devices and brain-inspired vision systems.

items.title: FlatSeek: LLM-Driven Symbolic Discovery of Flat Outputs via Backward Data Generation
items.abstract: Differential flatness enables efficient planning and control, but discovering explicit flat outputs for general nonlinear systems remains difficult due to the lack of general methods and supervised data. We propose FlatSeek, a framework combining backward data generation with task-specific large language model (LLM) training. By reversing the defining reconstruction of flatness, we generate system-flat-output pairs with known certificates, then fine-tune an LLM to propose symbolic flat-output candidates for unseen dynamics. On literature and synthetic benchmarks, FlatSeek outperforms both the traditional symbolic methods and the untuned reference models in flat-output discovery success, and uncovers alternative symbolic flat outputs not reported in the literature.

items.title: First-principles investigation of small polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO 3
items.abstract: Sodium niobate ( NaNbO 3 ) is a perovskite oxide and a key component of emerging lead-free antiferroelectric capacitors for high-energy-density applications. However, its performance can be hindered by irreversible phase transitions and leakage currents associated with low electrical resistivity. Defect and doping engineering offers a potential way to overcome these problems, but its use requires a detailed understanding of electronic, ionic, and polaron charge-compensation mechanisms, where the role of polarons remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the stability of small hole and electron polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO 3 , which is a structurally well-defined model system that avoids lattice-dynamical instabilities. Trapping energies are calculated using density functional theory corrected by a Hubbard U , using the enforced-piecewise-linearity approach including finite-size scaling. For the small hole-polaron centered on O- 2 p orbital, we find a trapping energy of − 0.65 eV and an adiabatic migration barrier of 0.32 eV determined by nudged-elastic-band calculations. In contrast, we show that excess electrons do not self-trap on Nb- 4 d orbitals, reflecting weak electron-phonon coupling in the conduction band manifold. These results identify oxygen as an intrinsic hole trap in NaNbO 3 and highlight the importance of including hole polarons in defect models of NaNbO 3 -based electroceramics.

items.title: Enhancing Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Generative AI-Based Data Augmentation
items.abstract: Credit card fraud detection is challenging due to the extreme class imbalance and the limited number of fraudulent transactions. To address this problem, this paper proposes a fraud detection framework that combines generative AI-based data augmentation with machine learning classification models. We generated synthetic fraud samples at augmentation ratios of 1%, 5%, and 10% using three generative approaches: a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP), a Variational Autoencoder (VAE), and a Large Language Model (LLM)-based data generator. The generated samples were evaluated using the Discriminator Test, Distance-to-Closest-Record (DCR) analysis, and t-SNE visualization to compare them to real fraud data and identify differences in their distributions. The augmented datasets were then used to train Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM classifiers. The baseline models trained on the original dataset achieved F1-scores of 0.857 for Random Forest, 0.856 for XGBoost, and 0.877 for LightGBM. After adding synthetic fraud samples to the training data, the results showed improvements in fraud detection performance in some cases. LightGBM achieved the highest F1-score of 0.897 when trained with VAE-generated data at the 10% augmentation ratio. Similarly, XGBoost achieved an F1-score of 0.880 using VAE-generated data at the 5% ratio. Overall, the findings demonstrate the potential of generative AI-based augmentation to improve fraud detection performance in highly imbalanced financial datasets, particularly when combined with LightGBM and XGBoost classifiers.

items.title: Enhancement of the Mechanical Properties of Low-k SiCOH Films by Plasma Treatment and Ultraviolet Curing
items.abstract: The integration of organosilicate SiCOH low-k dielectrics in back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnect structures requires a balance between low k and sufficient mechanical robustness. Low-k films with a thickness of approximately 2800 Å were deposited on 300 mm Si wafers via plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) using diethoxymethylsilane (DEMS) and O2 at 260 °C. To investigate the effects of process engineering on film properties, the total film thickness was divided into one, two, three, five, or 10 sublayers to compare segmentation, cyclic O2/He-plasma treatment, and interleaved ultraviolet (UV) curing. The resulting films were characterized by spectroscopic ellipsometry, nanoindentation, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiles, and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Segmentation increased the k value from 3.35 to 3.66, accompanied by a non-monotonic mechanical response. Extending the plasma treatment from 1 to 20 s led to a 19.8% rise in the k value, along with respective increases of 9.4% in hardness and 16.1% in the modulus, consistent with carbon/hydride removal and oxidative densification of the silicate network. Increasing RF power from 300 to 900 W caused smaller dielectric changes while raising the hardness and modulus by 8.7% and 10.6%, respectively, indicating diminishing changes at higher applied powers. Interleaved UV curing, comprising UV irradiation and concurrent thermal treatment, reduced the thickness, increased the refractive index (RI), and maintained a lower k relative to the as-deposited films. After five UV curing cycles, the hardness and modulus reached the highest mean values of 4.6 GPa and 35.8 GPa, respectively. FTIR analysis showed systematic depletion of Si–CH3 and Si–H groups and Si–O–Si network evolution, whereas XPS showed relatively stable plateau composition but treatment-sensitive transition regions. The combined results are consistent with oxidation-related modification during plasma treatment and network reorganization during UV curing, with possible differences in the spatial extent of these processes. These results further indicate that an intermediate cycle count provides a favorable balance between dielectric and mechanical properties.

items.title: Electrostatically driven organic modifier-assisted exfoliation of reduced graphene oxide-incorporated poly(vinyl alcohol) nanocomposites for high-performance triboelectric energy harvesting, pulse sensing, and IoT-enabled emergency systems
items.abstract: We report here a mono-lithium adipate (Li-AA)-assisted reduced graphene oxide (m-RGO)-incorporated poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) nanocomposite as a high-performance tribopositive layer for flexible triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) applications. Unlike conventional approaches based on direct incorporation of graphene derivatives, Li-AA was strategically employed as a multi-functional additive that simultaneously improved the flexibility of the PVA matrix and promoted the exfoliation of RGO nanosheets. The enhanced interfacial interactions between hydroxyl groups of PVA and oxygen-containing functionalities of m-RGO resulted in improved nanofiller-matrix compatibility, effective charge trapping sites, and optimized dielectric polarization. Dielectric investigations revealed enhanced permittivity and complex relaxation behaviour. Havriliak-Negami (HN) analysis demonstrated dual dielectric relaxation processes associated with polymer segmental dynamics and interfacial polarization, providing fundamental insights into charge accumulation and transport mechanisms. The optimized PVA/m-RGO nanocomposite-based TENG containing 0.5 wt% m-RGO exhibited outstanding electrical performance, delivering an open-circuit voltage of ∼242 V, a short-circuit current of ∼37 μA, and a maximum output power of ∼9600 μW at a load resistance of 5 MΩ. The fabricated device successfully harvested bio-mechanical energy from human motions and demonstrated real-time pulse sensing capability for wearable health monitoring. Furthermore, an IoT-integrated TENG prototype was developed for rapid emergency alert application. This work introduced a multi-functional additive-assisted nanocomposite design strategy that simultaneously enhanced mechanical flexibility, dielectric properties, and triboelectric output, providing a promising pathway toward next-generation self-powered wearable electronics and intelligent assistive technologies.

items.title: Electron donor–acceptor hybrid bonding polymers exhibit symmetry breaking and ferroelectricity
items.abstract: Hybrid bonding polymers chemically integrate supramolecular assemblies and covalent macromolecules and can therefore exhibit synergistic functionalities that can impact mechanical properties, catalytic activity, and robotic behavior, among others. In these materials, structural units are connected through both covalent and noncovalent bonds, and this hybrid bonding nature can lead to alterations in nanoscale morphology and internal ordering relative to purely supramolecular or purely covalent polymer systems. We report here on a hybrid bonding polymer in which an ionizable covalent polymer was partially functionalized with electron donor-acceptor dyads and co-assembled with similar dyad small molecules that could form supramolecular polymers on their own. Characterization with UV/Vis spectroscopy revealed charge-transfer interactions among the donor-acceptor dyads in the covalent polymer, the hybrids, and the supramolecular polymer, and wide-angle X-ray scattering indicated a gradual loss of internal order as more covalent polymer was incorporated into the hybrid structures. Interestingly, second harmonic generation confocal microscopy revealed the formation of noncentrosymmetric structures in the hybrid materials but not in the supramolecular polymer. Furthermore, measurements of polarization as a function of applied electric field yielded hysteresis loops characteristic of ferroelectric materials for the hybrid materials, but not for the pure covalent polymer or the pure supramolecular polymer. We found evidence of symmetry breaking and ferroelectricity in the hybrid assemblies only when the covalent polymer was moderately ionized, which suggested that electrostatic interactions played a key role in breaking the centrosymmetry of the donor-acceptor assemblies. Coarse-grained simulations further indicated that electrostatic repulsions between charged groups on the covalent polymers and the donor-acceptor dyad small molecules led to symmetry-breaking defects in these materials and that this effect was most prevalent at moderate degrees of covalent polymer ionization. Such defect-induced ferroelectricity has not been previously reported in other supramolecular ferroelectrics, and further investigation of this symmetry-breaking mechanism could enable simpler fabrication of flexible, lightweight ferroelectric materials.

items.title: Electric-Field-Driven Surface Ionic Transport on Hydroxylated SiO2 Governs Transient Leakage and Hybrid Bonding Reliability
items.abstract: Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding is critical for 3D integrated circuit packaging, where dielectric surface activation impacts bonding quality and long-term reliability. NaOH-based wet chemical activation is a promising approach for a scalable and cost-effective processing under ambient conditions. However, this route introduces residual ions at the SiO2 surface, raising concerns regarding electrical leakage and dielectric stability. In this study, electric-field-driven surface ionic transport on NaOH-activated SiO2 and its role in transient leakage and hybrid bonding reliability were investigated. Reversible and polarity-dependent transient current peaks observed in cyclic electrical measurements provide evidence for electric-field-driven migration of the mobile ionic species at the SiO2 interface. In addition, higher NaOH concentrations promoted greater residual Na+ accumulation and intensified transient leakage peaks, supporting the selection of 0.5 M NaOH as an effective activation condition. Systematic decoupling experiments demonstrate that residual mobile Na+ ions are the dominant contributors to the transient leakage current rather than fixed hydroxyl groups. Quantitative analysis reveals Na+ surface mobility of approximately 3 × 10-10 m2V-1s-1, an order-of-magnitude upper-bound estimate that is consistent between constant-bias and ramped-bias measurements and about six orders of magnitude higher than that in bulk SiO2, suggesting a surface-dominated transport. An optimized 3 min deionized water (DI) rinse reduces the mobile Na+ population below the electrical detection limit and decreases the Na 1s XPS intensity by roughly an order of magnitude, suppressing the transient leakage to near-baseline levels while maintaining hydrophilicity and achieving the SiO2-SiO2 bonding strength of 19.7 ± 1.8 MPa, comparable to Ar plasma activation. The leakage measurements were performed on Cu/SiO2 damascene comb structures, whereas the bonding validation addresses the dielectric part of the hybrid-bonding interface; Cu-Cu contact and long-term stress testing remain to be verified. This work provides a framework for understanding electric-field-driven surface ionic transport and practical guidelines for contamination control of the dielectric surface in wet-activated Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding.

items.title: Effects of Hyperthermal Atomic Oxygen and Surface Topology on Germanium Coatings Used to Reduce Drag in Low Earth Orbit
items.abstract: Low-altitude orbit spacecraft require materials that resist hyperthermal atomic oxygen (AO) erosion and maintain low-drag gas-surface interactions. In this work, we examine thin germanium (Ge) coatings as a non-native oxide-forming surface that generate a protective oxide layer in situ under AO exposure while preserving favorable scattering behavior. Ge-coated silicon samples are exposed to a hyperthermal O/O2 beam representative of low Earth orbit conditions and are analyzed using mass-loss measurements, atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), molecular-beam scattering experiments, and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) modeling. In particular, we use DSMC to examine the hypothesis that AO scattering and surface drag for shallow incidence impingement can be predicted accurately based on the AFMmeasured shape and the scattering properties of an unexposed flat Ge surface. Experiments show that Ge films show negligible mass loss at an AO fluence of 8.15 × 10 20 ± 5.28 × 10 19 O-atoms cm -2 , corresponding to an erosion yield below 0.03% of Kapton H, and exhibit a small change in roughness after exposure. XPS measurements show strong oxidation of the near-surface region, indicating formation of a GeO2-rich layer. Scattering experiments reveal quasi-specular, oxide-like angular distributions comparable to established reference materials, and DSMC results indicate only minor drag changes at the tested exposure level because AO-induced topographic changes were minimal. Notably, the microscopic distribution of slopes of the degraded surface, rather than the root mean square roughness, determines the scattering distribution and drag. Together, these results show that Ge coatings can couple AO resistance with favorable scattering behavior, making them a promising candidate for low-drag spacecraft surfaces in low-altitude orbits. The study also highlights the value of combining surface characterization, beam scattering, and roughnessresolved DSMC to link AO-driven surface evolution with orbital drag performance.

items.title: Effect of Gate Length Scaling on the Electrical Characteristics of a Ge/Si Double-Gate Heterojunction TFET
items.abstract: This paper investigates the effect of gate-length scaling on the electrical characteristics and band-to-band tunneling behavior of a Ge/Si double-gate heterojunction tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) using Silvaco ATLAS TCAD. Twelve gate lengths ranging from 1 to 20 nm are simulated while the principal device geometry, doping concentrations, gate dielectric thickness, and gate work function are kept constant. The electrical performance is evaluated in terms of ON-state current, OFF-state current, ON/OFF current ratio, threshold voltage, point subthreshold swing, and peak transconductance. The results show that the ON-state current increases from 9.99×10−9 to 1.51×10−4 A as gate length increases from 1 to 20 nm, while the ON/OFF current ratio reaches 1.08×1011. The extracted threshold voltage decreases from 1.24 to 0.46 V, and the point subthreshold swing decreases from 23.42 to 10.00 mV/dec. Peak transconductance reaches 1.63×10−3 S at a gate length of 19 nm before decreasing slightly at 20 nm. Energy-band, electric-field, and nonlocal band-to-band tunneling generation profiles are also examined to support the interpretation of the electrical trends. These findings demonstrate the influence of gate length on the simulated electrical performance and tunneling behavior of the investigated Ge/Si double-gate heterojunction TFET.

items.title: Dynamic Tunneling a Prior Phenomenon to Intermediate Resistive States in Defect Engineered Mn-SrTiO3 RRAM Devices
items.abstract: Resistive random-access memory devices work under the principle of resistive switching from high resistive state to low resistive state under applied electric field. In this work, 2%Mn doped SrTiO3, devices were fabricated using PLD in which, the defects are engineered such that the conducting filament formation is expected to have two oppositely charged defects: a) presence of Mn3+ dopants, giving rise to a negatively charged Mn and Ti and b) single and double positive oxygen vacancies. This process of two filaments emanating from both the electrodes has shown enhancement in the resistive switching characteristics aiding in forming-free switching that exhibits over 102 as ON/OFF ratio with a memory retention beyond 103 seconds at a low read voltage of 0.1V. All devices demonstrated a stable bipolar resistive switching dominated by conduction filament formation resulting from a synergic effect of oxygen vacancies and the varying oxidation states of Mn based negative defects that propagates toward each other under bias. The formation of defect-based filaments around the bias electrode was evidently observed using XPS of the devices before and after switching. A dynamic tunnelling process is observed as an intermediate process before the conduction filament forms in the SET region and following the snapping in the RESET region. Conduction filaments being heavily doped localizes conduction pathways with a small finite tunnelling barrier gap that are instantaneously formed and ruptures during switching cycles. The dynamic tunnelling behavior gives rise to a tiny spike in current and is observed at the intermediate resistive states which are potential for multi-state usage of these devices. Overall, Mn-STO devices of varying thicknesses show promising retention features and defect engineering offers control over single and/or multi-states memory.

items.title: Development of low-resistance ohmic contacts in GaN heterostructures using silicon Ion implantation
items.abstract: The formation of low-resistance Ohmic contacts remains an important consideration in the development of III-nitride electronic devices. This thesis investigates approaches for reducing Ohmic contact resistance (Rc) in AlGaN/GaN and AlN/GaN heterostructures, with particular emphasis on patterned recessed Ohmic contacts, silicon (Si) ion implantation, and the relative positioning of the recess and Ohmic metallisation. The first experimental study investigated the influence of recess patterning on Ohmic contact resistance. Localised recess patterns with dimensions of 4 µm × 150 µm and 4 µm × 10 µm were compared with a conventional planar contact without recess etching. The localised recess patterns did not provide an improvement in contact resistance compared with the conventional planar contact, which produced the lowest contact resistance of 0.81 Ω·mm among the structures investigated. These results demonstrate that, under the processing conditions used in this work, the introduction of the investigated localised recess patterns did not improve the Ohmic contact resistance. Si ion implantation was subsequently investigated as an approach for reducing Ohmic contact resistance. Blanket Si implantation was applied to GaN/AlGaN/GaN and AlN/GaN heterostructures, followed by high temperature activation and Ohmic contact formation. Low contact resistances were obtained from the implanted structures, with the implanted AlGaN/GaN heterostructure achieving Rc values of approximately 0.10–0.14 Ω ⋅ mm without post metallisation annealing. For the implanted AlN/GaN heterostructure, a minimum Rc of 0.46 Ω ⋅ mm was obtained following post metallisation annealing at 800 °C for 30 s. The effects of implantation activation, surface encapsulation and post metallisation annealing were also investigated as part of the process development. Building on the blanket implantation study, a selective area Si ion implantation process was developed to enable implantation to be confined to defined Ohmic contact regions. The process was applied to an available n-doped GaN capped AlN/GaN heterostructure, allowing implanted and un-implanted regions to be directly compared on the same sample. The implanted region exhibited a contact resistance of 0.14 Ω ⋅ mm, compared with 0.30 Ω ⋅ mm in the un-implanted region, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 53.5%. The corresponding sheet resistance decreased from 750 to 119 Ω/□. These results demonstrate the reduction in Ohmic contact resistance achieved through Si ion implantation and the applicability of selective area implantation to device fabrication. The final experimental study investigated the influence of recess-to-metallisation positioning on Ohmic contact resistance using aligned, overlap and gap designs. Overlap and gap distances of 2, 3 and 5 µm were investigated. Increasing the recess-to-metallisation overlap progressively reduced the extracted contact resistance, with the 5 µm overlap producing the lowest Rc of 0.95 Ω ⋅ mm among the investigated designs. In contrast, introducing a gap between the recessed and metallised regions resulted in a substantial increase in contact resistance. An optimum overlap distance was not established, as Rc continued to decrease up to the maximum investigated overlap of 5 µm. Overall, the results demonstrate that Ohmic contact resistance in III-nitride heterostructures is strongly influenced by recess patterning, Si ion implantation and recess-to-metallisation positioning. In particular, the ion implantation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach for achieving low-resistance Ohmic contacts, while the development of selective-area implantation demonstrates how the implantation process can be confined to defined contact regions for integration into device fabrication. The recess studies further highlight the importance of the extent of recessing and the positioning of the Ohmic metallisation relative to the recessed region. Together, these findings contribute to the development and understanding of fabrication approaches for achieving low-resistance Ohmic contacts in IIInitride electronic devices.

items.title: Development and validation of a scale assessing perceived trustworthiness in large language models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly part of everyday life, yet there is no established way to measure how users evaluate their trustworthiness. This study introduces the Perceived Trustworthiness of LLMs scale (PT-LLM-8), a self-report psychometric instrument measuring users’ perceived trustworthiness of their primary LLM. PT-LLM-8 is developed from the TrustLLM framework and adapted as a human-centred measure. The PT-LLM-8 comprises eight items representing truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, transparency, accountability, and compliance with laws. Psychometric properties of the scale were tested with 752 LLM users in the United Kingdom (Mean age = 28.58, SD = 6.11, 50.3% males, 48.8% females). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a one-factor structure, with high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.90, Composite Reliability = 0.91, strong item-total correlations (ranged between 0.62 and 0.75), and measurement invariance across gender. The total score measures overall perceived trustworthiness, while individual item responses may also be examined descriptively for information about the content represented by each item. For researchers, practitioners, and developers, the PT-LLM-8 offers a practical instrument for evaluating interventions, comparing groups and contexts, and examining whether technical safeguards are reflected in users’ perceived trustworthiness of LLM. The scale can also be applied to guide system design, support policy development, and help organisations monitor shifts in user trust toward LLMs over time, making it applicable across research, practice, and governance.

items.title: Deterministic Agentic Workflows and Cognitive Enterprise Search Framework (2026)
items.abstract: This technical report outlines the architectural paradigms required to deploy autonomous AI agents and enterprise cognitive search systems within strict corporate governance parameters. While large language models demonstrate high conversational capability, enterprise adoption requires deterministic tool execution, verifiable grounding, and full EU AI Act compliance. Enterprise AI consulting and operational frameworks are provided by Heinrich Co, developing tailored intelligence roadmaps for global institutions. 1. Cognitive Search & Enterprise Knowledge Synthesis Conventional keyword retrieval systems fail to capture semantic relationships across distributed corporate repositories. Implementing hybrid vector embeddings alongside deterministic BM25 lexical search enables context-aware discovery without hallucination risks. Review implementation details in AI Powered Enterprise Search. 2. AI Readiness & Corporate Operational Audits Successful AI transformation requires data hygiene, schema standardization, and organizational alignment. Before deploying autonomous agent pipelines, enterprises must assess infrastructure feasibility. Reference the structured framework in AI Readiness Consulting Assessment Deliverables. 3. Executive Governance and Future-Proof Roadmaps Strategic deployment must balance rapid innovation with ethical risk management and regulatory accountability. Learn more in the executive analysis Foreword Blog En.

items.title: Design of a novel dual-source III–V material-based junctionless line TFET for performance assessment
items.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a dual-source III–V material-based junctionless line TFET (III–V JL-LTFET) aimed at improving device performance. The incorporation of a dual-source configuration increases the effective tunneling area, which enhances the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) probability and boosts the ON-state current. Furthermore, the junctionless configuration is employed to eliminate the requirement for abrupt doping profiles, thereby reducing fabrication complexity while mitigating random dopant fluctuations (RDFs). To boost the ON-state current while simultaneously suppressing the ambipolar current, a heterojunction design is implemented using narrow-bandgap GaSb at the source and wider-bandgap GaAs for the channel and drain regions.The results demonstrate that the proposed III–V JL-LTFET achieves an ON-state current (I ON ) of 7.22 × 10 − 6 A/µm, an I ON /I OFF ratio of 1.32 × 10 12 with an average subthreshold swing (AVSS) of 13.21 mV/dec at V GS = 0.5 V. Additionally, the device exhibits promising radio-frequency (RF) characteristics, including a transconductance (gm) of 40 µS, a cut-off frequency ( f T ) of 5.87 GHz, a gain-bandwidth product (GBW) of 1.16 GHz, and a transconductance–frequency product (TFP) of 32.6 GHz.

items.title: Defect engineering in parylene memristors with ZnTe nanoparticles for enhanced switching reproducibility, photosensitivity, and neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: slope analysis, impedance and optical spectroscopy, temperature dependencies and photoresponse measurements, and is attributed to percolation chains of ZnTe nanoparticles bridged by Cu clusters with thin tunneling gaps. Finally, simulations of a memristive neural network and an in-sensor reservoir computing system, both based on the measured device characteristics with their nonidealities, indicate that the devices are promising for in-memory and in-sensor computing.

items.title: Data-Driven Estimation of Ship Manoeuvring Hydrodynamic Derivatives using a Hybrid MARUS–PINN Framework with LLM-Guided Symbolic Discovery
items.abstract: Identification of hydrodynamic derivatives that govern ship manoeuvring behaviour for autonomous vessels such as unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) is essential for diverse maritime purposes including oceanographic research, environmental monitoring, and autonomous navigation. However, conventional hydrodynamic modelling approaches, such as classical manoeuvring models, experimental methods, and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD), are often labour-intensive, costly, and time-consuming, and their estimated parameters may not fully capture real-world operating conditions due to nonlinearities, scale effects, and complex sea states. With the advent of machine learning, recent advances in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a promising alternative by embedding governing fluid-dynamic equations directly into the neural learning network, providing the advantages of data-driven learning while maintaining physical consistency. Hence, this thesis investigates a novel approach that combines Marine Robotics Unity Simulator (MARUS)–simulated manoeuvring data, PINN-based parameter learning, and symbolic discovery via Large Language Models (LLMs) to estimate hydrodynamic derivatives with improved robustness, reduced data requirements, and enhanced interpretability compared to conventional system identification methods, while promoting interoperability and standardization through its modular design. To evaluate this hybrid approach, the thesis addresses the following research question: Can a hybrid MARUS–PINN–LLM framework provide more accurate, interpretable, and data-efficient estimates of manoeuvring hydrodynamic derivatives than conventional system identification methods? To this end, an extensive set of experiments and ablation studies is conducted to compare the proposed hybrid model with its purely data-driven and purely physics-based counterparts across parameter accuracy, trajectory reconstruction quality, and generalization to diverse maneuvering conditions of various industry-standard USVs. The results demonstrate that integrating symbolic discovery with PINNs reduces sway-acceleration error by 86%, yaw-rate acceleration error by 66%, and heading-rollout error by 89% relative to purely data-driven baselines, producing compact, physically consistent residual terms that align with established nonlinear hydrodynamic effects while its physics-only counterparts catastrophically diverge from the ground-truths. Taken together, these findings highlight the potential of hybrid physics–machine-learning frameworks to advance the estimation of manoeuvring coefficients for the next generation of autonomous marine systems.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: DDRop: Active Memory Interposer Attacks on Confidential VMs by Dropping DDR5 Writes
items.abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) are increasingly deployed in the cloud to protect sensitive workloads through hardware-enforced isolation, remote attestation, and transparent memory encryption. However, to meet memory performance and size demands, modern TEEs omit cryptographic freshness guarantees, leaving them vulnerable to replay attacks by adversaries with physical memory access. Prior work demonstrated low-cost active interposition attacks on DDR4 without requiring expensive specialized equipment, but these techniques do not extend to DDR5, where existing approaches are limited to passive ciphertext side-channel analysis and rely on bus downclocking to accommodate legacy memory bus analyzers. We present the first low-cost (<200) DDR5 RDIMM interposer capable of active fault injection at native speeds. By injecting targeted parity errors to silently discard cache line writebacks, we introduce DDRop, a new primitive that exploits the absence of cryptographic freshness to break the integrity of Intel TDX, Scalable SGX, and AMD SEV-SNP. Building on this primitive and targeting the APIs exposed by the TDX module and AMD Secure Processor, we show that adversaries can gain ciphertext access, copy arbitrary victim pages, and inject malicious secure page-table entries. We demonstrate end-to-end attacks on an up-to-date TDX platform, including forcing any TD into debug mode and forging attestation reports. While software-level mitigations, including timing-based interposer detection and API hardening, may reduce the attack surface, our results demonstrate that active DDR5 bus interposition is practical at low cost, highlighting the need for robust cryptographic memory integrity protections against physical adversaries.

items.title: Conserved amount, negotiable placement. Prompting perturbs one architecture, an AI reviewer both
items.abstract: Tesler's conservation law holds that a problem carries an irreducible amount of complexity. Brooks separates that essential part from the accidental part a solution adds. If the essential part is fixed, architecture is placement rather than quantity, and the question is which levers move placement. An AI agent implements sixty accumulating change requests on one REST endpoint under two architectures, a mutative Spring controller and an additive OfficeFloor pipeline, under five conditions, ten runs per cell, model fixed. Four are external controls, from a bare change request to the disclosed structural cost function. The fifth is different in kind. A second agent reviews each change and reasons about cohesion itself. It consolidates the pipeline, raising change- and mass-concentration on every such metric, interval excluding zero, while leaving coupling, file count and per-node complexity untouched. The price is reported in full. Strict correctness fell in most comparisons though each rule was implemented correctly in over 99% of checkpoints, and all three outcome measures favour the concentrated codebase. items.title: Comparative analysis of a noise and count-rate performance of a charge-sensitive amplifier in planar CMOS and FinFET technologies for hybrid pixel detectors
items.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of a charge-sensitive amplifier (CSA) for hybrid pixel detectors operating in a single-photon counting mode, implemented in a 40 nm planar complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) and a 16 nm fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) technologies. Hybrid pixel detectors are widely used in particle physics, synchrotron radiation facilities, and X-ray imaging applications, where front-end electronics must support increasingly high photon flux while maintaining low noise and a compact pixel area. A folded-cascode charge-sensitive amplifier was designed in both technologies and evaluated through circuit simulations in terms of open-loop gain, gain-bandwidth product, maximum counting rate, and equivalent noise charge (ENC). The 16 nm FinFET implementation achieved significantly higher intrinsic gain and gain-bandwidth product than the 40 nm planar CMOS design, resulting in a substantially higher maximum counting rate while maintaining comparable noise. These performance improvements, however, come at the cost of increased design complexity, reduced flexibility in transistor sizing, greater sensitivity to layout parasitics, and higher fabrication costs. The results demonstrate that FinFET technology offers strong potential for next-generation high-speed front-end readout electronics for hybrid pixel detectors, particularly in applications requiring high count-rate capability, while highlighting the design trade-offs associated with advanced technology nodes.

items.title: Capabilities and limitations of MACE interatomic potentials for Fe-Ni alloys: a systematic benchmark
items.abstract: We present a systematic benchmark of MACE interatomic potentials for iron–nickel alloys, focusing on structural, elastic, and finite-temperature properties of chemically disordered body-centered-cubic (bcc) and face-centered-cubic (fcc) phases. The reference dataset comprises spin-polarized PBE density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations for special quasirandom structures (SQS) span- ning composition, volume, and shear deformation. A system-specific MACE–sqs model trained on this dataset achieves validation errors of 2.0 meV/atom for energies and 24.3 meV/Å for forces. We compare MACE–sqs with several MACE foundation models, including models trained using Hubbard corrections, through equations of state, equilibrium volumes, cubic elastic properties, and thermal lattice expansion. MACE–sqs gives the most consistent overall performance for several zero-temperature structural and elastic benchmarks, although its relative performance depends on property and composition and it does not reproduce all experimental elastic trends. In the finite-temperature comparison, no single model is uniformly superior, and MACE–matpes agrees more closely with experiment for some compositions and comparison metrics. Finite-temperature calculations yield reasonable thermal-expansion coefficients near 300 K, while deviations at elevated temperatures and for magnetovolume sensitive compositions highlight the limitation of representing magnetic effects only implicitly through the spin-polarized reference data. These results define the tested application domain in which targeted SQS-based training improves upon broad foundation models and identify explicit magnetic degrees of freedom and broader configurational sampling as priorities for future development.
items.venue: Modelling and Simulation in Materials Science and Engineering

items.title: CNN on ‘Top’: In search of scalable and lightweight image-based jet taggers
items.abstract: Abstract While Transformer-based and standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be the best performers in classifying different types of jets, they require substantial computational power. We explore the scope of using a lightweight and scalable version of EfficientNet architecture, along with global features of the jet. The end product is computationally inexpensive but is capable of competitive performance. We showcase the efficacy of our network in tagging top-quark jets in a sea of other light quark and gluon jets. The work also sheds light on the importance of global features for both the accuracy and the apparent redundancy of the network’s complexity.

items.title: Broadcast, Don't Replicate: Eliminating Weight HBM in Datacenter LLM Serving
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference at datacenter scale is fundamentally bottlenecked by memory capacity and bandwidth limits. Because model weights are read-only and identical across instances, conventional architectures that replicate these parameters across the local DRAM of tens of thousands of accelerators incur massive capital expenditures, significant static power dissipation, and redundant memory-fetch energy. A recent proposal to use optical fiber loops as delay-line memory alleviates these issues, but its recirculating loop must hold the whole model: loop length grows with model size, slack is fixed when the ring is built, and the layouts that serve modern Mixture of Experts (MoE) models efficiently do not fit in it. We propose Optical Broadcast Memory (OBM), an open-ended hierarchical Tap-and-Amplify fiber architecture that generalizes and replaces the optical ring paradigm. A centralized memory server continuously broadcasts weights to distributed inference nodes that passively tap the data stream using receive-only co-packaged optics, delivering parameters directly to compute units without intermediate buffering. To overcome the limitations of continuous weight streaming, we use dynamically-sized slack to accommodate large and variable context lengths. We show how removing the restrictions of the optical ring allows OBM to efficiently serve MoE models. Evaluated at a datacenter scale of 80,000 accelerators, OBM eliminates petabytes of HBM while being competitive or better in throughput and energy per token than an HBM-based system.

items.title: Beyond PCIe Thrashing and Recursive Sandboxes: High-Throughput 30B Sparse MoE Inference and Symbolic-Gated Hallucination Verification on 4 GB VRAM Workstations
