Among the investigated materials, AlYN exhibits the strongest carrier confinement and the highest electron density, reaching approximately 5.93 × 1013 cm−2 at 14% Y and 5.332 × 1013 cm−2 at 8% Y composition. The optimum AlYN barrier thickness is found to lie between 8 and 10 nm, and the incorporation of an AlN interlayer increases the electron density from 5.07 × 1013 cm−2–5.52 × 1013 cm−2. These results identify AlYN as a promising barrier material for next-generation GaN HEMTs, offering high carrier concentration, moderate strain, and enhanced design flexibility compared to existing Sc-based barrier technologies.

items.title: Demonstration of High Output Power (3.75 W/mm) With 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on Sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.
items.venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Technology Letters

items.title: Deep-UV lithographic realization of aperture arrays as etch masks for 3D nanostructures in silicon
items.abstract: Abstract State-of-the-art integrated circuits currently involve multi-layered architectures that rapidly extend towards three-dimensional (3D) semiconductor structures. To overcome out-of-plane alignment issues, we present an original method to employ conventional deep-UV lithography on pre-structured silicon substrates to pattern an etch mask for monolithic 3D nanostructures with N layers using only M = 1 overlay alignment step (instead of M = (N - 1) steps as in layer-by-layer assembly). The target nanostructures studied here consist of arrays of pores that intersect at oblique angles. To this end, we project elliptical apertures on the sidewalls of V-trenches at controllable depths relative to the wafer's top surface. We create V-trenches in Si by hot HF 50% and KOH 25% etching with θ = 54.7° sloping sidewalls. We successfully spin-coat photoresist on the sloping V-trench sidewalls with a thickness between 50 and 800 nm. The photoresist is remarkably homogeneous, better than 4 nm along 2.6μm of the V-trench sidewall. Using a single deep-UV lithography exposure at λ= 193nm (with a 25 mJ/cm 2 dose and a nominal focal plane at 500 nm depth below the Si wafer top-surface) we successfully expose apertures at various depths in the photoresist on sloping sidewall surfaces of the V-trenches. The apertures have diameters between d = 180 nm and 509 nm, to as deep as Z = 1180nm below the wafer surface. We develop an analytical model to successfully describe lithographic exposure on an inclined surface, which allows one to sculpt non-planar aperture arrays on inclined surfaces. In the future, aperture arrays on inclined surfaces may serve as etch masks to create monolithic and controllable 3D nanostructures deep inside silicon with a reduced number of overlay alignment steps, thus increasing the yield and throughput, and reducing costs and use of chemical and material resources.

items.title: Cu intercalation and field-driven filament formation in vertically aligned MoS$_2$ memristors
items.abstract: Vertically-aligned MoS$_2$ films paired with a Cu top electrode have been used as electrochemical metallization cell memristor devices. The memristive switching has been attributed to the formation of conductive filaments, yet their exact structure has remained elusive. Here we carry out a multi-scale computational study of Cu intercalation, clustering, and field-driven dynamics to eventually model the filament formation under operating conditions. We use density-functional theory results to fine-tune a machine learning force field, and the most important physical phenomena are further distilled into multi-particle kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. By exhaustive enumeration of Cu intercalated structures, we find the most stable structure at MoS$_2$Cu$_{0.11}$ composition, with Cu atoms forming a dice lattice between the MoS$_2$ layers. These structures are shown to exhibit metallic character and can thus form conductive filaments under memristor operation. The simulated switching speed and threshold voltage agree well with the available experimental data. Our results give fundamental insights on the device operation mechanism and guidelines for maximizing switching speed and endurance.

items.title: Cost Analysis of 310x310mm Panels for High-Performance Computing Driven by Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Using square or rectangular panels instead of round wafers has been a topic of interest in the microelectronics packaging industry for years. A more recent addition to the discussion is the potential to use panels for advanced packaging applications. This contrasts with earlier panel-level analyses that focused on smaller, basic fan-out packages. Whether evaluating panels for simpler or more complex packages, one primary focus of any panel-level discussion is the potential for cost savings. Previous analysis has been carried out with a focus on traditional fan-out packaging and large panels (600x600mm). At IMAPS Device Packaging this year, the author of this paper also did an analysis of the 310x310mm panel format, with a focus on an advanced fan-out process flow. This abstract proposes a fresh analysis of the 310x310mm formfactor, now with a focus on 300mm round silicon wafers versus square glass panels. Multiple interposer sizes will be evaluated, and yield trade-offs will be included as well. The goal of this paper is to understand the potential cost savings when building complex packages using a 310x310mm glass interposer in place of a 300mm round silicon interposer.

items.title: Computational screening of reconfigurable van der Waals ferroelectric semiconductor heterojunctions for all-in-one optoelectronic devices
items.abstract: Reconfigurable optoelectronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals semiconductor heterojunctions (VSHs) are potential candidates for multifunctional applications in a single device. However, device multifunctionalities highly rely on VSHs with tunable band alignment and band offsets for achieving reconfigurable optoelectronic properties. Herein, we report a new class of 2D VSHs consisting of atomically thin ABP2X6-type ferroelectric (FE) semiconductors for the development of an all-in-one optoelectronic architecture based on high-throughput first-principles calculations and the nonequilibrium Green’s function method. Our results reveal that the polarization coupling of dual FE layers in the VSHs leads to multiple polarization states, allowing a sequential band-alignment evolution. Using CuInP2S6/AuInP2S6 VSHs as a prototype example, we demonstrate the heterojunction with reversible band-alignment transitions and tunable band offsets by modulating the polarization state of dual FE layers. This enables the device to achieve a theoretical tunneling electroresistance ratio (TER) of 106% between the interlayer FE and antiferroelectric (AFE) states at the bias voltage of 1.5 V, as well as positive and negative photoresponses. The FE-polarization-dependent band alignment and photoresponse of the heterojunction device can be used to implement in-sensor broadband convolutional processing for image recognition and reconfigurable optoelectronic logic operations including AND, OR, and XOR. These findings suggest huge potential of 2D FE VSHs for exploiting multifunctional optoelectronic device applications.

items.title: Breaking the Oxide Barrier: Cost-Efficient Plasma De-oxidation of Copper Surfaces for Advanced Hybrid Bonding
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of semiconductor packaging has positioned copper-to-copper (Cu-Cu) hybrid bonding as a critical technology for high-performance interconnects. However, the spontaneous formation of copper oxides (Cu2O and CuO) presents a significant barrier, as these layers inhibit atomic diffusion and degrade electrical performance through interfacial voiding or delamination. This study investigates the efficacy of an Atmospheric-Pressure Dielectric Barrier Discharge (DBD) plasma process using an H2/N2 gas mixture, characterized by high energy density and uniformity, as a high-throughput deoxidation solution. Utilizing a test vehicle consisting of a 100 nm Ti barrier and a 500 nm Cu film, we demonstrate that plasma-dissociated hydrogen atoms can achieve a maximum reduction depth exceeding 4 nm at a scanning speed of 5 mm/s. Kinetic analysis establishes an inverse relationship between scanning speed and reduction depth, governed by the residence time of hydrogen (H*) radicals and the resulting penetration of the reaction front into the oxide layer. While the process significantly outperforms the industry standard requirement of >2 nm, the study identifies that the rate-limiting factor is not plasma chemistry but the mass transport efficiency of water vapor byproducts. According to Le Chatelier’s Principle, the accumulation of H2O triggers re-oxidation. We conclude that achieving high-volume manufacturing (HVM) stability requires hardware-level optimizations, such as localized exhaust, to lower the partial pressure of H2O and maintain a metallic surface state.

items.title: Bingham Fluid Rheology and a Dimensionless Analysis of Wire Cutting in Fresh Cementitious Filaments
items.abstract: Bingham fluids combine a finite yield stress with an approximately linear post-yield relation between shear stress and shear rate. This compact model is widely used for pastes, slurries, drilling muds, cementitious materials and other viscoplastic media, yet its apparent simplicity conceals the free-boundary problem created by yielded and unyielded regions. This article reviews the constitutive basis of the Bingham model, analytical results for simple flows, and numerical strategies based on regularization, finite elements and the lattice Boltzmann method. The review emphasizes that yield surfaces are stress-defined rather than material interfaces and that regularization parameters must be checked against mesh and time-step sensitivity. A feasible research object is then developed: transverse wire cutting of a freshly extruded cementitious filament. The wire is treated as a translating cylinder in a low-Reynolds-number yield-stress medium. A dimensionless analysis based on the Bingham number separates viscous-dominated, mixed and yield-dominated cutting regimes, while a transparent resistance scale links yield stress, plastic viscosity, wire diameter and cutting speed. The analysis shows why slower cutting does not necessarily minimize resistance when structural rebuilding raises the yield stress. A combined rheometry, force-measurement and regularized-flow simulation protocol is proposed. The Bingham model is suitable as a baseline for process design, but thixotropy, elasticity, wall slip, particle size and fracture must be added when they control the observed cutting response.

items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Adaptive peridynamic neural operators with fracture-aware topology
items.abstract: Predicting fracture in complex engineering systems requires the simultaneous treatment of nonlocal constitutive behaviour, multi-physics loading and multi-scale crack propagation – a combination that no existing framework addresses in a unified, data-driven way. Existing peridynamic neural operators use a fixed horizon that either over-smooths the crack tip or sacrifices the nonlocal bulk response, and none track how a material’s connectivity changes as it fractures. We introduce the adaptive peridynamic neural operator with fracture-aware topology, which learns bond-level constitutive laws inside a damage-adaptive peridynamic operator, couples a coarse (bulk) and fine (crack-tip) operator through a multi-fidelity mixture and tracks the topology of the fracturing domain through a bond-count invariant, while remaining trainable from simulation or experimental data. Applied to biological soft tissue, ductile metals, polymers, concrete and foams, the adaptive peridynamic neural operator with fracture-aware topology achieves a mean prediction error ≈ 4 . 1 % , against 9 . 0 % for the base peridynamic neural operator and 15 . 8 % for the Fourier neural operator. Five extended physics features (anisotropic horizon, thermomechanical coupling, grain-boundary kernel, learned Paris fatigue law, electro-mechanical coupling) extend the framework to artificial intelligence chip reliability – silicon die cracking, copper pillar fatigue, underfill delamination, through-silicon via (TSV) liner cracking and low-k dielectric fracture – where the full model reaches ≈ 2 . 7 % mean prediction error ( 70 % lower than the base peridynamic neural operator), outperforms the ANSYS cohesive-zone finite element method by 3 . 5 × in accuracy while running 18 × faster and yields three quantitative design rules for bump pitch, low-k material selection and TSV keep-out zones.

items.title: A Study on Performance Comparison and Application Scenarios of PVD, CVD and ALD Thin-Film Deposition Processes
items.abstract: Semiconductor thin films are the core functional structures of microelectronic and optoelectronic devices. The thickness, uniformity, and density of the thin film directly determine the performance, lifespan, and stability of the device. With the continuous miniaturization and three-dimensionalization of semiconductor devices, traditional deposition processes are struggling to meet the high-precision coating requirements of high aspect ratio micro/nano structures. Therefore, precise process selection has become crucial in semiconductor manufacturing. This paper focuses on three mainstream thin film deposition processes: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD), Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD), and Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD). It systematically elucidates the core working principles of these three processes, conducting a horizontal comparison from multiple dimensions, including deposition mechanism, thickness control accuracy, step coverage capability, film quality, and production cost. The paper analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of each process and clarifies the process selection logic in the context of semiconductor device fabrication. Research shows that there is no absolute superiority or inferiority among the three processes, each possesses differentiated application adaptability. PVD is suitable for low-cost planar thin film mass production, CVD balances efficiency and versatility, and ALD dominates the coating of high-end precision micro/nano devices. This paper also summarizes the technical bottlenecks of existing processes and clarifies the industry development trends of low-temperature processing, high-precision low-cost processing, and process integration.

items.title: A Review of Insulation Stress and Partial Dischargein Medium-Frequency Transformers Under Fast Repetitive Voltage Pulses
items.abstract: The use of wide-bandgap power devices in solid-state transformers enables higher switching frequencies and power densities, but it also exposes medium-frequency transformer insulation to fast repetitive voltage pulses. Short rise times, high dv/dt, high repetition frequencies, and harmonic content can produce nonuniform winding voltages, local field enhancement, and partial discharge. This review examines the resulting insulation stress, discharge mechanisms, detection methods, relevant IEC standards, and design approaches. The reviewed studies show that partial discharge inception and insulation lifetime depend on voltage amplitude, rise time, repetition frequency, polarity, temperature, and residual charge. They also show that power-frequency test results cannot be transferred directly to pulse-width modulation service. Reliable insulation assessment therefore requires complete waveform reporting, interference-resistant sensing, and product-specific test procedures. The resulting evidence should then guide an insulation design that combines electric-field control and thermal management while accounting for parasitic parameters and manufacturing tolerances. Future work should establish common test waveforms and relate discharge activity to long-term material damage under representative operating duty.

items.title: A Combined Atmospheric Argon Plasma and In-Situ Formic Acid Vapor Fluxless TCB Process for Advanced Packaging
items.abstract: This work investigates the fundamental interactions of both formic acid (FA) vapor and atmospheric plasma with Sn metal and its oxides (SnO and SnO₂) and compares their performance in fluxless TCB. Plasma-only processing was found to risk void formation and incomplete oxide removal due to its highly directional nature and sensitivity to exposure conditions. Prior work has shown that FA-related contamination strongly depends on initial oxide thickness, with thick SnO₂ layers requiring elevated temperatures or extended exposure times. Building on these insights, we introduce a combined process that applies atmospheric plasma followed by in-situ FA vapor exposure. Plasma pre-treatment effectively thins or disrupts the hard SnO₂ surface layer, enabling efficient reduction of residual oxides by FA while minimizing contamination. This synergistic approach overcomes the limitations of each individual method, improves bond quality, increases yield and throughput, and significantly reduces by-product formation without requiring aggressive over-exposure conditions.

items.title: van der Waals epitaxy of flexible κ -Ga2O3 thin films on mica for low-power near-linear solar-blind ultraviolet photodetection
items.abstract: Flexible solar-blind ultraviolet (UV) photodetectors based on ultrawide-bandgap Ga2O3 are attractive for wearable sensing and conformal optical monitoring, yet achieving high crystallinity and a linear photoresponse in metastable κ-Ga2O3 on flexible substrates remains challenging. Here, a highly [001]-oriented κ-Ga2O3 thin film is grown on flexible mica by van der Waals pulsed laser deposition and integrated into a solar-blind UV photoconductor. The κ-Ga2O3 (002) ω-rocking curve exhibits a narrow full width at half maximum of 0.108°. Consequently, at 10 V, the device delivers a low dark current of 8.6 × 10−11 A, a photo-to-dark current ratio of 5169, and a near-linear photocurrent dependence over 1–1600 μW/cm2 under 254 nm illumination with a power-law exponent of 0.968. Moreover, the detector maintains stable operation across bending radii of 8–12.5 mm and retains 97.8% of its initial photocurrent after 2000 bending cycles at an 8 mm radius, while post-bending x-ray diffraction confirms κ-phase retention. These results establish κ-Ga2O3/mica as a reliable platform for conformal deep-UV sensing.

items.title: WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU
items.abstract: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls. The first is capacity: the KV of Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of video in bf16 and after 2.8 minutes in int4. The second is the model's positional horizon of 4.3 minutes. We show that this memory is capacity-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and that its access set is known before compute, because the camera pose is an input. An analytical model built on these observations predicts spill points to within one chunk and classifies zero versus non-zero stalls correctly on held-out configurations. Guided by it, WorldPager stores int4 KV in a GPU/DRAM/NVMe hierarchy instead of recomputing it, prefetches each chunk's memory from the extrapolated pose, never waits on a miss, and writes back in the background; to our knowledge, it is the first to place the KV memory of an interactive world model on an NVMe tier with zero-stall prefetching. With training-free position handling, it generates 37.5 minutes of video continuously with zero stalls and constant host memory, at about 9.5 frames per second. On a sealed test set, int4 storage shows no measurable quality loss; on long-gap revisits it lowers image quality by about one MUSIQ point.

items.title: The Substrate is the PCB: A Packaging Architecture for Vertical Power Delivery in Multi-Kilowatt AI Processors
items.abstract: For multi-kilowatt AI processors, the package—not the transistor—has become the dominant constraint on power delivery. At 1 kW and a 0.7 V supply, 1,400 A must traverse the full interconnect stack, while electromigration limits each ~100 μm C4 bump to roughly 1 A, forcing 3,500–5,000 bumps onto the power and ground nets and into direct contention with high-density signal escape. As we continue the power trajectory into the multi-kilowatt regime, we argue that the resolution is a directional reorganization of the package: power and heat flow vertically through the stack while high-bandwidth signal flows horizontally to the perimeter, so that the C4 array is dedicated to signal and all high-current regulation is absorbed into the substrate. In this architecture the substrate takes on the traditional role of the printed circuit board. We analyze the packaging consequences: substrate-material selection (organic, glass, SiC, and diamond add-on layers) against four conflicting requirements; hot-spot-driven specification of the embedded inductor and power-delivery network (PDN) (6–10 A/mm²); and the assembly and known-good-die (KGD) reliability of embedding active and passive components. An embedded Package-Integrated Voltage Regulator (PIVR) reduces PDN droop from ~150 mV to under 40 mV; we identify inductor current density as one of the most challenging technology risks.

items.title: Switching Losses and Their Mitigation in Lateral β -Ga 2 O 3 Power MOSFETs With High-Permittivity Dielectric for Field Management
items.abstract: Ultrawide-bandgap beta-phase gallium oxide ($\beta $-Ga2O${}_{{3}}\text {)}$is promising for high-voltage, low-loss power devices. Field management in$\beta $-Ga2O3transistors using a high-permittivity (high-${k}\text {)}$dielectric can improve the devices’ power figure of merit (PFOM), but the increased drain-to-gate feedback capacitance degrades switching performance. This article reports on a simulation study of the switching losses and their mitigation in a 3.3-kV normally-offlateral$\beta $-Ga2O3MOSFET with high-$k$field management. A source-connected field plate (sFP) is proposed to mitigate the switching losses while maintaining the device’s blocking capability. Under the switching condition of 3.3 kV/20 A, the fall time and rise time are reduced by approximately 61% and 85%, respectively. The associated turn-off and turn-on losses decrease by approximately 63% and 51%, respectively. Meanwhile, the sFP can shield the gate from a high drain bias and improve gate stability. The effect of the sFP in mitigating switching losses is more effective at higher load currents, indicating that the proposed strategy is suitable for high-load switching scenarios. These findings provide guiding principles for the design of lateral$\beta $-Ga2O3MOSFETs to meet switching requirements in power electronics.

items.title: Sustainable Ambient-Air Cu-Cu Wedge Bonding via Cu-Selective Ultrathin Passivation
items.abstract: Despite advances in 2.5D and 3D packaging, wire bonding remains the most widely used interconnection method in the semiconductor industry. Direct copper-to-copper (Cu-Cu) wedge bonding is highly valued in IC packaging due to its excellent electrical and thermal properties and lower material cost compared to gold (Au). However, its industrial use is limited because bare Cu surfaces oxidize rapidly at typical assembly temperatures (198-200 °C), forming a native Cu oxide barrier that causes widespread non-stick-on-lead (NSOL) failures. Traditional solutions involve expensive silver (Ag) finishes or a reducing forming-gas atmosphere (95% N2, 5% H2), both of which increase cost, complexity, and environmental concerns. This study presents a sustainable, precious-metal-free, and forming-gas-free alternative by applying an ultrathin (12-20 nm) Cu-selective passivation layer as a thermal shield during wire bonding. Building on previous passivation studies focused on bimetallic systems such as aluminum (Al) and palladium-coated copper (PCC) wires, this work investigates true monometallic Cu-Cu wedge bonding using 33μm bare Cu wire. The non-passivated Cu leadframe showed 100% failure at lower bonding power [220-230 Ultrasonic Power (US)], with inconsistent adhesion and high pull-strength variability at higher power ranges. In contrast, the passivated leadframe achieved consistent bonding yield across all power levels, with stable pull strength of 3.0-5.0 gf at 220-230 US, 2.0-6.0 gf at 300 US, and 3.0-6.0 gf at 400 US. Post-bonding analysis confirmed the passivation remained chemically stable at 200 °C for 10 minutes, suppressing 60-70% of Cu-oxide growth. Post-pull test failure analysis further confirmed the mechanical integrity of the Cu-Cu interface, with failures primarily occurring as cohesive wire-neck breaks while the second wedge bond remained intact. These results demonstrate a scalable and eco-friendly alternative to traditional Ag-plated leadframes and costly PCC wires, aligning metallurgical reliability with environmental sustainability for next-generation microelectronics packaging.

items.title: SpikePID: Real-Time Neuromorphic Cluster Counting in Future Drift Chambers
items.abstract: Cluster counting ($dN/dx$) measures discrete ionization occurrences along a charged particle track traversing a gaseous medium and is currently being proposed to serve particle identification (PID) in next-generation drift chambers, as it is expected to offer higher separation power than the traditional approach based on the ionization energy loss measurement ($dE/dx$), which has intrinsically larger statistical fluctuations. However, measuring $dN/dx$ in drift chambers proposed for future colliders requires high-resolution waveforms, which result in very large data rates. Running the reconstruction at the edge would drastically reduce the bandwidth required to transmit data off the detector. In this paper, we introduce SpikePID, a neuromorphic computing approach applying spiking neural networks (SNNs) to this task due to their inherently sparse computing and processing nature. We show that an SNN with only 529 parameters improves the kaon-pion separation power by 17% over the traditional derivative-based method and by 4% over an MLP that has $8.6\times$ more parameters. When synthesized to an FPGA, it uses an order of magnitude fewer resources than the MLP, and has an inference latency compatible with the constraints of future collider experiments, making the SNN an excellent algorithmic candidate for real-time data readout in future drift chambers.

items.title: Spatially resolved heavy ion microprobe testing of lateral Ga2O3 MOSFETs
items.abstract: Ultrawide bandgap β-Ga2O3 has been intensively researched for power electronics applications after the first demonstration of high quality MOSFETs and MESFETs in 2012. Testing of β-Ga2O3 transistor structures under heavy ion irradiation is relatively unexplored despite its criticality in developing next-generation radiation-hardened electronics for space applications. Single ion irradiation was performed with 192 MeV Ar and 1182 MeV Au and a lateral spatial resolution of ∼0.5 μm to map the electrical characteristics of β-Ga2O3 MOSFETs as a function of irradiation position and identify the most sensitive regions of the device. This work determines that standard Ga2O3 MOSFETs are not susceptible to single event burnout under in operando irradiation under an applied field of 0.83 MV/cm for Ar irradiation as well as an applied field of 0.07 MV/cm for Au irradiation. Successive irradiations reveal transient increases in drain current associated with threshold voltage shifts attributed to defect generation/ionization in the top atomic layer deposited-Al2O3 dielectric or the semi-insulating Ga2O3 substrate and subsequent thermal relaxation. Fitting in situ transfer curve data reveals that the dominant effect under heavy ion irradiation is the activation of the parasitic channel via the generation of net positive charge at the buffer–substrate interface.

items.title: Single-domain, semiconducting κ-Ga2O3 grown on isostructural ε-GaFeO3 templates
items.abstract: The epitaxial growth of a phase-pure, single-domain, semiconducting κ-Ga2O3 thin film is demonstrated. Multiferroic ε-GaFeO3, being isostructural to κ-Ga2O3, was used as a substrate and was initially covered by a high-temperature MIST-CVD κ-Ga2O3 seed layer. Subsequently, tin-assisted pulsed laser deposition at 550 °C was applied to grow the single-crystalline epilayer with a thickness of 400 nm. The structural properties were investigated by x-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy. A reciprocal space map revealed that the κ-Ga2O3 layer sustains residual strain and is only partially relaxed. Consistently, misfit dislocations were observed, indicating ongoing but incomplete strain relaxation. Secondary ion mass spectrometry confirmed efficient Sn incorporation and revealed Fe diffusion from the ε-GaFeO3 substrate. The Fe impurities segregate predominantly at the advancing growth front, resulting in only moderate bulk compensation of the κ-Ga2O3/ε-GaFeO3 layer. Temperature-dependent in-plane transport measurements revealed freeze out of free electrons with activation energies of Ea,1=48 meV and Ea,2=253 meV at intermediate and high temperatures, respectively. No measurable in-plane conductivity was observed for a reference sample deposited on c-plane sapphire, which exhibited in-plane rotational domains and nanocolumnar growth. These results demonstrate that epitaxial growth on isostructural ε-GaFeO3 enables single-crystalline, semiconducting κ-Ga2O3 and establishes the κ-Ga2O3/ε-GaFeO3 heterostructure as a promising platform for exploring polarization-charge-induced two-dimensional electron gases in multifunctional ferroelectric/ferrimagnetic oxide systems.

items.title: Revisiting Temperature Dependence of d I C /d t and d V CE /d t for Field-Stop IGBTs Under Capacitor-Assisted Soft-Switching Turn-Off
items.abstract: Capacitor-assisted soft-switching turn-off (CATO) is widely used in high-power applications to reduce insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) switching loss and electrical stress. Since CATO changes both the terminal switching behavior and internal carrier dynamics compared with hard-switching turn-off (HSTO), the applicability of conventional collector-side dynamic temperature-sensitive electrical parameters (TSEPs) needs re-examination. This article investigates the temperature dependence of d${V}_{\text {CE}}$/d$t$and d${I}_{\text {C}}$/d$t$in field-stop IGBTs under CATO through TCAD simulation, analytical modeling, and experiments. The results show that d${V}_{\text {CE}}$/d$t$is mainly related to the external capacitor charging process and exhibits only weak temperature dependence, whereas d${I}_{\text {C}}$/d$t$shows a clear negative temperature dependence originating from carrier transport and recombination in the N-base region and field-stop layer. To avoid direct d${I}_{\text {C}}$/d$t$extraction, a commutation voltage spike${V}_{\text {cem}}$is further proposed for junction temperature measurement. Its feasibility is verified by infrared thermography, with a maximum temperature measurement error below$3~^{\circ }$C.

items.title: Reversing amorphous aging associated with resistance drift in phase-change memory via atomistic rejuvenation
items.abstract: Resistance drift in the amorphous RESET state limits phase-change memory (PCM) for multilevel storage and neuromorphic computing. Most mitigation strategies slow the drift rather than reverse the structural aging that develops after programming. Here, we use large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a Y–Sb–Te neuroevolution potential to examine atomistic rejuvenation in Sb–Te-based glasses. Aging and rejuvenation are quantified using potential energy, radial distribution functions, global Steinhardt order parameters, ring statistics, and homopolar bonding, which track short-range relaxation, topological ordering, and bond rearrangement. Binary Sb–Te models first establish competing thermal pathways: low-temperature annealing promotes energetic relaxation and ordering, whereas high-temperature reheating followed by requenching restores higher-energy, less-aged amorphous states while avoiding prolonged residence in the crystallization-prone window. In Y-doped Sb2Te3, Y reduces energetic relaxation, delays four-membered-ring ordering, and reduces bonding fluctuations while preserving reversible rejuvenation. Device-scale simulations further show that rejuvenation pulses reset key aging-sensitive descriptors in a 6.5 × 105-atom mushroom-cell PCM model. These results demonstrate that atomistic rejuvenation can reverse aging-sensitive structural features in Sb–Te-based PCM glasses, providing a structural route toward mitigating resistance drift.

items.title: Revelation of charge injection barrier at metal/thermal degraded epoxy resin interface by molecular dynamics and first-principles calculation
items.abstract: Molecular defects caused by the thermally degraded epoxy resin (EP) play significant roles in space charges of insulation in high-voltage power devices. This paper investigates the influence of molecular by-products of thermal degraded EP on charge injection at the electrode/EP interface. Interface structure models of the Cu (111) electrode/EP thermal decomposition molecules were studied by molecular simulation. Thermally degraded EP introduces CO, CO2, CH2O, H2O, and various small organic molecules. Compared to that of pure EP (3.08 eV), the majority of molecular defects enhance electron injection by reducing the electron injection barrier. Ethylene and vinyl alcohol reduce the electron injection barrier (∼1.6 eV). The carbon–carbon double bond (C=C) exhibits a significant decrease in the injection barrier. However, the hole injection barrier for all molecular products is higher than that of the epoxy molecular fragment. Except for formaldehyde and phenol molecules, space charge accumulation at the interface increases with the thermal degradation of EP. The Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and ultraviolet-visible spectra of the aged EP samples verify the molecular dynamics simulation results. The findings are useful for improving the reliability of insulation in high-power density electric devices.

items.title: Research on the Development Status and Patent Competition Situation of Advanced Wafer-level Packaging-Empirical Analysis based on Patents Worldwide
items.abstract: From the perspective of patents, this article analyzes the development trend of wafer-level advanced packaging, points out the direction for technology research and development of innovative subjects, and provides a reference for enterprises to formulate development strategies. This study uses patent information analysis as the core research method to systematically reveal the technological evolution trajectory and competitive situation in this field. The data retrieval in this study adopts the method of "retrieval validation analysis reasons continuation retrieval validation", which is repeated to achieve the retrieval goal, and the retrieval results are manually denoised to obtain the analysis dataset. Research has found that the number of patent applications in the field of wafer-level advanced packaging worldwide has shown a phased increase, and China has become the main technology source country and layout region. From the perspective of technology distribution, packaging structure is the focus of research and development, with bump technology and fan-out packaging process dominating. The main competitors in the industry are enterprises, and Chinese enterprises have significantly enhanced their competitiveness through mergers and acquisitions and international layout. This article provides a review of the development of wafer-level packaging technology from a patent perspective, providing certain support for innovative entities to grasp the technological situation and competition. How to combine patents and papers for analysis in order to draw more valuable conclusions is a question worth exploring. Based on the research results, this article proposes suggestions from the perspectives of core technology research, regional coordinated development, expanding overseas markets, and strengthening industry-university cooperation, providing a reference for policy formulation and corporate strategy.

items.title: Reliable Ru‐Based CBRAM Synapses for Energy‐Efficient Neuromorphic Computing: Suppressing Filament Overgrowth and Read Noise via Ru‐Pt Alloy and AlOx Engineering
items.abstract: Transition metal‐based conductive‐bridge RAM offers superior non‐volatility and stable low‐resistance states in the MΩ resistance range compared to noble metal (Ag, Cu) counterparts; however, achieving stable multi‐level operation with low read noise under low‐current conditions remains a critical challenge. This study reports a dual‐material engineering strategy altering filament transport by combining a Ru–Pt alloy electrode with an AlOx switching layer. Pt incorporation suppresses excessive Ru ion injection, while the low‐defect‐density AlOx matrix stabilizes filament evolution, leading to a nanocluster‐based conductive pathway rather than a continuous metallic filament. Temperature‐dependent electrical measurements reveal thermally activated hopping conduction (Ea ∼0.44 eV), and current–voltage analysis indicates hopping distances of 1.0–1.9 nm across resistance states, confirming gradual inter‐cluster spacing modulation. This filament structure enables 16 distinct conductance states with reduced read noise over TaOx‐ and HfOx‐based devices. Incorporated into a convolutional spiking neural network framework, the device achieves 80.97% FMNIST inference accuracy (post‐training quantization only) and ultralow inference energy of 0.817 pJ/inference in the FC layer—roughly three orders of magnitude lower than Ag‐ and Cu‐based ECM systems. These results establish a direct link between materials design, filament physics, and system‐level performance, highlighting dual‐material engineering as a pathway toward energy‐efficient, high‐density analog synaptic devices.

items.title: Random telegraph noise and excess leakage current due to extended defects in GaN pn and p–i–n diodes on Si substrate
items.abstract: Mechanisms of excess leakage current (ELC) and random telegraph noise (RTN) fluctuations are investigated in p-GaN/n-Al0.03Ga0.97N (pn) and p-GaN/i-Al0.2Ga0.8N/n-Al0.03Ga0.97N (p–i–n) diode devices on Si substrates. RTN at both bias polarizations is observed in devices exhibiting reverse ELC associated with localized light emission spots due to extended defect (ED). Analysis of RTN amplitude and mean pulse widths as a function of bias indicates that RTN is due to fluctuations in ELC. The RTN shows large relative amplitude up to 30% at room temperature and 50% at 78 K. In addition, a weak temperature dependence of ELC is observed at reverse bias, which indicates that the ELC flows through a narrow constriction with a high electric field at ED. Impurity segregation and strain-induced bandgap reduction at a dislocation are considered to be the origin of the constriction. The observed forward bias dependence of RTN mean pulse widths is explained in terms of capture and/or emission events on an RTN-controlling defect which is located in the constriction. An RTN model for p–i–n diodes is proposed, which relates the experimental data to the spatial positions of recombination centers and the RTN-controlling defect.

items.title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
items.abstract: Defect engineering of memristive materials offers a powerful strategy for regulating ionic transport and analog resistive switching required for neuromorphic computing. Here, we report a wet chemical synthesis route for chloride-vacancy (VCl) engineering in lead-free all-inorganic KCuCl3-x thin films and establish a direct correlation between defect concentration, electronic structure, transport dynamics, and neuromorphic performance. Controlled precursor-ratio variation systematically tunes the VCl concentration in KCuCl3-x thin films, driving preferential vacancy formation at the terminal chloride sites, band-gap narrowing, and enhanced electronic disorder. W/KCuCl3-x/FTO memristors exhibit stable bipolar VCM-type resistive switching, with increasing VCl concentration promoting forming-free operation. An optimal VCl concentration (~ 1.3*10^21 cm^-3) provides a balance between ionic mobility and defect controllability, resulting in highly linear potentiation/depression characteristics and superior pulse endurance (>104 cycles). When the experimentally measured conductance characteristics of the optimized memristor are implemented as synaptic weights in artificial neural network simulations, recognition accuracies of 98.96% and 91.82% are achieved on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, respectively. These findings establish precursor ratio-controlled VCl engineering as an effective strategy for simultaneously optimizing ionic transport, analog switching, and neuromorphic learning in lead-free halide perovskite memristors, providing a general materials design principle for energy-efficient neuromorphic electronics.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing and Its Applications in Decision Making
items.abstract: The proposed review combines an analysis of event-driven encoding, spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and reward-modulated learning rules with a discussion of how these mechanisms translate into real-time, low-power decision-making pipelines for robotics, autonomous navigation, and financial signal processing. A simulated spiking decision-network is described and evaluated on benchmark event-based datasets, comparing its accuracy, latency, and energy consumption against conventional artificial neural network (ANN) baselines. The results indicate that neuromorphic decision-making systems can achieve competitive accuracy while consuming substantially less energy and responding with lower latency, making them attractive for edge and real-time autonomous applications.

items.title: Negative-capacitance germanium-on-AlAs nanosheet FETs for ultra-low-power logic applications
items.abstract: Abstract This work presents the design and circuit-level evaluation of a lattice-matched germanium (Ge)-on-AlAs nanosheet field-effect transistor (NSFET) architecture incorporating a negative-capacitance (NC) gate stack for ultra-low-power logic applications. A calibrated Ge NSFET baseline was first established, followed by systematic optimization of nanosheet geometry, aspect ratio (scaled from 1 to 1/3), and sheet count (from 1 to 3) to maximize the I ON / I OFF ratio to 8.6 × 10 4 at a supply voltage of V DD = 0.5 V. Integration of a ferroelectric Hf 0.67 Zr 0.33 O 2 layer into the gate stack enabled marginal subthreshold slope reduction but increased I ON / I OFF to 1.1 × 10 5 for the n-NSFET at an aspect ratio of 1/3, while improving electrostatic control and maintaining a threshold voltage of 0.25 V, as well as a drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) of 40.5mV V − 1 and 43.0mV V − 1 , between the p-type and n-type devices, respectively, through dual work function engineering. The resulting NC-NSFETs were used to construct a complementary CMOS inverter, which demonstrated full rail-to-rail output swing, a sharp voltage transfer characteristic, and a logic threshold of ∼ 0.27 V. Transient simulations revealed a significant improvement in switching speed from 40 fs to 19 fs, particularly in the pull-down transition, confirming that the NC effect provides measurable benefits at both the device and circuit levels. These results establish the Ge NC-NSFET platform as a promising candidate for future ultra-low-power logic technologies.

items.title: Near-Data Processing in CHORYS
items.abstract: Data-intensive applications in the cloud are expected to service an ever-increasing number of users and handle exponentially growing volumes of data. Meeting these expectations is a challenge because they require balanced performance across the full memory hierarchy, from processor caches to disks accessed over the network. The problem is compounded by the cloud’s shift toward disaggregated architectures, where memory and storage are pooled across fabrics, thus lengthening the data path. CHORYS addresses this challenge through near-data processing with open, programmable accelerators embedded in storage and network devices. CHORYS considers an accelerator-based cloud model in which Solid State Drives (SSDs) and Network Interface Cards (NICs) execute data-intensive operations such as filtering, aggregation, and parsing directly on the data path, thus reducing latency, energy consumption, and resource usage. The project contributes both hardware platforms (OpenSSD‑V and OpenNIC‑V, built around RISC‑V cores) and a software stack including data-intensive pattern libraries, APIs, and runtime systems for the seamless integration of near-data execution into existing cloud infrastructures. CHORYS use cases illustrate near-data processing in the context of data lakes, object stores, and AI inference pipelines.

items.title: Low-Power High-Speed Sense-Amplifier- Based Flipflops with Conditional Bridging Using Tanner Eda.
items.abstract: One of the major challenges in modern VLSI design is power consumption, right up there with space and performance. Digital systems rely on the flip-flop. In sub-threshold operation, we examine and contrast four different flip-flop topologies: IP-DCO, MHLFF, CPSFF, and CPFF. Both pulse-triggered and conditional approaches are included in these topologies. Very low power consumption applications are now within reach, thanks to sub threshold technology. One advantage of this technique is that it decreases the number of power-hungry flip-flops. Compared to a strong inversion circuit, a subthreshold circuit consumes less power while running at the same frequency. Tanner uses 18nm technology in cmos for design. We test the flip-flops' power delay, power delay product, and average power at a 1V power supply voltage and look at them from every perspective. Keywords: Sub Threshold Technology, Flip Flop, Low Power.
items.venue: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management

items.title: Investigation on the Impact of Memristive Device Variability on Uncoupled Memristive Cellular Nonlinear Networks
items.abstract: Conventional von Neumann architectures suffer from an inherent bottleneck arising from the physical separation of memory and processing units, motivating alternative bio‐inspired computing paradigms. Cellular nonlinear networks (CellNNs) offer one such alternative, but implementations that rely on von Neumann‐style processors inherit the memory bottleneck. The integration of memristive devices into CellNN implementations can mitigate this bottleneck, enabling in‐memory computation with volatile and non‐volatile storage, and enhanced cell dynamics. In this work, an uncoupled Memristive CellNN (M‐CellNN) breadboard cell is physically implemented, and the device‐to‐device (D2D) variability of five nominally identical Pt///Ti/Pt (HOTO) VCM devices is experimentally characterized. These measurements calibrate variability‐aware SPICE‐level simulations of a M‐CellNN array implementing EDGE detection. A pixel‐level EDGE detection accuracy of 100% is demonstrated across five input images, with all true edge pixels correctly identified and no spurious detections, under D2D variability conditions calibrated from experimental data. Since cells operate independently, errors remain spatially isolated and do not cascade across the array. Furthermore, 100% accuracy is maintained under global passive component deviation of 20% and realistic local component mismatch of 2%, with the worst‐case robustness boundary located at 4% mismatch for the most demanding image, confirming suitability for monolithic hardware integration.

items.title: Investigation of hysteresis and polarization mechanism in top-gated aligned carbon nanotube FETs
items.abstract: The transfer characteristics and hysteresis of top-gated aligned carbon nanotube field-effect transistors are systematically investigated using a series of fast gate pulse schemes. The devices exhibit clockwise hysteresis accompanied by polarization-modulated charge transport. Controlled-environment experiments reveal that the clockwise hysteresis window is modulated by vacuum pumping, humidity variation, and nitrogen purging and can be restored upon returning to the original ambient conditions. As the fast gate sweep duration decreases, the hysteresis evolves from clockwise to counterclockwise, a signature of charge trapping effects. The underlying mechanism is ascribed to the coexistence of water molecular polarization and charge trapping within the device. By tuning the amplitude and duration of gate voltage pulses, we identify voltage- and time-dependent regimes dominated by either polarization or charge-trapping processes. These findings are further validated by current transient analysis upon the application and removal of tailored poling or trapping gate pulses.

items.title: Impact of oxidation conditions in SiO2 atomic layer deposition on interface state densities at β -Ga2O3 (001) MOS interfaces with 600 °C post-deposition annealing
items.abstract: We investigated the impact of SiO2 film deposition conditions in either thermal or plasma-enhanced atomic layer depositions (ALDs) on the interface characteristics of β-Ga2O3 metal–oxide–semiconductor (MOS) capacitors, especially focusing on oxidation reaction conditions in ALD. The formation of the interface with an interface state density as low as ∼1011 eV−1 cm−2 at 0.2 eV below the conduction band edge and a low near-interface oxide trap density was achieved by tuning the O3-dose in thermal-ALD, with a post-deposition-annealing temperature limited to a relatively low temperature of 600 °C to avoid the thermally induced damages on Ga2O3. The fixed charge density at the SiO2/β-Ga2O3 interface was also minimized by thermal-ALD with the sufficient dose of O3. These results demonstrate the significant role of the control of SiO2 deposition conditions to achieve high-quality SiO2/β-Ga2O3 MOS interfaces with low-thermal-budget processes.

items.title: High- k Gate Dielectrics for Organic Field-Effect Transistors: Interfacial Engineering, Performance Optimization, and Scalable Flexible Electronics
items.abstract: Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) are promising platforms for flexible, wearable, biointegrated, and large-area electronics owing to their mechanical compliance, solution processability, low-temperature fabrication, and molecular tunability. However, their practical application requires low-voltage operation, low power consumption, high operational stability, and scalable manufacturing, which are strongly influenced by the gate dielectric and its interface with the organic semiconductor. High-k gate dielectrics can increase gate capacitance and enhance electrostatic control, enabling low-voltage operation. However, a higher dielectric constant does not necessarily lead to better device performance, as strong polarization, surface polarity, interfacial trapping, dipolardisorder, remote phonon scattering, leakage, ion migration, and dielectric-semiconductor incompatibility can impair charge transport and device reliability. This Review presents a performance-oriented and interface-centered overview of high-k gate dielectrics for OFETs. We first classify high-k dielectric systems into inorganic oxides, molecularly engineered polymers, organic-inorganic hybrids and composites, and all-organic composite/multilayer structures, highlighting their polarization mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and structure-property relationships. We then discuss how dielectric properties and interfaces affect carrier mobility, threshold voltage, switching characteristics, charge injection, leakage current, hysteresis, and operational stability. Particular attention is given to interface engineering strategies, including surface modification, buffer layers, multilayer architectures, molecular design, composite construction, and defect/passivation control. We further discuss long-term reliability under electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses, as well as emerging dielectric systems, low-temperature and scalable fabrication, large-area uniformity, process integration, and commercialization challenges. Finally, we summarize key design considerations for balancing high capacitance, low leakage, interfacial compatibility, mechanical robustness, environmental stability, and scalable processability. By integrating dielectric design, interface engineering, device physics, reliability, and manufacturing, this Review provides guidelines for developing low-voltage, stable, and scalable OFETs for next-generation flexible electronics.

items.title: High Frequency Power Cycling of Three-Phase Inverters for Aircraft Applications
items.abstract: Accurate thermal cycle measurement is essential for estimating the lifetime of power modules, particularly those employing SiC MOSFETs characterized by extremely low thermal capacitance. This work presents a rigorous method for estimating the die temperature variation of SiC components within power modules utilized in three-phase inverters. The approach leverages high-speed thermal imaging to accurately characterize the individual thermal impedance of each die. The resulting thermal impedance model is coupled with high-fidelity loss calculations to predict dynamic SiC die temperatures during inverter operation. Experimental results obtained under conditions representative of a 540 V / 7.5 kW aeronautical inverter demonstrate the model's accuracy in tracking dynamic SiC die temperature variations.

items.title: FrontGI: Architecture-Aware Parallel GNN Inference on Chiplet-Based Multicore Systems
items.abstract: The realm of high-performance computing has expanded to include machine learning tasks of many forms. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are becoming increasingly popular, with their applications expanding across diverse domains. As the scale of graph data continues to grow, including larger numbers of nodes, edges, and higher embedding dimensions, standardized libraries such as DGL and PyG have been developed to facilitate GNN computation. These libraries allow the computation to be described a a high level of abstraction, providing high productivity on the part of the developer. However, with the rapid increase in the number of processor cores and the evolution of multicore architectures, these libraries often show poor scalability and fail to execute GNN inference efficiently on the latest multicore systems, particularly those with upwards of a hundred cores. To address this limitation, we introduce FrontGI, a fast and scalable set of techniques that advances the frontier of GNN inference on large-scale graphs (over 100,000 vertices) by leveraging graph-property- and architecture-aware design. FrontGI employs different parallelization strategies optimized for diverse graph structures, maximizing the utilization of multi-level cache hierarchies in multicore systems. We evaluate a number of GNN models with FrontGI on a 128-core AMD EPYC system. Compared to state-of-the-art libraries, FrontGI achieves up to 3.35$\times$, 3.20$\times$, 2.89$\times$ and 3.10$\times$ speedups over DGL for GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, and SGC models, respectively, and even greater improvements over PyG, across a range of large-scale, high-dimensional graph datasets with diverse structural properties.

items.title: Enabling nondestructive readout in ferroelectric capacitors for computing-in-memory through interface engineering
items.abstract: Ferroelectric capacitors based on hafnium materials hold significant potential in nonvolatile memory and compute-in-memory computing, yet their on/off ratio and endurance under nondestructive readout remain critical challenges. This paper proposes an interface engineering strategy that effectively modulates the capacitive memory window at zero bias by inserting an ultrathin tungsten metal interlayer at the ferroelectric–dielectric interface. Experiments have demonstrated that devices with a 5 nm tungsten interlayer achieve a capacitive on/off ratio of 1.18 and exhibit exceptional endurance exceeding 108 cycles. This enhancement in performance is primarily attributable to the synergistic effects of charge modulation and localized field enhancement at the interface. A LeNet-5 neural network constructed using this device achieved a recognition accuracy of 95.16% in the MNIST handwritten digit recognition task. This research provides a viable device solution for developing high-performance, highly reliable edge computing hardware.

items.title: Enabling Low-Temperature Cu-to-Cu Direct Bonding via Nanocrystalline Cu and Cu-Selective Oxide Suppression Coating
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and data-centric technologies is driving demand for interconnects with ultra-high density, low resistance, and superior reliability. While Cu-to-Cu direct bonding offers significant advantages over conventional Cu-to-solder interconnects, including ultra-fine pitch capability, lower electrical resistance, and improved thermal performance, its widespread adoption remains limited by the rapid oxidation of Cu surfaces under ambient conditions. Native Cu oxides act as diffusion barriers, requiring elevated bonding temperatures and pressures that increase wafer warpage, thermal stress, and process complexity. Nanocrystalline Cu (NC-Cu) has emerged as a promising approach for low-temperature Cu-to-Cu bonding due to its high grain boundary density, which enhances atomic diffusivity and promotes interfacial bonding at reduced temperatures. However, the increased surface area and high-energy grain boundaries of NC-Cu also accelerate oxidation, diminishing its bonding advantages. To address this challenge, we present a dual-strategy approach that combines controlled NC-Cu growth with an ultra-thin Cu-selective passivation coating. NC-Cu with a grain size of 80 nm and a surface roughness of 4.7 nm was engineered to facilitate rapid low-temperature bonding. A conformal 5 nm Cu-selective passivation coating was subsequently applied to suppress oxidation while preserving Cu atomic diffusion. The Cu-selective passivation coating was deposited using a liquid-phase deposition (LPD) process. The coating thickness and composition were optimized and monitored using attenuated total reflectance infrared (ATR-IR) spectroscopy. The passivation layer reduced oxide formation by ~ 85% at 200 °C without introducing measurable interfacial resistance. Combined with enhanced grain boundary diffusion, this approach enables oxidation-resistant, low-temperature Cu-to-Cu bonding under ambient conditions, providing a scalable and cost-effective pathway for next-generation heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging technologies.

items.title: Electrothermal parameter identification from DC I-V data for compact drain-current models of GaN-on-SiC RF HEMTs: a comparative metaheuristic study
items.abstract: Accurate electrothermal parameter extraction is essential for compact modeling of gallium nitride on silicon carbide (GaN-on-SiC) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) used in radio-frequency (RF) and high-power circuits. This study compares four published compact drain-current formulations: the Fager–Pedro LDMOS model, the Yang model, the Curtice cubic model, and the Cao enhanced EEHEMT model. We fitted each formulation to room-temperature, on-wafer direct-current (DC) current–voltage (I–V) measurements from devices with total gate peripheries of 1, 2, and 4 mm. We used African vulture optimization, Multi-trial differential evolution (MTDE), the Enzyme action optimizer, and the Equilibrium Optimizer (EO) to extract the electrical and effective thermal parameters. We evaluated each result using mean squared error (MSE) and physical-plausibility checks, including the expected decrease in effective thermal resistance with increasing device periphery. The Fager–Pedro model produced the lowest errors for the 1 and 4 mm devices, whereas the Cao enhanced EEHEMT model gave the best result for the 2 mm device. The Curtice cubic model generally represented the largest device more accurately than the Yang model. EO gave the lowest runtime in the benchmark test, while MTDE achieved the minimum fitting error in most cases, although the optimizers used different computational budgets. These results provide a comparative workflow for selecting drain-current formulations and parameter-extraction strategies for GaN-on-SiC HEMTs. The conclusions are limited to room-temperature, steady-state DC measurements and require validation under pulsed, transient, and large-signal RF conditions.

items.title: Electric-field redistribution via high- k dielectric trench in GaN-on-Si AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
items.abstract: We report a GaN-on-Si AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) incorporating a drain-side Pb(Zr,Ti)O3 (PZT) trench for electrostatic field management. The mechanism is formulated using the displacement-field boundary conditions and evaluated by two-dimensional technology computer aided design with a field-independent relative-permittivity sweep from 3.9 to 500. The calculations reveal the nonmonotonic dependence of terminal voltage on permittivity and a broader drain-side high-field distribution for the nominal εr=300 case. Experimentally, a representative PZT-trench HEMT reaches 1405 V at LGD=9 μm, compared with 783 V for a co-fabricated conventional device and 957 V for a previously reported hybrid Schottky–ohmic drain HEMT, corresponding to breakdown-voltage improvements of 79% and 47%, respectively, while retaining a specific ON-resistance of 1.47 mΩ cm2. The dynamic-to-static ON-resistance ratios, RON,dyn/RON,static, are 1.6× and 2.5× after 900 and 1200 V off-state stress, respectively, at a 3 μs extraction delay. These results demonstrate simultaneous enhancement of voltage handling and dynamic performance through drain-side dielectric-boundary engineering.

items.title: Don't Read Every Cell: Few-Read Fault Localization and Drift Calibration in Analog Crossbars
items.abstract: Deployed analog in-memory chips silently lose cells, and the default fix, reading every cell, costs 256 reads for a 256×256 tile. We show that a few random probe reads are enough. A sparse-recovery decoder over random ±1 probes localizes up to 64 stuck cells in a 256×256 tile with 4 to 12 counted reads at 1% read noise, on a simulated tile that is otherwise ideal. For k ≥ 4 faults it needs 4.3 to 6.4× fewer reads than a hybrid that we built from a published multi-outlier code (1.9 to 3.2× if its 8 noise-calibration reads are charged), and at least 2× fewer than tuned X-ABFT, which in this regime needs more reads than a full readout. The sharper finding is where the gain comes from: the decoder, not the second read direction. Forward reads alone already need 1.6 to 4.1× fewer reads than the hybrid; joint decoding with transposed reads needs a further 1.3 to 4× fewer at 1% noise, and gains less at higher noise. For drift, a 16-parameter field fitted per tile from a few probe reads restores programmed accuracy. As a digital correction that needs the stored weights, it gains +2.1 to +13.3 points over the best cheap digital baseline on CIFAR-10 from 1 h to 1 yr (+1.7 to +13.1 points with the 17 MVMs actually run); applied in the array, it keeps +0.6 to +3.7 points. Every claim is graded against criteria committed before the counted runs, and all code, data and pre-specified criteria are public.

items.title: Demonstration of enhanced electrical and thermal stability in NiO/Ga2O3 heterojunction diode adopting Li-doped p -type NiO
items.abstract: Constructing p-type nickel oxide (NiO)/n-type gallium oxide (Ga2O3) heterojunction diodes (HJDs) represents a promising strategy to enhance the performance of beta-phase Ga2O3 power diodes, yet their poor electrical and thermal stability remains a critical bottleneck that limits practical applications. This work demonstrates a NiO/Ga2O3 HJD with enhanced electrical and thermal stability enabled by lithium (Li)-doped p-type NiO. In Li-doped NiO films, Ni3+, as the dominant hole source, originates from the stable substitutional impurities (LiNi) rather than the metastable nickel vacancies (VNi) present in undoped NiO. This mechanism stabilizes hole concentration in Li-doped NiO, thus endowing the HJD with excellent electrical and thermal stability. The experimental results show that the grown Li-doped NiO film exhibits excellent crystalline quality, uniform Li doping distribution, and negligible resistivity variations after 700 °C thermal stress up to 60 min. Moreover, for the Li-doped NiO/Ga2O3 HJD, its forward and reverse J–V characteristics exhibit negligible degradation after 10 ks of forward electrical stress and 175 °C ambient thermal stress, demonstrating outstanding electrical and thermal stability of the device.

items.title: Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor-Compatible Phototransistor Platform for Neuromorphic Broadband Vision
items.abstract: Photodetection and neuromorphic computing promises sensing at the edge, yet most optoelectronic synapses lack spectral breadth or scalable silicon integration. Here we report a dual-gate synaptic transistor integrating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) channel in a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible platform. This architecture synergistically combines the SOI channel for efficient charge transport and signal amplification with the CQD layer serving a dual role as a broadband absorber (300–1700 nm) and a charge-trap medium. The device exhibits a responsivity of 639 A W–1 and specific detectivity exceeding 3 × 1012 Jones at 1550 nm, parallelly emulating short- and long-term plasticity, multilevel conductance tuning, and highly programmable synaptic dynamics. The top gate enables reversible potentiation and depression, and self-powered operation supports low-power sensing and light-driven learning. We demonstrate system-level utility in a synaptic array that achieves pattern recognition with peak accuracy exceeding 96%, establishing a pathway to silicon-integrated, energy-efficient neuromorphic vision.

items.title: Chip-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding using Polyimide Dielectric for Low-Temperature Process with High Yield and Reliability
items.abstract: Low-temperature processable dielectric polyimides (PIs) materials have been developed for chip-to-wafer (C2W) hybrid bonding. By using dielectric PIs materials during low-temperature PI-to-PI bonding test, higher bond strength was confirmed by shear test. Furthermore, C2W PI-PI/Cu-Cu hybrid bonding has been demonstrated with low-temperature process. In this paper, PI-SiO2/Cu-Cu hybrid bonding has been also investigated. For this investigation, a test vehicle was designed to have chips with PI dielectric and Cu pads, which were designed to be bonded on a 12-inch silicon wafer with SiO2 dielectric and Cu pads for daisy chain test. As a result of measuring resistance of the daisy chain after hybrid bonding, electrical continuity was confirmed for all chips. Furthermore, both pressure cooker test (PCT) and thermal cycling test (TCT) were conducted, and in each case, electrical continuity was maintained to confirm excellent reliability.

items.title: Characterizing the Impact of In-Plane Deformation in Die-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding from Die Warpage and Bonder Shape Effects
items.abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence is accelerating the adoption of advanced packaging technologies capable of supporting a higher number of interconnects with reduced pitch. Die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding has emerged as an important enabler for next-generation heterogeneous integration because it provides high-density interconnects with superior electrical performance. However, the process also introduces critical overlay challenges caused by mechanical deformation of the die during die chucking and bonding. In this work, a physics-based model is used to characterize in-plane deformation (IPD) in D2W hybrid bonding and to decouple the respective contributions from die chucking and bonding-induced deformation. The model captures the full bonding workflow, including incoming die warpage, vacuum chucking, bond-wave propagation, and final die-substrate gap closure. The results show that the final post-bonding IPD originates from two coupled sources: deformation introduced when the die is attached to the bonding head and additional deformation generated as the bonding wave propagates during hybrid bonding. Both contributions depend strongly on the incoming die warpage and on the bonder pedestal shape. For dies bonded with a symmetric round pedestal, the in-plane deformation remains nearly symmetric in the x and y directions. In contrast, strip-shaped pedestals introduce anisotropic deformation, and for a horizontal strip pedestal the in-plane deformation along the strip direction is shown to be largely dominated by post-chucking deformation, whereas the perpendicular direction contains a more significant bonding-induced contribution. The model results are consistent with measured die-stretching trends and provide a useful framework for optimizing incoming die warpage and bonder geometry to reduce overlay error in D2W hybrid bonding.

items.title: Cesium based laser-atomic oscillator
items.abstract: We report the first demonstration of a laser-atomic oscillator with cesium (Cs) atoms. A laser-atomic oscillator is analogous to an active mode-locked laser with a self-excited modulator, i.e., atoms, at a ground-state hyperfine transition frequency. Therefore, a laser-atomic oscillator can be configured as the simplest active atomic clock or a self-oscillating, earth-field atomic magnetometer that delivers oscillation signals both optically and electrically. With the current experimental Cs laser-atomic oscillator (Cs-LAO) setup, when it is configured as an atomic clock using the 0–0 hyperfine transition, the short-term fractional frequency instability is around the 10−10 level. When it is configured as a self-oscillating magnetometer using a magnetically sensitive 3–3 hyperfine transition, the magnetic field sensitivity is around 100 fT/Hz at 60 Hz. The presented Cs-LAO uses a cavity length from ∼6.5 to ∼11.4 cm. Ultimately, the minimal length of a Cs-LAO device can be ≤1.63 cm. Our new efforts unlock the potential of building truly chip-scale atomic clocks and magnetometers.

items.title: Back-gate pulse-controlled scheme for retention enhancement in double-gate nanosheet DRAM
items.abstract: Retention degradation in three-dimensional (3D) dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) becomes severe as access transistors adopt nanosheet structures. Using technology computer aided design simulations, the retention mechanisms of a double-gate nanosheet 1T1C DRAM are investigated under all four dynamic/static “1” and “0” conditions, revealing that the band-to-band tunneling-induced floating body effect (FBE) and quasi-static (QS) leakage dominate retention degradation in the 1 and 0 states, respectively. To exploit the independent controllability of the back-gate (BG), a state-dependent BG pulse-controlled scheme is proposed, in which a positive pulse is applied to suppress the FBE in the 1 states, while a negative pulse is used to suppress QS leakage in the 0 states, thereby enhancing retention under all conditions.

items.title: Architectural exploration and FPGA validation of a RISC-V instruction-set extension for Classic McEliece
items.abstract: Abstract NIST did not select Classic McEliece for standardisation in 2025 because it was sceptical that the scheme would see widespread use; the report nevertheless remained confident in its security, subject to a parameter-set qualification. In June 2026, Clause 13 of Amendment 2 to ISO/IEC 18033–2 specified the Classic McEliece KEM. This paper examines a tightly coupled RISC-V instruction-set extension (ISE) within an integrated implementation. Starting from the Kennedy–Halak RV32I ISE, we explore support-list Chien search, fixed-size Gaussian elimination for minimal-polynomial generation, and streaming systematic-form reduction for public-key generation. A direct-memory-access (DMA)-assisted candidate was rejected after integrated profiling showed only 1.0–1.1 $$\times$$ improvement in . We make the inherited design FPGA-executable by correcting its decryption path, moving the instructions into the RISC-V space, and replacing asynchronous memories with block-RAM-compatible synchronous memories. At $$\texttt{SYS}\_\texttt{T}=2$$ , $$\texttt{SYS}\_\texttt{N}=48$$ , and $$\texttt{GFBITS}=12$$ , the complete profile occupies 10,531 adaptive logic modules and reaches 118.89 MHz on a Cyclone V FPGA. Against an unaccelerated baseline under matched asynchronous-memory simulation, encapsulation cycle count is reduced by 87.4% and decapsulation by 86.1% (7.18 $$\times$$ ). The synchronous FPGA build completes both operations with host-generated keys and requires 3,654,113 decapsulation cycles. One reference known-answer test and four directed error-pattern tests pass. The key-generation accelerators are verified separately and in simulation, but software pushes full key generation beyond the 300-million-cycle budget. The evidence covers architectural analysis and reduced-parameter FPGA implementation; production-parameter performance and side-channel resistance remain unevaluated.

items.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. Through the combined operation of these layers, the device achieves a large memory window, an on/off current ratio exceeding 10^6, stable multilevel conductance states, and reliable retention over 10^4 s. Broadband visible-to-near-infrared optical excitation enables controllable synaptic weight modulation and the emulation of essential synaptic functions, including short- and long-term plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, and pulse-amplitude- and pulse-duration-dependent plasticity. Optical potentiation and electrical depression further enable bidirectional modulation of synaptic weights. Beyond these synaptic functions, the device demonstrates higher-order learning through associative and discrimination conditioning inspired by the Pavlovian learning paradigm, as well as reconfigurable Boolean logic driven by electro-optical inputs. These results establish a multifunctional van der Waals floating-gate platform that integrates nonvolatile memory, broadband optoelectronic learning, and adaptive information processing within a single transistor, providing a promising strategy for compact, energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: A high-sensitivity vertical electron–hole bilayer TFET biosensor based on charge plasma for label-free detection
items.abstract: Abstract To address the low detection sensitivity and high-power consumption of conventional tunneling field-effect transistor (TFET) biosensors, this paper proposes and numerically investigates a novel TFET-based biosensor. It induces an electron–hole bilayer via the charge-plasma principle and uses line tunneling as the on-state mechanism. An InAlAs barrier layer suppresses off-state leakage, and the overlap between the bio-cavity and the barrier layer is optimized to enhance device performance. For neutral biomolecule detection, threshold-voltage sensitivity, on-state current sensitivity, and on–off current ratio sensitivity increase with dielectric constant, reaching maximum values of 1276 mV, 1.3 × 10 10 , and 1.9 × 10 9 , respectively. Negatively charged biomolecule detection shows strong charge–dielectric synergy, with severe degradation under low- k and high- σ bio conditions. Optimization indicates that, under certain deviations in size and work function, the device can still detect biomolecules effectively. Temperature strongly affects current-based sensitivities, necessitating compensation, while non-uniform filling favors biomolecule enrichment at the cavity bottom. Moreover, nonlinear distortion analysis demonstrates strong resistance to nonlinear distortion at V gs = 1 V, particularly for high- k biomolecules. This work provides a theoretical basis for high-performance TFET biosensors in point‐of‐care diagnostics.

items.title: A high-performance depletion mode graded AlGaN/GaN HEMT with trilayer cap and AlInGaN back barrier for analog and RF applications
items.abstract: In this paper, a high-performance, depletion-mode GaN based High-Electron-Mobility Transistor (HEMT) is designed and investigated for analog and radio-frequency applications.
