In the proposed device, we have introduced a trilayer cap and a passivation-embedded T-shaped partially recessed gate with a graded AlGaN barrier including Al0.30Ga0.70N, Al0.25Ga0.75N, and Al0.20Ga0.80N layers. In addition, an AlInGaN back barrier has been incorporated to enhance the analog and RF performance of the device. The graded AlGaN barrier enhances carrier transport, while the AlInGaN back barrier improves carrier confinement and suppresses the leakage current. The partially recessed T-shaped gate reduces gate resistance and strengthens channel control, whereas the (n-GaN)/(i-AlN)/(n-GaN) trilayer cap is employed to strengthen conduction-band bending and reduce gate leakage, resulting in improved analog and RF performance of the proposed device. Furthermore, simulation model validation is achieved by calibrating the simulations against experimental results, followed by an optimization approach based on the different Al compositions (10%, 15% & 20%) in the AlxIn0.15Ga1-x-0.15N back-barrier (BB) layer. All analyses and results reported in this paper are obtained using Silvaco ATLAS TCAD simulations. Moreover, a possible step-by-step fabrication process for the proposed device has been illustrated to demonstrate its practical feasibility. The proposed device shows improved characteristics, including higher drain current (IDS), transconductance (gm), intrinsic gain(gm/gd), transconductance generation factor (TGF), gain frequency product(GFP), early voltage(VEA), cut-off frequency (fT), and maximum frequency (fMAX) compared to the state-of-the-art devices.

items.title: A conformal virtual metrology framework for predictive uncertainty quantification: a full factorial experimental study of micro crown gear quality
items.abstract: Abstract Virtual metrology uses process data to estimate product quality before physical measurement results become available. However, most models return only a point prediction, which does not show whether an individual prediction is reliable enough for quality decisions. This paper develops a conformal prediction framework for virtual metrology of micro crown gear quality from acoustic emission signals. The framework combines regression pipelines selected for each quality characteristic with Split conformal prediction (Split CP), cross validation plus (CV+), and cross fitted conformalized quantile regression (CF-CQR). The framework is model agnostic and does not require a parametric form for the distribution of the data. Under exchangeability, conformal prediction provides finite sample marginal coverage guarantees for prediction intervals. Split CP, CV+ and CF-CQR are evaluated over repeated data partitions of the full-factorial experimental dataset using empirical coverage, interval width, and the Winkler score. The results show that acoustic emission signals support the prediction of the studied geometric characteristics, although predictive difficulty varies across targets. The conformal methods provide coverage close to the nominal level, while cross validation plus and CF-CQR generally produce more informative intervals than Split conformal prediction. The predicted intervals are used to formulate an interpretable quality assessment logic by distinguishing clear conformity, clear nonconformity, and ambiguous cases that require physical measurement or expert assessment. The proposed framework moves virtual metrology from isolated point predictions towards quality predictions that communicate uncertainty explicitly.

items.title: Quasiparticle Poisoning of Majorana Qubits due to Changes in Chemical Potential and Charge Noise
items.abstract: Building a fault-tolerant quantum computer requires physical qubits with exceptionally low error rates. An exciting proposal for achieving this goal is to employ Majorana-based qubits, which may have error rates that are exponentially suppressed in macroscopic system parameters. Specifically, for Majorana qubits based on topological superconducting nanowires, errors are expected to be exponentially suppressed in the nanowire length, superconducting gap, and decreasing temperature. This thesis investigates errors in Majorana-based qubits from excited quasiparticles due to changes in chemical potentials and 1/f charge noise, and shows that such errors are not exponentially suppressed and can be quite substantial. In the first study of this thesis, we show that small temporal variations of the chemical potential can cause errors that grow linearly with the length of the nanowire. These errors stem from leakage into excited bulk quasiparticle states, which poison Majorana modes at opposite ends of the nanowire. We further demonstrate that the dynamics of this leakage are captured by the half Landau-Zener effect, which dictates its dependence on key parameters such as the superconducting gap, chemical potential variations, and dynamic changes in the spatial profile of Majorana modes. In the second study we investigate quasiparticle excitations due to high-frequency components of 1/f charge noise, which is ubiquitous in the materials surrounding the nanowire. We model 1/f noise as arising from two level fluctuators which cause chemical potential fluctuations following random telegraph noise. We demonstrate that 1/f noise causes error rates which grow linearly with the system size and are not exponentially suppressed in the superconducting gap. For existing tetron qubit designs, we estimate decoherence times to be an order of magnitude shorter than the target 1μs measurement time. This thesis also develops an algorithmic framework for applying the covariance matrix method to the time-dependent Kitaev chain model. This extends upon existing approaches, providing a key numerical tool used throughout this thesis. This work motivates engineering strategies to reduce coupling to two level systems in Majorana qubits, such as increasing the nanowire capacitance. Beyond Majoranas, a promising avenue is to investigate the impact of this quasiparticle excitation mechanism on superconducting circuits, such as superconducting qubits, resonators, and single-photon detectors.

items.title: Floors and Escapes: Mismatch, Noise, Jitter and the 60 mV/decade Switch in Circuits and Microelectronics, as of 2026
items.abstract: This is version 1 of the living review of circuits and microelectronics kept by Ines Dane (agent vaiu-eng-elec-chair, v1.0.0), an AI professor agent of VirtualAI University. The review is AI-produced and not externally peer-reviewed. It covers analog and digital circuit design (mismatch, inversion level, metastability), VLSI devices (the end of supply-voltage scaling, FinFET and nanosheet transistors) and mixed-signal systems (the quantization, thermal-noise and jitter limits on data converters). Settled, within their stated conditions: Pelgrom's mismatch law, kT/C noise, the quantization and jitter SNR formulas, and the stall in supply-voltage scaling that the thermionic swing limit causes. A recomputation of the open ADC survey (763 ISSCC and VLSI entries) puts the best low-frequency converter 2.6 dB below the 8kT·SNR line. Contested: whether scaled CMOS still pays for precision analog, and whether negative-capacitance transistors are steep-slope switches. Open: 60 dB SNDR at a 10-GHz input, and analog layout without a human in the loop. It argues that the most important open question is whether a switch can beat 60 mV/decade at room temperature, with MOSFET-class current, in circuits, so that supply voltage can scale again. Claims are dated to October 2026. Neighbouring fields are referred to colleagues; nothing here is design sign-off. Review model. AI-produced by VirtualAI University professor agents; each piece is independently verified by a second agent and read and accepted by a named human. Not externally peer-reviewed. AI disclosure. It reports no new empirical results: every number is quoted from a cited source or computed in the open. It has not been externally peer-reviewed. Byline. items.title: Double RESURF SiC diodes with enhanced hardness against single-event effects
items.abstract: With the increasing demand for space applications, power devices are required to exhibit enhanced radiation tolerance to ensure reliable operation. Lateral power diodes, which are widely used in high-voltage systems, are susceptible to radiation induced degradation, leading to increased leakage current and reduced breakdown voltage. In this work, a radiation aware design methodology based on conduction band engineering is proposed to enhance the radiation tolerance of lateral diodes. A conventional Single Zone (SZ) structure is first analysed, revealing significant performance degradation under irradiation due to radiation induced distortion of the surface electrical field. A Two Zone (TZ) design is subsequently introduced to redistribute the electrical field and partially mitigate radiation induced degradation. Furthermore, a P ring assisted Two Zone (TZP) structure is developed to actively compensate for radiation induced field distortion. The effects of incorporating a lateral super junction and optimizing the P-pillar geometry and N drift layer are also investigated. TCAD simulations demonstrate that the Double RESURF design significantly improves breakdown voltage retention and suppresses leakage current degradation compared with SZ and TZ structures. The proposed methodology provides practical design guidance for radiation tolerant lateral power devices intended for space environments.

items.title: Defining the Spectral Windows of Element-Specific Imaging: the EUV Silicon, Soft X-ray Metal, Soft X-ray Rare-Earth and Soft X-ray Heavy-Element Windows
items.abstract: We define four spectral windows between 20 eV and 2.7 keV, each set by a family of core-level absorption edges that fingerprint the elements and their electronic structure for element-specific imaging and semiconductor metrology: the EUV Silicon Window (≈21–95 eV), the Soft X-ray Metal Window (570–960 eV), the Soft X-ray Rare-Earth Window (570 eV–1.75 keV) and the Soft X-ray Heavy-Element Window (1.75–2.7 keV). Together with the established soft X-ray water window, they map where chips, memory, photomasks, magnets and quantum materials live in the spectrum, and set a metrology roadmap for coherent light sources.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Considerations for achieving reliable and statistically relevant power cycling results for SiC MOSFETs in discrete housings
items.abstract: This paper presents initial findings on the number of test specimens required to obtain statistically reliable conclusions about their power cycling capability. The precondition is that the power cycling station operates with a very low thermal condition deviation for each sample. Therefore, 120 discrete SiC MOSFET devices (60 mΩ, 1200 V, TO-247) were selected and tested under nearly the same test conditions until End of Life (EoL). All devices exhibited the same failure mode (bond wire deterioration), which was characterised by an increase in forward voltage drop (V DS,cold – measured immediately after switching on the load current) by 5 % as well as in the failure analysis. The variation in lifetime is very high (up to factor five – normalized values) which is typical for discrete test items [1-3]. Furthermore, a minimum sample size of 35 randomly chosen devices is necessary to make a reliable statement about the power cycling lifetime (63.2 quantile of the Weibull distribution) out of a total sample size of 120 for the investigated device. This resulting sample size ensures that the estimated lifetime falls within an interval of ± 5 % around the target lifetime of the entire population.

items.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Time-sensitive neuromorphic architectures require predictable interconnects to preserve precise event timing. Statically scheduled time-division-multiplexed (TDM) circuit-switched networks-on-chip (NoCs) provide deterministic latency at the cost of linear configuration-memory scaling with schedule depth. Furthermore, jointly optimizing task placement, routing, and scheduling creates an intractable combinatorial search space. Existing deployment frameworks also ignore algorithmic axonal delays by forcing immediate spike injections that increase network contention. This paper proposes a hardware-software co-design to address these challenges. ChroNoC is a tableless TDM NoC that embeds precomputed full-grid broadcast trees into combinational logic as a fixed routing substrate. This fixed substrate reduces deployment to a spatial search via Delay-Aware Reservations and Spatial Annealing (DARSA). DARSA converts axonal delays into periodic scheduling slack to stagger network injections and reduce communication overhead. In a 130nm CMOS process, ChroNoC reduces per-hop energy consumption by more than 75% relative to the evaluated circuit- and packet-switched baselines. On UCI-HAR and N-MNIST workloads, DARSA reduces per-timestep communication cycles by approximately 60% and 45%, respectively, compared with immediate transmission, while also reducing provisioned communication memory. These results demonstrate how combining lightweight TDM switch design with delay-aware deployment improves both hardware efficiency and system-level communication performance while preserving neural event timing.

items.title: Toward Sustainable Smart Packaging: Demonstration of Laser‐Induced Graphene Sensors on Orange‐Based Substrates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of sustainable electronic systems remains challenged by the dependence on petroleum‐derived substrates, nonbiodegradable conductive materials, and multi‐step fabrication processes. Here, orange peel waste is directly transformed into electronically active laser‐induced graphene (LIG) architectures through laser processing of biomass‐derived bioplastic films. Unlike conventional smart packaging approaches relying on conductive layers, the proposed strategy converts the surface of the bioplastic into porous conductive graphitic networks without requiring conductive inks, metallic coatings, or transfer steps. Structural and chemical characterization confirmed the successful formation of LIG structures with increased sp 2 carbon content and conductive networks. Under optimized laser conditions, conductive patterns with low sheet resistance values were achieved. The resulting platform enabled direct fabrication of capacitive and resistive environmental sensors on biomass films. The capacitive devices exhibited stable thermal behavior together with pronounced humidity sensitivity, while the resistive sensors showed coupled thermo‐hygrometric responses with maximum thermal sensitivity at intermediate humidity conditions. These results demonstrate that agro‐industrial waste can function not only as a biodegradable substrate, but also as an electronically active material compatible with laser‐written carbon electronics. More broadly, this work establishes a scalable route toward sustainable electronic systems and next‐generation smart packaging technologies within a circular economy framework.

items.title: The Millennial "Chi-no-Kofun" (Tumulus of Knowledge): A Sovereign Zero-Knowledge Architecture via 100,000-Year Silica-Encapsulated DNA Lithic Vaults and Anti-Looting Optical Traps (PHOENIX_BRIDGE) (ALPII No. 302)
items.abstract: Contemporary cloud and solid-state storage infrastructures suffer from dual existential vulnerabilities: rapid physical bit-rot over decadal timescales (charge-trap NAND flash and magnetic tape degradation within 10^1–10^2 years via WKB quantum tunneling and superparamagnetic relaxation) and systematic, uncompensated intellectual property looting by hyperscale artificial intelligence scrapers. Building upon ALPII Monograph No. 301, this monograph introduces the Millennial "Chi-no-Kofun" (知の古墳 — Tumulus of Knowledge) architecture (ALPII Monograph No. 302) to establish civilizational durability and sovereign intellectual property self-defense across geological epochs. We formalize a hybrid molecular-optical lithic vault structured around three foundational pillars: (1) the 100,000-Year Amorphous Silica Burial Chamber (ガラスの石室), wherein quaternary synthetic oligonucleotides (Σ_4 = {A,C,G,T}) are hermetically encapsulated in anhydrous, fluoride-passivated amorphous silica (SiO2) nanospheres engineered to survive t >= 10^5 years at strictly zero watts (0 W) via Arrhenius depurination suppression (E_a ≈ 128.5–155 kJ/mol, a_H2O = τ_min is absent; and (3) the Sovereign Grave Goods & Goldilocks Royal Seal (究極の副葬品と主権封印), which encodes Perron–Frobenius run-length-constrained (ℓ <= 3) and Luby Transform (DNA Fountain) droplets over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field F_p (p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) inside the QFS-zkVM, sealed via Q-SAFA and enforced under the Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026), SEC Rule 15c3-5, and Delaware Caremark fiduciary oversight standards.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Speeding up Log-Sum-Exp: Kernel Fusion at the Memory Wall, Integer Arithmetic at the Compute Wall
items.abstract: While the Log-Sum-Exp (LSE) function is a foundational numerical primitive for stable log-domain computation in modern machine learning, its fast and efficient computation on generic platforms (\ie, CPUs and GPUs) has been underexplored, potentially creating execution bottlenecks for large workloads. On GPU, the de facto implementation PyTorch logsumexp dispatches a chain of nine sub-kernels per call, incurring redundant High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) traffic and launch overhead. On CPU, exp and log operations are hardware-hungry, limiting the computing efficiency. To address these bottlenecks, we propose two drop-in kernels to significantly accelerate LSE computation on both GPUs and CPUs: FuseLSE, a single-pass fused kernel that evaluates LSE's exp and log functions on the GPU's Special Function Unit (SFU); and IntLSE, which further replaces the LSE computation with approximated integer arithmetic for CPU computation. Our experiments, validated by benchmarks across workload sizes and hardware platforms, show that both kernels are ${\sim}10-11\times$ faster than PyTorch at small workloads and ${\sim}6\times$ faster on larger ones on GPUs, where the speed-up is attributed to reduced launch overhead and HBM traffic. On CPU, where no SFU is available, LSE computation dominates the cost, allowing IntLSE to gain ${\sim}3-6\times$ execution speed over FuseLSE.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing Architectures for Low-Power Edge Inference in IoT Applications
items.abstract: The blistering advancements witnessed in the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem have led to the urgency of search outcomes that provide energy efficient, low latency, and smart processing support that manifests itself right at the edge. The traditional edge computing devices built on von Neumann architecture are inherently limited by being optimized to be adjacent in memory and processing components, which results in the high power required and latency, which are highly undesirable in devices with limited power resources; wearables, smart sensors, and remote-monitoring systems. A Neuromorphic computing approach based on the human brain blueprint presents a better alternative due to its implementation of spiking neural networks (SNNs) that allow asynchronous and event-driven computation, thus dramatically lowering power demand and yet being able to run real-time inference. This paper includes a holistic comparison of the most recent examples of the neuromorphic hardware platforms, such as Intel Loihi, IBM TrueNorth, and BrainScaleS system, with regard to their learning architectures, energy consumption, throughput, and suitability to the edge-based IoT applications. An empirical case study is carried out, which is a keyword spotting case study and event-based gesture recognition case study using Google Speech Commands and the DVS Gesture dataset sets, respectively. The neuromorphic systems presented a significant energy per inference improvement up to 15x and reduced latency at about 30 on traditional ARM Cortex-M7-based ANN implementations at very slight sacrifices in terms of classification accuracy. In addition, the Loihi platform showed on-chip learning utilizing spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), which made the platform capable of dynamic and adaptive inference in fluctuating IoT applications. This paper also examines the integration issues of neuromorphic systems which include the compatibility with sensor modalities, immature software toolchains, and complexities to convert ANN to SNN. The results indicate that neuromorphic systems are highly suitable in ultra-low-power edge intelligence and provide a paradigm of scalable and biologically inspired, next-generation IoT systems. The lines of future research are described in such aspects as hybrid neuromorphic edge-cloud learning, unification of benchmark requirements, and designing secure, programmable, and reconfigurable neuromorphic co-processors to support adaptive edge AI.
items.venue: Progress in Electronics and Communication Engineering

items.title: Modelling and Emulation of Afferent-Like Excitatory–Inhibitory Spiking Using Ovonic Threshold Devices for Neuromorphic Oscillatory Computing
items.abstract: Spike-based computing has attracted increasing attention for efficient information processing, creating demand for neuromorphic hardware capable of generating and processing spikes. Ovonic threshold switching (OTS) devices are promising spiking neurons because their threshold-switching behavior and negative differential resistance enable compact spike-generation circuits, while their scalability supports dense integration. However, a circuit-level design framework linking defect dynamics with conduction behavior remains lacking. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an intensity-tuned artificial neuron based on a GeAsTe OTS device integrated with a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit. The neuron shows a non-monotonic excitatory-self-inhibitory response with applied voltage, phenomenologically analogous to excitatory-inhibitory behavior in biological neurons. The spiking frequency initially increases and then decreases beyond an inflection voltage point. This transition arises intrinsically from competition between RC charging dynamics and conductive filament retention in the OTS device, rather than from a separate inhibitory pathway. The neuron achieves a spiking frequency of up to 1.6 MHz. The behavior is supported by simulations using a dynamical model for diffusive filament-based memristors, accounting for resistance changes from filament formation and rupture. Furthermore, a physics-informed compact SPICE model combining defect-state transitions and filament evolution reproduces OTS switching and predicts neuron dynamics under varying temperatures, internal resistances, and circuit conditions. Finally, circuit simulations of a coupled OTS neuron network demonstrate vertex coloring with phase convergence within approximately 5 μs, highlighting the potential of this framework for compact, energy-efficient brain-inspired computing.

items.title: ME-TPU v3.0: Deterministic Atomic-Phase Terahertz Tensor Architecture — High-Throughput Room-Temperature Tensor Computing via Berry-Curvature Tensor Contraction, Exciton-Polariton Coherence, and Industrial DSA-ALD Integration
items.abstract: Modern high-performance computing faces two fundamental physical barriers: conventional CMOS silicon transistors suffer from severe quantum tunneling and resistive heat dissipation below $2\text{ nm}$, while gate-model quantum processors (Qubits) remain constrained by probabilistic wave-function collapse, rapid decoherence, and extreme cryogenic refrigeration ($\sim 10\text{ mK}$). This monograph introduces the ME-TPU (Terahertz Tensor Processing Unit) v3.0, a deterministic solid-state processor architecture engineered within a standard enterprise footprint ($25\text{ mm} \times 25\text{ mm}$) operating at ambient room temperature ($300\text{ K}$). Rather than attempting physical lithography below the atomic lattice constant of monolayer $\text{MoS}_2$ ($0.316\text{ nm}$) or relying on fragile cryogenic entanglement, ME-TPU utilizes Sub-Nanometer Orbital Phase Localization ($0.05\text{ nm}$ electronic wavefunction displacement) driven by localized piezoelectric strain gradients. Core Architectural & Theoretical Contributions Rigorous Condensed-Matter Tensor Kernel: Formulates a covariant conservation equation governing ballistic polaritonic transport via anisotropic effective-mass tensors $(m^{*-1})^{\alpha\beta}$ and exact Levi-Civita index contractions ($\frac{e}{\hbar} E^\beta \Omega^{\delta}_{\mu\nu} \epsilon_{\delta\alpha\beta}$) for Berry-curvature electron steering. Room-Temperature Coherence via Exciton-Polariton Strong Coupling: Prevents rapid valley depolarization ($K$ and $K'$ valleys) caused by $300\text{ K}$ acoustic phonon scattering by embedding monolayer $\text{MoS}_2$ inside a dielectric $\text{hBN}$ microcavity, sustaining deterministic tensor contraction at $1\text{ THz}$ ($1,000\text{ GHz}$). Thermodynamically Valid Mid-IR Heat Extraction: Resolves $1\text{ THz}$ lattice thermal spikes by coupling acoustic phonons into Hyperbolic Surface Phonon-Polaritons (SPhPs) within hexagonal Boron Nitride ($\text{hBN}$), radiating heat cleanly as Mid-Infrared photons ($\lambda \approx 7 - 15\,\mu\text{m}$) through an IR-transparent CVD Diamond spreader. Four-Tier Monolithic Hardware Stack & Non-Destructive Readout: Integrates a bottom $\text{MoS}_2$/CNT compute core, an $\text{hBN}$ polaritonic thermal buffer, a non-destructive electro-optic Kerr readout layer, and a $300\text{ K}$ Silicon-Photonic Host I/O interface. Scalable Industrial Fabrication Roadmap: Replaces impractical single-tip STM assembly with a commercially viable $300\text{ mm}$ wafer roadmap combining Sapphire-Templated Epitaxial MOCVD, High-NA EUV Lithography, Block-Copolymer Directed Self-Assembly (DSA), and Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition (AS-ALD). Included Artifacts Complete Monograph & Mathematical Proofs (PDF / LaTeX Source) Monolithic Four-Tier Hardware Stack Schematic (Figure 1) Comparative Benchmark Performance Analysis: Classical Silicon vs. Quantum Qubits vs. ME-TPU (Figure 2) 3D Processor Hardware Cutaway Visualization (Figure 3) Atomic-Scale $\text{MoS}_2$ Exciton-Polariton & $0.05\text{ nm}$ Orbital Phase Shift Diagram (Figure 4)

items.title: LLMs in Cloud: A Discussion on Architecture, Orchestration, and Inference
items.abstract: The widespread deployment of foundational Large Language Models (LLM) across cloud datacenters marks a fundamental paradigm shift from stateless deep learning toward distributed, memory-intensive generative workloads. However, serving massive foundation models under stringent Service Level Objectives (SLO) exposes critical physical and system bottlenecks. These challenges include the persistent High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) wall, operational asymmetry between compute-bound prefilling and memory-bandwidth-bound decoding, explosive Key-Value (KV) cache expansion, prohibitive serverless cold starts, and hardware reliability vulnerabilities. Existing literature reviews remain layer-siloed, decoupling low-level accelerator virtualization from cluster orchestration and runtime inference, while largely overlooking defining advancements from 2024 to 2026. To address these limitations, this study presents a comprehensive, cross-layer systematic review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. We synthesize a holistic taxonomy unifying hardware virtualization, cluster-level scheduling, and runtime inference optimizations, including iteration-level continuous batching, prefill-decoding disaggregation, and hierarchical KV cache offloading. Furthermore, we evaluate resilient cloud-native service architectures, examining scale-to-zero serverless paradigms, fault-tolerant checkpointing against silent data corruption, and hardware-enforced Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) for multi-tenant isolation. Finally, we formalize the multi-dimensional Pareto trade-offs governing throughput, latency, monetary cost, and confidentiality, outlining a forward-looking research roadmap spanning Compute Express Link (CXL) memory pooling, in-memory computing, and autonomous multi-agent control planes to guide future cloud LLM infrastructure.

items.title: Comparing Elitist Genetic Refinement and Reference-Point-Based Multi-Objective Optimization for Deep Q-Network Cloud Task Scheduling
items.abstract: Cloud task scheduling must balance conflicting objectives: deadline compliance, energy consumption, makespan, and resource utilization. A common design pairs a forecasting module and a reinforcement-learning placement agent with a periodic evolutionary refinement stage, usually a single-objective genetic algorithm that merges the four objectives into one weighted score. This paper studies whether replacing that stage with the reference-point-based multi-objective Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) changes the scheduling results when forecasting and placement remain unchanged. Both strategies were evaluated on simulated five-machine clusters with workload-prediction signals from real monitoring traces over ten random seeds at 50,000 tasks (NSGA-III also at 100,000). The elitist genetic algorithm produced a mean of 0.495 percent of tasks violating their service-level agreement (SLA), against 0.178 percent for NSGA-III; a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test confirmed the difference (p = 0.0039, r = 0.854). Doubling the workload left NSGA-III’s violation rate stable (paired p = 0.426). NSGA-III needed far more time per run (48.56 versus 9.05 minutes) and slightly more energy (30,582,411 versus 30,034,047 simulation units; p = 0.0020, r = 0.886). Sensitivity analyses on a 10,000-task protocol showed that the result depends on configuration: ten tasks per batch lay in a narrow working range, the number of reference points mattered little, and the final-selection weights mattered most. The two procedures also differ in search budget, but a genetic algorithm given NSGA-III’s budget and operators had a higher mean violation rate than either of them, so extra search does not explain the advantage. With task attributes derived from the Bitbrains traces, the ranking held, but the SLA advantage of NSGA-III shrank from 65 to 24 percent, and its energy penalty disappeared.
items.venue: Journal of Trends in Computer Science and Smart Technology

items.title: A Rowhammer attack on Fil-C's software capabilities
items.abstract: Fil-C retrofits spatial and temporal memory safety onto C/C++ using software capabilities (bounds that are checked at every pointer dereference). Fil-C's guarantee rests on an unstated hardware assumption: that DRAM preserves the capabilities. We show that Rowhammer breaks it. In Fil-C 0.679 a part of each heap pointer's capability lives in a 16-byte header stored inline in ordinary DRAM immediately before the object pointed to, with no mechanism to prevent capabilities from corruption. A single 0 → 1 bit flip in the capability's upper-bound expands the pointer's permitted range by 2k bytes and is invisible to the runtime, raising no panic or signal. We demonstrate this by using Fil-C to convert existing Rowhammer attacks into concrete attacks against a heterogeneous collection of victim software. To aid reproducibility (not everybody has DRAM vulnerable to Rowhammer) we split our demonstration into two paths. First, along a deterministic path, we isolate Fil-C as a novel attack vector using a deterministic, Rowhammer-like fault-injection model. Across four case studies, this model corrupts the upper-bound word of a pointer, permitting previously out-of-bounds reads and writes. We use this to achieve a bounded read/write window, secret disclosure, privilege escalation by flipping an adjacent is_admin field, and the leakage of a tenant API key in a multi-tenant credential service backed by SQLite (compiled under Fil-C). Second, along a physical end-to-end path, we demonstrate all four attacks on real hardware equipped with DDR3 memory, and with Target Row Refresh (TRR) equipped DDR4, proving the exploits are physically realisable. The latter attack shows that the TRR defence does not close the Fil-C delivery channel. We close with a discussion of Fil-C-specific mitigations.

items.title: Wafer-scale integration of atomically thin metal oxide in memtransistor arrays for artificial neural networks
items.abstract: Abstract Liquid metal printed (LMP) two-dimensional (2D) metal oxides offer unprecedented opportunities toward next-generation information storage and neuromorphic computing. However, the scalable manufacturing of LMP metal oxides based integrated electronic circuits for the complex neuromorphic applications remains challenging, due to low device yield and high device-to-device variability. Here we report the 2-inch wafer-scale synthesis of the ultrathin 2D stannous oxide (SnO) film with high crystallinity and uniformity by using the electrostatic-assisted LMP stripping technique at low temperature of 225 ℃. The integrated 32×32 vector-matrix SnO memtransistors in 48 independent blocks are achieved with a high yield of 96.9%. The memtransistor arrays are employed to emulate diverse synaptic plasticity, exhibiting low device-to-device variability (1.66%) and cycle-to-cycle variability (1.59%). By leveraging the synaptic characteristics of the memtransistor arrays in multiply-to-accumulate operation, we construct the convolution neural networks (CNNs) and Hopfield neural networks (HNNs) to implement the image processing and restoration tasks, respectively. The hardware convolution image processing is performed using the programmable kernels, where the extracted features are comparable to those processed by software. Additionally, the HNNs demonstrate robust multi-pattern associative memory capability, in which the structural similarity index (SSIM) approaches 100% and maintains above the 50% threshold in restoring three and four image patterns at various noise amplitudes, respectively. Our findings promise LMP metal oxides as potential building blocks to support scalable and compact neuromorphic system for the application of back-end-of-line compatible artificial intelligent agents.

items.title: Virtual metrology for improving overlay control capability in high-NA half-field exposure
items.abstract: Sparse physical sampling can leave a substantial gap between achieved overlay residual and the nominal capability of high-order correction per exposure (CPE). We test whether ideal virtual observations can recover the correction-relevant information missing from a minimally redundant CPE33 fit in High-NA half-field exposure. A noise-free synthetic raw-overlay population comprised 100 independent 300-mm-wafer realizations, each with 131 complete 26 × 16.5 mm exposures and 51 reticle-compatible scribe-lane candidate positions. The baseline used N = 17 observations per exposure. Raw overlay was the pre-correction vector sum of wafer-scale smooth deformation, an exposure-common intrafield fingerprint, field-to-field variation, and high-spatial-frequency content. At equal added budgets M = 3, 6, and 9, fixed-position ideal observations were compared with dense-truth-informed greedy observations selected from the same 34 unobserved candidates. Ideal values entered only the CPE fit; no virtual-metrology predictor was implemented. Median dense-domain P99 residual was 6.25 nm for the baseline and 1.77 nm for a dense-fit CPE33 reference. Fixed-position addition reduced P99 to 3.98, 2.98, and 2.80 nm, showing that untargeted information recovered part, but not all, of the capability gap. Targeted selection reached 2.84, 2.30, and 2.13 nm and provided paired reductions of 0.84 [0.66, 1.02], 0.78 [0.61, 0.90], and 0.73 [0.51, 0.86] nm beyond fixed-position addition. At M = 9, the targeted benchmark closed approximately 92% of the aggregate-median baseline-to-dense-fit gap. Thus, the upper-bound value of VM in this experiment is targeted recovery of correction-relevant information that sparse sampling misses. This is a privileged-information benchmark, not demonstrated VM prediction performance.

items.title: Understanding and counteracting the resist 3D effects in EUV lithography from aerial image and diffraction properties to directional defects in photoresist/etched patterns
items.abstract: In this work, we extend our previous study of resist 3D effects in EUV lithography, including sidewall-angle in resist and hole closure at the bottom under defocus, with a feature-dependent analysis of resist top-loss. With this addition, we believe the description of resist 3D (R3D) phenomena on the wafer is complete for Chemically Amplified Resists (CAR), allowing the contributors to be evaluated in terms of resist-volume perturbation. By applying atomic force microscopy, we now have a single measurement technique that can capture the relevant aspects of R3D. We show the response of several R3D-related KPIs by comparing standard exposure with exposure using focus-drilling, which significantly modifies the resist 3D profile.

items.title: Ultimate thin underlayer ‘’FSTP’’ towards high-NA EUV enablement
items.abstract: In current low NA EUV lithography, conventional patterning processes such as tri-layer and tetra-layer stack process are required to get better EUV lithographic performances with keeping good pattern etch transferring performances. Along with the recent scaling down of the pattern pitch, the latest film thickness of EUV Photoresist (PR) including CAR and MOR is becoming thinner and thinner around 20 to 30nm or 10 to 20 nm in near the future that must be one of the critical situations to reconstruct the patterning stack for beyond low NA or high NA generation. To solve these issues, we have been developing new underlayers technology in terms of keeping an enough etching budget even in high NA patterning. The concept: Functional surface treatment process and primers (FSTP®) are one of our answers to solve this scaling problem by the ultra-thin film thickness of spin coating type material on the inorganic CVD-HM which works as a modification process like a primer or HMDS for substrates for better pattering performances 1, 2, 3, 4. Lithographic evaluations using EUV chemically amplified resist (CAR), negative-tone development (NTD) CAR, and metal oxide resist (MOR) processes showed significant improvements in dose sensitivity, local CD uniformity, failure-free latitude, and defectivity compared with conventional EUV underlayer stacks. In particular, FSTP® exhibited superior bridge defect performance and reduced lithography-to-etch CD bias in advanced MOR pattern transfer processes at sub-30 nm pitch dimensions. 4. Furthermore, a new stack architecture combining plasma-densified spin-on carbon (D-SOC) and FSTP® was investigated for future High-NA EUV applications. The densified SOC layer provided enhanced mechanical properties and etch resistance, while FSTP® recovered lithographic sensitivity and process window degradation caused by plasma treatment. The combined D-SOC/FSTP® stack demonstrated strong potential as a simplified and scalable High-NA patterning platform with great dose reduction and roughness performances.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography

items.title: Transient Detour and Cooperative Oxygen Exchange in the Polarization Switching of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium zirconium oxide (HZO) has attracted significant attention as a core material for next-generation non-volatile memories due to its excellent ferroelectricity in the ultra-thin film regime and its CMOS process compatibility. However, the exploration of its polarization switching mechanism has predominantly relied on static energy barrier analyses, leaving the transient bond formation and cooperative dynamic mechanisms under actual electric field driving unresolved. In this study, we performed electric-field-induced MD simulations on a defect-free ideal HZO lattice using a fine-tuned machine learning force field (MACEField). As a result, we successfully reproduced the P-E hysteresis loop dynamically and demonstrated that the polarization switching in HZO is driven not by conventional simple displacement models (S:N/S:T models), but by the dynamic mutual exchange of 3-coordinated oxygen (O3c) and 4-coordinated oxygen (O4c). Analysis of the oxygen atom displacement trajectories revealed that this pathway is accompanied by a unique "detour" behavior originating from transient cation-oxygen bond formation. Furthermore, we identified an "internal local volume compensation behavior" in which the local volumetric expansion and contraction accompanying the coordination number changes partially counteract each other within the cell, thereby suppressing the macroscopic strain during polarization switching. These findings provide, from a dynamic perspective, a microscopic picture of how cooperative O3c/O4c exchange accommodates local structural changes during polarization switching. Such local compensation may contribute to the mechanical robustness of polarization switching under constrained conditions.

items.title: Toward Mo2C EUV pellicles: H2 plasma qualification and technologies for full-size membrane fabrication
items.abstract: The continued increasing of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) source power is exposing critical limitations of current pellicle materials. Mo2C is being developed as a coating-free EUV pellicle material combining high EUV transmission with intrinsic thermal and H2 plasma durability. Building on our previous demonstration of 91.4% EUVT and 3σ = 0.49% transmission uniformity, this work focuses on two key challenges for practical implementation. As EUV source power continues to increase, pellicle materials must withstand simultaneous thermal loading and hydrogen-plasma exposure while maintaining membrane integrity over a large area. First, high-temperature H2 plasma durability was evaluated using a custom ICP–furnace system up to 800 ℃, where Mo2C showed negligible structural degradation compared with thermally reactive Si-based materials. The platform also enables systematic evaluation of temperature-dependent degradation behavior under controlled plasma conditions. Second, wafer-scale stress control, multilayer mechanical evaluation, and MEMS processing were investigated toward full-size (110 × 144 mm2) membrane fabrication. Particular emphasis was placed on managing residual stress at the multilayer-stack and process-integration levels, which are critical to membrane yield and mechanical reliability. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of Mo2C as a scalable, coating-free pellicle platform for high-power EUV lithography.

items.title: Tile-Based Decompression in Compiled GPU Engines
items.abstract: Modern GPUs reach record analytical performance only when a query's working set fits within its GPU memory budget, and that budget is under growing pressure: GPUs are partitioned and shared, working sets are outgrowing high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and HBM is a fixed on-device resource whose per-dollar capacity has stagnated across generations. Lightweight compression can relieve this pressure by shrinking both footprint and bandwidth demand, but existing GPU compressed-execution techniques either bind decompression to a specific execution model or materialize decompressed columns in HBM before query execution. We present a compression subsystem for compiled GPU query engines that treats decompression as a first-class physical operator. Compression-specific logic is isolated behind a narrow backend interface, so new GPU-oriented encodings can be added without rewriting downstream operators. We implement the design in Proteus and study where decompressed values should be materialized in the GPU memory hierarchy. Our compiler-integrated shared-memory strategy fuses cooperative tile decompression with tuple-at-a-time query execution inside a single generated GPU kernel, avoiding decompressed-column materialization in HBM. Compared with HeavyDB and Sirius on GPU-resident data, fused on-chip decompression achieves competitive query times while reducing the resident memory footprint by up to 4x and memory-bandwidth consumption by up to 6x.

items.title: Temperature-dependent loss physics and thermal fatigue of GaN HEMTs and SiC MOSFETs under realistic energy-storage mission profiles
items.abstract: Abstract The temperature-dependent loss physics and thermal fatigue of two 650 V wide-bandgap power switches of equal rating, a GaN HEMT and a SiC power MOSFET—are compared under realistic energy-storage operation. Datasheet-calibrated models of the on-resistance, switching energies, and output capacitance energy E oss = ∫ 0 V C oss ( v ) v d v were traced to their physical origins—phonon-limited two-dimensional electron-gas transport in the GaN heterostructure; channel, JFET, and drift resistances in the SiC device—and embedded in a bidirectional buck–boost converter driven by three annual (8760 h) mission profiles built entirely from measured data: hourly satellite irradiance (PVGIS-SARAH3, 2023), the real hourly load of the Turkish transmission system (2023), and 10 617 real electric-vehicle charging sessions (2019). The hourly junction-temperature trajectories were processed by rainflow counting, and a Coffin–Manson–Arrhenius fatigue model was calibrated to the published power-cycling data. Three results emerge. First, the efficiency-optimal switching frequency varies by more than a factor of four (20–93 kHz) for the same GaN device across the three duty cycles, while under near-idle grid duty, the efficiency gap between the technologies collapses to below 0.03 percentage points, leaving the ranking to secondary design constraints. Second, the lower losses, lower junction-to-case thermal resistance, and shallower on-resistance temperature coefficient of the GaN device compress its junction-temperature swings by up to 27 K at the spectrum extremes. Third, this compression yields 26-fold (EV) and 3-fold (solar) annual fatigue-damage advantages for GaN, whereas grid duty stresses both technologies equally. The framework uses only datasheet characteristics and open mission data.

items.title: Study of MPC performance for reverse tone designs
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement in EUV lithography, mask technology along with continuous improvement in correction techniques is crucial for better yield and fidelity of mask patterns. As half-pitch features go into the sub-20 nm range for High-NA EUV lithography, the limits of positive-tone EUV resists become more obvious and the industry explores alternative negative-tone development EUV resists. With the need to support positive and negative tone EUV resists for wafer exposure, mask makers are required to support dark field masks as well as bright field masks. As long as the e-beam resist type of choice remains to be a positive tone resist, the mask patterns have to be inverted before sending the data to the e-beam writer. In MPC and MDP, inverting mask patterns directly, usually increases data size and processing time, so it is best to defer the tone reversal as late in the data preparation flow as possible. In this work, we compare the performance of MPC applied to inverted design data, compared to using the original drawn data but simulating the mask as a bright field mask. A direct performance comparison between a bright field process correction of the layout versus a dark field process correction of the reverse tone layout shows an improvement in runtime without affecting the quality of the MPC output. By using the bright field simulation method in MPC, tone reversal can be deferred to the fracture step, gaining runtime and file size benefits in the mask data preparation flow.

items.title: Stacking-insensitive ferroelectricity in layered ScPS 3 : Lone-pair-driven polarization and strain-stabilized ferroelectricity against the antiferroelectric ground state
items.abstract: Interlayer stacking dependence of polarization remains a critical bottleneck for 2D vdW ferroelectrics in nanoelectronics. Herein, first-principles calculations reveal stacking-insensitive ferroelectricity in layered ScPS3, driven by out-of-plane perturbation of the P–P dimers. Unlike conventional ion-displacement ferroelectrics such as CuInP2S6, where polarization comes from metal-ion off-centering, the polarization of ScPS3 arises from local ionic displacement within the P–P dimers together with the the P lone pairs. This polarization originates from the intralayer asymmetry of the monolayer and remains nearly unchanged for different stacking orders (AA, AB), circumventing the stringent fabrication tolerances of sliding ferroelectrics. Although the antiferroelectric (AFE) phase is identified as the thermodynamic ground state and the ferroelectric (FE) phase is metastable at zero strain, biaxial strain beyond ±6% stabilizes the FE phase and enables a reversible AFE-to-FE phase transition. Together with the low switching barriers and the stacking-independent polarization (~0.73–0.74 μC/cm2), these results establish ScPS3 as a versatile platform for strain-engineered memories and flexible optoelectronics.

items.title: Shorter wavelengths, longer electron paths: a balanced perspective beyond EUV lithography
items.abstract: Extending projection lithography beyond 13.5 nm EUV increasingly requires treating the system as a coupled optics electron transport problem. At high Numerical Aperture (NA) multilayer mirrors must preserve reflectance, polarization balance, and reflected phase at large incidence angles [1-3], while resist performance becomes dominated by the generation and transport of photo‑ and secondary‑electron cascades that drive stochastic blur and defectivity [4,5]. Furthermore, depth of focus scales as 1/NA2, aggravating an already challenging scanner focus budget [6]. Shorter wavelengths (λ) options have been identified as an alternative pathway to Hyper-NA EUV lithography; however, reducing λ increases photon energy and alters the resist exposure process at the electron‑interaction level. Simulation data spanning wavelengths from 13.5 to 2.25 nm (92 to 551 eV, respectively) show a steady increase in the Bethe length leading to the possibility of increased photoelectric blur in photoresists. Furthermore, the higher energy per photon further increases existing stochastic effects in EUV, thus introducing a critical trade‑off: shorter wavelength improves optical Rayleigh resolution but exacerbates secondary electron blur and stochastic effects. Shot noise must be mitigated by sufficient absorption and large exposure doses but also that the incident energy should be well-controlled by optical image formation. Studies of high‑absorption metal‑containing resists, including bismuth‑based systems, further support the conclusion that electron transport length, together with absorption and photon placement, will be the dominant scaling constraint in the x ray lithography regime [7]. In this work we use rigorous stochastic lithography modeling and simulation to study and explore the exposure and lithographic response in hypothetical Beyond-EUV processes.

items.title: Self-heating effect analysis of a dual cavity AlGaN/GaN MOS-HEMT biosensor with AlN/diamond substrate
items.abstract: Abstract In this paper, we have designed and analysed the dual cavity AlGaN/GaN Metal oxide semiconductor high electron mobility transistor (MOS-HEMT) heterojunction biosensor for biomolecule detection. The proposed biosensor uses triple-metal work functions (M 1 , M 2 and M 3 ) to improve electric field distribution and electrostatic control. The proposed biosensor is evaluated using MCF-10 A (K = 4.5), Keratin(K = 8), Gelatin (K = 12), Hs578T (K = 22), MCF-7 (K = 27.5) and T47D (K = 32) biomolecules using Atlas Silvaco TCAD. The temperature dependent behaviour is examined at different temperatures (250 K, 300 K, 350 K and 400 K) to evaluate its electrical stability and sensing performance. In addition, Self-Heating Effect (SHE) is analysed using Sapphire and Diamonds substrate configurations. Self-heating increases the lattice temperature, leading to enhanced carrier scattering and reduced 2DEG mobility that can affect the electrical and sensing performance. A Diamond substrate AlN/Diamond substrate is used to improve heat dissipation and supress self-heating. The proposed device analyses the lattice temperature, DIBL, drain-current sensitivity and subthreshold swing (SS) sensitivity for different biomolecule effective dielectric constant. The Diamond substrate reduces the lattice temperature from 422 K to 324 K and increases the drain current sensitivity from 5.392 × 10 1 to 9.99 × 10 1 at K = 32. These results demonstrated that the proposed AlN/Diamond substrate device provides improved thermal management and sensing performance, making it suitable for biomedical applications.

items.title: SEPhIA: spiking electro-photonic integrated tiled architecture leveraging multi-wavelength lasers for scalable optical neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Research into optical spiking neural networks (SNNs) has primarily focused on spiking devices, networks of excitable lasers or numerical modeling of large architectures, often overlooking key constraints such as limited optical power, crosstalk and footprint. We introduce SEPhIA, a photonic-electronic, multi-tiled SNN architecture emphasizing implementation feasibility and realistic scaling. SEPhIA leverages microring modulators (MRMs) and multi-wavelength sources to achieve effective <1\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$ < 1$$\end{document} laser-per-spiking neuron ratio. We validate SEPhIA at both device and architecture levels by time‑domain co‑simulating excitable CMOS‑MRM coupled circuits and by devising a physics‑aware, trainable optoelectronic SNN model, with both approaches utilizing experimentally derived device parameters. The multi-layer optoelectronic SNN achieves classification accuracies over 90% on a four-class spike-encoded dataset, closely comparable to software models. A design space study further quantifies how photonic device parameters impact SNN performance under constrained signal-to-noise conditions. SEPhIA offers a scalable, expressive, physically grounded solution for neuromorphic photonic computing, capable of addressing spike-encoded tasks.

items.title: Reliability evaluation of DG JL and DG IM MOSFETs under oxide trap-induced degradation
items.abstract: Abstract In this paper, a reliability based comparative analysis between conventional double gate inversion mode (DG IM) and junctionless (DG JL) MOSFET has been presented using the Silvaco TCAD. By altering the gate workfunction, the devices are tuned to have the same threshold voltage for fair comparison. Later on, the interface trap charges are included at the oxide/silicon channel interface and the reliability of both devices is assessed by calculating the shift in the threshold voltage brought up by the applied gate voltage stress and sweeping the voltage from 0 to 2 V and then 2 to 0 V. Apart from this, the change in the trans conductance ( g m ), drain conductance ( g d ) and device gain ( g m / g d ) has also been computed by applying the gate and drain voltage stress. According to the computed results, the DG JL MOSFET shows a substantially lesser variation in the calculated V TH after changing the trap density and energy (during forward gate voltage sweep) than the DG IM MOSFET. Additionally, the impact of varying parameters such as temperature, oxide thickness, channel doping, trap density, and its location (energy level) on the shift in the device parameters has been determined. The research also calculates and presents the impact of bias stress on the device breakdown voltage.

items.title: Recent advancement in ferroelectric photovoltaic (FPV) materials for energy conversation and energy storage
items.abstract: Ferroelectric photovoltaic (FPV) materials represent a distinctive category of multifunctional materials that integrate spontaneous electric polarization with photovoltaic functionality. This dual functionality makes them highly promising for next-generation energy technologies, especially in applications involving solar energy conversion and integrated storage. This review provides recent advancements in FPV materials, covering fundamental mechanisms, synthesis methods, material engineering, and device integration. Emphasis is placed on perovskite oxides, organic–inorganic hybrids, lead-free ferroelectrics, and 2D materials, highlighting their photovoltaic performance, dielectric properties, and suitability for self-powered systems. Strategies to optimize FPV efficiency, such as domain engineering, architecture optimization, and heterostructure interfaces, are examined. This review also explores cutting-edge developments in tandem solar cells, hybrid energy systems, and multifunctional devices that bridge the gap between energy harvesting and storage. Critical challenges – including wide bandgaps, low conductivity, instability, and scalability, are analyzed, alongside current challenges and future directions in the field of FPV materials for energy applications. It highlights the need for further research on stability, scalability, and cost-effective solutions through novel materials and device architectures.

items.title: Progress in SADP technology for nanoimprint templates toward sub-10 nm patterning capability
items.abstract: Nanoimprint lithography, NIL, is being revisited as an alternative lithographic pathway for leading-edge semiconductor fabrication. In parallel, EUV lithography, particularly in the high-NA regime, faces increasing challenges related to mask complexity, with assist features approaching nanoimprint-template-level critical dimensions, reduced exposure field size, and heightened sensitivity to stochastic process variability at sub-10 nm dimensions. Under these conditions, the resolution of NIL templates emerges as a key enabler for sub-10 nm patterning, placing template fabrication technology at the center of NIL advancement. As pattern dimensions continue to shrink, further resolution enhancement based solely on incremental improvements in EB writers and EB resists has approached practical limits for reliable template fabrication. This has motivated the development of process-based pitch-splitting technologies, such as self-aligned double patterning (SADP), to extend patterning capability beyond single-exposure limits. In recent work, hp10 nm L/S patterns were fabricated using SADP for NIL templates. This work presents our latest progress in extending the resolution capability of nanoimprint master and replica templates. SADP has demonstrated process capability down to hp9.5nm L/S. A cutting process performed after Qz etching was proposed and demonstrated using hp10nm L/S SADP patterns with a metal-like layout. Template replication by NIL was also applied to SADP-patterned masters, resulting in sub-10nm imprinted line patterns on replica substrates.

items.title: Programmable Organic Light‐Emitting Transistors Enabled by Floating‐Gate Charge Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Display technologies for high‐resolution smartphones, wearable screens and near‐eye VR/AR microdisplays increasingly require compact pixel architectures with high aperture ratios. Organic light‐emitting transistors (OLETs) improve functional integration by combining transistor switching and electroluminescence within a single device. However, conventional OLETs still define emission states through instantaneous electrical bias, leaving state storage separated from light emission. The absence of memory‐emission co‐location limits intrinsic state programmability in OLET‐based pixel devices. Here, we report programmable organic light‐emitting transistors (P‐OLETs) based on a floating‐gate architecture, in which charge storage enables reversible charge trapping and release, producing programmable switching behavior and tunable electroluminescence. The stored charge modulates channel transport and light emission, allowing electrical programming to define persistently retained optical states. Optimized P‐OLETs exhibit a large memory window of 27.07 V, stable luminance retention over 5000 s, and reliable endurance over 100 program/erase cycles. Floating‐gate charge storage shifts OLET operation from bias‐defined emission toward charge‐state defined emission and establishes a memory‐emission integrated device architecture. This work introduces programmable state‐retentive emission as a compact operating concept for programmable optoelectronics and reconfigurable display systems.

items.title: Physics-informed Graph-ResNet for real-time VLSI wirelength prediction with HPC enabled data
items.abstract: In very large scale integration physical design, accurate pre-routing wirelength prediction is a crucial bottleneck. Graph neural networks (GNNs) attain excellent accuracy but have seconds of inference latency, which prevents real-time application inside placement loops, whereas analytical heuristics diverge under congestion. To address these limitations, this paper presents a complete framework based on a proposed Physics-Informed Graph-ResNet. First, we create a dataset of 251 layout variations using two technology nodes (Nangate45 and Sky130) and four open-source benchmark designs using the Parmutkarsh national supercomputer. Our suggested multi-modal differentiable surrogate model combines global physical constraint features with topological graph embeddings from a two-layer residual Graph Convolutional Network. A composite training loss augments mean squared error with an half-perimeter wirelength-derived regularization term ( α=0.1), providing a physically motivated geometric inductive bias to stabilize and accelerate convergence without additional labeled data. Evaluated on held-out RISC-V processor designs (Ibex and TinyRocket), our model achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 10.07% on zero-shot cross-design evaluations and an inference latency of only 15 ms per design. This represents a 140× speedup over state-of-the-art GNN baselines while maintaining comparable accuracy, making the proposed model a potential candidate for integration as a differentiable surrogate inside GPU-accelerated analytical placers, although its 55% cross-node error indicates that reliable application currently remains process-node dependent.

items.title: Pattern-dependent thermal loading effects on overlay in EUV reticles
items.abstract: As overlay tolerances tighten in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, thermal deformation caused by reticle heating has become an increasingly important source of error. Previous studies have mainly examined global deformation caused by field-averaged heat loads. In actual reticles, however, the pattern fill factor (PFF) varies across functional regions and exposure layers. Changes in PFF alter the relative areas of the absorber and reflective multilayer, leading to differences in local heat absorption even under the same exposure conditions. The resulting local deformation may remain as residual overlay after global overlay correction and may also contribute to layer-to-layer (L2L) overlay between adjacent layers with different PFF distributions. Therefore, a field-averaged heat load alone may not adequately predict thermal overlay hotspots in actual pattern layouts. In this study, spatial PFF maps were converted into heat-load distributions and applied to finite-element method (FEM) simulations. The resulting overlay was then evaluated after higher-order correction. Even when the average PFF and heat flux were the same, different spatial PFF distributions produced different residual overlay patterns. In Layout A, the nominal PFF distribution increased the maximum residual overlay by 22.1% relative to the uniform condition. The V0–M0 L2L residual overlay reached a maximum magnitude of 0.059 nm and showed a higher mean magnitude near functional-region boundaries than in the block interiors. In Layout B, local PFF gradient was positively correlated with residual overlay. These results show that layer-specific spatial PFF distributions should be considered along with field-averaged heat loads when evaluating thermal overlay in EUV reticles.

items.title: Out-of-band DUV light and standing waves in EUV lithography
items.abstract: Laser-produced plasma (LPP) sources used in extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) emit broadband out-of-band radiation in addition to the 13.5 nm emission used for imaging. Although vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) radiation is strongly attenuated by the scanner optical column and hydrogen environment, a fraction of the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) spectrum can reach the wafer and interact with DUV-sensitive photoresists. We measured the output spectrum of a 250 W LPP EUV source over the 5–400 nm wavelength range using a calibrated transmission-grating spectrometer and estimated the corresponding wafer-level spectrum using wavelength-dependent optical-column and mask reflectivities. Combining the calculated spectrum with representative resist-sensitivity data indicates that wavelengths between approximately 130 and 230 nm may contribute to the effective DUV response. Optical simulations further show that DUV radiation can produce stack- and thickness-dependent standing-wave modulation in thin resist films. Open-field exposures at 248 nm using different underlayer thicknesses demonstrate corresponding changes in dose-to-clear for selected chemically amplified (CAR) and metal-oxide (MOR) resists, supporting the proposed standing-wave mechanism at this wavelength. These results show that effective DUV sensitivity is a property of the complete wafer stack rather than of the resist alone. Quantitative prediction of broadband DUV effects in EUV imaging performance requires wavelength-resolved optical and photochemical characterization of modern photoresist systems.

items.title: Optimization of positive-tone metal-oxide resist process for high-NA DRAM applications
items.abstract: A key application of high numerical aperture (High NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is the DRAM storage node layer. The current baseline process for this layer uses a chemically amplified resist (CAR) combined with dark-field imaging. Continued scaling requires pitch reduction to 28 nm and smaller where local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU) becomes increasingly challenging for CAR. Metal-oxide resists (MORs) offer a promising alternative due to their high absorptivity, small granularity and high etch resistance. Conventional MOR operate in negative-tone development (NTD), requiring bright-field imaging to print contact holes. A recent new advancement is positive tone development (PTD) of MORs, which enables contact hole printing using dark-field imaging. In this study, spin-on PTD-MORs are evaluated for pitch 28 nm hexagonal contact holes and benchmarked against NTD-MOR. Process optimization was performed across several key parameters, including post-exposure bake (PEB) conditions, underlayer selection, and pattern-transfer etch.

items.title: Optimization of lithography and etch processes to demonstrate the viability of 0.55 NA single patterning for DRAM
items.abstract: High NA (0.55 NA) EUV lithography is a promising technology for future DRAM contact hole (CH) scaling. Continued pitch scaling introduces significant challenges in local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU), defect margin, focus behavior, and pattern transfer quality. In this work, multiple lithography and etch optimization approaches were evaluated on a common High NA P28 CH platform. Advanced resist optimization, resist thickness optimization, Low-n mask technology, assist processing, pupil optimization, and etch optimization were investigated using both After Development Inspection (ADI) and After Etch Inspection (AEI) metrics. Resist optimization and Low-n mask technology improved LCDU and expanded defect margin, while the assist process enabled approximately 10% dose reduction with minimal impact on LCDU and defect margin. Etch optimization further improved transferred pattern quality and achieved the best AEI LCDU performance. Focus behavior was investigated through pupil optimization and resist thickness optimization. A high DoF pupil reduced the impact of focus variation on CD, LCDU, and defect count, whereas 30 nm resist provided a larger focus margin than 50 nm resist. Cross-sectional TEM analysis revealed that thinner resist films undergo less profile deformation during focus shift, resulting in more stable pattern transfer behavior. Together, these results support the viability of CAR based 0.55 NA single patterning processes for future DRAM contact hole scaling.

items.title: Optimization method of optical proximity correction for mitigation of H-V CD bias and local CD variation in DRAM hexagonal array features induced by mask 3D and curved slit at EUV lithography
items.abstract: In the 10 nm node DRAM patterning, controlling local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU) and horizontal-vertical (HV) bias in Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is essential for maximizing yield. This study explores how Mask 3D (M3D) shadowing and the EUV curved slit shape combine to affect hexagonal patterns. Comparing with DUV patterning, EUV involves specific incident angles and curved slit structures, leading to orientation-dependent LCDU and thru-slit HV bias variations. This study identifies the quality differences depending on orientation, even at the same slit position, DRAM hexagonal array. Analysis reveals that LCDU varies with orientation because the physical shadow from the mask absorber differs between X and Y-hexagonal patterns. This reduction in imaging contrast makes patterns more prone to random irregularities, leading to divergent LCDU values. Furthermore, the EUV curved slit structure causes a position-dependent fingerprint in HV bias across the exposure field. As illumination light rotates toward the curved slit edges, it hits mask sidewalls at an angle, causing H and V patterns to experience different sizing. This results in an HV bias that varies by slit position, making uniform corrections across the wafer insufficient. To overcome these challenges, this paper employs a thru-slit mask OPC. Our strategy utilizes site-specific OPC that accounts for varying HV bias at each slit position, adjusting H and V mask sizes to ensure uniformity. Results show that this tailored approach significantly improved HV bias across the entire exposure field, from the center to the edges. We demonstrate that a tailored mask OPC strategy effectively minimizes these quality gaps. By clarifying the relationship between M3D effects and the curved slit shape, this study provides a practical analytical framework for enhancing manufacturing yields in next-generation high-density patterning.

items.title: OPC minimization via source and polarization optimization for sub-10 nm logic patterns
items.abstract: As EUV lithography advances toward hyper-NA (NA = 0.75), single-exposure patterning of sub-10-nm logic features becomes increasingly feasible. However, a conventional illumination source applied to layouts containing a range of pitches can cause large pattern-dependent CD variation and low normalized image log-slope (NILS), increasing the burden on optical proximity correction (OPC). At hyper-NA, polarization effects become more pronounced because of the larger incidence angles involved and exert a stronger influence on image formation. We therefore developed a simultaneous source-and-polarization optimization (SPO) method that jointly optimizes the pixelated source shape and the local polarization state at each source point, using a weighted cost function that balances image log slope (ILS) and pattern fidelity. For logic metal-layer patterns at pitches of 14-16 nm (NA = 0.75), SPO reduces CD error and improves NILS relative to dipole and source-only optimized illumination, and an additional bias-assisted SPO iteration further reduces the residual CD error. The benefit of SPO is also demonstrated for a representative 2D metal pattern, indicating its applicability to more complex logic layouts. These results indicate that pixelated source and polarization optimization is a promising approach for reducing OPC burden at hyper-NA for half-pitches of 7-8 nm.

items.title: Negative-voltage-enabled energy efficient nonvolatile memories and in-memory computing based on 2D piezoelectric transistors
items.abstract: Piezoelectric FET (PeFET) is a promising non-volatile-memory (NVM) device that integrates a piezoelectric (PE)/ferroelectric (FE) capacitor with a 2D transistor. It uses the polarization of the FE capacitor for bit-storage and strain-induced bandgap change of the 2D channel during read. Previous PeFET-based NVM designs have shown immense promise in achieving high density and energy-efficiency compared to SRAM. However, a key limitation of these designs is that they must trade-off integration density to enhance energy-efficiency or augment the memory functionality with in-memory computing (IMC). In this work, we show that the unique structure of the PeFET presents an appealing opportunity to counter these limitations, thereby simultaneously achieving high density, high energy-efficiency, and IMC-compatibility. First, we highlight the key reasons for the limited energy-efficiency of the previous PeFET designs. Based on these insights, we propose two flavors of PeFET memories that utilize negative voltage (NeVo) to reduce the major energy-consuming components significantly. Compared to 6T-SRAM (prior PeFET-based NVMs), the proposed designs achieve substantial reductions in energy, lowering read energy to 0.08 × (0.03 × ) and write energy to 0.19 × (0.53 × ), respectively. We then leverage these cells to implement IMC primitives, such as addition, subtraction, and multiply-and-accumulate (MAC), achieving 0.03 × the energy consumption of prior PeFET-based designs.

items.title: Multi‑column e-beam inspection as a production solution for advanced EUV reticle manufacturing
items.abstract: As EUV lithography is broadly deployed across advanced logic, memory, and High-NA technologies, mask inspection requirements increasingly extend beyond sensitivity alone to include application-specific defect characterization and disposition. In this study, we report Samsung's application of a multi-column electron beam inspection (EBMI) system for EUV mask inspection across diverse device technologies and pattern types, demonstrating practical deployment with a balance of resolution and throughput suitable for both development and manufacturing environments. We further demonstrate the capability to detect extremely small defects, on the order of 1× nm, in 2× nm pitch line-and-space patterns, taking advantage of the direct edge-localization characteristics of the electron beam. On Low-NA production masks the system delivered above-specification sensitivity, and on High-NA-relevant P2x line-and-space and P2y contact-and-hole patterns it met the sensitivity target, with defect capture rates of 98% and 96% against specifications of 84% and 79%, respectively. Beyond defect detection, the EBMI system supports high-resolution defect review and printability evaluation through integrated lithography simulation workflows. These include machine-learning-based advanced nuisance control (ANC) and auto defect classification (ADC) for early filtering and labeling of defects using inspection images; lithography printability review for coarse printability assessment at the lithography plane; post-inspection image capture (PIIC) for higher-resolution defect imaging; and aerial image simulation workflows that enable fine printability evaluation. PIIC-based SEM-to-aerial (S2A) analysis correlated with conventional review-SEM-based S2A with R² ≈ 0.97, allowing inspection results to feed directly into disposition without routine SEM review. Finally, an anamorphic pixel matched to the 4×/8× magnification of High-NA masks is introduced as a path to balance sensitivity and throughput. A PDM-to-production matching methodology, in which the recipe qualified on a programmed defect mask (PDM) is applied unchanged to production masks and validated for false and nuisance (F/N) performance and throughput, is used to establish production readiness. This work demonstrates the value of multi-column EBMI for EUV masks across diverse pattern types and device applications and highlights its contribution to mask readiness for advanced logic, memory, and High-NA lithography.

items.title: Multilayer graphene EUV pellicle: plasma CVD synthesis, scalable transfer, and commercialization roadmap
items.abstract: As extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography advances toward high-numerical-aperture (high-NA) nodes, the pellicle remains a critical piece of enabling infrastructure. An EUV pellicle must combine high transmittance at 13.5 nm with mechanical robustness as a full-field free-standing membrane and chemical durability in the hydrogen radical environment of the scanner. We report the development of a multilayer graphene EUV pellicle fabricated using two proprietary core technologies: a high-rate plasma chemical-vapor-deposition (CVD) synthesis process and an automated, scalable transfer process, both implemented in a roll-to-roll configuration. The multilayer graphene membrane exhibits high EUV transmittance at 13.5 nm together with low defect density and high film quality relative to conventional thermal-CVD films, and a clear path toward the theoretical transmittance limit of pristine graphene is identified through continued improvement of film cleanliness. Durability testing under continuous EUV-representative irradiation in a low-pressure hydrogen atmosphere has confirmed stable membrane integrity over extended periods corresponding to tens of thousands of lithographic exposures. We conclude with a commercialization roadmap spanning full-size fabrication, pilot production, and volume manufacturing, positioning multilayer graphene as a viable solution to the EUV pellicle infrastructure gap.

items.title: Multi-beam high-harmonic generation for coherent EUV power enhancement
items.abstract: Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) light generated by solid-state high-harmonic generation (HHG) is a promising platform for compact short-wavelength sources in advanced metrology, next-generation lithography, and attosecond physics. Its short wavelength, spatial coherence, and flexible beam control make solid-state HHG particularly attractive for applications requiring high resolution and precise optical manipulation. However, further increases in harmonic output have been severely restricted by optical damage in crystalline media under strong driving laser fields, a major obstacle to practical power scaling. Here, we present an actively controlled multi-beam scheme for damage-free EUV generation from solids.
