items.title: A BDPR-Feedback-Based LNA with Programmable RF Metrics in Real-World Settings for Wideband Wireless Communication Systems
items.abstract: Abstract This work presents a low-voltage (0.6 V), low-power Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA) operating in the $1.8-4.0$ GHz wide-band wireless communication standards. The proposed LNA, implemented in the Cadence simulation environment using a standard 45 nm PDK, integrates a tunable bulk-driven pseudo-resistor (BDPR) feedback network with the conventional architecture. Simulation results show a noise figure of 1.66 dB, a forward gain of 14.18 dB, and an input return loss of $33.7$ dB at 3.6 GHz, and almost the same can be achieved across the $1.8-4.0$ GHz wide-band by tuning the bulk bias voltage, (\(V_{bulk}\). Closely matched RF metrics achieved by the post-layout simulation validates the robustness of the proposed LNA against the parasitics. PVT analysis demonstrates its less sensitivity against the process corner variations, supply voltage fluctuations and temperature changes, whereas, Monte Carlo analysis reveals its high yield against the device-mismatches during fabrication. Moreover, the \(V_{bulk}\)-tuning leads to achieve almost the same RF metrics in these real-world scenarios, and hence, offers an effective and simple on-chip programming mechanism in real-world scenarios. Finally, low power consumption (only 6 mW) and compact design (active area is $\approx 0.080$ mm$^2$) makes the proposed LNA well-suited for 5G, IoT, and wearable RF front-ends.

items.title: Stacking-factor-integrated production planning for 3D-Stacked high-bandwidth memory manufacturing: an optimization approach
items.abstract: As AI-driven computing accelerates, demand for High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) manufactured through 3D DRAM stacking and Through-Silicon-Via (TSV) technology has surged, yet existing production-planning models risk overestimating package-level capacity by treating multi-layer stacking conversion linearly. We develop a mixed-integer optimization framework that explicitly incorporates a stacking factor ( S j ) for 4-, 8-, 12-, and 16-layer HBM structures and refines turn-around-time logic to preserve physical flow consistency across extended lead times. Applied to a 6-month, three-line, fourteen-configuration case study solved via CPLEX, the baseline model produced 554,163 chips over the planning horizon while accurately converting die-level output into package-level demand fulfillment; a demand-stabilizing extension substantially reduced production disruption for high-volume configurations relative to low-volume configurations under simulated demand fluctuation. These results indicate that explicitly modeling commercial stacking constraints prevents capacity overestimation at the die-to-package conversion stage and supports more reliable production planning for high-performance, multi-layer semiconductor manufacturing.

items.title: Single event transient effects and variability in hybrid RRAM-CMOS spiking neural network
Screening of Deep Ultraviolet Plasmonic Materials for Enhanced High-Order Harmonic Generation in the Extreme Ultraviolet
items.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense deep ultraviolet (DUV) pulsed lasers provides a bright, narrow-line width source of vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), extreme ultraviolet (EUV), and soft X-ray light. Its spectral and temporal properties are distinct and complementary to the radiation produced by infrared-driven HHG. Plasmonic nanostructures that can confine electromagnetic energy tightly enable the enhancement of weak nonlinear optical effects and are therefore promising for boosting the efficiency of HHG in solid-state nonlinear media. However, the DUV plasmonic nanostructures for enhanced HHG are rarely explored. We identified DUV plasmonic materials through dielectric function analysis of 19 elemental candidates and proposed a DUV plasmonic nanostructure-enhanced HHG strategy to efficiently produce coherent EUV light. Our finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations on nanodisks and nanodisk dimers revealed that Al, Mo, and Si nanostructures are superior for the confinement of DUV optical fields. Further calculations demonstrated that employing a dual-step HHG approach, involving the conversion of 810 nm light to 270 nm using a commercially accessible nonlinear crystal, followed by further conversion to 90 nm EUV through DUV plasmonic nanostructure-enhanced HHG, could result in a theoretical EUV HHG conversion enhancement of up to 107 times compared to direct ninth-harmonic generation at the surface of the solid medium. Moreover, we evaluated the thermal stability of various DUV plasmonic nanostructures under the illumination of DUV laser light. We found that Al nanobowties exhibit the strongest local electric field enhancement but suffer from the lowest thermal stability, while their Mo and Si counterparts with high material melting points are able to maintain structural integrity at the same laser intensity. We believe that our work will provide an accessible methodology to boost the development of coherent EUV light sources with improved brightness and narrow line width, which will facilitate their applications in coherent diffractive imaging as well as advanced EUV lithography.

items.title: Saliency-Guided Replay for Continual Learning in Deep Spiking Neural Networks
items.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are promising for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing, but they still suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning tasks sequentially. This work investigates the integration of Experience Packing and Replay (EPR) as a memory-efficient continual learning strategy for deep SNNs under low-latency constraints. The proposed framework combines Batch Normalization Through Time stabilized VGG9 SNNs with Spike Activation Maps (SAM), which provide forward-only explanations based on spike activity. These explanations are temporally aggregated into spatial attention maps and used to select the most informative image patches for replay, instead of storing full images. Experiments on Split CIFAR10 and Split CIFAR100 show that SAM-guided EPR improves the accuracy-memory trade-off under tight memory budgets, and remains competitive while requiring substantially less storage.

items.title: Polarization Modulation in Se-Engineered GeTe Selector-Only Memory With Enhanced Memory Window
items.abstract: Selector-only memory (SOM) has emerged as a promising candidate for next-generation nonvolatile memory owing to its high integration density and ultrafast switching speed. Although Te-based ovonic threshold switching (OTS) selectors exhibit rapid switching characteristics, their practical application is limited by a narrow memory window. In this work, we employ selenium (Se) engineering to modulate polarization behavior and systematically investigate the switching mechanism and degradation process of GeTe-based OTS SOM devices. A polar-group model, supported by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and amorphous structural simulations, reveals that Se incorporation modulates defect states and carrier-injection barriers and reconstructs the local coordination environment, leading to enhanced threshold-voltage separation. Failure analysis under transmission electron microscopy indicates that prolonged cycling induces elemental migration, reducing the effective switching region and consequently degrading the memory window. The optimized device achieves a memory window of 0.6 V while retaining a 5 ns switching speed. The device maintains over$10^{\mathbf {{9}}}$read cycles and${9}\times {10}^{\mathbf {{6}}}$read–write–erase cycles. These results demonstrate that Se engineering provides an effective strategy for simultaneously improving the switching margin, reliability, and operational stability of GeTe-based OTS SOM. This work contributes to the application of OTS selectors and performance improvement of the SOM.

items.title: Optimization of Stepped Gate Field-Plates for High-Performance MIS-HEMTs on 6-in Sapphire
items.abstract: The stepped gate field-plates (GFPs) structure has been widely used in HEMTs in cascode Gallium Nitride high-electron-mobility transistors (GaN). However, dedicated research on this structure is extremely scarce. In this work, depletion-mode MIS-HEMTs were successfully fabricated on 6-in sapphire using a CMOS-compatible process. A detailed comparison between GFP-HEMTs and source-field-plate HEMTs (SFP-HEMTs) was conducted, revealing that: 1) an moderate dielectric thickness under the field plates helps balance the field peaks at the gate edge and the drift region, effectively suppressing current collapse; 2) the stepped GFPs provide better gate-near field modulation effect than the SFPs; and 3) the field-plate length must be optimized: too long creates drain-side field peaks that degrades breakdown; too short raises field peaks at the gate edge and in the drift region, degrading dynamic${R}_{\text {ON}}$. Finally, GFP-HEMTs with${L}_{\text {GD}}$of$16~\mu $m achieved a high${V}_{\text {BD}}$of 1870 V and low dynamic${R}_{\text {ON}}$of$1.15\times $. This work profoundly reveals the regulation mechanism of GFPs on the electric field, pointing the way for further improving device performance in the future.

items.title: Neuromorphic Devices for Extreme Environments: State‐Variable Reliability and Stabilization Strategies
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic devices are increasingly considered for edge‐intelligence systems operating in spaceborne, aerospace, nuclear, cryogenic, and other harsh environments, where local decision‐making is constrained by limited power, communication bandwidth, and latency. Reliable operation in these environments requires more than the preservation of basic electrical functionality because neuromorphic computation is physically encoded in material and interfacial state variables. Environmental stress can reshape these variables and alter analog modulation, plasticity, memory retention, threshold dynamics, and readout stability. This review discusses neuromorphic devices for extreme environments from the perspective of state‐variable reliability and stabilization. Radiation, temperature extremes, and vacuum or low‐pressure conditions are examined as major stressors that perturb defect generation, ionic and electronic transport, interfacial chemistry, switching pathways, and signal readout. Emerging space‐relevant factors, including microgravity‐assisted fabrication and mechanical loading, are also considered with respect to device formation, structural integrity, and long‐term reliability. Stabilization strategies are organized across material‐level design, environmental boundary control, and programming or readout compensation. By connecting device‐level degradation to neuromorphic metrics, array operation, soft‐error response, and inference accuracy, this review provides a framework for evaluating and designing reliable neuromorphic hardware under realistic environmental constraints.

items.title: Network-on-Chip Technology for Chiplet Integration Architecture
items.abstract: In today's era, the marginal benefits of transistor scaling are continuously decreasing, and Chiplet heterogeneous integration has become the mainstream path for scaling AI chip computing power. Meanwhile, on-chip interconnect performance is increasingly becoming the key factor limiting system computing power and energy efficiency. This paper focuses on on-chip network technology for Chiplet-integrated AI chip architectures, providing a systematic review and analysis of its technical principles, research status, existing limitations, and development directions. The study first breaks down the on-chip network's dual-layer architecture of 'physical architecture layer - protocol mechanism layer,' clarifying the functional roles of each core hardware unit and protocol mechanism and the complete data transmission logic. Next, from the perspectives of topology, routing algorithms, switching mechanisms, and flow control mechanisms, it summarizes the evolution of on-chip network technology and the customized research results for AI computing features and Chiplet heterogeneous scenarios. It then identifies two core current issues—inter-chiplet interconnect performance bottlenecks and lack of cross-layer collaborative design, as well as insufficient dynamic load adaptation and lagging industry standards — and outlines the key paths for future technology optimization. This research can provide clear insights into the technological development path for researchers in the field and offer theoretical support and direction for the interconnect architecture design and industrial implementation of the next-generation highly integrated AI chips.

items.title: MultiBranchFusionNet: A Lightweight Attention-Guided Dual-Branch Framework for Tomato Leaf Disease Classification Using Heterogeneous Field and Public Images
items.abstract: Tomato foliar diseases reduce yield, degrade fruit quality, and cause major economic losses, especially in regions such as Nigeria where diagnosis still relies largely on manual visual inspection. Although deep learning has improved automated plant disease recognition, many models are trained on controlled datasets that do not capture field variability. This study presents an attention-guided multi-branch transfer learning framework for tomato leaf disease classification using a heterogeneous dataset of 20,245 images from South-West Nigerian farms and public sources, spanning ten disease categories. Field-acquired labels were assigned through visual symptom assessment with expert adjudication of uncertain cases and should therefore be interpreted as symptom-based classifications rather than pathogen-confirmed diagnoses. During preliminary backbone screening, MobileNetV2 was selected as the pretrained feature-extraction pathway because it combined strong recorded classification performance with a compact model profile. MultiBranchFusionNet integrates a frozen ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 branch enhanced with Squeeze-and-Excitation attention and a custom convolutional branch, with feature-level fusion used to improve discrimination among visually similar disease classes. Under the evaluated mixed-source image-level protocol, the proposed model achieved 97.28% test accuracy, with macro-precision, macro-recall, and macro-F1-score values of 96.75%, 96.69%, and 96.66%, respectively. Calibration and qualitative Grad-CAM analyses were used to examine model behaviour. The image-level partitioning strategy, together with the absence of systematically retained plant- and acquisition-group identifiers, prevented verification of independence at the plant, farm, acquisition-session, state, collection-phase, or source level. Although combining field-acquired and public images increased acquisition diversity within the assembled dataset, it did not constitute source-independent external validation. The reported performance should therefore be interpreted as internal mixed-source image-level performance rather than evidence of independent field-domain generalisation. The model has a compact size of approximately 15.28 MB, supporting its characterisation as architecturally lightweight; however, practical mobile or edge deployment remains to be established through direct device-level evaluation.

items.title: Modeling spin-orbit torque driven magnetization dynamics in emerging magnetoresistive devices: a finite element method approach
items.abstract: We present a versatile three-dimensional finite element simulation framework that couples a charge and spin drift-diffusion formalism, extended to include interfacial spin-orbit coupling, with the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. The resulting solver provides an efficient and accurate platform for modeling magnetization dynamics in emerging magnetoresistive devices such as SOT-MRAM. Its capabilities are demonstrated through simulations of current-induced magnetization switching with spin-orbit torques in a representative SOT-MRAM cell.

items.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
items.abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. Our Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes, together with published Llama-style experiments, show that our law predicts loss with up to $11\times$ lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. Finally, we extend our law to layer-wise mixed precision and identify the optimal quantized-pretraining recipe, i.e., model size, training tokens, and per-layer forward/backward precision, under a hardware-aware compute budget. Unlike prior precision scaling laws, our law predicts that the optimal precision increases with the compute budget.

items.title: Leakage-aware wide fan-in domino logic architecture using controlled keeper and stacked footer for low-power high-speed CMOS with tag comparator design
items.abstract: Abstract Wide fan-in domino logic circuits are widely used in high-speed applications such as tag comparators; however, their performance is degraded by contention, leakage and dynamic node instability in scaled CMOS technologies. A new wide fan-in domino logic circuit is presented to improve power efficiency, reduce contention and increase robustness. The proposed design employs a conditionally controlled keeper with a stacked footer network to regulate PDN, thereby suppressing leakage, reducing contention and minimizing unnecessary switching at the dynamic node. This results in lowering effective capacitance and improving evaluation speed. Simulation results in 90 nm CMOS technology for 8-64 input OR gates demonstrate up to 20% reduction in power consumption, 19% improvement in PDP and up to 1.8× improvement in noise immunity, along with 1.86× improvement in FOM and reduced variability under Monte Carlo analysis. A tag comparator implemented using the proposed circuit achieves up to 29% reduction in power consumption and 23% reduction in delay, while maintaining robust operation across PVT variations.
items.venue: Analog Integrated Circuits and Signal Processing

items.title: Integrated GaN HEMT-based terahertz metasensor with q-BIC spectral modulation for thin-film molecular fingerprinting
items.abstract: Terahertz molecular fingerprinting of thin films is limited by weak absorption and the bulky free-space paths commonly required for spectral readout. We propose a vertically integrated metasensor that combines a gap-tuned quasi-bound-state-in-the-continuum (q-BIC) metasurface with a GaN high-electron-mobility-transistor (HEMT) self-mixing detector. Radiative interference between an LC mode and a dipole mode produces a finite-linewidth q-BIC resonance, providing a frequency-selective sampling channel. The sector-antenna HEMT provides broadband electrical response. To account for electromagnetic coupling between the metasurface and antenna layers, we introduce an interlayer-corrected cascaded model that captures the effect of antenna loading on the q-BIC response. Full-wave simulations confirm that this correction preserves the designed spectral ordering and reproduces the integrated-device response with high fidelity. The resulting 36 electrical sampling channels cover 700– 1200 GHz. Within the 750– 1100 GHz analysis window, the device-encoded fingerprint features of L-tyrosine, L-arginine, and sucralose show spectral-shape correlations of 0.984, 0.976, and 0.970 with their reference absorption trends, respectively. Further loading analysis and mixture decoding show that the multichannel electrical features support thin-film thickness estimation and binary or ternary composition recovery. These results indicate that a coordinated architecture in which q-BIC pixels perform molecular spectral encoding and GaN HEMTs provide electrical transduction offers a feasible route toward compact terahertz molecular fingerprint sensors with transistor-based readout.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

items.title: In Vacuo X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Insights into the Chemical Selectivity of MgO ALD
items.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) holds great promise for many applications, such as microelectronics and catalysis, due to its capability to achieve precise material deposition on targeted regions while leaving others uncoated. However, direct observation of the surface chemistry during selective deposition, a critical aspect of AS-ALD, remains limited. In this work, we utilize an integrated X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)-ALD system, enabling in vacuo XPS measurements after each half or full ALD cycle to monitor elemental and chemical state evolution. Both homogeneous metal and oxide films (i.e., Ni, SiO2 and Al2O3) and heterogeneous samples consisting of metal nanoparticles on oxide supports (i.e., Ni/SiO2 and Ni/Al2O3) are employed as substrates to investigate the inherent chemical selectivity of MgO ALD from Mg(EtCp)2 and H2O at different deposition temperatures in the range of 100 to 250 °C. These MgO/Ni materials are particularly relevant for CO2 conversion catalysis. In vacuo XPS confirms the thermal reduction of native Ni oxide in high vacuum prior to MgO deposition, with supported Ni nanoparticles requiring higher temperatures than blanket Ni films. Monitoring the growth of MgO with in situ spectroscopic ellipsometry reveals differences in nucleation behavior on homogeneous blanket Ni, SiO2 and Al2O3 films during the initial ALD cycles. The inhibition of MgO ALD growth on Ni and Al2O3 at 100 °C is attributed to the presence of adventitious carbon species on the substrate surfaces, as confirmed with in vacuo XPS. However, the chemical selectivity observed on blanket SiO2 films is not fully replicated on heterogeneous Ni/SiO2 samples, underscoring the complexity of inherent AS-ALD on nanostructured substrates. Overall, this study demonstrates an effective approach for characterizing surface chemistry during (AS-)ALD and provides critical insights into the mechanisms governing inherently selective MgO deposition.

items.title: High-Responsivity and >43.5 GHz Bandwidth Ge/Si PIN Photodetector Enabled by Microcrystalline Ge Wafer Bonding and Smart-Cut Technology
items.abstract: We propose a device fabrication method based on a 5nm thick microcrystalline Ge (mc-Ge) bonding interlayer combined with step annealing and Smart-cut exfoliation technology. High-quality Ge thin films with a thickness of 600nm are successfully transferred onto SOI substrates, and Ge/Si PIN photodetectors are fabricated. The results show that the fabricated device with a$10~\mu $m mesa diameter exhibits a low dark current of${2}.{31}~\times ~{10} ^{-{6}}$A at −2V. Its responsivities at wavelengths of 1310and 1550nm are 0.6and 0.43A/W, respectively, and the 3dB bandwidth exceeds 43.5GHz. The synergistic improvement of high responsivity and high bandwidth is jointly contributed by the Ge thin film with high crystalline quality, the optimally designed intrinsic region thickness, and the small-sized mesa structure. This study provides an effective technical route for the application of high-performance Ge/Si photodetectors in high-speed optical communication systems.

items.title: Heterogeneous Computing Systems: A Review of Architectural Evolution and Design Methodologies
items.abstract: Heterogeneous computing has emerged as an important architectural response to the slowdown of conventional semiconductor scaling, particularly in the post-Moore era. This review follows the shift from homogeneous multicore processors toward integrated platforms that place CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, and domain-specific accelerators on the same die. The transition is closely related to two long-standing technology constraints, namely the slowing of Moore's Law and the breakdown of Dennard scaling, while Amdahl's Law still limits the speedup that can be obtained from parallel acceleration. From the system perspective, the review focuses on three recurring obstacles: the memory wall, cache coherence in shared-memory heterogeneous architectures, and on-chip communication supported by Network-on-Chip (NoC) designs. I also reviewed low-power VLSI approaches, especially clock gating and low-swing flip-flop designs, together with design methodologies such as SystemC-based high-level synthesis (HLS), the Catapult HLS flow, and latency-insensitive design. Based on these 24 research contributions, I organize the discussion into a multi-level technical framework for heterogeneous SoC design in AI and IoT applications.

items.title: Global-in-time Spectral Duhamel-Picard Method for Post-Exposure Bake Simulation and Physics-Informed Neural Operators for EUV Lithography
items.abstract: We present a global-in-time spectral Duhamel-Picard method with polynomial expansions for post-exposure bake (PEB) simulation. The coupled acid-quencher reaction-diffusion equations are reformulated as nonlinear Volterra integral equations using the Duhamel principle. Full trajectories are represented by finite polynomial expansions, with temporal coefficient fields determined over the bake interval by Anderson-accelerated Picard iteration, thereby avoiding sequential time marching. In 3-D PEB simulations, we employ Chebyshev and Legendre temporal bases while evaluating the Duhamel integrals using the corresponding Gaussian quadrature rules. We demonstrate that the proposed method simulates a large domain of $1200\times1200\times100$ voxels on the order of one minute. The representation is further incorporated into a physics-informed neural operator (PINO) with a mixed-transform variant of a factorized Fourier neural operator, which is trained without precomputed solution trajectories. Together, the integral formulation and its PINO extension enable accelerated, time-marching-free prediction of concentration fields at arbitrary times within the bake interval.

items.title: From Soldering to Sintering: Novel Interconnection Technology for SiC Power Device Package
items.abstract: As new energy vehicles and wide-bandgap semiconductor power devices have been used more widely, higher requirements have been put forward for packaging interconnections, above all under repeated thermomechanical loading, at high operating temperature, and at high current density. Conventional solder joints do not perform well in such a situation, since intermetallic compounds grow, voids form, and fatigue damage develops during long service, and the long-term reliability is thus weakened; therefore, three typical interconnection technologies of next-generation power devices are reviewed in this paper, that is, transient liquid-phase sintering/bonding, silver sintering, and copper sintering. Their bonding mechanisms, processing characteristics, mechanical properties, electrical and thermal performance, and major challenges are compared. TLPS can achieve low-temperature bonding and high-temperature service, but its reliability is restricted by brittle intermetallic compounds and void evolution. Ag sintering provides excellent thermal conductivity, electrical conductivity, bonding strength, and high-temperature stability, but high cost, electrochemical migration, and large-area bonding remain important concerns. Cu sintering offers low cost, good conductivity, and better resistance to electrochemical migration, while oxidation sensitivity and pressure-dependent densification limit its practical application. Finally, this review suggests that future interconnection design should balance performance, cost, process compatibility, and long-term reliability for high-power semiconductor packaging.

items.title: Fabrication and Electrical Characterization of ZnO Thin-Film Transistors Using Anodized Aluminum Oxide as Gate Dielectric
items.abstract: This study reports the deposition and characterization of zinc oxide (ZnO) thin films and the fabrication of a ZnO thin-film transistor (TFT) employing anodized aluminium oxide (AAO) as the gate dielectric. Profilometric analysis revealed a ZnO film thickness of 1,308.14 nm and an AAO dielectric thickness of 15,414.41 nm. The optical properties of the ZnO film were investigated using absorbance, transmittance, reflectance and direct optical band-gap measurements. The film exhibited stronger absorption in the short-wavelength region and increasing optical transmission toward longer wavelengths, indicating the characteristic wide band-gap optical response of ZnO. The direct optical band gap was determined to be 3.20 eV. Electrical characterization of the fabricated ZnO/AAO TFT demonstrated clear gate-voltage dependent drain-current modulation, consistent with n-channel ZnO TFT operation. The threshold voltage was approximately 6.20 V, while the maximum drain current reached 2.864 mA. An off-state current of 17.37 µA resulted in an on/off current ratio of approximately 164.84. The maximum transconductance was 3.002 mS, and the subthreshold swing was approximately 206 mV/decade. The extracted field-effect mobility was 4.15 cm²/Vs, indicating measurable charge transport and effective gate modulation in the ZnO channel. The results demonstrate that the ZnO/AAO structure possesses the essential optical and electrical characteristics required for thin-film transistor applications. Further optimization of ZnO microstructure, defect concentration, dielectric/interface quality and deposition conditions could improve carrier transport and switching characteristics.
items.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY

items.title: Emergent Phenomena in Wurtzite Ferroelectric Semiconductors
items.abstract: The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.

items.title: Electroluminescent photoresists make LEDs easy to pattern
Device Design Implications on RON×QOSS FOM in p-GaN Power HEMTs: A Simulation Study
items.abstract: In this paper, we analyze by means of numerical simulations the device design implications on the RON×QOSS Figure of Merit (FOM) in p-GaN power HEMTs to be employed in soft-switching converters. During switching, p-GaN power HEMTs experience dynamic RON increase but also dynamic QOSS reduction, effectively establishing a trade-off between the two device parameters. This trade-off stems from the physical mechanism of hole redistribution within the C-doped buffer. Device design choices such as field plate length, channel and buffer thickness as well as C-doping concentration influence both parameters; however, the relative variation of the two parameters is not necessarily symmetric. Simulations are therefore carried out to identify the best device design choices depending on the target trade-off between RON and QOSS.

items.title: Crystallographic Parity and Inverse Area Scaling in Two-Dimensional Perovskite Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions
items.abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for next-generation high-density non-volatile memory; however, conventional polycrystalline oxide FTJs face issues with defect-induced leakage and degraded ferroelectricity at nanometer scales. Here, we demonstrate atomically defined nanocrossbar FTJs based on single-crystalline two-dimensional (2D) Dion-Jacobson perovskite nanosheets designed to address these scaling challenges. Electrical transport measurements reveal crystallographic-parity-dependent switching behavior: odd-layered (m = 3, 5) homologs exhibit hysteretic switching consistent with ferroelectric tunnel barriers, whereas even-layered (m = 4, 6) homologs show non-switching behavior consistent with paraelectric controls. Simmons-model analysis supports direct tunneling as the dominant transport mechanism through the atomically uniform nanosheet barriers, even at the smallest junction area of 520 nm2. Notably, the tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio increases as the junction area decreases, reaching approximately 35, consistent with the suppression of defect-induced OFF-state current inhomogeneity under nanoconfinement. These FTJs show strong non-volatile retention (extrapolated to 10 years) and reliable switching endurance (100 cycles) at room temperature. These results highlight that crystallographic layer parity and nanoconfinement-enabled defect avoidance serve as key design principles for scalable 2D ferroelectric tunnel devices and facilitate pathways toward ultra-dense post-Moore memory and neuromorphic computing architectures. This favorable scaling behavior aligns lateral miniaturization with improved memory contrast and, together with the metal-electrode nanocrossbar architecture, provides a promising basis for high-density integration if wafer-scale nanosheet assembly and reproducible interface control can be established.

items.title: Analysis on Optoelectronic Properties of ZnO/TiO₂ Heterostructure-Based Phototransistors with Semiconductor Process and Device Characterizations
items.abstract: Wide-bandgap oxide semiconductors such as ZnO and TiO₂ are traditionally limited to ultraviolet photodetection due to their bandgaps exceeding 3.0 eV. This paper examines the optoelectronic properties of a visible-light phototransistor based on the heterostructure of ZnO and TiO₂, fabricated through atomic layer deposition (ALD) of TiO₂ onto spin-coated ZnO films. The study demonstrates that oxygen-related subgap states introduced within the TiO₂ layer enable visible-light absorption through trap-assisted photocurrent generation, circumventing the intrinsic bandgap limitation. Photoelectron spectroscopy measurements confirm the presence of these subgap states and reveal a favorable conduction band offset of approximately 0.08 eV between TiO₂ and ZnO, facilitating efficient electron transfer. The optimized TiO₂/ZnO phototransistor, achieved by controlling the titanium isopropoxide purge time during ALD to 10 seconds, exhibits a photoresponsivity of 99.3 A W⁻¹ and photosensitivity of 1.5 × 10⁵ under 520 nm illumination. This approach offers a viable pathway for developing visible-light photodetectors using environmentally stable, all-oxide heterostructures.

items.title: AiSAQ-in-Filtering for DRAM-free Filtered Information Retrieval
items.abstract: Filtering search is one of the crucial applications of approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS). In filtering search, label information is used in conjunction with unstructured vector data. ANNS provides efficient similarity search in large-scale datasets, however, the memory footprint of storing both vector data and their associated label becomes a significant cost factor as dataset sizes grow. To address this problem of increasing DRAM usage, we propose AiSAQ-in-Filtering, with a novel quantization method called LiPQ (Label-inclusive Product Quantization). LiPQ combines unstructured data and structured labels into a single representation, leading no growth of encoded data. Our proposal increased recall@1 of single-label searches by up to 55% and fewer disk I/Os compared with existing methods. This also retains the main advantages of AiSAQ, which can reduce DRAM footprint by up to 1/78 and index switching time comparing with existing methods. This proposal can also be applied to sparse-dense hybrid search beyond label filtering such as semantic and keyword search of documents.

items.title: A Variational Neural-Field Interpretation of the Stereo-CeNN Architecture in Light of Disparity-Tuned Cortical Organization
items.abstract: Stereoscopic vision relies on the ability of the visual system to estimate binocular disparity across the visual field. In computational models, stereo matching can be represented through multiple candidate disparity hypotheses defined over retinotopic position. In this work, we reinterpret the Stereo Cellular Neural Network, here referred to as Stereo-CeNN, within a continuous variational framework and introduce a neural-field representation defined over the joint domain of retinotopic position and disparity. In this interpretation, the discrete activities of the Stereo-CeNN are regarded as samples of a continuous activity field r(x,d,t), where different disparity layers correspond to populations tuned to different disparity preferences. The binocular input drives these populations according to local matching evidence, while spatial interactions within each disparity channel promote coherent activity across neighboring retinotopic locations. The final disparity estimate is obtained, consistently with the original Stereo-CeNN architecture, by selecting the disparity channel with the largest steady-state response at each retinotopic position. We show that the layer-wise organization and local spatial dynamics of the Stereo-CeNN admit a continuous neural-field counterpart, establishing an explicit structural and variational correspondence between the discrete retinotopy–disparity lattice and a population-level representation of stereopsis. This formulation provides a conceptual bridge between the independently developed Stereo-CeNN architecture and the mesoscale organization of disparity-selective populations observed in visual cortex, without implying a one-to-one anatomical or physiological correspondence. Because Cellular Neural Networks are locally connected dynamical systems originally conceived for analog and mixed-signal VLSI implementation, the same organization is also compatible with general neuromorphic principles of local, parallel, and distributed computation.

items.title: Voltage-weighted effective charge as a statistical damage coordinate for time-dependent dielectric breakdown in 1.2-kV SiC MOSFET gate oxides

items.title: Toward Partitioned Reference Readout for Four-Level IGZO Memory: Device Statistics, Confusion Matrices, and INT4 Error Propagation
items.abstract: Four-level indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) 2T0C memory needs reliable state formation, sensing references, and a path from cell errors to digital weights. We analyze 107 measured DC transfer curves from 37 isolated IGZO transistors (W/L = 3/0.5 micrometers). Four gate-bias operating points inferred from the first sweep are evaluated on later sweeps of 35 devices. Device-resolved operating points reduce second-sweep across-device current standard deviation by 49.4-52.4%, yet retaining initial thresholds increases misclassified points from 37/140 to 55/140. Leave-one-device-out reference estimation gives 0/140 on the second sweep; freezing second-sweep thresholds yields 6/140 on the third. Sampling eight reference transistors on the third sweep gives a mean held-out error fraction of 0.15% over 2,000 selections, versus 4.33% with frozen thresholds on matched held-out devices. We present conditional confusion matrices, a counterfactual common-gain sensitivity, and an INT4 error-propagation proxy. A simultaneous four-state bank with eight reference cells per state requires at least 32 physical reference cells, 12.5% of a proposed 256-cell data bank before peripheral overhead. A charge-conservation model and a partitioned hierarchical error model specify the pulse, retention, and array measurements needed to test transfer from DC device statistics to pulsed 2T0C operation.

items.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Parameter Optimization of Oxide-Based Memristor Characteristics Using Genetic Algorithms
items.abstract: Abstract We present a multiobjective, physics-informed optimization framework for oxide-based memristive devices that jointly minimizes forming voltage (Vf) and maximizes memory contrast (HRS/LRS). The proposed approach integrates COMSOL Multiphysics with MATLAB through a genetic algorithm (GA), enabling self-consistent electrothermal simulations and systematic exploration of a high-dimensional design space encompassing geometrical, electrical, thermal, and operational parameters. By optimizing 13 key variables, the GA efficiently identifies optimal trade-offs between switching efficiency and resistance ratio. The optimization results demonstrate a substantial enhancement in device performance, with the high-resistance-state to low-resistance-state ratio (HRS/LRS) improved by up to 21× relative to the reference device, while alternative optimized configurations achieve a reduction in Vf down to 0.7× of the reference value. A parameter-importance analysis based on a random forest model highlights oxide thickness and effective electrical and thermal conductivities as influential parameters. Importantly, the optimization further reveals nontrivial multiparameter trade-offs, demonstrating that reductions in Vf and enhancements in HRS/LRS can be simultaneously achieved through coordinated tuning of geometrical, material, and pulse-related parameters beyond simple intuitive design rules. Overall, the MATLAB–COMSOL co-optimization strategy provides a scalable and generalizable computational design methodology for next-generation low-power, high-contrast RRAM devices, and offers quantitative insights into the coupled physical mechanisms underlying filament formation and rupture.

items.title: MoS 2 Memristors Made by Liquid–Liquid Interface Assembly and Ultraprecise Metal Printing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT A cleanroom‐free process was developed for the fabrication of ultralow‐power resistive switching devices. Sub‐micron‐thick silver (Ag) electrodes are printed by XTPL's Ultraprecise Dispensing technology in a fully additive process. Two‐layer molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) is used as the active layer, which was prepared and deposited by the Langmuir‐Schaefer technique. Devices with 30 × 30 µm 2 with volatile and non‐volatile operation were produced. These exhibit SET and RESET voltages of 0.32 ± 0.09 V and −0.29 ± 0.09 V, respectively, a memory window up to 10 6 , an endurance of 300 cycles achieved by voltage sweep, and stable operation under vacuum. The devices can retain the state for over 10 5 s. By employing high‐resolution printing techniques and an ultra‐conformable liquid‐based two‐dimensional materials deposition process, cost‐efficient and high‐performance resistive switching devices were fabricated for next‐generation computation and communication.

items.title: LATCH: LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness for Post-Route FPGA Optimisation
items.abstract: Post-route FPGA timing closure remains expert-dependent and computationally expensive. We present LATCH (LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness), a two-layer framework that separates large language model (LLM) orchestration from deterministic FPGA implementation and evaluation. Across sixteen designs and seven LLMs, a single-iteration study compares three agent control granularities - expert-written recipes, direct EDA operations and LLM-constructed procedures - to ask how much control an agent needs per attempt. Functional-pass rates are 98.2%, 71.4% and 17.9%, respectively; yet direct operations give slightly larger 3.4% median Fmax gains when passing, versus 3.2% for recipes. This exposes a trade-off between execution reliability and timing improvement. Informed by this trade-off, a multi-iteration study fixes the action tier at expert recipes to ask how repeated attempts are best organised, comparing a fitted deterministic heuristic with sequential LLM reasoning, branching exploration and knowledge base-guided exploration within 12 checkpoints per run. Branching raises mean maximum-frequency improvement from 10.5% (sequential) to 16.0%, and the knowledge base to 20.3%, improving 15 of 16 designs. Characterisation across 2,421 recipe attempts profiled their gain and validation rates, showing hard-block re-placement gives the largest cumulative mean gain at 41.4MHz.

items.title: Indium gallium zinc oxide channel-integrated crystallization for wake-up-free HfZrO x metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor gate stacks
items.abstract: Multilevel programming in ferroelectric neuromorphic hardware benefits from a well-defined initial polarization state; wake-up-induced polarization evolution can cause the same programming pulse to produce different polarization states during early operation. Here, we identify the semiconductor/ferroelectric integration sequence as a critical materials-design variable and demonstrate an indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) channel-integrated crystallization route for HfZrOₓ metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor (MFS) gate stacks. The 10-nm-thick IGZO channel is deposited on 16-nm-thick HfZrOₓ before annealing and retained during crystallization, enabling completion of the MFS gate stack with a single anneal and without sacrificial-metal removal. The completed stack exhibits a well-developed as-fabricated polarization–voltage (P–V) loop and only a 2.3% change in switchable polarization after 105 bipolar cycles. By contrast, a complete sacrificial-TiN reference route shows a 39.0% wake-up increase followed by a 20.9% post-wake-up decrease. Starting from this well-defined as-fabricated polarization state, pulse amplitude, pulse width, and displacement-current compliance provide controlled access to intermediate polarization, including 16 current-controlled polarization levels. Ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) fabricated from the same gate stack convert the programmed polarization into four ordered threshold-voltage states. By linking the integration sequence to wake-up-free initialization, multilevel programming, and transistor-level readout, this work establishes a direct materials-to-function pathway relevant to oxide-semiconductor neuromorphic applications.
items.venue: Science and Technology of Advanced Materials

items.title: Implications of aging through HV-H3TRB on the repetitive avalanche mode ruggedness of 1.2 kV SiC MOSFETs
High-mobility enhancement-mode thin-film transistors with 1.5 nm-thick ALD-grown Sn-doped In2O3 channels
items.abstract: Aggressive channel thickness scaling to the sub-2 nm regime is essential for strengthening electrostatic gate control in monolithic three-dimensional electronics, but it causes severe carrier depletion and transport degradation in In2O3 thin-film transistors (TFTs). Here, we demonstrate enhancement-mode TFTs with 1.5 nm-thick Sn-doped In2O3 (ITO) channels prepared by inhibitor-assisted atomic layer deposition. At the same physical channel thickness, the ITO TFT exhibits a field-effect mobility of 25.7 ± 1.4 cm2V−1s−1, a subthreshold swing of 129 ± 31 mV/dec, and a threshold voltage of 0.2 ± 0.2 V, whereas the undoped In2O3 TFT undergoes severe transport degradation. The ITO TFT also shows markedly improved positive-bias-stress stability, with a threshold voltage shift of 0.37 V after 3600 s, whereas the thickness-matched In2O3 TFT reaches 2.07 V within 1000 s and fails before 3600 s. Analysis of the effective mobility and sheet carrier density indicates that Sn doping mitigates carrier depletion in the sub-2 nm channel. The resulting carrier replenishment improves on-state transport and strengthens electrostatic screening against positive-bias-induced trap charging, thereby improving the mobility–positive-bias-stress stability balance. These results establish controlled Sn doping as an effective strategy for realizing high-mobility ultrathin In2O3 TFTs with positive-bias-stress stability for monolithic three-dimensional electronics.

items.title: From FD-SOI to MoS2 MOSFETs: non-uniform coupling mechanisms
FlashT2S: GPU-Accelerated Tensor-to-Spike Conversion Operators for Heterogeneous Neuromorphic LLM Backends
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence faces two growing challenges: computational bottlenecks and energy inefficiency inherent to the von Neumann architecture. Neuromorphic computing offers a promising alternative, yet its immature ecosystem still relies on conventional systems for data supply, requiring efficient conversion between tensor and spike dataflow. We observe a clear mismatch, where data conversion is slow while downstream computation is fast. As data size grows quadratically with large language models, this mismatch becomes a major bottleneck. In this work, we examine the data-conversion components that appear on the critical path of training and inference in neuromorphic LLMs. The work presents FlashT2S (Flash Tensor-to-Spike): GPU-Accelerated Tensor-to-Spike Conversion Operators, which applies architecture-aware and data-centric optimizations to reduce conversion latency. Experimental results show that FlashT2S delivers an average speedup of 850.78x over the native operators across individual operators and 802.83x in realistic workloads. Additionally, compared with GPU kernels automatically generated by torch.compile, our kernels achieve 5-11x speedups. Notably, it achieves near-optimal absolute performance: large-scale conversions are reduced to tens of microseconds (10-99 us), while small-scale conversions reach single-digit microsecond levels (less than 10 us). Furthermore, its standardized output enables seamless integration across heterogeneous backends, including diverse neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: FPGA-based Power & EM Side-Channel Cryptanalysis on GIFT-128 and Development of secure Trojan-free physical design for GIFT-128 with minimized transistors
items.abstract: The rapidly evolving field of the Internet of Things revolves around the transmission of data through wired or wireless networks. A crucial aspect within this domain is ensuring the security of the data being transmitted within optimal timeframes. PRESENT is a well-known lightweight cryptosystem for wireless communication. GIFT is an improved version of it. It is designed to optimize throughput. This paper presents the hardware implementation of the GIFT cipher on an FPGA, including simulation with a testbed. The process involves the generation of random plaintext and keys, which are inputs to the cipher, followed by conducting power leakage analysis and electromagnetic (EM) leakage analysis on GIFT. Subsequently, based on these analyses, a secure Trojan-free VLSI Physical design of GIFT has been presented. The paper also outlines the schematic designs of the GIFT cipher, along with the verification of layout and simulation results.

items.title: Evolution mechanism of damage locations in drift region of SiC MOSFETs under heavy ion irradiation
items.abstract: This paper investigates the evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations in the drift region of the SiC MOSFETs under different applied drain voltages (VDS(irra)) during heavy ion irradiation using 587 MeV 36Kr ions. It is interesting to find from the post-irradiation blocking I–V curves that the drain–source leakage current increases significantly at about 500 V for the case under relatively low VDS(irra) (175–300 V) and increases rapidly at low voltage for the case under relatively high VDS(irra) (350 V). To explain this phenomenon, a local damage-related lifetime-model along the ion track is proposed and validated by technology computer-aided design simulations. The model indicates that thermal damage will develop near the p-base/n-drift junction once the damage near the n-drift/n-sub junction along the ion track becomes sufficiently serious with increasing VDS(irra). The proposed evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations can help analyze mechanisms of single-event leakage current and single-event burnout in SiC devices and guide radiation-hardening designs for SiC devices.

items.title: Engineering Ag+ flux via PMMA incorporation for stable threshold switching and temporal neuromorphic processing in flexible SnO2 quantum dot memristors
items.abstract: In this work, flexible Ag/SnO2 quantum dots (QDs):PMMA (1:0, 1:0.5, 1:1, and 1:1.5)/ITO memristors were fabricated by blending SnO2 QDs and PMMA at different volume ratios. The polymer-assisted Ag+ migration engineering strategy enables effective regulation of conductive filament evolution, inducing a controllable transition from unstable nonvolatile resistive switching to highly stable threshold switching (TS). The Ag/SnO2 QDs:PMMA (1:1)/ITO device exhibits a switching window of ∼25, stable TS over 104 cycles, and excellent mechanical reliability after 104 bending cycles at a bending radius of 4 mm. The polymer matrix modulates Ag+ migration kinetics, facilitating the formation of uniformly distributed metastable. Benefiting from these characteristics, the Ag/SnO2 QDs:PMMA (1:1)/ITO device enables leaky integrate-and-fire and adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire neuron functions. Furthermore, the intrinsic volatile conductance relaxation enables time-dependent image feature extraction by dynamically modulating convolutional weights through Ag filament evolution. This work demonstrates that polymer-assisted Ag+ migration engineering provides an effective strategy for developing flexible volatile memristors toward compact neuromorphic computing hardware.

items.title: Energy constraints in large scale artificial intelligence and insights from human cognition for efficient large language models
items.abstract: Large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) systems, especially large language models (LLMs), face growing constraints related to energy use, power delivery, memory traffic, experimentation, and infrastructure capacity. These pressures are often studied separately, which makes it difficult to understand how they interact across the full AI lifecycle. This review develops a cross-layer framework that brings these constraints together and examines whether resource-allocation strategies observed in human cognition can inform more sustainable AI design. We compare human and artificial systems by function rather than anatomy, focusing on how each allocates limited resources to learning, search, memory, external support, optimization, and inference. Using a systematized narrative-review approach, we identified 6284 records, screened 898 at the full-text stage, and selected an initial set of 150 focal studies for detailed synthesis. We organize the evidence into seven interacting regimes covering scaling, experimentation, hardware power limits, data movement, infrastructure, evaluation incentives, and inference allocation. The framework extends Green AI by linking these layers and translating insights from human cognition into testable design hypotheses and measurable evaluation criteria. The strongest near-term opportunities include data selection, energy-aware experimentation, hardware-supported low-precision computation, and demand-adaptive inference. However, most reported gains are based on proxy measures such as operations, memory, latency, or data volume rather than direct end-to-end energy measurements. Near- and in-memory computing show longer-term promise, while retrieval, tool use, distributed experts, and multi-agent systems may shift or increase energy costs through communication and repeated inference. These findings support cross-layer co-design and end-to-end evaluation at matched capability, reliability, latency, and service quality.

items.title: Emerging Nanoelectronic Technologies for Next-Generation VLSI: Devices, Challenges, and Prospects
items.abstract: The continuous scaling of CMOS technology enables significant progress in performance and integration density in VLSI. However, due to short-channel effects, leakage currents, interconnection delays, variability effects, and power-density limitations, at the current sub-5 nm feature size, the conventional scaling down of CMOS is becoming more and more challenging. This research work discusses a few promising nanoelectronic devices beyond the conventional CMOS, such as CNTFETs, TFETs, nanowire FETs, SETs, graphene-based devices, and spintronic devices. The principle of operation, characteristics, scalability, CMOS compatibility, and perspectives of VLSI application of the devices under consideration are comparatively analyzed. Possible problems related to the integration of the devices, including fabrication scalability, device variability, process complexity, cost, reliability, and thermal issues, are discussed. It is shown that heterogeneous and monolithic 3D integration can be effective methods for combining special-purpose nanoelectronic devices with traditional CMOS technology. Perspectives related to the application of 2D materials and negative-capacitance devices are discussed.

items.title: EXPERIMENTAL STUDY OF THE DEAD-TIME COMPENSATION ALGORITHM FOR GAN HEMT BASED INVERTER FOR AC ELECTRIC DRIVES
items.abstract: This paper presents the experimental evaluation of a dead-time compensation algorithm based on the instantaneous directions of phase currents in a voltage source inverter (VSI). The mechanism by which dead time affects the accuracy of stator voltage vector reproduction is analyzed. The compensation algorithm is implemented in the stationary (a-b) reference frame by introducing a corrective voltage vector whose magnitude and polarity are determined by the dead-time interval and the signs of the motor phase currents. The algorithm was investigated through both experimental testing and mathematical simulation for six dead-time values using two induction motors with different power ratings. The results demonstrate a high level of agreement between simulation and experimental data and confirm that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the nonlinearity of the inverter input-output characteristic and mitigates phase-current waveform distortion over the entire range of investigated dead-time values. The greatest improvement is achieved in the low-output-voltage region, where the influence of dead time is most pronounced.

items.title: Dynamic Landau–Khalatnikov Modeling of Ferroelectric Hafnium–Zirconium Oxides Across Volatile and Non‐Volatile Switching
items.abstract: The design of energy‐efficient neuromorphic devices demands compact, physically grounded models that seamlessly connect microscopic ferroelectric dynamics to macroscopic circuit behavior. Hafnium–zirconium oxides ( HfxZr${\rm Hf}_x{\rm Zr}$ 1−xO$_{1-x}{\rm O}$ 2$_2$ , HZO) are compelling candidates owing to their CMOS compatibility, scalability below 10 nm, and tunable transition between ferroelectric and volatile responses. Yet, conventional first‐order Landau–Khalatnikov (LK) formulations cannot capture key experimental features such as negative differential capacitance, pseudo‐inductive transients, and leakage interplay. Here we introduce an extended LK framework incorporating inertial second‐order terms, nonlinear charge‐dependent damping, and a modular leakage branch. This unified, simulation‐ready model quantitatively reproduces experimental Q–V characteristics across Hf‐rich, equiatomic, and Zr‐rich HZO compositions, defining operational regimes from non‐volatile memory to volatile, reservoir‐like dynamics. By linking free‐energy landscapes to compact circuit representations, the approach establishes a predictive device–model–circuit co‐design framework that connects atomistic energetics with system‐level simulation, enabling composition‐specific design rules for scalable, low‐power neuromorphic architectures.

items.title: Decoupling Trap States in Amorphous Oxide Semiconductor Transistor Using a Conductive-Semiconducting-Conductive MOS Structure
items.abstract: We propose a novel amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS)-based conductive-semiconducting-conductive (CSC) MOS test structure to effectively sense, discriminate, and analyze distinct trap-induced conductance losses in AOS transistors. In conventional test structures, non-ideal metal-AOS contacts convolute the conductance loss generated by various trap states. The CSC architecture mitigates these contact-related artifacts, enabling the decoupling of interface states and shallow states. Furthermore, the contributions from leakage, series resistance, and device-geometry effects are identified and calibrated. Our results yield bias-resolved trap profiles and reveal three distinct regimes: (1) In the depletion region, interface states dominate the conductance loss. These states exhibit sub-microsecond time constants and their density increases slightly with deeper depletion, which is associated with donor-like states. (2) From weak to moderate accumulation, shallow states become the primary contributor, displaying a Gaussian-like volumetric density-of-states distribution with response times spanning from microseconds to nanoseconds. (3) In the strong accumulation regime, interface states regain dominance with an increased state quantity, while their time constants remain invariant. These bias-resolved profiles clarify how different trap populations impact AOS transistors under distinct operating conditions, providing intuitive metrics for understanding reliability degradation. Consequently, the CSC structure offers a simple, scalable, and robust platform for trap characterization in AOS transistors.

items.title: Decoupled Multiplicative Physics-Guided Neural Network for Extrapolative Modeling of GaN HEMT
items.abstract: Rapid direct-current (DC) surrogate modeling of gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) requires accurate prediction of the current-capability, conduction-loss, and self-heating indicators used in geometry screening. This work presents an electrothermal decoupled multiplicative physics-guided neural network (ET-DM-PGNN) for this task. It combines a gray-box backbone, separate high- and low-field polarization channels, a latent DC self-heating update, and bounded target-specific multiplicative residuals. A two-stage strategy first calibrates the complete surrogate and then refines the current branch while preserving resistance and temperature. On 32 interstitial samples, ET-DM-PGNN achieves R2>0.997, with mean absolute percentage errors of 0.13%, 0.15%, and 0.04% for Imax, Ron, and Tmax, respectively. The corresponding errors on nine external cases are 1.46%, 0.94%, and 0.74%. A leakage-controlled, three-seed level-held-out audit yields errors of 0.44-6.40% in four composition and lateral-geometry directions, whereas holding out the 0.015 µm barrier level produces errors of 12.41-21.21% under the tested training protocol. Across 365 geometries, 4 updates differ from a 12-step reference by at most 0.0076%. Numerically validated at Vgs=3 V using TCAD DC sweeps extending to Vds=15 V, the surrogate supports rapid fixed-protocol geometry screening and identifies the ultrathin-barrier direction as the least reliable tested extrapolation regime.

items.title: Competing hysteresis mechanisms in HZO/MoS2 transistors with a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor gate stack
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors based on hafnium oxide offer a versatile platform for advanced memory concepts. Here, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept top-gated Hf0.5Zr0.5O2-based transistor integrating a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) gate stack with a two-dimensional MoS2 channel. The implementation of such an architecture is particularly challenging in MoS2, where the strong sensitivity of the channel to trapped charge can further complicate the balance between ferroelectric switching and charge redistribution within the MFMIS stack. By varying the MFM-to-MIS area ratio and the applied gate-voltage amplitude, we observe a systematic evolution of the transfer hysteresis consistent with competing ferroelectric polarization switching and trap-related contributions. Temperature-dependent measurements, zero-bias write/read experiments, and compact Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis modeling provide additional support for this interpretation. Despite the non-optimized gate stack, a substantial ferroelectric contribution to the device response is retained, while retention measurements reveal limitations associated with depolarization and trapping. These results demonstrate the feasibility of MFMIS ferroelectric transistors based on MoS2 and provide a basis for further optimization of their gate-stack design and memory performance.

items.title: Bipolar Hot Carrier‐Driven Switchable Photocurrent Polarity in Plasmonic‐Functionalized Phototransistor for All‐Optical‐Configured Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocarrier engineering in semiconductors is critical for developing advanced optoelectronic devices. Plasmonic hot carriers enable effective modulation of the photocarrier behavior in semiconductor systems, yet their full potential is restricted by the exploitation of unipolar charges. Herein, by integrating a plasmonic Ag nanoplate layer with an asymmetric MoS 2 transistor, we introduce a plasmon‐enabled photocarrier engineering strategy that achieves vertical bipolar‐hot‐carrier (both hot electrons and hot holes) harvesting and utilization in an n‐type 2D material device for the first time. Hot electron injection into the MoS 2 channel leads to a maximum 50‐fold photoresponsivity enhancement, while hot hole diffusion to the MoS 2 ‐Au electrode interface enables the barrier‐controllable regulation of photoconductivity polarity triggered by optical intensity and wavelength. The multiple‐stimuli‐responsive polarity‐switching characteristic of the hybrid architecture allows for the hardware implementation of an artificial plasmonic neuromorphic system capable of simulating different neural plasticity and performing logical operations with enhanced accuracy. This work presents an innovative framework for the rational design of plasmonic bipolar‐hot‐carrier engineered semiconductor devices with novel functionalities and highlights opportunities for the development of next‐generation optoelectronic intelligence applications.

items.title: AlGaN Barrier Thickness Dependence of Ferroelectric Switching and Interface-Trap Effects in AlScN/HfO2 Gate Stack HEMTs
items.abstract: We investigate the effect of AlGaN barrier thickness (23, 15, and 7 nm) on the transport and switching characteristics of AlScN/HfO2/AlGaN/GaN ferroelectric high-electron-mobility transistors (FeHEMTs). While the 7 nm device exhibits the largest apparent memory window (MW) under quasi-static DC conditions, it suffers from degraded transport, increased leakage, and pronounced trap-induced effects. Pulsed measurements, which reduce the contribution of slower interface-trapping processes, yield representative MWs of 1.6, 3.4, and 2.8 V for the 23, 15, and 7 nm devices, respectively, under their respective program/erase conditions. Prolonged pulse-width measurements demonstrate MW closure and inversion, indicating dominant electron trapping rather than polarization fatigue. Under the present experimental conditions, including a fixed 70 nm AlScN layer, the 15 nm barrier provides the most favorable balance among electrostatic coupling, channel transport, and trap-related effects.

items.title: Activated clotting time in cardiac surgery, cardiological interventional procedures, vascular surgery, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and haemodialysis
items.abstract: The activated clotting time (ACT) is a point-of-care test used to monitor unfractionated heparin (UFH) in acute care settings. Although widely recommended in cardiac surgery, interventional cardiology, vascular surgery, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and haemodialysis, important uncertainties remain regarding its use. Given the lack of interchangeability between ACT devices and consumables, clear information on targets and analytical systems is essential. We reviewed guideline documents published before November 1, 2025, as well as recommendations from major scientific societies, to assess ACT use, thresholds, and reported levels of evidence. Studies cited within these guidelines were also analysed, and the characteristics of ACT devices were compared with those currently available. A total of 24 guideline documents were identified, of which 17 specified ACT target values and only two mentioned the device or reagent used. The level of evidence was generally low or not graded. For example, during cardiopulmonary bypass, recommended ACT thresholds vary (e.g., 480 s without heparin-coated circuits or 400 s with the so-called maximal activation), without specification of the analytical system. Guidelines often rely on outdated studies using devices no longer available. Moreover, ACT analysers differ substantially in consumables, clot detection methods, blood volume, and reagents, which are rarely considered in recommendations. In conclusion, current guidelines provide limited guidance on ACT measurement despite significant inter-device variability. We recommend that future guidelines specify devices and consumables, or at least their sensitivity to UFH, to ensure reliable interpretation. Further studies are needed to optimise UFH monitoring in clinical practice.
items.venue: European Journal of Anaesthesiology Intensive Care

items.title: Vertical NAND Flash Memory‐Based Bayesian Neural Networks With Intrinsic Gaussian Weight Sampling
items.abstract: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) provide improved robustness and well‐calibrated uncertainty estimates compared with deterministic networks, but their hardware realization remains challenging because Gaussian weight sampling typically requires random number generators, substantial memory overhead, or additional circuitry. Here we experimentally characterize commercial vertical NAND (V‐NAND) flash memory and show that a fully hardware‐compatible BNN can be realized without modifying the native array structure. We demonstrate that although individual ISPP‐programmed V‐NAND cells exhibit non‐Gaussian conductance distributions, the differential current between adjacent cells naturally forms a zero‐mean Gaussian distribution. The variance of these Gaussian weights can be tuned using only the read voltage, introducing no extra storage or peripheral circuitry. Using this hardware‐aware mapping, we construct a Bayesian last‐layer on top of a ResNet‐34 classifier and evaluate it in hardware‐calibrated simulations on the Tiny‐ImageNet‐C dataset. The resulting V‐NAND BNN achieves up to a 9.0% point improvement in accuracy over a deterministic counterpart under severe corruptions, along with enhanced calibration, ROC/PR performance, and separation of epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. These results establish V‐NAND flash memory as a practical and scalable platform for uncertainty‐aware in‐memory computing and provide a blueprint for hardware BNNs.

items.title: SpikeOcc: Towards Resilient Multimodal 3D Occupancy Perception via Spiking Experts
items.abstract: Multimodal 3D occupancy prediction underpins safe autonomous driving through comprehensive scene understanding. However, existing methods have largely pursued higher accuracy through sophisticated fusion, leaving resilience to missing sensors underexplored. In this paper, we investigate spiking neural networks (SNNs) as a means of building more resilient multimodal perception. Still, the discrete nature of spiking neurons makes optimization challenging. To overcome this difficulty, SpikeOcc is introduced with two complementary components, a Spiking Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) and Sensor Availability Learning (SAL). Specifically, SMoE organizes RGB, LiDAR, and joint fusion into specialized pathways, enabling full-width unimodal representations while retaining the original multimodal features via a bounded residual. Beyond sensor dropout, SAL employs a staged curriculum with explicit routing supervision, progressively improving robustness under severe sensing conditions. Remarkably, SAL also yields notable gains for conventional models, highlighting its broader potential for resilient multimodal learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpikeOcc maintains competitive full-sensor accuracy while markedly raising the performance floor under sensor outages. SpikeOcc illustrates the promise of neuromorphic computing, pointing toward more reliable and energy-efficient autonomous driving.

items.title: Spatially Complementary In‐Plane Lattice Strain Engineering for Reduced Contact Resistance and Enhanced Ferroelectric Switching in Van Der Waals α‐In 2 Se 3 Ferroelectric Semiconductor Field‐Effect Transistors
items.abstract: ABSTRACT α‐In 2 Se 3 ferroelectric semiconductor field‐effect transistors (FeS‐FETs) offer attractive non‐volatile memory characteristics but are limited by high source/drain (S/D) contact resistance and inefficient ferroelectric polarization switching. Here, we demonstrate a low‐temperature, CMOS‐compatible strain‐engineering strategy based on region‐dependent in‐plane (IP) lattice strain. A silicon nitride stress layer induces tensile strain in the S/D regions and compressive strain in the channel, producing spatially differentiated effects within a single device. The contact‐side tensile strain modifies the interfacial electronic structure and reduces contact resistance, whereas the channel‐side compressive strain facilitates ferroelectric polarization switching. Consequently, the strained α‐In 2 Se 3 FeS‐FET achieves a 12.03‐fold reduction in S/D contact resistance, a 19.21‐fold increase in on‐state current, a 4.4%p increase in normalized memory window, and a 22.4‐fold enhancement in the ferroelectric resistance switching ratio. Raman characterization and finite‐element method simulations establish the region‐dependent strain distribution, while interface‐pinning analysis and first‐principles calculations provide mechanistic support for the distinct contact‐ and channel‐side effects. These results establish region‐dependent IP lattice strain as a unified device‐engineering framework for jointly controlling contact transport and ferroelectric memory functionality in vdW α‐In 2 Se 3 FeS‐FETs.

items.title: High-Performance Uncooled Infrared Photodetection Based on van der Waals Metallic FePd2Te2 Nanoflakes
items.abstract: Uncooled infrared photodetectors that combine high sensitivity, low power consumption, and broad spectral coverage remain highly desirable. However, they are still hindered by the complex epitaxial processes and cooling requirements of mainstream semiconductor technologies. Here, we demonstrate a high-performance infrared photodetector based on FePd2Te2 nanoflakes, a van der Waals metallic material that enables efficient photothermal conversion. The device operates at room temperature under a bias of 0.1 V and exhibits a broadband photoresponse spanning from the visible to the long-wave infrared. Across the measured infrared range, a wavelength-independent responsivity (R) above 50 A/W, a noise equivalent power (NEP) below 2.83 × 10−16 W/Hz1/2, and a specific detectivity (D*) exceeding 3.86 × 1012 cm Hz1/2/W are achieved. The photoresponse appears to arise from the photobolometric effect, in which the temperature rise at the contact interface is considered to modulate the contact resistance and thereby amplify the photocurrent. These results establish FePd2Te2 as a promising platform for room-temperature, low-power, and highly sensitive infrared detection.

items.title: An optimized majority-feedback QCA D-latch and SET/RESET-enabled SRAM cell for compact, low-latency nanoelectronic memory design
items.abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata is a contender to replace the scaling of semiconductor technology as it hits physical limits of complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology, with its ability to switch faster, take up less space and consume less power. In this study, the design and functional verification of compact QCA data latch circuit and a memory cell suitable for SRAM operation are presented, which are designed, implemented and simulated in the QCA designer (QCAD) 2.0.3 software. The main contribution is a single-layer 14-cell D-latch with a 0.007 µm 2 footprint, reducing the layout area, latency and QCA cost compared with a similar design previously reported in the literature. Another 15-cell variant is proposed, incorporating SET and RESET control, for SRAM-type applications, reducing peak energy dissipation by approximately 22% from the 14-cell baseline. The circuits are found to be compact, low-latency circuits for next-generation nanoelectronics memory and different logic circuit design applications with reduced power dissipation. The power dissipation and polarization map of proposed circuits are implemented in QCAPro Software.

items.title: Air-gap engineering enabled ultrafast 9-bit ferroelectric semi-gate transistor array for high-efficiency image denoising
items.abstract: Abstract The insufficient lateral electric field gradient limits the programming/erasing speed of conventional semi-floating gate transistors, while charge leakage leads to poor data retention and compromised operating characteristics. Here we design a ferroelectric semi-gate (FSG) transistor featuring a triangular air gap adjacent to the drain region. The device exhibits an as-programmed on–off ratio exceeding 107, remaining above 105 after 11 weeks, and a memory window of approximately 6 V. The localized lateral electric field accelerates program and erase operations to 60 ns and 75 ns, respectively. The spontaneous polarization field of the ferroelectric HfZrO layer strengthens charge retention in the HfO2 charge-trapping layer, enabling robust nonvolatile memory performance with a retention time exceeding 106 s. This synergistic integration of air-gap engineering and ferroelectric polarization yields an optimal trade-off between speed, retention and multilevel operation. By exploiting its superior multilevel capability with 9-bit distinguishable current states, we realize Ising-model-based image denoising using a 32 × 32 transistor array. These FSG transistors show promising potential for high-speed, low-power random-access memory applications.

items.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space.
