In this paper, we present TileCas, a unified, pluggable interface that enables coding agents to develop kernels across multiple editable abstraction levels. Rather than committing to a single representation, TileCas allows an agent to transfer and refine candidates across levels through Cross-Level Diagnosis, which maps correctness and performance feedback to actionable controls at different abstraction levels; Abstraction Scheduling, which selects both the candidate and representation from which subsequent refinement should proceed; and a Heterogeneous Search Tree, which preserves and revisits alternative search trajectories spanning multiple representations. We integrate TileCas with two code agents AKO and KDA, and evaluate both integrations on 50 end-to-end KernelBench Level 3 workloads across two accelerator platforms and two language models. Giving equal weight to the four accelerator-model configurations, AKO with TileCas achieves an arithmetic-mean speedup of $4.84\times$, compared with $3.75\times$ for the strongest evaluated baseline without TileCas, an improvement of 29.0%. Integrating the same interface with KDA improves its mean speedup by 69.2%, with gains in every configuration. These results show that allowing coding agents to navigate across programming abstractions can improve machine-driven software development and can be reused across different base workflows.

items.title: Scalable Ion‐Electron Coupled Poly(Benzodifurandione) Inks Enabling Biosignal Amplification and Neuromorphic Memory
items.abstract: Printed organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising for next‐generation biosensing and neuromorphic computing, owing to their high transconductance, low operating voltage, mechanical flexibility, and efficient volumetric ionic–electronic coupling. Yet, printable n ‐type OECTs have lagged their p ‐type counterparts due to limited stability and poor printability. The key challenge lies in achieving high electronic conductivity, efficient ionic accessibility, and rheological properties compatible with scalable printing. To address this, we developed a screen‐printable, air‐stable, n ‐type OECT channel by blending high‐conductivity poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) with poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO). Devices fabricated using 5wt.% PEO blend and a gelatin‐based electrolyte exhibited tunable transient responses (turn‐on time; 9.6 to 419 ms, turn‐off time; 4.3 ms to 17.8 ms), stable operation (92.4% ON current retained over 1,000 cycles), and high uniformity across 50 devices (I ds, ON = 2.47 ± 0.29 mA and transconductance g m = 3.55 ± 0.57 mS). PEO transforms low‐viscosity PBFDO solutions into shear‐thinning pastes suitable for screen printing, while enhancing film wettability and electrolyte infiltration. This dual role promotes efficient ion penetration and improves printability, enabling devices with improved transient speeds and rheological properties optimized for scalable fabrication. By controlling channel thickness, thin devices enable electrocardiogram signal acquisition while thick devices act as artificial synapses, highlighting PBFDO‐based inks as versatile platforms for integrated bioelectronic interfaces.

items.title: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Policies for Chiplet Design Space Exploration
items.abstract: Chiplet technology is a key approach for extending Moore's Law. However, its design process is constrained by two primary challenges: the scarcity of early-stage platforms for rapidly evaluating chiplet-based heterogeneous systems, and the complex relationships between design parameters and optimization metrics. To address these challenges, we propose a synergistic framework that integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) with Bayesian Optimization (BO), enabling architectural-level simulation and automated optimization for the 2.5D/3D CPU-GPU heterogeneous chiplets. We extend the open-source chiplet simulator to evaluate 3D designs by supporting graph topologies. Further, to enhance the exploration efficiency of BO, we introduce an LLM that generates high-quality policies to guide the optimization process, enabled by our proposed adaptive directional policy reasoning (ADPR) and an exploration gain-aware fine-tuning method. Finally, we use the policy-guided BO to perform an automated and efficient exploration of the complex chiplet design space. Experiments on 2.5D and 3D chiplet reveal that our framework improves design space exploration efficiency.

items.title: HADES: A Programmable Processing-Near-Memory Engine for Binary Similarity Search
items.abstract: Moving operands to a processor can cost more than the arithmetic performed on them, and for small binary similarity and search workloads data movement can dominate. We present HADES, a programmable processing-near-memory engine built around one shared 32x32-bit 2R1W register-file macro that holds both data and program. Twelve 16-bit opcodes, three working registers and a 32-slot program express ten search workloads in 8 to 19 slots, and SCANP and SCANSEL shorten dual-row and selected scans. A post-layout 2x2 Tiny Tapeout implementation closes timing at 40 MHz with 26,968 square microns of standard cells beside a 15,744 square microns macro. All HADES results come from RTL or gate-level simulation of this implementation, and HADES energy is estimated. Against ESP8266 and ESP32 microcontrollers running plain C, and with an ideal host, HADES answers a resident query 10x to 32x and 2.2x to 11x faster, respectively. End to end, it wins at the evaluated batch sizes of B = 16 and B = 256 against both boards and loses the single-query (B = 1) runs to the ESP32. An Arduino Nano runs a restricted subset. Kernel power stays within about 2% of a spin loop on all three boards. These results hold for plain-C baselines under the evaluated conditions. At this scale the control and instruction storage fit around a shared memory macro, while the byte-wide interface and the loading path remain significant costs.

items.title: Comparative Electro-Thermal Evaluation of IGBT- and SiC MOSFET-Based Bidirectional DC-DC Converters for Supercapacitor Energy Storage Systems
items.abstract: Bidirectional DC-DC converters are key interfaces between supercapacitor energy storage systems and DC networks in applications requiring rapid bidirectional power exchange, particularly regenerative braking and acceleration support. This paper presents a like-for-like comparison of IGBT- and SiC MOSFET-based implementations of the same 125 kW rated non-isolated bidirectional buck–boost converter platform. The novelty lies in a controlled system-level comparison in which the semiconductor technology is changed, while the converter architecture, control structure and operating conditions are retained, enabling the electro-thermal impact of the device technology to be assessed in both directions of power flow. Both semiconductor technologies are evaluated in buck and boost operation through analytical loss calculations, manufacturer-based electro-thermal simulations, and laboratory measurements. The laboratory measurements reached approximately 50 kW in buck mode and 38 kW in boost mode for both semiconductor implementations; the 125 kW results are analytical/manufacturer tool projections rather than rated-power experimental validation. The results obtained from the manufacturer tool simulations show that the relative benefit of SiC depends on both the switching frequency and power flow direction. In particular, the SiC implementation provides a substantially greater thermal margin in boost operation, while the buck-mode comparison reveals a frequency-dependent crossover for the selected devices. The partial-power experimental results support the electro-thermal trends observed in the analysis and simulations, particularly the reduced thermal stress of the SiC implementation. These results highlight the importance of considering both the switching frequency and power flow direction when selecting the semiconductor technology for high-power bidirectional supercapacitor converters.

items.title: Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor based Voltage Differencing Inverting Buffered Amplifier with Enhanced Analog Performance
items.abstract: This article describes how to develop and operate a Voltage Differencing Inverting Buffered Amplifier (CNTFET-VDIBA) using Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistors (CNTFETs). It utilizes the superior characteristics of CNTFETs to facilitate enhanced transconductance, a wideband range of operation, and a low power demand compared to conventional CMOS alternatives. The effect of increasing numbers of CNTs on device performance was thoroughly studied and characterized. Simulation results specify that by increasing the number of CNTs significantly improves transconductance. The proposed VDIBA, CNT has the highest transconductance of around 1.32mS, while maintaining the high BW. The 3-db BW was observed to be 7.9 GHz, enabling this proposed VDIBA to apply for high-frequency analog signals. These results demonstrate that CNTFET-based VDIBA is a feasible substitute to CMOS, providing ultra-low power consumption, scalability, and high-performance analog building blocks for future integrated circuits.
items.venue: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering

items.title: 2D MoS2 ASOSIDAGI MAYDONIY TRANZISTORLAR ANALOG XARAKTERISTIKALARIGA STRUKTURAVIY PARAMETRLAR TASIRI
items.abstract: So‘nggi yillarda 2D MoS2 asosidagi maydoniy tranzistorlar (FETlar) o‘zining noyob elektron xususiyatlari tufayli analog ilovalar uchun katta qiziqish uyg‘otmoqda, chunki ular yuqori transkonduktans, past shovqin va yuqori chiqish qarshiligini talab qiladi. An’anaviy kremniy qurilmalarining masshtablash chegaralariga yaqinlashib borishi bilan, MoS2 FETlar simsiz aloqa, sensorlar va signalni qayta ishlash tizimlarida yuqori samarali kuchaytirgichlar va mikserlarni yaratish uchun yangi imkoniyatlar ochadi. Ushbu tadqiqotning maqsadi 2D MoS2 asosidagi maydoniy tranzistorlarning analog xarakteristikalariga strukturaviy parametrlar ta'sirini tizimli adabiyot tahlili orqali o‘rganishdir. Tadqiqot Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar kabi xalqaro va O‘zbekiston Fizika Jurnali kabi mahalliy ilmiy ma’lumotlar bazalarida 2020-yildan hozirgi kungacha nashr etilgan 75 ta tegishli maqolani tahlil qilishga asoslangan. Tahlil shuni ko‘rsatdiki, eshik dielektrik qatlamining qalinligi va materiali, shuningdek kanal uzunligi qurilmaning transkonduktans (gm), chiqish qarshiligi (rout) va past chastotali shovqin (LFN) kabi ko‘rsatkichlariga sezilarli ta’sir ko‘rsatadi. Xususan, atom qatlamli cho‘ktirish (ALD) usuli bilan hosil qilingan yupqa (~5 nm) Al2O3 dielektrik qatlamlari FET masshtablashini yaxshilaydi va yuqori-k HfO2 dielektriklari analog xarakteristikalarni sezilarli darajada oshiradi. Kanal uzunligini qisqartirish gm ni oshirsa-da, qisqa kanal effektlari rout ni pasaytiradi. Ushbu natijalar yuqori samarali MoS2 FETlarni analog sxemalar uchun loyihalashda strukturaviy parametrlarni optimallashtirish muhimligini takidlaydi.

items.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
items.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior. In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. DFIT captures high-level, semantically meaningful data that reflect the true dataflow of computation. These data can be exported for visualization and analysis. Our approach demonstrates how instrumentation can be generalized beyond traditional hardware to support heterogeneous architectures, providing portability without modifying tool logic. By opening the black box of dataflow execution, DFIT establishes a foundation for new classes of performance analysis tools for AI accelerators. It provides a practical path toward reproducible, architecture-aware introspection across heterogeneous systems, bridging the long-standing visibility gap between compiler design, runtime scheduling, and hardware realization. Evaluation across Cerebras, SambaNova, and TPU shows practical overhead of 3.53%-13.62% across instrumentation modes with robust cross-platform portability.

items.title: Unveiling Phosphorus Vacancy-Mediated Resistive Switching in Cu/HfO2/BP/Pt Memristors: Experimental and First-Principles Investigations
items.abstract: Memristors integrating 2D materials are promising for neuromorphic computing, yet their microscopic resistive switching mechanisms require further clarification. In this study, a Cu/HfO2/BP/Pt memristor was fabricated to investigate its electrical characteristics and conductive filament (CF) dynamics. The device exhibits compliance-dependent behavior, enabling unipolar volatile switching at 100 μA and bipolar nonvolatile switching at 200 μA. In nonvolatile mode, it demonstrates a concentrated switching voltage distribution (Vset ≈ −1.491 V, Vreset ≈ 1.669 V), stable endurance exceeding 150 cycles, and an ON/OFF ratio of ∼104. The low- and high-resistance states follow ohmic conduction (a hybrid ohmic conduction of electron capture/decapture under negative bias) and Schottky emission, respectively. Furthermore, first-principles CI-NEB calculations indicate that intrinsic phosphorus vacancies (Vp) within the BP layer facilitate directional Cu+ migration (1.54 eV barrier) and spontaneous Pt atom trapping (0.1 eV barrier). This defect-mediated interfacial interaction promotes stable orbital hybridization, anchoring localized CFs. This work provides experimental and theoretical insights for designing oxide/2D material-based neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips
items.abstract: We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips. Our extensive characterization yields 1) the empirical basis for developing new, accurate HBM power models or validating existing power models and 2) key insights into structural and data-pattern-dependent variation of power in HBM2 chips. Out of our 13 new findings and 6 key takeaway messages, we highlight: 1) a read operation consumes significantly higher current than any other operation and 2) the toggled data bus signals in a data transfer burst significantly affect current draw where toggling all HBM2-internal bank group bus signals causes 29.4% higher power consumption than keeping them constant. Leveraging our empirical insights into HBM2 power consumption, we engineer an access pattern that yields 23.6% higher power consumption on average across 36 tested HBM2 chips than the highest-power-consuming JEDEC-specified current measurement loop. Our results have important implications for HBM-based system design and validation. Relying solely on JEDEC- or vendor-specified test loops to bound HBM power could cause system failures and/or thermal throttling in real-world high-power AI/ML workloads. To improve 3D-stacked DRAM power modeling in open source architectural simulation infrastructures, we develop a new HBM power model. Our model predicts the power of 36 real HBM2 chips across diverse workloads (including a real LLM decode workload) with 7.6 -- 8.1% mean absolute percentage error, substantially more accurately than state-of-the-art HBM power models. The power consumption predicted by our model for a power-intensive microbenchmark closely matches (with 2.4% to 5.3% error across HBM3E's specified supply voltage range) the average HBM3E memory power consumed by three tested NVIDIA H200 GPUs. We publicly release our power model at https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/HBM-Power.

items.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
items.abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. The chip is opto-electronic and features co-packaged electronics using tiny electronic chiplets that are bonded to the sapphire. These consist of an LD driver and transimpedance amplifier for the UV photonics, together with ASICs, ADC, microcontroller, micro-battery and RF-wireless or Ethernet chiplets. The mission of this self-contained cost-effective chip is sensing targeted medical-chemical-biological (MCB) agents in a local or network setting. Eight significant MCB applications are detailed here.

items.title: Trap engineering in InP/ZnSe/ZnS colloidal quantum-dot memristors for neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are attractive memristive materials because their electronic structure and interfaces can be engineered to control charge transport and trapping for neuromorphic synaptic devices. However, many QD-based memristors exhibit resistive switching based on filament formation via silver migration, without utilizing the unique properties of QDs. In this presentation, we combine mechanism-guided engineering of device architecture and material properties to achieve non-filamentary resistive switching in InP/ZnSe/ZnS QDs. Based on device-architecture engineering, we found that interlayers adjacent to QDs have an important role in charge trapping and detrapping governing hysteresis and retention characteristics. Guided by these insights, a multilayer stack of metal oxide nanoparticles and QDs promotes spatially uniform areal trapping, while oxide nanoparticle interlayers enhance electron transport, suppress hole injection, and create interfacial trap sites via controlled interfacial chemistry. The strategies enabled robust resistive switching and synaptic plasticity for neural network operation.

items.title: Thickness scaling in hafnium ferroelectrics: insights into oxygen vacancy clustering and its impact on ferroelectricity and reliability
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium-based ferroelectrics have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation non-volatile memory technologies owing to their excellent complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) compatibility and exceptional thickness scalability. However, the defect mechanisms governing the evolution of ferroelectricity and reliability during thickness scaling remain poorly understood. In particular, the role of oxygen-vacancy-related defects has primarily been discussed from the perspective of defect concentration, while their spatial organization has received far less attention. Here, we systematically investigate the impact of thickness scaling on the ferroelectric properties and reliability of Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 (HZO) capacitors. Although thinner HZO films exhibit reduced remanent polarization due to enhanced dead-layer effects, increased depolarization fields, and stabilization of nonpolar phases, they surprisingly demonstrate superior breakdown tolerance and endurance performance. Notably, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis revealed a higher oxygen vacancy concentration in thinner films, indicating that defect concentration alone cannot explain the observed reliability evolution. Time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) analysis using the time-dependent clustering model, together with density functional theory (DFT) calculations and atomic force microscopy (AFM) characterization, suggests that thickness scaling modifies the spatial organization of oxygen-vacancy-related defects. Grain refinement in ultrathin films increases the grain-boundary density, thereby suppressing severe defect clustering and promoting a more dispersed defect organization, which delays breakdown and improves long-term reliability. These findings identify defect organization as a critical factor governing the thickness-scaling behavior of hafnium ferroelectrics and provide new insights for the design of highly scaled and reliable ferroelectric memory devices.

items.title: The role of various scattering mechanisms on electron velocity in Al0.21Ga0.79N/GaN HEMTs
items.abstract: In the present study, the mobility corresponding to various scattering mechanisms under low-field conditions was calculated. Among all scattering mechanisms, polarization Coulomb field (PCF) and polar optical phonon (POP) scattering exhibited the highest mean momentum relaxation rates under low-field conditions. Sentaurus technology computer-aided design (TCAD) coupled Monte Carlo (MC) simulations were employed to calculate the electron drift velocity (ve) of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs under high-field conditions. Individual scattering mechanisms were removed sequentially in the MC framework. The impact of each mechanism on ve under high-field conditions was quantified. The results reveal that under high-field conditions, PCF scattering can reduce ve of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs by 20%–30%. Meanwhile, a method based on the mean momentum relaxation rate was proposed. It can be used to approximate scattering strength and to rank the contributions of different mechanisms in the MC simulations. The highest mean momentum relaxation rate was also obtained for PCF and POP scattering. PCF and POP scattering are, therefore, identified as the dominant carrier-scattering mechanism in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs. Further, a correlation between device geometry and the mean momentum relaxation rate of PCF scattering was further established. Devices with a larger ratio of source-spacing (drain-spacing)-to-gate-length [Lgs(gd)/Lg] exhibited stronger PCF scattering strength.

items.title: The Effect of Passive Substrate Terminations on RON Degradation in GaN Bidirectional Switches
items.abstract: In this paper, four passive terminations are considered for the substrate biasing of Gallium Nitride (GaN) bidirectional high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs). These substrate networks are analyzed via switching simulations and by adopting a physical model for the bidirectional transistor based on the well-known Advanced SPICE Model (ASM) for GaN HEMT, including an enhanced formulation of back-gating phenomena. The most promising network, which exploits resistances and diodes in the common anode configuration, was implemented with discrete components and tested. The measurement data turned out to be in line with the simulations results in terms of substrate voltage, which is pushed toward zero at low resistance values, thus reducing the back-gating effect. Consequently, a remarkable reduction in the on-resistance (RON) degradation compared to the floating substrate configuration is observed, with a proper trade-off between RON drift and off-state leakage current. Finally, some considerations about the partial recovery of on-resistance due to the substrate termination are discussed.

items.title: TPCS: A Cycle-Level Simulation Paradigm with Native Execution Semantics for RTL Modeling and Generation
items.abstract: The growing diversity of domain-specific architectures and microarchitectural designs demands fast and accurate evaluation methods during early design stages. However, existing approaches suffer from a fundamental trade-off: high-level simulators offer speed but lack fidelity, while RTL-based tools provide accuracy at the cost of significant simulation overhead. This gap limits efficient pre-RTL microarchitecture exploration. Therefore, we propose Transaction-Pruned Cycle Simulation (TPCS), a novel modeling and simulation framework. It serves as a unified intermediate abstraction spanning microarchitecture modeling, cycle-accurate simulation, and synthesizable RTL implementation. TPCS organizes combinational logic as transaction-based function invocations and leverages host CPU control flow to naturally prune inactive logic, eliminating the need for explicit event scheduling or signal tracking. This enables cycle-accurate simulation with significantly improved performance. TPCS preserves structural correspondence with RTL and supports automatic generation of synthesizable designs. TPCS achieves 36$\times$-42$\times$ speedups over parallel Verilator on SMP systems and 3.4$\times$-7.2$\times$ over single-threaded Verilator on accelerators, with cycle-level waveform agreement on the evaluated traces. The generated RTL demonstrates comparable timing and area to handcrafted implementations, with relative changes of -4.7\% to +2.6\% in clock period and -3.3\% to +4.0\% in standard-cell area. By bridging the abstraction gap between high-level modeling and RTL design, TPCS enables a unified and agile pre-RTL workflow, allowing efficient microarchitecture exploration with both high performance and implementation fidelity.

items.title: Role of lateral surface conduction in barrier modulation of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs under optical illumination and elevated temperature
items.abstract: Optical and thermal excitation are known to enhance OFF-state leakage and modify the electrostatics of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), yet the role of lateral surface conduction in mediating these effects remains insufficiently understood. In this work, a geometry-defined ring-break architecture is introduced to probe the interplay between lateral surface conduction and channel electrostatics. Simultaneous measurements of gate leakage current ( IG) and floating channel potential ( Va) reveal correlated transport and electrostatic responses together with a characteristic transition at a critical gate bias, Vcrit. Under optical illumination and elevated temperature, both ring-break and conventional HEMTs exhibit systematic evolution of IG and Vcrit, supporting a common field-dependent lateral surface-conduction mechanism. However, the illumination-induced Va response differs qualitatively between the two geometries: |Va| decreases in the conventional structure but increases in the ring-break structure. This opposite response is attributed to the geometry-dependent balance between positive surface charging, which reduces |Va|, and negative virtual gating associated with distributed surface resistance, which increases |Va|. These results establish lateral surface conduction as an important contributor to barrier modulation and OFF-state leakage in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs and demonstrate the ring-break architecture as a geometry-controlled platform for probing surface transport, charge redistribution, and the influence of surface passivation.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-transport framework treats the source, drain, and gate as current-carrying quantum-mechanical contacts and resolves the local current density throughout the device. The spatially resolved current density shows that gate-injected carriers tunnel through the high-$k$ dielectric preferentially near the drain side of the gate, where the dielectric barrier is most strongly lowered by the drain bias, and are collected by the drain. This provides a direct real-space picture of the DIDBL-driven gate-drain leakage mechanism.

items.title: Phase imaging of vortex laser beams in antiresonant and hollow waveguides for high harmonic generation and telecommunications in the IR-to-x-ray regime
items.abstract: We interrogate experimentally the conservation of orbital angular momentum (OAM) of laser beams in the VIS–IR spectral range propagating in anti-resonant waveguides for next-generation high harmonic generation in the soft and hard x-ray region, and telecommunication applications. Vortex beams with effective fractional OAM of 0.6–1.3 are coupled to hollow-core or anti-resonant waveguides of 30–150μm inner diameters, sharing an identical revolver substructure of 6–12 hollow-core capillaries. First, using holography, we interfere the fractional OAM beams with a Gaussian reference beam, yielding characteristic multi-spiral phase patterns in Fourier space. Experimental analyses and theoretical beam propagation show excellent quantitative agreement, suggesting conservation of OAM for large bandwidths of at least ~400nm. This enables structured laser pulses of extended femtosecond bandwidth to be combined with waveguides optimized for high transmission, especially relevant for the near-IR–mid-IR regimes. Second, ptychographic coherent diffractive imaging can detail the phase topology with near-wavelength resolution across a vortex beam. We demonstrate enhanced OAM characterization using structured light with quantum properties combined with ptychography — which we term quanthography — further confirming that OAM is preserved. In perspective, guided twisted laser beams with large bandwidth can produce ultrahigh harmonics in the IR-to-x-ray region with inherently large OAM of 10–1000, as well as multiply data transmission capacity using structured IR light in novel anti-resonance fiber-optic telecommunication systems. Furthermore, highly structured EUV–soft x-ray light can greatly enhance phase contrast in coherent diffractive imaging using tabletop apparatus at the sub-1–10 nm spatial scale for semiconductor metrology.
items.venue: Unconventional Imaging, Sensing, and Adaptive Optics

items.title: Performance modeling of photonic accelerators for attention kernel
items.abstract: In modern machine learning models such as Transformers, the attention kernel serves as the core computational kernel and is typically accelerated using transistor-based systems. Photonic in-memory computing offers a promising alternative by leveraging high optical bandwidth and operating frequencies for efficient multiply-accumulate operations. However, photonic compute arrays, such as photonic-SRAM (pSRAM) in-memory compute arrays, cannot support the large on-chip storage required for intermediate data in the attention kernel, necessitating integration with conventional electronic external memory. In addition, non-linear operations such as softmax require electronic execution. These constraints require a hybrid photonic-electronic architecture for attention acceleration. Developing such an accelerator requires understanding how hybrid photonic-electronic system parameters influence sustained performance. Therefore, a system-level performance model is necessary to identify and tune parameters and guide the design decisions required to achieve the target performance. We address this need by developing a system-level performance model for photonic accelerators that quantifies the impact of pSRAM compute arrays and electronic external memory on sustained performance (TOPS) for the attention kernel. We decompose the attention kernel into computation primitives and map them onto pSRAM-based compute arrays fabricated using GlobalFoundries’ standard silicon photonics process. We evaluate pSRAM configurations with 256x64 array size, 4-16-bit precision, 40-200 WDM channels, and electronic external memory such as HBM3E. Using our system performance model, we identify operating regions where photonic acceleration yields significant performance gains with sustained performance reaching up to 85 PetaOps/s at 200 WDM channels, as well as regions where memory overhead dominates.

items.title: Neural bolometers: designing next-generation infrared thermal imagers with in-pixel neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Emerging applications like Heat-Assisted Detection and Ranging and thermal LIDAR necessitate a shift toward high-resolution, information-rich infrared perception. However, conventional infrared detectors face challenges in area, latency, and power consumption. To address these limitations, we demonstrated a Spintronic Poisson Bolometer that operates in a Poisson-counting regime, where infrared detection is achieved through thermally activated transitions between discrete magnetization states. Building on this platform, we present the concept of a neural bolometer that integrates spintronic poisson bolometers with artificial neural network architectures. Leveraging their tunable stochastic response, nanoscale footprint, and CMOS compatibility, these devices enable in-pixel computation. Our approach enables long-wave infrared (LWIR) detectors to function as both imaging sensors and stochastic computing units. The system achieves LWIR MNIST classification with 92.5% accuracy, 2.82μs inference time, and 1.9μW power consumption. The proposed approach can usher-in a new generation of thermal imagers with in-pixel computing for next-generation of thermal vision.
items.venue: Unconventional Imaging, Sensing, and Adaptive Optics 2026

items.title: Morphotropic Phase Boundary Engineering in HfO2-Based High-k Dielectric Nanosystems for Dynamic Random-Access Memory Capacitors: A Review
items.abstract: Abstract HfO2-based dielectrics engineered into an MPB-like regime have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) capacitors because they offer enhanced dielectric permittivity while preserving the wide bandgap and CMOS compatibility of fluorite-structured oxides. At the nanometer-scale film thicknesses and grain dimensions relevant to DRAM, surface and interface energies, electrode confinement, stress, and defect distributions strongly reshape the relative stability and accessibility of fluorite-derived phases. However, the physical origin of the high-k response and its relationship with leakage current and reliability remain under active discussion. In this review, we summarize recent progress in HfO2-based MPB dielectrics from three perspectives. First, we discuss two complementary interpretations of dielectric enhancement: spatial phase coexistence between orthorhombic and tetragonal phases at the MPB, and dynamic nonlinear dielectric response associated with low transition barriers and field-induced structural evolution. Second, we review major engineering strategies for achieving MPB-like behavior, including stoichiometric and oxygen-vacancy control, advanced annealing processes, doping, bilayer and superlattice heterostructures, and electrode/interface engineering. Third, we evaluate the practical performance and reliability requirements for DRAM applications, with emphasis on the coupled trade-offs among dielectric constant, leakage current, equivalent oxide thickness, and time-dependent dielectric breakdown. Representative reports include k ≈ 67 with a leakage current density of 3 × 10−8 A/cm2 at 0.8 V and, in a separate ultrathin HZO device, an EOT of approximately 2.42 Å with k ≈ 64.24. Finally, we highlight that the optimization of MPB HfO2-based dielectrics requires a holistic design framework that simultaneously considers phase stability, defect dynamics, interface quality, and realistic low-voltage benchmarking conditions.

items.title: Low-resistance ohmic contacts: a strategy for ideal 2D semiconductor transistors
items.abstract: The rapid development of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) field-effect transistors (FETs) highlights the critical need to reduce the contact resistance for the future of Moore’s law using 2D complementary metal-oxide semiconductors. Electrical metal contacts with 2D TMDs-based FETs remain a critical challenge because of their high contact resistance, which primarily results from the Schottky barrier, poor interface quality, and Fermi level pinning. In this study, we report a significant reduction in the contact resistance of 2D TMDs using several strategies including plasma knowledge based polymorphic engineering, controllable doping, band matching, phase engineering and insertion buffer layer.

items.title: Low Dark Current and High Responsivity in Asymmetric-Electrode Ultraviolet Photodetectors Based on GaN/AlGaN High-Electron-Mobility Transistor
items.abstract: In this work, an ultraviolet photodetector (UV PD) with an asymmetric- interdigitated-electrode structure based on an AlGaN/GaN heterojunction is demonstrated. By optimizing the metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) epitaxial process, high-quality GaN epitaxial layers with low dislocation density were successfully grown on Si substrates. The combination of the asymmetric-electrode design and the polarization effect of the AlGaN/GaN heterojunction effectively suppresses the dark current while enhancing the ultraviolet responsivity. The device achieves a self-powered peak responsivity (${R}\text {)}$of 0.53A/W and a high specific detectivity (${D}^{\ast } \text {)}$of$1.90\times 10^{{13}}$Jones. Under a bias voltage of 5V, the dark current (${I}_{\text {dark}}\text {)}$is as low as 7.81pA, the peak responsivity reaches 7541 A/W, the photo-to-dark current ratio (PDCR) reaches$10^{{8}}$, and the rise and fall times are 12.01 and 5.96 ms, respectively. The correlation between material defects and device performance is systematically analyzed, revealing the enhancement mechanism of carrier separation and transport in the AlGaN/GaN heterojunction.

items.title: Laser plasma x-ray sources for semiconductor metrology
items.abstract: This paper discusses the development of compact laser-driven ultrabrilliant microfocus x-ray sources (LPXSs) and their application to semiconductor micro-XRF metrology. LPXSs also offer significant advantages in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, x-ray microscopy, and x-ray imaging applications. The LPXSs employ mJ laser pulses with tens of kHz repetition rate. These pulses are focused onto liquid metal targets, generating characteristic line emissions in the soft, tender, and hard x-ray regimes (200eV to 24keV). LPXSs offer a significant potential enhancement over typical microfocus X-ray tubes because they offer x-ray source brightness that exceed that of tubes. LPXS data from bismuth and gallium-based targets have been measured. The LPXS spectra were used for highly sensitive quantification of germanium on silicon wafers. These results establish a credible pathway to elevate micro-XRF from a near-line analytical technique to a viable inline metrology solution for Ge detection and depth profile measurements during the production of GAA and CFET semiconductor nodes.
items.venue: Advances in X-Ray/EUV Sources, Optics, and Components

items.title: Introducing Hardware Neurotechnology: A Non-Reconfigurable, Monolithic Transistor-as-a-Perceptron Architecture for Instantaneous AI Inference
items.abstract: Modern artificial intelligence is structurally constrained by the von Neumann bottleneck, which enforces an energy-intensive physical separation between arithmetic logic circuits and memory storage banks. This paper formalizes the architectural paradigm of Hardware Neurotechnology, an invention authored by Dr. Nitnem Singh Sodhi, wherein the physical silicon lattice natively embodies the artificial neural network graph, completely eliminating algorithmic instruction cycles and memory access overhead. By utilizing multi-input floating-gate (MIFG) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors operating in the subthreshold (weak-inversion) regime, the fundamental mathematical operations of a perceptron—linear synaptic weighting, multi-input accumulation, bias offset, and non-linear sigmoidal activation—are mapped directly onto single semiconductor device pairs. To overcome the catastrophic interconnect scaling, parasitic routing overhead, and silicon area expansion that have historically stalled analog neuromorphic engineering, the proposed architecture abandons dynamic reconfigurability in favor of a strictly hardwired, application-specific monolithic topology. Sacrificing field reconfigurability eliminates routing crossbar switches, SRAM routing memory, and intermediate analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), realizing an Application-Specific Neuromorphic Integrated Circuit (ASNIC) that executes complex inference tasks near-instantaneously at sub-femtojoule energy dissipation per synaptic operation.
items.venue: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

items.title: Interface-Engineered Diffuse Morphotropic Phase Boundary in Hafnia–Zirconia Nanolaminates for DRAM Capacitors
items.abstract: Abstract The morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) in Hf₁₋ ₓ Zr ₓ O₂ enables enhanced dielectric permittivity through the energetic competition between tetragonal and orthorhombic phases, yet its strong compositional sensitivity imposes stringent requirements on stoichiometric control in scaled DRAM capacitors. Here, we show that this limitation can be mitigated by converting a composition-defined MPB into an interface-defined one using tetragonal/orthorhombic HfO₂–ZrO₂ nanolaminates. First-principles calculations reveal that the lattice-distorted heterointerface reduces the tetragonal-to-orthorhombic transition barrier from approximately 50 to 7 meV per formula unit relative to composition-matched bulk HZO. The interfacial structural distortion and local cation coordination further modify the lattice polarization response, producing an extended region with MPB-like dielectric susceptibility across the interface. The calculated interfacial region extends over approximately 1.3–1.5 nm, substantially broader than the corresponding transition region in compositionally homogeneous HZO. Guided by this prediction, nanolaminates with sublayer thicknesses near 1.2 nm exhibit the highest dielectric response. In cylindrical TiN/HZO/ZrO₂/TiN DRAM-type capacitors, the optimized nanolaminate reaches a dielectric constant of ~ 40 at ± 0.6 V and ~ 49 near zero bias at 1 kHz, corresponding to an approximately 13% enhancement over a homogeneous MPB reference, while maintaining a leakage current density below 10⁻⁷ A cm⁻² at 0.6 V. These results establish interfacial lattice distortion as a route to relaxing the stringent compositional constraint of conventional HZO MPBs and provide an architecture-based strategy for high-κ dielectric engineering in scaled DRAM capacitors.

items.title: III-Nitride ferroelectrics for information storage and processing at low power and in extreme environments
items.abstract: in this talk, I will try to make the case of how novel III-nitride materials might present interesting avenues to overcome some of the above limitations being faced by both Silicon and Silicon Carbide (SiC) hardware. I will start by presenting our ongoing and recent work on integration of 2D chalcogenide semiconductors emerging wurtzite structure ferroelectric nitride materials1 namely aluminium scandium nitride (AlScN). First, I will present on Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors (FE-FETs) made from 2D materials when integrated with AlScN and make the case for 2D semiconductors in this application. I will then show our most recent results on scaling 2D/AlScN FE-FETs, achieving ultra-high carrier and current densities in ferroelectrically gated MoS2 and also demonstrate negative-capacitance FETs by engineering the AlScN/dielectric/2D interface. Then, I will switch gears to introduce the ferroelectric diode (FeD) memory device and demonstrate multi-bit operation8 as well as compute in memory (CIM) using FeD devices made from AlScN.

items.title: Giant Tunneling Electroresistance up to 108% via Synchronous Ohmic–Schottky Switching at Dual Interfaces in Ti2CF2/Bilayer GaN Sliding Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions
items.abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) based on sliding ferroelectrics hold promise for next-generation nonvolatile memories, yet achieving a high tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio remains challenging. In this work, the Ti2CF2/bilayer GaN sliding FTJ is theoretically constructed, and its electronic transport properties are explored using density functional theory (DFT) combined with nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. Our calculations reveal that ferroelectric polarization reversal in bilayer GaN modulates interfacial work function differences, enabling reversible transitions between Ohmic and Schottky contacts at both vertical and lateral interfaces. In the P↑ state, dual Ohmic contacts yield a high-conductance ON state. In contrast, the P↓ state produces large Schottky barriers at both interfaces that suppress tunneling current, corresponding to an OFF state. This dual-interface Ohmic-Schottky switching mechanism yields an ultrahigh TER ratio of up to 108%. Our findings provide critical insights into interface engineering and material selection for ultrahigh-TER FTJ devices based on sliding ferroelectrics.
items.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters

items.title: Enhanced atomic layer etching of aluminum and aluminum oxide
items.abstract: Thermal atomic layer etching (ALE) provides a precise pathway for aluminum surface preparation, optimizing optical performance at vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) wavelengths. This study investigates using trimethylaluminum (TMA) and anhydrous hydrogen fluoride (HF) to remove native aluminum oxide prior to encapsulation with dielectric thin films via atomic layer deposition (ALD). This integrated ALE/ALD process enables high-reflectance coatings and bandpass filters for applications below 200 nm. We demonstrate that the Al2O3 etch rate is highly sensitive to chamber conditioning; specifically, alkali halides like cesium fluoride catalyze the reaction. This effect lowers the thermal threshold for etching from >300 °C to 125 °C, protecting sensitive substrates and minimizing subsurface damage. While deep etching can increase roughness, lower temperatures enhance selectivity for native oxide removal. Consequently, a VUV mirror with ALD MgF2 improves from 60% to 80% reflectivity at 120 nm using this method. We discuss applications in electronics, superconductors, and the scalability of these methods for meter-class mirrors intended for future NASA large-aperture space observatories.

items.title: Engineering Neuromorphic Computing Systems for Brain-Inspired Processing
items.abstract: Neuromorphic computing is a computer-system design approach inspired by the structure and information-processing principles of biological neural systems. Unlike conventional von Neumann architectures, neuromorphic systems integrate computation and memory more closely and exploit event-driven communication, sparse activity, parallelism, and, in some implementations, on-chip learning. This paper presents a structured, source-audited review of neuromorphic computing, focusing on architecture, spiking neural networks, learning mechanisms, hardware implementation, scalability, energy efficiency, edge intelligence, and engineering challenges. Rather than combining heterogeneous measurements through unsupported statistical meta-analysis, the review distinguishes documented hardware specifications, workload-specific experimental measurements, and reported performance claims. Representative platforms, including IBM TrueNorth, Intel Loihi, Loihi 2, and Hala Point, are examined in terms of neuron and synaptic capacity, architectural organization, learning capabilities, and deployment context. Evidence indicates that neuromorphic systems can provide energy and latency advantages for selected sparse, event-driven workloads, although performance depends strongly on workload characteristics, algorithms, implementation, and measurement methods. TrueNorth demonstrated large-scale digital neuromorphic integration, while Loihi introduced programmable on-chip learning and Loihi 2 expanded neuron-model flexibility and capacity. Hala Point demonstrates further multi-chip scaling potential, but its specifications should not be interpreted as biological equivalence. Recent initiatives such as NeuroBench improve evaluation consistency by distinguishing algorithm-level and deployed-system measurements. Key challenges include training large spiking networks, hardware variability, software interoperability, benchmarking, memory and communication constraints, and integration with established AI workflows. The review concludes that neuromorphic computing is a complementary paradigm with strong potential for sparse temporal workloads, low-latency applications, and power-constrained environments.
items.venue: International Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science

items.title: Distributed Authorization and Reliability-Aware Hardware Security for Photovoltaic Monitoring
items.abstract: Unattended photovoltaic monitoring nodes must maintain authenticated operation under physical access, intermittent connectivity, and environmentally induced key-reconstruction errors. We present a distributed adaptive hardware security framework (DAHSF) combining trusted-gateway threshold authorization, adaptive static random-access memory (SRAM) physical unclonable function (PUF) reconstruction, and incident-driven inspection. Independent epoch secrets separate current authorization from retained historical shares. A nested Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (BCH) error-correction scheme reconstructs a fixed 2016-bit SRAM-PUF response, from which universal hashing extracts a 256-bit seed; federated estimation guides decoding effort. The cost and defense trade-offs are assessed under the tested workload, gateway trust, prediction-calibration, and availability conditions. On a 30-node ESP32 platform, DAHSF reduces median startup and mean node power by 4.8% and 4.4% relative to a matched lightweight baseline, with 14.3% more incremental RAM. Predicted-bound decoding reduces mean decoding time from 96 to 59 microseconds. A separate confirmatory cohort records three failures in 120,000 stressed reconstructions; its board-clustered 95% upper bound is 8.6×10−5. In the moderate attack scenario, the full inspection profile reduces compromised-node exposure by 30.0% relative to a risk-threshold policy and by 18.0% relative to frozen propagation-rate estimates. The recorded control workload has no observed 1 ms MPPT deadline misses, while fault injection still bypasses authorization in 168 of 4000 attempts.

items.title: Development of high-precision nickel electroforming process for EUV and x-ray optics
items.abstract: Electroforming is a replication technique that produces metal components with inverse geometries of a mandrel by electrodepositing thick metal layers onto its surface and subsequently separating them. Owing to its superior replication accuracy, this technique is widely used for optical components, precision molds, and micro-patterned structures. In particular, electroforming has been employed for x-ray optics, which demand extremely high shape accuracy on the order of nanometers. Mimura et al. have developed a high-precision nickel electroforming process for axially symmetric mirrors with a shape accuracy better than 15nm(P-V), which is characterized by the unconventional conditions of electrodeposition: low current density, room temperature, and no stirring. This process has also been successfully applied to the fabrication of a Wolter-I mirror of an x-ray telescope for the purpose of solar observation. In the field of space science, demand for higher-precision x-ray mirrors is increasing for future missions. Furthermore, this process has the potential to be applied to EUV collector mirrors, essential but expensive consumable components in EUV lithography systems, which are indispensable for further semiconductor miniaturization. This study aims to establish a high-precision nickel electroforming process for both space and semiconductor applications. To investigate whether the electroforming process can be applicable to fabrication of EUV collector mirrors, Mo/Si multilayers are formed on an electroformed nickel mirror, and the reflectance of EUV light is measured, comparing with that of the multilayers formed on the silicon wafer.

items.title: Comparative ECCI metrology of threading dislocations in commercial GaN HEMT structures
items.abstract: Heteroepitaxy is the predominant mode of thin-film growth for gallium nitride (GaN) in LEDs, RF electronics and power electronic applications. A major factor hindering GaN from wider adoption in the higher-voltage regime is the pervasiveness of threading dislocations generated during heteroepitaxial growth on lattice and thermally mismatched substrates. In this work, the dislocation populations of commercially-obtained GaN HEMT structures grown on sapphire, silicon and SiC substrates are characterized. Spatial maps of threading dislocations are obtained using the SEM-based technique of electron channeling contrast imaging (ECCI) which allows for the comparison of defect densities across the HEMT wafers. It is demonstrated that the sapphire and silicon-grown HEMT structures have similar dislocation densities of approximately 3 × 109 cm-2 whereas the SiC-based structure has a density around 71% lower at 8.7 × 108 cm-2. Through further variation of ECCI operating conditions, determination of relative concentration of edge dislocations to dislocations with a screw component is obtained in the SiC HEMT structure.

items.title: Characterising CPU-initiated High Bandwidth Memory Access
items.abstract: An increasing number of high-performance computers are equipped with high bandwidth memory. Their CPUs have cache-coherent access to this memory type over high-speed interconnects or as unified memory. We analyse two such systems, NVIDIA’s GH200 and AMD’s MI300A. We discuss their memory setup and measure memory access latency and throughput. We evaluate weighted memory page interleaving and strided memory access as candidates for increasing the measured throughput. Weighted interleaving utilises CPU and GPU memory simultaneously and enables exceeding the measured throughput on only CPU or GPU memory for all tested workloads. Using strided memory access, which accesses memory at fixed intervals, we achieve higher throughput than using a non-strided sequential pattern.

items.title: Best Match: Enhanced Hybrid-Row-Height Standard Cell Placement with Macro Blockages
items.abstract: Hybrid-row-height IC design incorporates placement rows of two or more distinct heights which do not have to be integer multiples of a single height. This design strategy is more flexible for optimizing power, performance, and area simultaneously. Several attempts have been made to deal with the hybrid-row-height standard cell placement problem with customizable row configuration by intelligently leveraging a commercial placement tool. Here we propose an enhanced algorithm, Best Match, to determine the best matching row configuration for a given netlist which leads to minimal disturbance to the initial timing-optimized placement after placement legalization. Our row planning approach has a number of enhancements over previous works, including (1) consideration of horizontal displacement of cells in addition to vertical displacement of cells, (2) precise positioning of the hybrid rows, and (3) ability to handle macros in a design. As a result, we obtained a much smaller total displacement of cells after placement legalization compared to the state-of-the-art works. The experimental results show that our approach outperforms the flow-based method in [9] with 48.4%, 24.9%, and 68.8% reduction in the total displacement of cells, final routed wirelength, and post-route total negative slack, respectively. It yielded 13.4% reduction in the total displacement of cells, 4.5% reduction in the final routed wirelength, and 26.3% reduction in the post-route total negative slack compared to [7]. Furthermore, compared to the legalized placement generated by a commercial tool under the uniformly hybrid row configuration, the routed wirelength and post-route total negative slack are reduced by 27.4% and 91.8%, respectively, under the customized row configuration determined by Best Match.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems

items.title: Atomic layer deposition of AlFx on 2D MoS2
items.abstract: Semiconducting 2D materials such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) show promising capabilities in use as field effect transistors, memory devices, and photodetectors, many of which structures require the addition of a dielectric top layer. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is a well established method for producing dielectric films, however this process presents a problem for 2D materials as ALD relies on active surface chemistry that is generally not provided by 2D materials. Over enough ALD cycles, a dielectric film will eventually form on 2D materials by edge nucleation, however this loses ALD’s control over the film’s composition and thickness. In this study, we explore aluminum-flouride (AlFx) as a dielectric material deposited directly on MoS2. As the most electronegative element fluorine is expected to be more reactive than oxygen, potentially generating uniform nucleation sites on the 2D material’s surface. Preliminary results indicate that AlFx is capable of depositing directly onto exfoliated MoS2 within 5 ALD cycles. Research is ongoing to determine if ALD of AlFx causes any damages to the underlying MoS2. and to determine if 1 nm of AlFx is capable of fully covering MoS2.

items.title: Atomic layer deposition approaches for future extremely scaled microelectronic devices
items.abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) National Laboratories advance microelectronics through coordinated programs and premier user facilities that connect fundamental science with technological innovation. This talk will overview key microelectronics research at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL), focusing on next-generation extreme ultraviolet (EUV) photoresists and atomic layer deposition (ALD) of interconnect and dielectric materials for highly scaled semiconductor devices. These efforts leverage BNL’s DOE user facilities, including the Center for Functional Nanomaterials (CFN)—one of five DOE Nanoscale Science Research Centers (NSRCs)—with expertise in ALD-enabled hybrid material synthesis for EUV lithography, and the National Synchrotron Light Source II (NSLS-II) for advanced structural and chemical characterization. Recent progress in vapor-phase synthesis of organic-inorganic hybrid EUV resists and their patterning performance will be presented, along with studies clarifying ALD growth of ruthenium for advanced interconnects and dielectric deposition on two-dimensional (2D) materials for future channel applications.

items.title: Ant‐inspired Trimodal Hair‐Like BiVO 4 Memristor for Intelligent Diving‐Assistance Systems
items.abstract: In biological systems, single‐modal stimuli are often insufficient for complex behaviors, whereas multimodal integration significantly enhances environmental perception and decision‐making. Inspired by ants, which synergistically process optical, chemical, and mechanical signals, the development of multimodal neuromorphic devices is highly desirable. However, most existing memristive systems remain limited to single electrical modulation, restricting the realization of integrated sensing‐memory‐computing platforms. In this work, an electro‐opto‐liquid trimodal memristor based on a hair‐like BiVO 4 architecture is developed, enabling the intrinsic integration of electrical synaptic plasticity, optical detection, and liquid sensing within single device. The antenna‐like hair‐like morphology promotes efficient multimodal signal coupling and interaction, resulting in stable conductance modulation, broadband photoresponse extending into the near‐infrared region, over 27,000 optical endurance cycles, and high sensitivity to liquid environments. Benefiting from these characteristics, the device demonstrates effective multimodal information fusion in neuromorphic computing, achieving a high underwater sensing and recognition accuracy of ∼92% with a low loss of ∼0.23. Furthermore, it enables dynamic visual recognition, attaining ∼91% accuracy in identifying the burst motion of fish schools. This work highlights a viable strategy for constructing compact, multifunctional neuromorphic systems toward complex environmental perception and adaptive intelligence.

items.title: Multifunctional synaptic learning and neuromorphic computing using crystalline TiO$_x$/NiO$_x$ heterojunction-based memory devices
items.abstract: An attempt is made here to mimic different properties of biological synapses using Ag/TiO$_x$/NiO$_x$/p$^{++}$-Si memristor structure by studying its different transport properties under dc and pulsed bias. The presence of crystalline NiO$_x$ with smaller gains is found to be helpful to get TiO$_x$ deposited on its top with crystalline properties and larger grains. The heterostructure offers stable bipolar forming free non-volatile resistive switching characteristics under reverse biased condition with gradual set and reset features. These devices are also able to successfully implement the classical Pavlov's learning, study artificial nociceptor and Morse code detection. While incorporating synaptic weights derived from the measured conductance programming pulse relationship, an artificial neural network achieves nearly 95\% accuracy in MNIST digit recognition. In brief, NiO$_x$/TiO$_x$ heterojunction plays the pivotal role in getting such reproducible $I-V$ characteristics for mimicking different properties of biological synapses.

items.title: Vertical organic electrochemical transistors: recent developments and applications
items.abstract: Since their advent in 1984, Organic Electrochemical Transistors (OECT) have emerged as a versatile platform for biosensing, logic circuitry, and neuromorphic computing, thanks to their unique combination of low-voltage operation, high transconductance, biocompatibility and ion-to-electron transduction capabilities. In the 2010s, a design change characterized by the vertical stacking of the source and drain electrodes resulted in the vertical OECT (vOECT). This new architecture allowed a reduction of device footprint while increasing its transconductance (gm) and operational speed, thus improving performance and enabling further miniaturization. Here, I present a case where the vertical architecture promotes enhanced performance for p-type accumulation mode OECTs, resulting in one of best ratios of gm by footprint area. Next, design of vOECT complementary inverters is discussed, achieving large gains (≈200 V/V), switching times of 1ms and stability around 18000 cycles. Finally, non-volatile memories based on vOECTs are presented as promising candidates for neuromorphic computing building blocks. In these devices, the memory level transition is associated with the physical deposition or removal of a fiber-like channel within cavities between the source and drain electrodes via electropolymerization.

items.title: Thermally Oxidized Al x In 1–x N/GaN Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Capacitors
items.abstract: Vertical metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) capacitors formed by thermally oxidizing Al${}_{{0}.{82}}$In${}_{{0}.{18}}$N on GaN are investigated. The structures are grown on GaN substrates and consist of 1-$\mu $m-thick n-type GaN followed by a 30-nm thick Al${}_{{0}.{82}}$In${}_{{0}.{18}}$N-layer. The Al${}_{{0}.{82}}$In${}_{{0}.{18}}$N-layer is oxidized in O2at elevated temperatures to two different depths, resulting in a completely oxidized AlInN layer with a ~56-nm-thick oxide layer and a partially oxidized layer with an oxide thickness of ~20 nm. The partially oxidized capacitor exhibits less hysteresis, a large catastrophic dielectric breakdown of ~10 MV/cm, and the ability to measure trap density ($\sim 10^{{12}}$–${1}.{5}{\,}{\,}\times {\,}{\,}{10} ^{{12}}\text {)}$. The estimated relative dielectric constants of the oxide from the capacitance versus voltage ($CV$) measurements are 9.3 for the fully oxidized sample and 5.8 for the partially oxidized sample.

items.title: Progress of Artificial Olfactory Systems in Computing Architectures: From Von Neumann to Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial olfactory systems (AOS) are emerging as a pivotal technology for intelligent odor detection, drawing inspiration from the remarkable sensitivity and adaptability of the biological olfactory system. This review provides a comprehensive summary of recent advances in AOS, from traditional designs based on von Neumann architectures to cutting‐edge neuromorphic platforms that closely integrate sensing, memory, and computation. We introduce a systematic classification of AOS according to their computational architecture: (1) von Neumann‐based systems that combine sensor arrays and advanced pattern recognition algorithms for odor classification and multi‐modal analysis; (2) integrated perception‐memory devices that emulate synaptic plasticity, enabling adaptive response and memory for complex olfactory environments; and (3) neuromorphic olfactory systems featuring near‐sensor and in‐sensor computing, leveraging memristor arrays and monolithic integration for real‐time, energy‐efficient, and robust odor processing. This review focuses on the recent progress, working mechanisms, and advanced features of AOS from traditional von Neumann architectures to neuromorphic computing. Finally, we offer a critical outlook on overcoming systemic bottlenecks, and propose a strategic roadmap for realizing robust, autonomous olfactory intelligence.

items.title: Polarization aberrations in EUV projection objectives: effects of numerical aperture and illumination incidence angle
items.abstract: Polarization aberrations become increasingly significant in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) projection objectives as the numerical aperture increases and multilayer coating structures become more complex. In this work, polarization ray tracing is employed to investigate the effects of numerical aperture and illumination incidence angle on polarization aberrations. The P -matrix pupil is constructed to characterize the spatially varying polarization response, and the amplitude response matrix is calculated to evaluate its coherent-light impulse response. The effects of NA are investigated using MET3 and MET5 projection objectives with image-side NAs of 0.3 and 0.5, respectively. Increasing the NA increases the maximum diattenuation from 0.00926 to 0.22286 and the maximum retardance from 0.01784 rad to 0.20921 rad, accompanied by stronger off-diagonal ARM responses and spatial modulation. Under pseudo-total-reflection conditions, increasing the illumination-side plane-mirror tilt angle from 80° to 85° reduces the maximum diattenuation from 0.0264 to 0.0220 and the retardance range from 0.218 ∼ 0.486 rad to 0.077 ∼ 0.286 rad, with slightly weaker off-diagonal ARM responses. These results demonstrate distinct effects of numerical aperture and illumination incidence angle on polarization aberrations. The observed angular dependence is influenced by the multilayer reflection mechanism, coating properties, and optical configuration. This work provides a basis for analyzing polarization aberrations in high-NA EUV projection objectives under different multilayer-reflection conditions.

items.title: Performance enhancement of complementary FETs and circuits via a hybrid dual-κ spacer strategy at sub-1 nm node
items.abstract: The complementary field-effect transistor (CFET) is considered the most promising structure at sub-1 nm node for denser integration through vertical stacking of n/pFETs. However, large parasitic capacitance and resistance remain severe restrains of device performance. In this work, to solve the parasitic issues, the hybrid dual-κ spacer strategy is proposed and carried out on CFET. To optimize circuit performance, the material for inner spacers (ISPs) is investigated to optimize parasitic resistance while low-κ is used for the larger outer spacer (OSP) to lower parasitic capacitance. Results show that the hybrid dual-κ spacer CFET performs best with a low-κ OSP and Si 3 N 4 ISPs compared with single low-κ spacer, with I ON improved by 11.18% in top nFET and 87.42% in bottom pFET, increasing C gg by 20.31% and 42.19%, respectively. The device demonstrates 53.48% improvement in RO frequency, the highest noise margin and 8.58% faster write speed in SRAM. Results indicate that the hybrid dual-κ spacer design provides a pathway for further device-and-circuit co-optimization of CFET.

items.title: Optically Tuneable Memristors Based on Au NP–PDR1A Nanocomposites Probed by Impedance Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Optical memristors are promising building blocks for neuromorphic vision systems because they can emulate retina‐like adaptive signal processing. However, the development of practical devices remains limited by an incomplete understanding of the coupled electrical–optical responses and the mechanisms governing switching. In this work, gold nanoparticles (Au NPs) were dispersed in poly(disperse red 1 acrylate) (PDR1A) to form a photo‐responsive composite that was used to fabricate optical memristor devices via a simple solution‐based process. The optoelectronic behavior was systematically investigated using impedance spectroscopy to probe charge‐transport dynamics and interfacial processes under operating conditions, complementing structural TEM imaging studies that reveals the underlying morphology. The devices exhibit light‐tuneable resistive–capacitive switching, with a transition from purely capacitive behavior in pristine PDR1A devices to coupled resistive–capacitive transport in Au NP:PDR1A composites. Impedance analysis indicates trap‐mediated conduction together with nanoparticle‐assisted conductive pathways that are dynamically modulated by light‐induced photomechanical expansion and contraction of the polymer matrix. Equivalent‐circuit modeling further clarifies the resistive–capacitive interplay responsible for optically controlled switching. These findings provide mechanistic insight into light‐responsive memristive behavior and establish a framework for the design of optically tuneable memristive devices for neuromorphic computing and vision applications.

items.title: Modeling SiC MOSFETs threshold voltage drift: Constant and varying gate voltage stress conditions
items.abstract: This work presents a comprehensive methodology for modeling the threshold voltage drift of SiC MOSFETs based on experimental gate switching stress data. The proposed approach enables the evaluation of cumulative degradation under successive or combined electrical stresses. The developed model provides deep insight into the underlying aging mechanisms and allows the prediction of parameter shifts under realistic converter operation conditions. Furthermore, integrating the proposed drift model into a circuit-level simulation environment could facilitate the prediction of threshold voltage evolution in parallel SiC MOSFET configurations, which are common in high-power applications. Such integration supports the development of predictive maintenance strategies and reliability-oriented design frameworks for next-generation SiC-based power converters. The proposed methodology thus contributes to improving both the reliability modeling accuracy and the lifecycle gate switching stress performance assessment of advanced power electronic systems.

items.title: MORDOR: Mitigating Overheads of Read Disturbance Preventive Operations via Elastic Refresh Scheduling
items.abstract: Modern DRAM chips are susceptible to read disturbance phenomena such as RowHammer, where repeatedly accessing (hammering) a row of DRAM cells (i.e., a DRAM row) induces bitflips in other physically nearby (victim) DRAM rows. A common practice to avoid such bitflips is to preventively refresh victim rows that might otherwise experience bitflips. Unfortunately, preventive refreshes cause long latencies and need to be performed urgently before the aggressor row is activated again to ensure data integrity. This is done by prioritizing them over demand memory requests, thereby potentially imposing significant delays on those requests and causing performance and energy overheads. Our goal in this work is to alleviate these overheads by scheduling preventive refreshes off the critical path of demand memory requests. We propose MORDOR, a new preventive refresh scheduling policy that significantly reduces system performance degradation and energy consumption caused by preventive refresh operations. MORDOR is integrated into the memory controller and operates alongside memory-controller-based read disturbance mitigation techniques to intelligently delay preventive refresh operations, while maintaining their data integrity guarantees. MORDOR leverages the key observation that a preventive refresh operation targeting an aggressor row can be delayed to serve any other demand memory request, as long as that memory request does not access the aggressor row. By doing so, MORDOR executes latency-critical memory requests before long-latency preventive refresh operations, while mitigating read disturbance bitflips. We evaluate MORDOR by integrating it into six state-of-the-art read disturbance mitigation techniques. Our comprehensive evaluation shows that MORDOR significantly improves system performance and energy efficiency at low area cost.

items.title: IA generativa en la fabricación avanzada. Una revisión y un caso de uso en la electrónica de potencia
items.abstract: La Inteligencia Artificial está transformando la fabricación avanzada mediante gemelos digitales, modelos generativos, aprendizaje federado y sistemas explicables. Este trabajo revisa estos avances y los conecta con el proyecto europeo Moore4Power, centrado en la próxima generación de sistemas y componentes de electrónica de potencia. El enfoque combina modelos multifísicos, estimación probabilística de vida útil remanente e IA generativa para apoyar el mantenimiento predictivo de dispositivos IGBT y SiC MOSFET. Se identifican oportunidades y límites para el despliegue industrial, incluyendo interoperabilidad, incertidumbre, explicabilidad y validación en condiciones reales.
items.venue: Workshop on Multimedia for Cooking and Eating Activities

items.title: HOMARD: Hammering Off-chip Memory via Aggregate power Rail Disclosure
items.abstract: Software-based microarchitectural attacks have mainly exploited timing differences to infer information from DRAM. However, defenses and optimizations can prevent timing-based approaches from resolving precise microarchitectural behaviors. We show that unprivileged millisecond- and milliampere-resolution power sensors on modern Arm SoCs can recover DRAM mapping functions and reveal the data dependence of memory accesses without timers. We present HOMARD, a methodology that reads DRAM activity from this telemetry, and two attack primitives. HOMARD-RE is a hierarchy-aware linear-algebraic method that reverse-engineers DRAM addressing functions from power alone. HOMARD-DATA recovers the Hamming weight of a fetched cache line through joint-power rail templating and secret byte values through correlation power analysis on the same rails. Across an AMD ZCU102, a Raspberry Pi 5, and a multi-chip-based LPDDR4 NVIDIA Jetson TX2, HOMARD-RE succeeds where row-buffer timing methods fail. On the Pi 5, HOMARD-DATA classifies 9 Hamming-weight levels at 81.5% accuracy and recovers secret bytes in minutes by correlating rail current with data-dependent bit toggling between neighbors in a row. Both primitives work with an architectural load or a mispredicted Spectre-RSB path on which no value is architecturally read. These results establish unprivileged power telemetry as an independent side channel for profiled microarchitectural attacks, particularly when timing falls silent.

items.title: Design-Technology Co-Optimization for 3-nm GAAFET and Standard Cells With a Mixture-of-Experts Actor--Critic Method
items.abstract: At advanced nodes, optimizing isolated device intrinsic metrics does not necessarily translate into postlayout gains in standard cell delay and power, creating a device-to-cell objective mismatch. To address this issue, we develop a closed-loop design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) flow using a predictive 3-nm GAAFET PDK that shifts the optimization targets to postlayout cell-level delay and power obtained after layout generation, parasitic extraction (PEX), and characterization. Each candidate parameter set requires a complete EDA evaluation, while the nonlinear parameter to performance mapping and conflicting delay and power objectives further complicate the search. Within this closed loop framework, we propose mixture-of-experts actor–critic (MOE-AC), which uses multiple expert networks to explore distinct objective regions and efficiently identify the cell-level Pareto front under a limited evaluation budget. The proposed flow reduces the average power delay product (PDP) of representative cells by 18.09% over the baseline. Under an identical evaluation budget, the MOE-AC increases the Pareto hypervolume (HV) by 11.1% and reduces the best PDP by 7.7% relative to a conventional actor–critic method, while achieving a$6.3\times $speedup over Bayesian optimization. Furthermore, the optimized parameter set maintains performance gains across cell topologies not included in the optimization and at the evaluated extreme PVT corners, indicating cross topology transferability and PVT robustness.

items.title: Cooperative STT and SOT switching in perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions: Role of the pulse-end magnetization state
items.abstract: Spin--orbit torque MRAM (SOT-MRAM) is a leading candidate for next-generation nonvolatile memory, offering high speed, endurance, and architectural compatibility. However, in conventional SOT switching, the magnetization remains near the in-plane region at pulse termination, making the final state highly sensitive to post-pulse relaxation dynamics and prone to back-switching. To overcome this, we propose a field-free scheme in which the transverse SOT drives large-angle precessional excitation while the perpendicular spin-transfer torque (STT) biases the trajectory toward the reversed $-z$ state.
