By rigorously subsuming top-down (EUV) and bottom-up (DSA, ALD) processes into a Lagrangian extremum problem within an 8-Dimensional topological tensor space, this framework mathematically suppresses cumulative fabrication errors and spectacularlyelevates destructive metrology into the continuous measurement of symplectic topological invariants.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: ML-Predicted EOTPR Reference Waveforms from CAD with Layout-Aware Correlation for Efficient Fault Isolation in Advanced Packages
items.abstract: Electro-Optical Terahertz Pulse Reflectometry (EOTPR) is widely used for fault isolation in advanced semiconductor packages, where interpretation of measured waveforms relies on comparison with reference responses. These reference waveforms are traditionally generated through physics-based simulation using trace models derived from CAD layout data, a process that remains time-consuming and dependent on iterative refinement despite prior automation efforts. In this work, we present a machine learning-based approach for predicting EOTPR reference waveforms directly from CAD-derived interconnect features. The model is trained on simulation-generated reference waveforms, enabling it to learn the relationship between interconnect geometry and waveform characteristics. This eliminates the need for explicit per-signal simulation during inference and enables rapid, on-demand waveform generation. In addition, we introduce a layout-aware analysis capability that maps waveform features to interconnect geometry, enabling interactive correlation between signal-domain behavior and physical structure. The proposed framework significantly accelerates reference waveform generation while improving interpretability in failure analysis workflows.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Localization of Gate Oxide Defects within Pool Capacitors in NAND-type 3D Flash Memory
items.abstract: As NAND-type 3D Flash memory continues to scale in performance, speed, and storage density, the underlying architecture has grown significantly more complex. Global reference signals and clock networks must traverse large areas of the chip while driving numerous loads. A defect affecting even a single load can disturb the integrity of the shared global signal, causing degradation across multiple functional blocks and potentially resulting in fatal system-level failures. Therefore, rapid and accurate localization of defects on these global signal paths is critical for root cause identification and for enabling design, layout, and process teams to collaborate to reduce DPPM and improve overall yield. In this work, we demonstrate the localization of a subtle defect within the pool capacitor of a global signal line in a NAND-type 3D Flash memory device. This type of defect is challenging to detect due to its small physical footprint and its location buried deep within the die, which makes typical OBIRCH hotspots diffused or smeared out. The methodology presented here enables precise identification of such hidden failures.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: IAIA: Interrupt-Aware Index Analysis for SSD Firmware
items.abstract: Interrupts make SSD (Solid State Drive) firmware hard to analyze because they can update shared state at nondeterministic points. An array index that looks safe in the main code may therefore become out of bounds after an interrupt handler runs. This paper presents IAIA, an interrupt-aware index analysis that reports OOB candidates whose values may be affected by interrupt handlers. IAIA defines interrupt-aware semantics and implements it as an abstract interpreter. The interpreter models handler effects, computes provenance information, and collects OOB candidates. Post-processing then traces the provenance of each candidate and reports a warning only when the trace reaches an interrupt handler. On the benchmark suite, IAIA reports the intended interrupt-related warnings and produces no warnings for fixed versions or non-handler OOB cases.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 1st International Workshop on Firmware Testing and Analysis

items.title: High-Quality Passive Voltage Contrast Imaging Enabled by a Novel Integrated Low-Angle Ion Milling-SEM Delayering System
items.abstract: The increasing integration density and structural complexity of advanced semiconductor devices have made delayering processes for failure analysis and structural characterization significantly more challenging. Conventional approaches such as chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) and plasma focused ion beam (FIB) milling often suffer from process-induced damage, surface contamination, and material-dependent milling variability, all of which can critically degrade the reliability of passive voltage contrast (PVC) observation. In this work, we present a newly developed air-free low-angle ion milling-scanning electron microscopy (LIM-SEM) platform, in which a LIM system is directly integrated into the sample exchange chamber of a high-resolution SEM, enabling uninterrupted delayering and observation without atmospheric exposure. Using this platform, direct delayering from the under-bump metallization (UBM) layer was successfully performed without any mechanical pre-treatment. The method provided uniform, wide-area, and damage-free material removal within practical processing times. The resulting surfaces remained free of contamination and mechanical artifacts, allowing stable SEM imaging from low magnifications up to beyond 100kx magnification. A direct comparison between air-exposed and air-free conditions clearly demonstrates that even short atmospheric exposure causes noticeable PVC degradation due to surface contamination, whereas the air-free workflow effectively preserves intrinsic voltage contrast. As a result, PVC visualization in advanced-node (7 nm) SRAM devices was substantially enhanced. These results demonstrate that the proposed LIM-SEM platform enables reliable visualization of intrinsic delayering behavior and voltage contrast in advanced semiconductor devices that are high-sensitive to oxidation and contamination. The air-free LIM-SEM platform provides a powerful and practical solution for next-generation failure analysis, establishing a highly reliable methodology for preserving surface integrity and enhancing PVC performance in advanced semiconductor technologies.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Few-Shot Segmentation of Advanced 3D IC Structures Under Varying X-ray Acquisition Strategies
items.abstract: Advanced semiconductor packaging technologies such as heterogeneous integration, chiplets, high-bandwidth memory, and three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D ICs) require non-destructive imaging techniques capable of resolving dense buried interconnect structures. This work investigates few-shot segmentation of semiconductor X-ray cross-sectional imagery acquired using computed tomography (CT) and precision angle laminography (PAL) under varying acquisition conditions. A prompt-based few-shot segmentation framework, referred to as FSS-SAM3, was implemented using the Segment Anything Model 3 operating entirely at inference time without gradient-based fine-tuning. Experiments were conducted on a dataset collected from NVIDIA H100 advanced packaging chiplets containing annotated C4 and microbump structures acquired under multiple laminographic slant-angle configurations. Quantitative evaluation under 1-shot and 5-shot protocols demonstrated substantial segmentation improvement for sparse interconnect structures, with C4 segmentation increasing from 29.19% to 65.03% mIoU when additional support examples were introduced. Comparative analysis between CT and PAL additionally demonstrated differences in reconstruction fidelity, artifact behavior, and interconnect visibility across varying acquisition geometries and slant angles. While the proposed framework showed strong correspondence-learning capability for sparse semiconductor structures, dense repetitive microbump arrays remained challenging due to extreme instance density and limited prompt propagation across the query image. The results demonstrate the potential of foundation-model-based few-shot segmentation for semiconductor failure analysis while highlighting key challenges associated with dense-instance segmentation in advanced packaging environments.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Failure Analysis Methodology for STT-MRAM Bit Cells and Emerging Memories
items.abstract: This work presents a novel methodology for STT-MRAM failure analysis, enabling systematic identification and characterization of defects at both device and circuit levels. Beyond STT-MRAM, the proposed framework is adaptable to other emerging memories such as RRAM (resistive RAM) and FeRAM (Ferroelectric RAM), which share similar structure as well as variability and endurance challenges.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Failure Analysis Approach on Intricate Redistribution Layer (RDL) Failures
items.abstract: Redistribution layers (RDLs) are critical in advanced packaging, yet their fine-pitch geometries and complex material interfaces make failure localization increasingly challenging during failure analysis. This paper presents two contrasting case studies that illustrate how electrical signatures guide the selection of an effective failure analysis approach for RDL-related failures. The first case demonstrates how simulation-referenced Comparative Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) enables non-destructive localization of open-circuit RDL defects prior to physical analysis. Correlation between measured and simulated waveforms facilitated targeted cross-sectioning that confirmed RDL delamination and cracking as the root cause. The second case investigates leakage failure in the absence of the RDL structure following chemical decapsulation, traditionally limiting direct physical localization. A coordinated workflow integrating backside OBIRCh, layout correlation, topside infrared (IR) imaging, and optical inspection enabled successful identification of mechanical damages consistent with stress-related mechanisms associated with RDL bonding process. These results demonstrate a practical, electrically driven methodology for RDL failure analysis, where comparative interpretation and multi-modal correlation improve diagnostic efficiency and enable reliable localization even when critical structures are no longer accessible.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Explainable artificial intelligence-based prediction of electrical characteristics in GAA MOSFETs
items.abstract: In this paper, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) based prediction is used for gate all around (GAA) MOSFET to predict its electrical behaviour. The data set is produced using TCAD simulations by changing device parameters like channel length (L g ), Radius of silicon pillar (R), work function (Φ m ), doping concentration (N d ), oxide thickness (t ox ) and drain bias (V ds ). The Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm is considered for training. The R 2 of 99.5% is achieved for threshold voltage prediction. The contribution of each device parameter to the model predictions at the global and local levels is determined by using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) for the purpose of model interpretability. SHAP measures the relative relevance of input factors for the overall dataset, while LIME explains individual predictions through the construction of local surrogate models. SHAP analysis revealed that gate length was the most influential parameter with a mean absolute SHAP value of 0.1. This was followed by the metal gate work function, drain bias, nanowire radius, channel doping concentration and oxide thickness with mean absolute SHAP values of 0.065, 0.05, 0.041, 0.026 and 0.015 respectively. The concordance between the SHAP, LIME and the well-established electrostatic principles of GAA MOSFETs confirm that the proposed XAI framework delivers accurate, transparent and physically interpretable predictions, making it a potential tool for AI-assisted design and optimization of semiconductor devices.

items.title: Enhancing Cross-Sectional Milling Performance in Plasma Focused Ion Beam using Shadow Masking
items.abstract: The increasing adoption of High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and advanced semiconductor packaging technologies has increased the demand for large-area and high-quality cross-sectional analysis. Consequently, the demand for Plasma Focused Ion Beam (PFIB) systems has also increased. PFIB enables rapid and efficient analysis through high-current ion beam milling. However, curtain effects in the cross section and the formation of a surface damage layer remain major obstacles to accurate analysis. To improve milling performance, this study presents a needle-based shadow masking technique for PFIB milling to enhance milling performance during semiconductor sample preparation. By physically blocking the beam tail near the Region Of Interest (ROI), the proposed method minimizes surface damage and curtain effects without requiring protective layers. Cross-sectional milling experiments using the shadow masking technique significantly reduced the surface damage layer and curtain effects. In addition, the experiments improved the sample perpendicularity by up to 43.3%. Owing to these benefits, the shadow masking approach reduced the overall process time by approximately 64.8% relative to the deposition sample during the Ar beam milling test. Accordingly, the throughput was calculated to increase by 184% compared with deposition conditions while maintaining high-quality cross sections. In addition, application expansion tests were conducted to evaluate the potential of shadow masking. These results demonstrate that shadow masking enables reduced process time and damage-minimized semiconductor analysis.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Enhanced Passive Voltage Contrast Imaging Using a Compound Lens Enabled by In-Lens Detector Optimization for Advanced Semiconductor Devices
items.abstract: Passive voltage contrast (PVC) imaging using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is a key technique for semiconductor failure analysis; however, continued device scaling to the nanometer regime has made it increasingly difficult to obtain high-resolution, high-contrast images under low accelerating voltage conditions. Conventional approaches often employ semi-in-lens configurations and/or specimen biasing, but challenges remain in achieving stable and practical PVC imaging for advanced devices. In this study, we present a bias-free PVC observation method using a compound lens SEM that superposes magnetic and electrostatic fields, enabling stable imaging with reduced sensitivity to specimen topography. To further enhance performance at ultra-low accelerating voltages, the in-lens detector (ILD) was optimized in a JSM-IT810SHL system by improving the effective signal detection region for low-energy secondary electrons. Experiments were conducted at accelerating voltages down to 0.2 kV with a working distance of 1 mm and low probe current, targeting a 3 nm process SRAM device. The optimized ILD significantly improved detection efficiency for low-energy electrons in the 4-8 eV range to approximately 80%, resulting in clear PVC images without degradation even at ultra-low voltage. In addition, enhanced signal intensity improved live image visibility and enabled stable automatic imaging adjustments. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach enables robust and practical high-resolution PVC imaging at ultra-low accelerating voltage without specimen bias, providing an effective solution for advanced semiconductor failure analysis.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Electrostatic and Radio Frequency Performance Optimization of a Triple Metal Gate Hybrid Nanowire Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor
items.abstract: This paper presents a simulated study on a 2D Asymmetric Gate Stack-Triple Metal Gate-All-Around (AGS-TM-GAA) Nanowire MOSFET with a SiGe-Ge-InGaAs hybrid channel, multi-work function metal gates, and optimally structured high-k dielectric stack (TiO2/Hf O2/Si3N4). The device has lightly p-doped source/drain, the highly n-doped channel and gate work functions 4.0 eV, 3.9 eV, 4.4 eV to have a greater threshold voltage stability, to lower the potential barriers and to have a better carrier injection. This has been demonstrated to be excellent electrostatic integrity, with steep conduction-band bending ≈-1.5 eV, uniform distribution of fields in the mid-channel ≈1.3-1.5x106 V/m and constant electron mobility ≈8-10 cm2/Vs with ATLAS simulator. The proposed device has the following highest gate-to-drain and gate-coupling capacitances Cgd ≈ 7.5x10-4-2.4x10-3 fF/µm and Cgg ≈ 4.8×10⁻³ fF/µm, maximum drive current Ids ≈ 5x10-3 A, subthreshold slope 2.2x10-4-1.45x10-3 mV/dec and drain conductance ~1x10-3 µS/nm. Short-channel effects, including the variation in threshold-voltage, and degradation of mobility and enhancement of leakage, are substantially reduced due to the GAA, asymmetric gate stack and enhanced quantum confinement. Cut-off frequency (ft), robust FTP behaviour and peak current density are high-frequency metrics that verify the suitability of the architecture to high-speed and Radio Frequency applications.

items.title: E-Beam Probing for Hardware Security Assessment of Data Leakage in Microcontrollers: A Flash Memory Case Study
items.abstract: Electron beam (e-beam) probing was investigated as a hardware security assessment technique for evaluating data leakage vulnerabilities in microcontrollers. Using flash memory as a case study, e-beam probing extracted data by observing internal signal lines within peripheral circuits during device operation. Critically, e-beam probing demonstrated single-acquisition capability for single event or non-periodic signals. An internal signal line at lower metal layers was identified through optical microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), then exposed using localized focus ion beam (FIB) milling. E-beam voltage probing (EVP) identified the line as one of 256 parallel output signals, enabling data extraction from the embedded flash memory. With optimized parameters, EVP extracted data from single operations without averaging. E-beam voltage imaging (EVI) provided spatial frequency mapping at 332 kHz. This study has demonstrated e-beam probing as a valuable technique for assessing data leakage vulnerabilities through internal signal paths in microcontrollers.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Direct Backside Failure Analysis of High Resistance Failures in High-Layer-Count 3D Flash Memory
items.abstract: Traditional frontside Physical Failure Analysis (PFA) is becoming increasingly challenging as 3D flash memory scales in vertical, lateral, logical and architectural dimensions. In CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA) architectures, buried CMOS logic circuitry beneath the array stack extends defect localization time and increases top-down delayering complexity. This paper presents a bulk silicon backside delayering workflow that provides direct physical path to the defect in the buried CMOS logic circuitry responsible for the functional failure of the flash memory device. The approach utilizes a high-precision navigation suite combining frontside layout mapping, Focused Ion Beam (FIB) through bulk silicon marking, and Infrared (IR) microscopy to precisely correlate electrical failure coordinates with the backside surface.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: DRAM Capacitor-Metal Redistribution Layer Overlay Measurement Using Image Processing with Dimple-Grinder Sample Preparation
items.abstract: Accurate capacitor-to-metal redistribution layer (RDL) overlay (OVL) measurement in advanced DRAM becomes difficult when severe capacitor tilt limits the reliability of inline fab metrology, particularly near the wafer edge. This paper presents an integrated workflow that combines dimple-grinder sample preparation with optical endpoint guidance and an automated ImageJ-Python-Excel analysis flow for SEM SE/Y AG overlay images. Compared with conventional hand polishing, the preferred dimple-grinding condition provided better location control and more uniform thinning with lower risk of over-polishing. The final preparation condition used a felt wheel, a 20 g counterweight, a wheel-speed setting of 99, Planerlite 4101 slurry, and a nominal endpoint time of 4 min 30 s, producing smooth surfaces suitable for segmentation. The automated analysis required approximately 7 min per two-channel image pair and extracted multiple local OVL measurements from a single field of view. A wafer-edge non-zero offset (NZO) skew case study further showed that the method can resolve location-dependent capacitor-to-metal RDL overlay behavior when inline monitoring is ineffective.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Cut Binary Cross Entropy: Efficient Large-Vocabulary Loss and Gradient Kernels for Sequential Recommendation
items.abstract: Industrial sequential recommender systems operate over massive item catalogs (e.g., 10^5--10^7 items). Multi-label recommendation models are trained with Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) loss over the full vocabulary, but standard BCE materializes a dense [B, N, V] logits tensor in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), incurring prohibitive $O(BNV)$ memory and fatal Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors. While chunked loss optimizations exist for Softmax Cross-Entropy in LLMs, large-scale multi-label BCE optimization remains unexplored across deep learning ecosystems. We propose CutBCE, an exact, hardware-accelerated BCE loss and gradient operator implemented in JAX and Pallas for large-vocabulary workloads. CutBCE introduces (1) an exact fused reformulation evaluating dense background loss and sparse target corrections; (2) a custom Vector-Jacobian Product (VJP) with a dedicated Pallas TPU backward kernel computing logit tiles on-chip in both passes so logits and their gradients never reside in HBM; (3) dynamic VMEM budgeting and sharding-aware collective hoisting for distributed meshes; and (4) count-based zero-overhead training metrics. On single-chip TPU v5e/v6e mini-benchmarks, CutBCE eliminates OOM errors with up to 91.9% speedup. On 8-chip TPU slice training for multi-label SASRec with 876k items (Yambda-50M), CutBCE reduces peak HBM by 65.7% (>14 GiB saved per chip) and increases training speed by 225.9% with comparable accuracy. CutBCE is open-sourced at https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/RecML/blob/main/recml/core/ops/binary_cross_entropy_ops.py.

items.title: Control optimized AES-128 cryptographic architectures achieving 94.2% logic reduction and 50% power savings
items.abstract: The growing deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, embedded systems, and hardware security platforms has increased the demand for lightweight cryptographic architectures capable of delivering strong security under stringent area and power constraints. Although the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is widely adopted for secure communication, conventional hardware implementations often incur substantial logic utilization, power consumption, and design complexity, limiting their applicability in resource-constrained environments. This paper presents two control-optimized ultra-compact AES-128 VLSI architectures to improve hardware efficiency while preserving full AES-128 functionality. The proposed designs employ finite state machine (FSM)-based control, iterative datapath reuse, shared functional units, and resource-aware architectural optimization to minimize implementation overhead. Furthermore, the Serial Key-Based AES architecture introduces a shared S-Box structure and a serial-key integration mechanism, eliminating redundant hardware resources and simplifying key management operations. Both architectures were described in VHDL, functionally verified using ModelSim, and synthesized using Quartus II. Experimental results demonstrate that the Serial Key-Based AES architecture requires only 580 logic elements and 441 lookup tables, achieving reductions of up to 94.2% in logic utilization and 95.3% in lookup-table usage compared to a conventional AES implementation. The design operates at a maximum frequency of 135.65 MHz, achieves a throughput of 17.36 Gbps, and reduces power consumption by approximately 50%. The proposed architectures provide an effective balance among security, throughput, area efficiency, and energy consumption, making them well-suited for lightweight cryptography, secure embedded systems, IoT devices, and next-generation VLSI security applications.

items.title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
items.abstract: The exponential, pervasive rise of artificial intelligence (AI), hosted in large data centres, will test the limits of the underpinning infrastructure, including electricity and water supplies, which are becoming increasingly precious resources. Rather than performing all AI computations in centralized servers, for many functionalities, these can be performed locally across a network of billions of small, autonomous nodes, saving substantial energy costs associated with communication. This alternative paradigm is known as edge computing, or distributed intelligence (DI), but has been held back by the lack of availability of reliable local energy supplies matching the energy requirements of the computational infrastructure. Opportunities to address this challenge are emerging with rapid advances in high-performance indoor photovoltaics (IPVs) for local energy harvesting, as well as reductions in computational cost through neuromorphic or in-memory computing devices. In this perspective, we discuss the requirements of IPVs for DI, the extent to which emerging materials fulfil these requirements, and how current gaps could be addressed. We make the case that (anti)ferroelectric materials can surpass bottlenecks for both electrostatic energy storage and low-power in-memory neuromorphic computing. The core theme of this perspective is that co-creation between energy harvesting, storage and computing is essential for making DI a reliable and more sustainable alternative to centralized AI.

items.title: Application of EBIC/EBIRCh in Failure Analysis for 2nm SRAM Failures: Case Studies
items.abstract: Fault Isolation (FI) serves as a critical link between electrical failure characterization and physical root-cause analysis in advanced semiconductor technologies. As semiconductor technology node scales into the sub-7nm regime, traditional optics-based isolation methods face diffraction-limited resolution, reducing their effectiveness in defect localization. This work explores electron-beam-based techniques -specifically Electron Beam Induced Current (EBIC) and Electron Beam Induced Resistance Change (EBIRCh), as high-resolution alternatives for Local Fault Isolation (LFI). Leveraging the ultra-high resolution of Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), these techniques enable identification of FET-level short/open, well anomaly due to anneal/doping failure, and other types of subtle defects undetectable by global screening. Through three different cases studies, this paper highlights practical challenges and demonstrates the effectiveness of EBIC and EBIRCh in FI in advanced nodes.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Analytical Approach for Revealing Latent Intermittent Column Failures Associated with Bit-Line Sense Amplifier Vulnerability in DRAM
items.abstract: Intermittent column failures in high-density DRAM are investigated to identify their underlying physical mechanism. Comprehensive electrical characterization revealed that failing DRAM chips consistently exhibit relatively low threshold voltages (Vt) in the bit-line sense amplifier transistors (BLSA Tr), which markedly increase their susceptibility to sub-threshold leakage currents. However, this vulnerability can remain hidden due to circuit-level bit-line compensation, making it difficult to detect and screen using conventional analysis methods. To expose the concealed mechanism, multi-factor analytical conditions are devised that deliberately minimize the bit-line differential voltage (ΔVbl) by combining elevated temperature, prolonged retention time, and a controlled delay in sensing interval (tDS ). Under these conditions, the failure behavior of the low-Vt group, previously indistinguishable from that of the reference group, becomes clearly separated. In particular, extending tDS demonstrates the progressive degradation of ΔVbl induced by leakage, ultimately leading to functional sensing failure. These results confirm that the proposed methodology effectively unmasks hidden column-failure mechanisms and provides a robust, product-level failure analysis framework for identifying root causes in advanced DRAM technologies.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: All-In-One Nanoprobing Technique on Advance Technology Node FEOL
items.abstract: Continuous advancements in IC manufacturing have driven Physical Failure Analysis (PFA) to adopt innovative defect detection techniques. Nanoprobing, a key PFA process, enables precise localization of defective regions. A prior study demonstrated front-end-of-line (FEOL) analysis without exposing fragile cobalt contacts by probing the middle-end-of-line (MEOL) copper via layer in advanced technology nodes. This approach eliminates challenges in sample preparation and cobalt contact probing. However, in SRAM nanoprobing, repeated probe landings on word lines (WL) and bit lines (BL) pose risks of copper via smearing, hindering subsequent analysis. To address this, an All-in-One (AIO) nanoprobing methodology has been developed, enhancing MEOL probing while extending applicability to unfavorable FEOL cobalt contact probing. This paper details these techniques and presents experimental results showcasing how these innovative approaches overcome key obstacles in failure analysis for advanced technology node devices.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Adaptive Milling Guided by a 3D Digital Twin for Large-Area Deprocessing of Warped Advanced Packages and BEOL Stacks
items.abstract: Chip warpage presents a significant challenge to the large-area deprocessing of advanced integrated circuits. Conventional uniform milling techniques often result in the simultaneous exposure of multiple interconnect layers, thereby compromising high-fidelity failure analysis. Here we report a closed-loop deprocessing framework utilizing adaptive milling guided by a 3D digital twin, which is continuously synchronized via high-frequency 2D top-down imaging. This workflow integrates image-based layer/interface identification with spatially customized material removal, employing variable-Z CNC milling for package-level removal and variable-dose focused ion beam milling for back-end-of-line delayering. Validation on warped package structures and a non-planar die region demonstrates that this adaptive approach improves target-layer continuity across large areas, including uniform exposure to the C4 bump level over an approximately 2500 mm2 CoW-scale package area. By enabling warpage-aware material removal, this method facilitates more controlled and scalable physical failure analysis for complex semiconductor architectures.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: AI-Driven Super-Resolution Enhancement of Scanning Electron Microscopy Images for Semiconductor Failure Analysis
items.abstract: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is central to semiconductor failure analysis (FA), but high-resolution acquisition is slow, and fast survey scans often lack the detail needed to decide where to look closely. We report two results on enhancing low-detail SEM images of static random-access memory (SRAM) arrays. First, an honest evaluation of learned single-image super-resolution (SR): against bicubic interpolation on real paired backscattered-electron (BSE) data, SR is tied on pixel metrics (structural similarity, SSIM; peak signal-to-noise ratio, PSNR) because those metrics reward smoothing on noisy BSE - yet SR is structurally better, recovering SRAM cell modulation depth to 102-112 % of the native high-resolution (HR) value (versus 94-103 % for bicubic) and tracking the SRAM lattice spectrum closest to HR, while suppressing shot noise. Second, and more fundamental, we cast enhancement as physics-informed reconstruction: from one measured image we infer a simple, piecewise-constant scene of metal lines, dielectric voids, and bright tungsten contacts; we render that scene back through a fitted SEM point-spread function (PSF) and confirm it reproduces the measurement (relative-L2 error 0.04, correlation 0.984); then we render the same scene through an idealized point-probe to obtain a sharp visualization of the inferred geometry. We are explicit about the bound: SEM resolution is not wavelength-limited (the 10 keV electron wavelength is ≈0.12 Å, far below 1 Å), so this is prior-constrained, measurement-verified deconvolution of blur and noise - not new measurement, and not atomic resolution.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: A Novel Accurate Thickness Measurement Method Using Specific Structure within a DRAM Sample and Tilt Adjustment
items.abstract: Accurate specimen thickness measurement is critical in Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) because it directly affects imaging and analytical performance, while conventional methods often require specialized instrumentation or complex procedures. In this study, we propose a quantitative TEM thickness measurement method based on tilt-induced variations in projected width, enabling thickness determination using a conventional TEM without additional analytical equipment. The method was validated through simulations and experimental measurements on DRAM samples, demonstrating high consistency across multiple tilt conditions with a small standard deviation. Furthermore, the measured thickness values showed good agreement with Focused Ion Beam-Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM) cross-sectional imaging and Electron Energy-Loss Spectroscopy (EELS) measurements, confirming the accuracy and reliability of the proposed approach. These results demonstrate that the method provides a reliable, cost-effective, and automation-compatible solution for routine TEM thickness measurement and semiconductor failure analysis.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: A Lumped-Element Circuit Model for Improved Spatial Localization of Open Defects in Radio Frequency Lock-in Thermography (RF-LiT)
items.abstract: As heterogeneous integration introduces complex chiplet architectures and extensive trace routing, conventional fault localization methods become less effective, especially for open defects invisible to DC or low-frequency techniques. While distance-based approaches such as time domain reflectometry can be used, precise correlation across multiple dies connected through redistribution layers or fan out bridges is challenging; designs for each component need to be integrated into a single database to enable the ease of trace distance extraction and tracing to find the exact location of the defect. This paper presents a physics-grounded lumped-element circuit model to improve spatial localization of open circuit defects in advanced semiconductor chips using radio frequency lock-in thermography (RF-LiT). The proposed model provides practical guidance for selecting optimal stimulus frequencies, maximizing power dissipation, and reducing acquisition time. Theoretical insights on frequency-dependent power dissipation are consolidated with case studies spanning die- and package-level defects.
items.venue: International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: A FeFET Voltage-to-Time Converter with Offset Trim by Programmed Multilevel State in 28-nm CMOS
items.abstract: The offset and gain of voltage-to-time converters (VTCs) in time-domain circuits vary with process, supply, and temperature. This work presents a VTC whose nonvolatile input-referred offset trim is the programmed multilevel state of the ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) that converts the input. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, the 6.07-$\mu$m$^2$ VTC consists of a current-starved inverter with the FeFET and a parallel NMOS leaker in its tail, a capacitor bank, and a following inverter. The programmed state shifts the transfer curve onto the input range, leaving the gain to the capacitor bank and the leaker bias. Measured at 10~MS/s, centered states weaken the second harmonic from $-$12.5~dB in the low-threshold state to $-$32.2~dB and lower the static integral nonlinearity (INL) at 5~bit from 2.42 to 0.92~LSB. Post-layout simulations indicate that the proposed VTC can operate at 500~MS/s, drawing 2.0~$\mu$W from a 0.9-V supply, with nearly unchanged distortion and gain up to 700~MS/s. Across simulated process corners and $\pm$10\,\% supply variation, the input-referred offset is calibrated to within 10~mV and the gain to within 4\,\% of nominal by adjusting the programmed state and leaker bias.

items.title: Toward a Locally Deployable Agentic Co-Scientist: Small-Model Planning for Early-Stage Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Early-stage computational drug discovery requires coordinating heterogeneous scientific tools across multi-step workflows. We present a lightweight, tool-augmented framework in which a locally deployable compact language model plans calls to 18 modular tools. A Unified Molecular Schema maintains shared molecular records, while a plug-in interface supports tool replacement and extension. We construct 1,263 manually refined query-plan pairs through workflow-graph path coverage and apply LoRA fine-tuning to three compact model families. Under the query-level split, all fine-tuned models generate fully parseable and schema-compliant plans on 47 held-out cross-group queries. Llama 3.2-3B achieves a tool-selection F1 of 0.998, sequence exact match of 0.979, and argument F1 of 0.960. Under the stricter workflow-grouped split, which excludes identical ordered tool sequences across partitions, sequence exact match reaches 0.452 to 0.548, highlighting the remaining difficulty for compact models in generating complete workflow paths unseen during training. These results demonstrate the feasibility of compact, locally deployable planning while identifying compositional generalization as an important direction for further improvement.

items.title: Silver-Corpus Transfer for Kazakh Morphosyntactic Analysis: A Cross-Validated Benchmark of Compact and Pretrained Models
items.abstract: The limited amount of manually annotated data remains a major constraint for supervised Kazakh morphosyntactic analysis: UD_Kazakh-KTB contains 1078 sentences and 10,536 syntactic words and is too small for a conventional train–development–test split. We therefore benchmark five systems—a compact 2.5 M-parameter hybrid tagger (CAGF-CBT+CRF), a classical Stanza pipeline trained from scratch (5.5 M), and fine-tuned KazRoBERTa (83.7 M) and XLM-R (278.6 M) encoders—under identical cross-validation folds, prediction targets, and official CoNLL-2018 scoring, with pooled out-of-fold evaluation over all 1078 sentences. Pretraining the compact model on a 210 K-token automatically annotated corpus improves Lemmas F1 from 74.93 to 82.81 and UPOS from 82.99 to 87.83; the effect is stable across three training seeds and the lemma gain replicates on all three neural architectures tested (+7.9, +3.5, and +3.1 for CAGF-CBT+CRF, KazRoBERTa, and XLM-R, respectively). Under the stricter protocols added in this revision—source-grouped five-fold cross-validation and leave-one-source-out evaluation on fully held-out documents—the silver effect on the compact model does not shrink but grows, reaching +13.30 Lemmas and +17.07 AllTags on a held-out Wikipedia document. Fine-tuning large pretrained encoders on this treebank is intermittently unstable: three of 18 KazRoBERTa and three of 10 XLM-R runs collapse on morphological features under early stopping, whereas none of 60 compact-model runs does. Under the stratified protocol, the from-scratch Stanza pipeline is the strongest system on Lemmas, UFeats, and AllTags (92.07/85.90/82.85), and XLM-R the strongest on UPOS (93.39); we report these results as obtained and frame the contribution accordingly—a reproducible cross-validated benchmark for UD_Kazakh-KTB, a quantification of silver-corpus transfer and its robustness to domain shift, and a documented instability of encoder fine-tuning at this corpus scale—rather than state-of-the-art accuracy. A scaling experiment with 100 K, 210 K, 500 K, and 1 M silver tokens shows continued improvement with diminishing returns beyond 500 K tokens. The source code, fold definitions, predictions, and analysis materials are publicly available.

items.title: Scalable, Simple, and Versatile Encapsulation of 2D Materials and Devices
items.abstract: Air-sensitive 2D materials present fundamental challenges for device integration. Encapsulation is required to preserve intrinsic properties, yet conventional strategies require complicated fabrication workflows and fail with thicker flakes. We demonstrate that electron-beam (e-beam) evaporated aluminum oxide (AlOx) serves as an effective encapsulation layer and sacrificial fabrication mask, protecting sensitive flakes from air, photoresists, and chemicals. Unlike transfer-based approaches, this scalable technique requires no stacking and enables contacts without postencapsulation etching or harsh chemistry. Using rare-earth tritellurides (RTe3, R = La, Er), semimetallic WTe2, and superconducting FeTexSe1-x, we show that AlOx suppresses oxidation and preserves optical and electronic properties. We establish substrate-dependent optimization of encapsulation across a range of flake thicknesses, demonstrate that ultrathin AlOx preserves WTe2's plasmonic response, and enhances superconducting performance in FeTexSe1-x devices when employed as a mask. Thus, we overcome the longstanding trade-off between encapsulation and straightforward device fabrication in fragile quantum materials.

items.title: RepTC: Representation-Aware Optimization for Efficient Traffic Classification on Edge IoT Devices
items.abstract: Traffic classification (TC) is crucial to secure Internet of Things (IoT) networks, whose edge nodes often operate under privacy, bandwidth, and energy constraints. Yet, encrypted payloads and limited computing power make accurate, real-time TC a challenging task. Existing learning-based TC approaches often fix the input configuration a priori, even though it directly influences both predictive performance and computational cost. This paper presents RepTC, a representation-aware hardware-constrained strategy that addresses session-level TC through joint model and input optimization. The method co-optimizes network architecture, session length, and header preprocessing; this enables joint control of model complexity, input scale, and data representation within a unified resource-constrained design space. The proposed approach enforces microcontroller-class constraints on memory, model size, and computation, and yields compact models deployable on low-power edge devices. A gateway monitors traffic by aggregating sessions and either performs inference locally or offloads to a low-power edge node. Both scenarios are validated on heterogeneous embedded hardware, including a Raspberry Pi 3B+, STM32 Nucleo-F401RE, and XIAO ESP32-C3, spanning Cortex-A, Cortex-M, and RISC-V processor architectures; measured inference latency ranges from 0.63 to 18.59 ms, with MCU-side inference energy between 0.50 and 1.41 mJ per session. RepTC yields configurations that achieve high accuracy on a variety of established benchmarks: 96.21% on ISCX VPN-nonVPN, 99.62% on USTC-TFC2016, and 99.97% on Edge-IIoTset; at the same time, model size and computational requirements were reduced by up to three orders of magnitude compared with state-of-the-art methods. The results show that representation-aware optimization can improve efficiency while preserving competitive classification performance.

items.title: Phase-matching in high-order harmonic generation with a plasma-reshaped driving field
items.abstract: The transition from titanium-sapphire to ytterbium-based laser technology enables turnkey implementations of high-order harmonic generation (HHG) setups at high repetition rates, opening up new applications, e.g., in semiconductor metrology. This, however, requires exploring and understanding the impact of new experimental conditions. Here, we study HHG in neon over the spectral range 8-17 nm with high spectral resolution, using a post-compressed ytterbium laser. Our measurements reveal a large pulse-energy- and pressure-dependent spectral shift, spanning more than two harmonic orders. The femto-chirp of the harmonic emission combined with the blueshift of the fundamental field allows us to relate the observed spectral shifts to the temporal window of harmonic generation, which is determined by phase-matching. To understand these dynamics, it is essential to consider the reshaping of the driving laser field inside the plasma, despite the low driving intensity and long pulse duration. We introduce an on-axis phase-matching description that captures these effects and reproduces the experimental and simulated trends. These results demonstrate the central role of plasma-induced laser reshaping in phase-matching of HHG, which should be accounted for when optimizing sources in a multi-parameter landscape.

items.title: Maximizing $p$-Mean Social Welfare in the High-Multiplicity Setting: Few Agent Types and Few Item Types
items.abstract: The $p$-mean welfare objective unifies several classical social welfare criteria for the allocation of indivisible goods. We study its maximization under additive nonnegative utilities when item and agent multiplicities are encoded in binary. For every fixed finite rational $p<1$, $p\neq0$, we show that the problem is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard with only two item types. Nash welfare ($p=0$) and egalitarian welfare ($p=-\infty$) are NP-hard with three item types. These results hold both for computing an optimal allocation and for rational-threshold decision, and the utilities and threshold can be required to be positive integers. We also show that maximizing $p$-mean social welfare is strongly NP-hard with one agent type and an unrestricted number of item types, for every fixed finite rational $p<1$ and for $p=-\infty$. A quantitative gap in this reduction rules out an FPTAS in the latter setting unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$. On the positive side, for a fixed number of item types and an arbitrary number of agent types, we give an FPTAS for every fixed $p\in\mathbb Q\cup\{-\infty\}$. Its running time is polynomial in the compact input length and in $1/\varepsilon$, and it returns a compressed allocation. For a fixed number of agent types and an unrestricted number of item types, we give a PTAS for every fixed finite rational $p<1$, also in the fully compact model. We further give explicit compact-model proofs of the classical exact allocation algorithms for one item type, and for egalitarian welfare with two item types. These results essentially settle the complexity and approximability of $p$-mean welfare maximization with few item types and/or few agent types, leaving only the exact complexity of Nash welfare maximization with two item types unresolved in the small-item-type classification.

items.title: Machine Learning Approach to ATPG in VLSI Circuits Using Random Forest Regressor
items.abstract: As the need for highly advanced chip technology and high-performance computing grows, semiconductor technology must develop rapidly. Also, as VLSI circuits become more complex, it is more difficult and time-consuming to test circuits using traditional test methods. Hence, Chip design, verification, and testing become extremely complex and critical processes. To confirm the chip as fault-free, testing examines its functionality, timing, and connectivity. Various automatic test pattern generation (ATPG) tools have been available for a long time for fault detection. For large combinational circuits, a lot of computing resources and more time are required to use such tools. To tackle this challenge, machine learning (ML) techniques have recently been introduced as a promising alternative to improve the efficiency of test generation. Machine learning has advanced dramatically over the last few years, and it currently plays an important role in enhancing automation, efficiency, and decision-making in a variety of domains. The main purpose of this work is to explore the possibility of using machine learning to predict test vectors in digital combinational circuits and achieve comparable fault coverage. The Random Forest Regressor method is utilized for generating test vectors. Experimental results showcase that this method performs well compared to traditional tools like ATALANTA on most ISCAS85 benchmark circuits. This approach reduced test pattern generation time to 0.0146 sec, while the standard tool requires 0.02 sec for test set generation, retaining almost similar fault coverage. This research demonstrated the highest fault coverage of 96.523 for the c5315_13 circuit and the lowest coverage of 60.404 for c1908_23, compared to the ATALANTA Tool. The results demonstrate that machine learning is a promising complementary testing method for conventional ATPG tools in VLSI testing.
items.venue: Journal of Electronics Electromedical Engineering and Medical Informatics

items.title: High-Pressure Deuterium Annealing Enables Robust Trap Passivation in ALD HfO2/Si MOS Capacitors under High-Temperature Bias Stress
items.abstract: The continuous scaling down of semiconductor devices has driven the replacement of SiO2-based gate insulators with HfO2 deposited via atomic layer deposition (ALD) to mitigate the leakage current induced by direct tunneling. However, HfO2 thin films deposited via ALD contain process-induced trap states that degrade the device performance, and high-temperature operating conditions owing to device miniaturization further exacerbate trap-related degradation. In this study, high-pressure hydrogen annealing (HPHA) and high-pressure deuterium annealing (HPDA) were applied to HfO2-based metal−oxide−semiconductor (MOS) capacitors for trap passivation, and their electrical characteristics were compared with those of an as-deposited HfO2 MOS capacitor from 30 to 100 °C. HPDA reduced the interface trap density from 1.61 × 1012 eV−1 cm−2 to 1.72 × 1010 eV−1 cm−2 and suppressed the flat-band voltage hysteresis (ΔVFB) to nearly 0 V, showing the best electrical characteristics among the three conditions. Both HPHA and HPDA successfully passivated the interface and bulk trap states within the HfO2 film. Temperature-dependent electrical characteristics revealed that HfO2 annealed with HPHA exhibited a gradual ΔVFB deterioration with increasing measurement temperature, which was attributed to the dissociation of hydrogen-based trap passivation under high-temperature and bias stress. In contrast, HfO2 annealed with HPDA maintained a ΔVFB of nearly 0 V over the entire measurement temperature range, confirming the robust thermal and bias stability of the deuterium-based trap passivation. Furthermore, the suppression of the trap-assisted conduction path through high-pressure annealing demonstrated that HPDA provides the most stable trap passivation in HfO2-based MOS capacitors under high-temperature and high-bias operating conditions.

items.title: Development of logistics 4.0 efficiency indicators system in supply chain management
items.abstract: The study aims to develop an integrated system of key performance indicators (KPIs) to evaluate digital logistics processes in Industry 4.0 conditions. The research is relevant because traditional performance measurement systems must adapt to the specifics of digital supply chain transformation and the growing importance of sustainability metrics in modern business operations. The methodology is based on systematic analysis of modern scientific approaches to supply chain performance measurement, adaptation of the Balanced Scorecard framework with integration of a fifth sustainability perspective, and mathematical modeling for logistics efficiency forecasting using the Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) method with a modified range-adjusted measure. The results include the development of a comprehensive multi-level KPI system covering operational indicators (order cycle time, picking accuracy, inventory turnover, digital integration index), financial metrics (logistics costs per unit, investment ROI, transportation costs per ton-kilometer), environmental indicators (carbon footprint, energy efficiency, waste management, recycling coefficient), and customer-oriented metrics (on-time delivery rate, order fill rate, customer satisfaction index, Net Promoter Score). We propose and empirically validate a mathematical model to forecast logistics process efficiency using a modified DEA-MRAM method with a digitalization impact coefficient. The scientific novelty lies in creating an integrated framework for Logistics 4.0 assessment that combines traditional metrics with digital maturity and sustainability indicators; systematizing sustainability indicators for logistics systems across three Triple Bottom Line dimensions (environmental, social, economic); and adapting the MRAM-DEA mathematical model with the integration of the digitalization impact coefficient, which allows quantitative assessment of digital transformation effects on operational performance. The practical significance lies in applying the developed KPI system to diagnose and optimize enterprise logistics processes across industries amid economic digital transformation and ESG reporting requirements. The developed implementation methodology includes four sequential stages: diagnostics, design, implementation, and monitoring using the PDCA continuous improvement cycle. Future research should empirically validate the KPI system in Ukrainian enterprises, develop industry-specific framework adaptations for different economic sectors, and investigate the impact of geopolitical factors on logistics system efficiency. Keywords: Logistics 4.0, key performance indicators, supply chain, digital transformation, balanced scorecard, sustainable development, DEA analysis, digital maturity.
items.venue: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

items.title: Detecting Program Flow Anomalies via Instruction Monitoring with Neural Networks: A Comparison of Methods
items.abstract: Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) systems form the backbone of modern complex electronics. Yet, as device features shrink and chips grow in complexity, the rate at which faults emerge from various sources increases. While an expansive and mature field of techniques exists to detect, classify and/or ameliorate said faults, they are noted to have significant shortcomings with faults that manifest primarily in the temporal domain. This paper aims to address these kinds of fault scenarios through the use of neural networks as a means to detect anomalies in the flow of a program. The methodology for the creation and evaluation of a fault injection dataset, using recordings from a RISC-V processor, is detailed, followed by an analysis of the properties of the instruction progression of said recordings, so as to illustrate the utility of this approach. This dataset is then used to evaluate a number of different neural network architectures, specifically a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN); Recurrent Neural Network (RNN); Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM); and Spiking Neural Network (SNN). The performance and properties of these network architectures are compared, with the results showing that SNNs possess a desirable combination of low relative neuron count, high accuracy and low output delay.

items.title: CoDPlacer: A Fast Approach for Digital IC Placement via Consistency Distillation
items.abstract: Modern digital IC placement requires methods that balance placement quality, legality, and runtime as circuit sizes continue to grow. Learning-based generative placers provide a promising alternative to analytical and sequential approaches, but they remain computationally expensive because high-quality generation requires large number of steps. This paper presents CoDPlacer, a consistency-distilled framework for accelerating generative chip placement. The method distills a pretrained diffusion placer into a consistency model for faster macro- and cluster-level placement. Two full-chip placement flows are evaluated: macro placement followed by DREAMPlace standard-cell refinement (conventional method), and a hierarchical flow using standard-cell clustering, boundary-aware expansion, local DREAMPlace optimization, and final assembly. Experiments on 18 IBM benchmarks and five ISPD2005 circuits evaluate inference-step sensitivity, macro placement, and downstream detailed placement. The 128-step consistency model achieves 4.1×, 3.11×, and 7.82× generation speedups relative to the strongest evaluated baseline on clustered IBM, macro-only IBM, and macro-only ISPD2005 benchmarks, respectively, while maintaining competitive HPWL. In conventional full-chip placement, the consistency-distilled model achieves the lowest average HPWL among the evaluated baselines. These results show that consistency distillation provides an effective quality-runtime tradeoff and useful initialization for downstream analytical placement.

items.title: A UTILIZAÇÃO DO MÉTODO PILATES COMO RECURSO TERAPÊUTICO NA REABILITAÇÃO DA DIÁSTASE ABDOMINAL: UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA
items.abstract: Diastasis of the rectus abdominis muscles (DRAM) is characterized by separation of the rectus muscles along the linea alba and may be associated with changes in abdominal wall function and stability. The Pilates method has been used as a physiotherapeutic resource because it involves exercises aimed at strengthening, controlling, and stabilizing the trunk musculature. This study aimed to analyze the evidence on the use of Pilates in the rehabilitation of DRAM. This systematic literature review was conducted using PubMed, SciELO, LILACS, PEDro, and Google Scholar. Primary studies published between 2015 and 2025 in Portuguese, English, and Spanish, directly related to Pilates and abdominal diastasis, were included. After identification, screening, and eligibility assessment, four studies were included. Three studies observed a reduction in inter-recti distance, whereas one study conducted during pregnancy did not identify a reduction in diastasis. Improvements in abdominal muscle strength and endurance and a reduction in low back pain were also observed. The findings indicate that Pilates was effective in reducing inter-recti distance in most studies and may be considered a physiotherapeutic resource applicable to the management of DRAM, although study heterogeneity limits the generalization of the results.
items.venue: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

items.title: VLSI Design for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications
items.abstract: Unlock the next generation of AI chip design with this comprehensive guide to overcoming VLSI challenges, combining state-of-the-art nanomaterials, semiconductor modeling, and low-power circuit design into an essential roadmap for researchers and engineers. Very large-scale integration (VLSI) is the interdisciplinary science of utilizing advanced semiconductor technology to create various functions of a computer system. By combining VLSI technology, a very powerful computer architecture is possible to overcome the problems at different design stages. AI techniques such as knowledge-based and expert systems first define the problem and then choose the best solution from a range of possible approaches. This book comprehensively covers nanomaterials, semiconductor devices, and modeling and simulation techniques used to address the challenges of low-power VLSI chip design. It explores process variability, device sizing, power supply scaling, conventional and emerging materials, leakage mitigation techniques, and critical design tradeoffs. The book presents state-of-the-art research in nanomaterials and semiconductor technologies alongside practical design considerations for low-power VLSI circuits, making it an essential resource for scientists, researchers, and postgraduate students interested in AI hardware, semiconductor devices, modeling, and simulation.

items.title: Toward Intelligent Chemical Mechanical Polishing: Integrating Multiscale Modeling and Machine Learning
items.abstract: Chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) remains the cornerstone planarization technology in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. As device architectures transition toward FinFETs, gate-all-around structures, heterogeneous integration, and wide-bandgap semiconductors, CMP must simultaneously deliver angstrom-level flatness, high selectivity, low damage, and improved sustainability. Against this background, research in CMP is moving beyond empirical trial-and-error toward a more integrated paradigm that combines consumables design, physics-based modeling, and data-driven intelligence. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in CMP from four interrelated perspectives. First, we examine advances in slurry and abrasive design, including morphology engineering, porous and core-shell abrasives, defect-controlled ceria systems, and environmentally friendlier chemical formulations, together with the emergence of photo-, electro-, ultrasonic-, plasma-, and gas-assisted CMP. Second, we review the multiscale modeling landscape, spanning macroscale planarization and profile evolution, mesoscale contact mechanics and slurry transport, and atomistic simulations based on first-principles calculations and reactive molecular dynamics. Third, we assess the rapidly growing role of machine learning in CMP, with emphasis on material removal rate prediction, surface quality evaluation, process monitoring, virtual metrology, and intelligent run-to-run control. Fourth, we discuss sustainability-oriented CMP, including source reduction, wastewater treatment and recycling, and the use of modeling and digital control to reduce non-productive resource consumption. By synthesizing developments across these areas, this manuscript highlights the current gaps in cross-scale model integration, physics-informed intelligent control, transferability across tools and materials, and life-cycle-oriented process design. We conclude by outlining how a closed-loop CMP ecosystem-linking materials innovation, mechanistic understanding, in situ sensing, and intelligent optimization-may support the next generation of high-efficiency, green, and manufacturable planarization technologies.

items.title: SSRESF-OPT: A Sensitivity-Aware Framework for Single-Particle Radiation Effects Simulation and Optimization in SoC Platforms Using Machine Learning
items.abstract: The increasing scale of System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures exacerbates the reliability risks of single-particle radiation effects, rendering traditional exhaustive gate-level fault injection prohibitively slow. To address this, we propose SSRESF-OPT, an end-to-end simulation and optimization framework combining accelerated dynamic fault injection with machine learning-driven prediction. The framework first introduces a cross-layer static binding mechanism to eliminate runtime string resolution, reducing per-injection simulation overhead to \(\mathcal {O}(1) \) complexity. Building on this optimized engine, an SVM-based classification pipeline, guided by structural clustering, accurately predicts the radiation vulnerability of unsimulated circuit nodes using netlist-derived features. To maximize resource efficiency, an OPT-based top- k hardening strategy is then employed to prioritize critical architectural bottlenecks. Evaluations across 15 gate-level netlists, including massive AES subsystems and RISC-V PULP SoCs, demonstrate the framework’s efficacy. The model-assisted approach achieves an average end-to-end runtime speedup of 6.35 × over the highly optimized simulation baseline while maintaining a 94.58% prediction accuracy. Furthermore, hardening only the top 10% of ranked nodes reduces system Soft Error Rate (SER) by 85%, providing a fast and actionable methodology for radiation-hardened microprocessor design.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems

items.title: SGAnalog: An End-to-End Circuit Benchmark from Open-Source Silicon Tapeouts
items.abstract: Existing analog integrated circuit design benchmarks make two questions hard to answer: whether a model has learned transferable circuit skills rather than recalled familiar examples, and whether its output works under defined process and test conditions. We introduce a benchmark built from human-designed, open-source circuits associated with Tiny Tapeout manufacturing shuttles. The collection contains 273 topologically distinct top-level designs. Every source is retrieved at the revision recorded for its shuttle submission and processed in a fixed containerized environment. The pipeline exports each eligible schematic image and its SPICE netlist from the same source file, giving transcription an exact structural reference. Commit dates support model-specific training-cutoff analysis, while author testbenches provide the simulation context for sizing. The benchmark evaluates schematic-to-netlist transcription and device sizing. Across seven models on a fixed set of 66 transcription tasks, the strongest model reaches 56.1% exact graph isomorphism, and six of seven models drop sharply from the small to the medium tier. For one frontier model, removing author-chosen labels reduces exact matches while preserving aggregate structural F1, suggesting that labels can aid connectivity tracing. On the 17 sizing tasks, the leading model converges on all 17 proposals and reaches 91.2 out of 100 against the human reference, while the two newest Claude models refuse 4 and 11 of the same prompts they transcribe without objection; a proposal without sizes scores zero. The two tasks produce different model rankings, exposing distinct visual and design capabilities and, in one family, a policy rather than capability limit.

items.title: Reversing the Clock: Layout-Aware Recovery of Design Intent from Clock Distribution Networks
items.abstract: Hardware reverse engineering supports competitive analysis and hardware assurance by recovering information about an integrated circuit (IC) from its physical implementation. While existing techniques primarily recover the gate-level netlist, which represents logical functionality, they often overlook physical design decisions such as placement, routing, delay insertion, and interconnect optimization. The clock distribution network encapsulates many of these decisions; however, no prior published work has recovered this network from a fabricated IC to infer design intent. We present a layout-aware methodology that recovers and analyzes the clock distribution network by integrating a recovered gate-level netlist with layout information extracted from scanning electron microscope imagery. Our four-phase pipeline recovers clock-tree topology, buffering, gating and switching, interconnect delay, and crosstalk-mitigation measures. We demonstrate our methodology on a commercial 450 nm IC, recovering a global H-tree backbone with local X-tree-like branching, identifying an independent clock tree and global clock gating, quantifying latency, skew, and routing lengths, and confirming the absence of dedicated crosstalk mitigation. Together, these findings let us reason about the designer's intent. To encourage further research and support reproducibility, we release our clock tree recovery algorithm as open source.

items.title: RaBitQ-SSD: Split Codes and Pipelined I/O for SSD-Resident Vector Search
items.abstract: SSD-resident approximate nearest-neighbor search is essential when vector collections exceed DRAM capacity. The challenge is to reduce SSD reads and hide I/O latency through concurrent reads and overlap with computation. However, for graph-based search, progressive candidate discovery limits advance I/O planning while IVF search reads inverted lists in full, incurring unnecessary SSD reads. In this paper, we present RaBitQ-SSD, an extension of IVF-RaBitQ for SSD-resident vector search. Specifically, we propose Split-RaBitQ, which retains a configurable prefix of each binary code in DRAM, allowing in-memory code storage below one bit per dimension. Using this partial representation, it provides an unbiased distance estimator with a probabilistic error bound. Once the in-memory coarse quantizer identifies candidate lists, this bound supports pruning individual candidates within them, enabling finer-grained SSD access. We also design an asynchronous search pipeline that coordinates candidate pruning with SSD read scheduling to reduce unnecessary reads while overlapping I/O with computation. On datasets ranging from $5$ million to $1$ billion vectors, RaBitQ-SSD delivers up to $1.74\times$ the throughput of graph-based baselines at $90\%$ recall, while reducing SSD page reads by up to $3.8\times$. Its on-SSD indexes are up to $7.0\times$ smaller and $10.0\times$ faster to build than DiskANN. We also build and search an index of $10$ billion vectors on a single machine with one SSD, achieving over $3{,}000$ queries per second at $90\%$ recall.

items.title: Overcoming the Resistance Penalty in Large-Bandgap Carbon Nanotube Electronics via Synergistic Interfacial Engineering
items.abstract: High-pressure carbon monoxide (HiPCO) carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer superior ION/IOFF ratios due to their larger bandgap (EG), yet they suffer from high series resistance limiting drive currents. Here, we demonstrate a synergistic dual-engineering strategy to simultaneously minimize channel and contact resistance in top-gate HiPCO CNT field-effect transistors (FETs). A 200 °C forming gas annealing (FGA) process effectively scavenges organic residues, reducing the intrinsic channel resistance to 318 Ω·μm for specific 50 nm gate-length devices. Furthermore, localized p-type contact doping using contact-defined self-aligned MoOx nanoparticles deposited selectively within the source/drain windows reduces the effective Schottky barrier height from 233 meV to 66 meV. Optimized HiPCO CNTFETs exhibit a record-high on-current density of 2.5 mA/μm at VDS = -0.5 V while maintaining excellent off-state suppression. Our devices outperform existing benchmarks and exceed the IRDS 2039 conductance projections by 4×. This synergistic approach provides a robust pathway for high-performance, low-power carbon-based nanoelectronics.

items.title: Optimization of Gate‐All‐Around Field‐Effect Transistors Design Using Genetic Algorithm
items.abstract: Gate-all-around field-effect transistors (GAAFETs) have come to the fore as a hopeful replacement for fin field-effect transistors in leading-edge semiconductor technology with better electrostatic control, shorter short-channel effects, and increased scalability for sub-3-nm nodes. GAAFETs utilize a surrounding gate geometry, allowing larger drive currents and smaller leakage relative to conventional transistor structures. Optimizing the design of GAAFETs remains a serious problem due to intricate interactions between structure parameters, material characteristics, and process variability. Design optimization of GAAFETs consists of several challenges, such as nanowire or nanosheet dimension selection being optimal, gate dielectric engineering, strain engineering, and managing variability. Accurate but time-consuming and computation-intensive physics-based simulations and traditional process optimization strategies are not practicable. Machine learning (ML) methods are very useful and efficient tools in speeding up the design and optimization process as they can quickly predict important electrical parameters like threshold voltage, subthreshold swing, and drive current. Unsupervised learning methods help to determine important design parameters and process variations. Using ML with physics simulations, one can effectively survey the large design space, minimize fabrication cycles, and improve device performance.

items.title: Negative‐Capacitance FET
items.abstract: The negative-capacitance field-effect transistor (NC-FET) enables effectively lowering of the power supply voltage (VDD) of conventional metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET) because of its super steep switching feature, i.e., sub-60-mV/decade subthreshold swing (SS) at room temperature. The idea of overcoming the Boltzmann limit(S=60 mV/decade) by negative-capacitance (NC) lies in the fact that in a series combination of a negative and a positive capacitor, the total capacitance becomes larger than its constituent positive capacitor. Interestingly and particularly, this is just the opposite of two positive capacitors, where the total capacitance is always reduced. For a ferroelectric gate FET, the negative gate capacitance can make the total capacitance, looking into the gate, larger than the semiconductor capacitance. Thus, to induce the same amount of charge in the channel, the ferroelectric gate FET would require a smaller gate voltage than what required for a traditional FET. That is to say, the gate voltage could be reduced below the Boltzmann limit(S<60 mV/decade). Very recently, it has been demonstrated that temperature is an effective tuning parameter for the ferroelectric negative capacitance. The NCFET requires an additional ferroelectric layer in its gate stack. In this chapter, a negative-capacitance field-effect transistor (NC-FET) is designed with their added ferroelectric layer over SiO2 under the gate, having unique negative-capacitance behavior, which enables steeper subthreshold slopes and less power dissipation compared to traditional n-channel MOSFET (NMOS) devices. The examined performance parameters are threshold voltage, subthreshold slope, leakage current, and on-off current ratio to show that the NC-FET indeed offers all the advantages coupled with some limitations. Simulated results are found to be showing a better power consumption reduction and improvement in switching efficiency than NMOS transistors for NC-FETs. The focus here is on the potential of NC-FETs for energized VLSI circuits with insight into integrated applicability to future low-power digital designs. The conventional NMOS transistor performance is compared and analyzed with NC-FETs in terms of important parameters, such as power consumption, switching speed, subthreshold swing, and device efficiency. In this comparison, the potential advantages of NC-FETs over conventional devices is examined in terms of eliminating scaling barriers, increasing energy efficiency, and scaling the threshold voltage so that they allow for more efficient and compact VLSI designs for next-generation semiconductor applications.

items.title: Nanowire, Nanotube FET, and CNTFET
items.abstract: The evolution of today's electronics will remain directly associated with the improvisation in Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) technology, which is the building block of present computing and communication systems as well as intelligent electronic devices. The semiconductor devices are being ultra scaled down into nanometer regime, the industry is experiencing a shift from planar CMOS to advanced device structures. As traditional CMOS shrinks, short-channel effects increase (SCEs) increment in leakage current. For solving CMOS conventional scaling limitations Carbon Nanotube Field-Effect Transistor (CNTFETs) utilize a one-dimensional (1D) nanotube channel, which provides better electrostatic control over the channel, minimizing short-channel effects (SCEs) and lowering static power consumption. The CNTFETs alos offer ballistic transport, leading to high driving capability, 18 times faster switching speeds, and roughly less power consumption compared to bulk silicon. The CNTFETs are necessary in VLSI design to surpass the physical limitations of silicon CMOS at sub-10nm nodes, offering higher electron mobility, superior electrostatic control, and near-ballistic transport. This chapter has described the progress in nanowire field-effect transistors, nanotube field-effect transistors, and carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNTFETs) according to their structural, electrical, and functional properties. The chapter explains the fabrication process, performance optimization methods, and the influence of scaling on these transistor technologies. The use of one- dimensional nanostructures, i.e., nanowires and carbon nanotubes, in contemporary electronic devices provides enhanced electrical conductivity, increased mobility, and energy efficiency. Moreover, this chapter also suggests the advancement in dual-gate CNTFET geometries, thermoelectric nano transistors, and novel applications in high-speed logic circuits. The potential of these nanodevices in next-generation electronic and optoelectronic devices is evaluated critically in the future, which opens new areas of thrust in nanoelectronics.

items.title: Investigation on Hot-Carrier Injection Mechanisms and Reliability Design-Based Strategies in Cryogenically Operated CMOS ROICs for Infrared Focal Plane Arrays
items.abstract: Cryogenic operation of CMOS read-out integrated circuits (ROICs) is essential for high-performance infrared focal plane arrays but significantly affects carrier transport and device reliability. This work investigates hot-carrier injection (HCI) mechanisms in 180 nm NMOS transistors operating from room temperature down to 140 K. Electrical characterization and accelerated stress measurements reveal a strong impact of hot-carrier effects at low temperatures, resulting in increased degradation of device characteristics, particularly under channel hot-electron (CHE) and drain avalanche hot carrier (DAHC) stress conditions. Time-to-failure modeling confirms accelerated degradation kinetics while validating conventional substrate-current-based reliability methodologies at cryogenic temperatures. Geometry-based design strategies, notably gate-length optimization, are proposed to mitigate cryogenic HCI effects, enabling an improved performance-reliability trade-off. These results provide key guidelines for design reliability of cryogenic CMOS ROICs for infrared imaging applications.

items.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning on the Design of Systems and the Future
