This study examines the effects of post‐deposition rapid thermal annealing (RTA) on AlN thin films used in microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) resonators. RTA is performed in a N 2 ‐purged chamber at temperatures ranging from 200°C to 1000°C on AlN thin films deposited via DC reactive magnetron sputtering. The effects of RTA temperature on the crystallinity, morphology, composition, and piezoelectric properties of AlN are systematically analysed. A practical temperature threshold is established at 400°C for AlN, above which the material properties change markedly due to rapid oxidation of the material. Up to that temperature, the grain size decreases, and the grains reorient toward the c‐axis of the wurtzite phase. The piezoelectric coefficient ( d 33 ) increased approximately 160%, and AlN/Si based MEMS showed an amplification of the electromechanical properties to 400 pm/V altogether with an output power density of ∼0.12 µW/cm 3 . Furthermore, this work identifies the thermal stability within the CMOS‐compatible temperature range. Devices employing Ti/Pt electrodes exhibit a degradation threshold between 400°C and 600°C, where the metals undergo diffusion and form undesired bonds and structures. Meanwhile, the AlN/Ta/Nb devices remained stable for temperatures up to 600°C, indicating their suitability for integration into high‐temperature MEMS fabrication.

items.title: Highly Scalable Selectorless Cryogenic Memory Array Using Ferroelectric Josephson Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Scalable memory systems that satisfy the temperature, speed, and energy requirements of cryogenic environments are essential for the development of large-scale quantum computers. They may also benefit high-performance computing and space applications. However, existing cryogenic memory technologies often suffer from limited scalability, low operating speed, and/or high power consumption, restricting the scalability of target applications. Ferroelectric Josephson field-effect transistors (Fe-JoFETs), which combine ferroelectric polarization with the superconducting properties of Josephson junctions, offer a promising solution. The ferroelectric layer enables nonvolatile storage capability, while the Josephson junction supports high-speed, energy-efficient operations. In this work, we leverage Fe-JoFETs to develop a highly scalable, ultra-low-power, nonvolatile cryogenic memory array that does not need additional selector devices for random access. Moreover, the superconducting component of Fe-JoFET provides a binary decision during read, eliminating the need for sensing peripheral circuitry. We first develop a physics-based Verilog-A compact model for Fe-JoFETs and use it to verify the functionality of the proposed memory array. By eliminating both selector and sensing circuitry, the proposed memory architecture offers higher scalability than existing technologies. The ultra-low-power operation of this memory also makes it compatible with strict power budgets of cryogenic applications.

items.title: High breakdown voltage Mg/Au gated AlGaN/GaN HEMTs enabled by Fermi-level pinning
items.abstract: The impact of Ni/Au and Mg/Au gate contacts on the electrical performance of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) is investigated. The experimental and simulated results reveal that Mg/Au gate contact exhibits a higher Schottky barrier height than conventional Ni/Au gate contact. This enhancement is attributed to metal-induced gap states at the Mg/Au Schottky interface, which pin the Fermi level near a relatively high charge neutrality level to maintain local charge neutrality and reduce the dependence of the barrier height on the metal work function. Consequently, compared with Ni/Au gated HEMTs, Mg/Au gated HEMTs exhibit a ∼3 orders reduction in gate leakage current and a ∼2 orders increase in on/off current ratio due to the enhanced gate Schottky barrier. The effective lateral breakdown field and breakdown voltage are improved from 0.54 MV cm−1 to 0.94 MV cm−1 and from 1310 V to 2090 V, respectively, owing to suppressed gate leakage and reduced electric field beneath the gate, while the on-resistance also increases. These results demonstrate that Mg/Au gated devices exhibit great potential for GaN-based power device applications.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

items.title: Development of LGAD Sensor Technology on 12 inch Wafers for 3D Integration with advanced CMOS processes
items.abstract: We report on the design, simulation, and initial testing of Low Gain Avalanche Diode (LGAD) sensors fabricated in 65 nm CMOS technology on 12 inch wafers. These sensors were developed as part of a project to demonstrate full wafer to wafer hybrid bonding of sensors and 28 nm Readout Integrated Circuits (ROICs). The sensor submission and test included standard (reach-through) LGADs, AC coupled LGADs, and Deep Junction LGADs as well as various test structures.

items.title: Defect Engineering in Gallium Nitride Semiconductors for Improving Carrier Mobility and High-Power Electronic Device Reliability
items.abstract: Gallium nitride power devices increasingly operate at electric-field, switching-frequency, and junction-temperature regimes where defect-mediated carrier trapping becomes a principal constraint on transport stability and operational lifetime. This study investigates how targeted defect engineering can modify the relationship between GaN microstructure, electron mobility, and degradation in high-power electronic devices. The analysis focuses on nitrogen vacancies, gallium vacancies, carbon- and oxygen-related impurities, threading dislocations, and interface traps whose electronic states promote Coulomb scattering, carrier capture, dynamic on-resistance, leakage, and threshold-voltage instability. A defect–transport–reliability framework is developed to connect defect concentration and trap energetics with mobility degradation and electrically activated failure mechanisms. Engineering interventions including epitaxial growth-condition control, compensation management, dislocation reduction, interface passivation, and post-growth thermal processing are comparatively examined. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing defects that primarily limit channel transport from deep-level traps activated under high-field and high-temperature stress. The framework establishes measurable links among trap density, electron mobility, current collapse, leakage evolution, and device degradation, providing a pathway for optimizing GaN heterostructures for sustained high-voltage operation without sacrificing transport performance or switching efficiency.
items.venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews

items.title: Comparative evaluation of encapsulation methods for endohedral doping of single-wall carbon nanotubes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT. Single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are promising building blocks for nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices, yet reliable and stable doping, particularly n-type, remains challenging due to strong environmental sensitivity and competing extrinsic effects. Encapsulation of charge-transfer molecules within the SWCNT cavity offers a promising route to stable doping while preserving the nanotube’s outer surface for subsequent processing. Here, we systematically investigate the filling of arc-discharge SWCNTs with the electron donor tetrathiafulvalene and electron acceptor tetracyanoquinodimethane, comparing different methods for filling, including melt filling, solution reflux, and vacuum-phase sublimation. We follow the entire processing workflow from raw, unfilled powders to aqueous dispersions and employ density gradient ultracentrifugation to separate filled from empty nanotubes as well as metallic from semiconducting ones. Encapsulation efficiency and electronic modification are assessed using absorption spectroscopy, resonant Raman scattering, thermogravimetric analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and electron paramagnetic resonance. Finally, we introduce a complementary vacuum-phase method that removes externally adsorbed molecules without extensive solvent washing, enabling cleaner encapsulated systems.

items.title: Aluminum Oxide-Assisted Ga2O3 Nanostructures for Enhanced Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Photodetection
items.abstract: This study presents a nanostructure design strategy based on the functional integration of anodic aluminum oxide (AAO). Unlike the conventional use of AAO as a sacrificial template, it is directly retained as a functional substrate, preserving both its structural integrity and functional advantages. Using atomic layer deposition (ALD), Ga2O3 is deposited in three forms: thin films, nanopillar arrays, and nanopore arrays. Compared with thin-film device, the nanostructured devices exhibit significantly enhanced photoresponse. In particular, the nanopore device achieves a responsivity of 87 A/W, which is approximately 6 times higher than that of the thin-film device, together with an external quantum efficiency of 4.25 × 104%, and a detectivity of 1 × 1014 Jones. The performance enhancement is mainly attributed to the following mechanisms: the retained AAO template enhances ultraviolet absorption through light scattering and localized electromagnetic field effects; Meanwhile, its high specific surface area strengthens the regulation of oxygen adsorption/desorption, thereby modulating the depletion layer and Schottky barrier, and optimizing carrier transport behavior. This work demonstrates that transforming AAO from a “sacrificial template” into a “functional structural unit” provides a simple and effective strategy for designing high-performance solar-blind ultraviolet photodetectors.

items.title: AI-based smart load balancing for sustainable electric vehicle charging hubs using LSTM forecasting and reinforcement learning
items.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) on a global scale has put a significant burden on existing electricity distribution structures. Traditional charging methods at a public charger, utilizing fixed rates, cannot adjust to the continually changing supply and demand for renewable electricity or the effect of peak loads on the electric power grid system. To solve this very important limitation, this research presented an AI-Based Smart Load Balancing Electric Vehicle Charging Hub (AI-SLBECH). The proposed framework includes a simulation-validated, multi-layer intelligent ecosystem that uses all of the following components: a 200 W solar photovoltaic (PV) array, a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery energy storage system (BESS), grid interconnectivity, IoT monitoring system, all being operated under an adaptive energy management architecture. The proposed framework consists of an integration of three complementary AI components: (1) an AI-based Finite State Machine (FSM) for tri-modal energy dispatch, (2) a two-layer Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) neural network for predicting 15–30 min ahead, demand (NRMSE = 7.2%, MAPE = 6.8%), and (3) a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning (RL) scheduling agent, trained over 10,000 episodes with a composite reward function, achieved convergence from episode 8,200 on and produced a Jain’s Fairness Index of 0.94. The complete control pipeline was implemented on an ESP32 microcontroller (operating under constraints) with TensorFlow Lite Micro, on-device LSTM was using only 78KB of flash memory. In comparison with the leading AI-powered EV charging systems that have been examined in a variety of published materials, this AI-SLBECH has unique design features. It offers an effective method for integrating all three service modalities (dispatch mode, predictive scheduling using LSTM models and optimal policies through PPO-RL algorithms), as well as real-time monitoring via Internet of Things (IoT) devices and was designed to operate on edge-deployable, hardware-constrained systems. When tested over 30 days using actual NASA POWER solar irradiance data for Chennai, India, the AI-SLBECH produced several remarkable results compared to a traditional grid-based solution. It reduced the peak demand of the grid by 38.1% (42.3 KW-26.2 KW), lowered the average session cost for EV charging from 88.43 INR to 61.20 INR (a 30.7% reduction), decreased the total amount of carbon dioxide CO₂ released during the month by 61.3% (921 kg to 356 kg), achieved a 48.4% use of renewable energy and exhibited a Jain’s Fairness Index score exceeding 0.94. A preliminary techno-economic feasibility analysis indicates that this project will require a capital investment of about Rs. 2.8 Lakh (approximately $3,360US) and will generate substantial returns on investment approximately every 28–34 months, based on current utility tariff rate structures.

items.title: Vulnerability-Weighted Routing of Timing-Critical Nets for Configuration-Upset-Resilient SRAM-Based FPGAs
items.abstract: Conventional FPGA routing optimizes timing, congestion, and routability but does not distinguish routes with similar nominal performance and substantially different susceptibility to configuration-induced delay degradation. This paper presents a vulnerability-weighted routing methodology for SRAM-based field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) that incorporates predicted routing-fault severity directly into the routing objective. A continuous vulnerability cost relates delay perturbations caused by electrically attachable dormant routing resources to the available downstream timing slack, while a complementary configuration-concentration term discourages excessive localization of vulnerable resources. To limit implementation disruption, only the highest-risk nets are selectively ripped up and rerouted while unaffected routes remain fixed. The method is implemented on a Zynq UltraScale+ XCZU7EV using a Vivado/RapidWright-based flow and evaluated across four routed benchmarks against commercial timing-driven routing, vulnerability-agnostic rerouting, and binary vulnerable-resource avoidance. Controlled configuration-equivalent perturbations provide hardware-level validation. The proposed method reduces aggregate configuration-induced timing vulnerability by 41.7% with approximately 1.0% nominal timing degradation and captures 85.8% of the vulnerability reduction obtained at the expanded routing budget by rerouting only the highest-risk 5% of eligible nets. The results demonstrate that continuous vulnerability information can improve configuration-upset resilience with limited impact on nominal routing quality.

items.title: From Routing Delay Shifts to Silent Data Corruption: Neutron-Induced SEU Effects in AXI-Based Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoCs
items.abstract: SRAM-based FPGA system-on-chip devices are vulnerable to single-event upsets (SEUs) in configuration memory, which may perturb programmable routing resources and degrade communication fabrics. In modern Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoCs, such routing disturbances can introduce small propagation delay shifts that remain logically transparent yet compromise AXI-based data transfers and lead to silent data corruption. Although routing delay degradation and AXI interconnect failures have been studied independently, their experimental correlation under neutron irradiation has not been established. This work presents a cross-layer investigation on a ZCU104 platform integrating routing-dominated delay sensors with an AXI interconnect benchmark comprising replicated accelerators. Neutron irradiation experiments were conducted on the fully operational system, while a frame-level configuration fault injector implemented via the internal configuration access port enables controlled upset emulation. Measured routing delay events are statistically correlated with communication failures, and cross-sections for both timing shifts and AXI malfunctions are derived. The results experimentally demonstrate how neutron-induced routing perturbations propagate into system-level silent data corruption in UltraScale+ MPSoCs, providing insight for resilience-oriented AXI-based design in neutron-rich environments.

items.title: GRACIDIT: Graph-Circuit Digital Twin for Configuration-Induced Routing Delay Prediction in Zynq UltraScale+ FPGAs
items.abstract: Configuration-induced perturbations in SRAM-based FPGAs may activate dormant programmable routing branches and increase path delay without immediately producing a functional error. Although prior studies have separately investigated the electrical origin of these delay changes, their in-situ detection, and the topology of commercial routing fabrics, a scalable method for predicting their timing impact at the granularity of programmable interconnect points and routed nets remains unavailable. This paper presents GRACIDIT, a graph-circuit digital twin framework for predicting configuration-induced routing delay degradation in Zynq UltraScale+ FPGAs. The proposed framework extracts the routing-resource graph of the XCZU7EV programmable fabric from the vendor design database, identifies inactive programmable interconnect points adjacent to active routes, and represents each candidate perturbation through its branch topology, geometric span, fan-out, physical region, and downstream loading. These graph features are combined with a calibrated reduced-order electrical model to estimate the delay introduced by single and cumulative routing-branch activations. Controlled configuration-equivalent perturbations are generated on a ZCU104 platform and characterized using complementary routing-domain oscillators and phase-sweep probes. The resulting model associates predicted delay shifts with available timing slack to rank vulnerable programmable interconnect points and routed nets and to construct a spatial vulnerability atlas of the programmable fabric. Experimental evaluation demonstrates a mean absolute prediction error of 7.8 ps, achieves 87.4 percent recall for slack-violating perturbations, and attains a Recall at 10 value of 0.90 for the most vulnerable routing resources.

items.title: Write Disturb Model for 3D XPoint Array
items.abstract: This work investigates write disturb (WD) in 3D XPoint technology, focusing on thermally induced crosstalk between adjacent cells. A physics-based electro-thermal model has been developed and implemented in a TCAD framework, calibrated against large-statistics of experimental physical and electrical data. The model reproduces the observed WD behavior by accounting for both the deck to deck asymmetry and program-induced stoichiometry gradients. It provides a predictive framework to improve WD control and reliability in 3D XPoint arrays.

items.title: Unifying Field and Temperature Acceleration in Semiconductor Device Reliability Through Entropic Kinetics
items.abstract: Time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) is an important failure mechanism that affects semiconductor device reliability. The degradation lifetime depends strongly on both electric field and temperature, yet these dependencies are commonly treated using separate empirical acceleration factors. This work develops a thermodynamic description in which electrical stress changes the accessible microscopic states of the dielectric and therefore contributes an entropic term to the Gibbs free energy. The resulting formulation separates the field-independent activation barrier, Ea, from a field-dependent entropic contribution characterized by α. This relation predicts a linear decrease in apparent activation energy with the logarithm of the electric field. Published TDDB data for SiO2, high-k, low-k, and Cu/low-k dielectric systems exhibit this behavior. Independent temperature- and field-dependent measurements from the same source yield a common entropic field-energy scale of approximately 1.2 eV. A one-second reference field, E1sec, provides a physical time anchor that allows field and temperature acceleration to be compared without assuming a common pre-exponential factor across temperatures. For an absolute time temperature series, independently extracted values of α vary by 11.9% across three temperatures, while a fixed α produces a normalized relation with R2 ≈ 0.97. The parameters Ea, α, and E1sec provide a compact thermodynamic representation of field- and temperature-dependent TDDB kinetics across the datasets examined here.

items.title: Transition metal dichalcogenides-based flexible transistors: from material and interface engineering to intelligent system integration
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as a promising platform for flexible electronics owing to their atomic-scale thickness, tunable electronic structures, and mechanical flexibility. Compared with conventional silicon-based devices, TMDs offer unique advantages in extreme scaling, and low-power operation, and electromechanical adaptability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of TMD-based flexible transistors, focusing on cross-scale optimization from atomic-level materials engineering to system integration. We first summarize structural modulation strategies, including polymorphic phases, alloying, Janus architectures, defect regulation, and doping engineering, for tailoring electronic properties and device functionalities. Interfacial engineering strategies involving Schottky barrier modulation, dielectric passivation, and contact resistance reduction are further discussed to improve carrier injection and reliability. The role of mechanical strain in regulating transport behavior and enhancing device stability is systematically evaluated. Finally, emerging system-level applications, including wearable sensing nodes, edge-Artificial intelligence of Things (AIoT) platforms, and neuromorphic computing systems, are highlighted, followed by perspectives on scalable manufacturing, reliability assessment, and material–device–system co-optimization toward next-generation intelligent flexible electronics.

items.title: Thickness Engineering in HfO2-Based Ferroelectrics: A Critical Review of Phase, Switching, Reliability, and Device Trade-Offs
items.abstract: HfO2-based ferroelectrics have extended a familiar CMOS high-κ dielectric into a materials platform for nonvolatile memory, low-power logic, and in-memory hardware. This review examines thickness engineering in hafnia, especially Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO), through the state produced during fabrication, the voltage and time available for switching, and the signal retained during operation. Representative quantitative comparisons retain stack, anneal, electrical state, and endpoint definitions; they show that conditioning and drive voltage can change the apparent thickness trend substantially. Capacitor memory, FeFETs, tunnel junctions, negative-capacitance transistors, and computing devices are compared through architecture-specific read margins and failure criteria. The main unresolved challenge is to isolate thickness effects from coupled process and interface changes and establish reproducible, device-specific operating windows.

items.title: Systematic Device-Level Design Exploration of Complementary Stacked Vertical-Channel Transistors (CVFETs) for Advanced Logic Applications
items.abstract: This article presents a systematic device-level design exploration of complementary stacked vertical-channel transistors (CVFETs) and dual-channel CVFETs (dCVFETs). Key device factors are investigated, including source–drain asymmetry, nMOS/pMOS stacking order, terminal selection, electrode routing, and channel count. Their circuit-level impact is evaluated in terms of standard-cell area and energy–delay product (EDP). With the optimized device configuration, dual-sidewall routing reduces the average standard-cell area by 35.4% while maintaining EDP comparable to complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs). The dCVFET further reduces standard-cell EDP by 17.3% at the cost of a 9.3% area penalty. A 6T static random access memory (6T-SRAM) cell is also implemented using a novel dual-cut strategy, achieving a 37.8% area reduction and improved static noise margin compared with CFETs. These results show that device-level choices in CVFETs directly translate into logic benefits, providing design guidelines for future CVFET-based technologies.

items.title: Synthetic mask layout generation for machine learning-based OPC modeling in NA 0.33 EUV lithography
items.abstract: As NA 0.33 EUV lithography operates increasingly close to fundamental resolution limits, accurate and robust optical proximity correction (OPC) models become critical for advanced logic technology development. In early technology phases, OPC calibration is challenged by limited availability of real product layouts. To address these challenges, this work integrates Layout Schematic Generation with machine learning (ML) based OPC modeling to enhance calibration pattern diversity for 28nm metal pitch in single‑patterning NA 0.33 EUV lithography. Synthetic layouts are generated from a limited set of manufacturable ground rules. The generated patterns are fabricated using a bright‑field low‑n attenuated phase‑shift mask and metal‑organic resist with dry development. ML OPC model experiments demonstrate that incorporating LSG‑generated layouts leads to systematic improvements in prediction accuracy across multiple pattern categories, with root‑mean‑square (RMS) error reductions ranging from approximately 28% to 15% compared with conventional calibration strategies. The proposed LSG‑driven calibration framework provides an efficient and scalable solution to improve OPC model robustness for NA 0.33 EUV lithography and is directly applicable to future high‑NA EUV technology nodes.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: Solution Processed Tellurium Single‐Crystal Nanocubes and Polycrystalline Films for 2 µm Wavelength Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Tellurium (Te) is a p‐type semiconductor with a narrow bandgap, promising for infrared optoelectronics. This work presents a solution‐based synthesis of novel single‐crystal Te nanocubes and polycrystalline films. Te is dissolved in ethylenediamine‐ethanethiol, mixed with ethanolamine, and spin‐coated to form nanocrystals and films. We achieved monodispersed single‐crystal Te nanocubes ∼500–900 nm in size, confirmed by electron microscopy and diffraction. The crystal morphology can be tuned by the annealing temperature and air exposure time. We show patterning of Te nanocubes by exploiting the deposition dependence on the substrate's wetting properties. We also demonstrate ∼500 nm thick polycrystalline Te films processed in air at 150°C. The Te films exhibit p‐type behavior, an electrical resistivity of 0.115 Ω·cm, and photoconductance at wavelengths up to 2100 nm without optical cavities or complex gain mechanisms. The films exhibit responsivities of 0.93 A W − 1 at 1720 nm and 137 mA W − 1 at 2100 nm under intensities of 0.98 and 6.4 mW/cm 2 , respectively. The large dark current remains a limitation for the current photoconductor configuration, but device engineering can improve speed and ON/OFF ratio. Overall, this low‐temperature method provides an alternative, cost‐effective pathway for Te‐based infrared optoelectronics beyond the operating ranges of Si, Ge, and conventional InGaAs.

items.title: Selective etching for high-NA EUV mask film stack
items.abstract: As semiconductor devices are shrinking to the sub-nanometer node, next-generation high-NA EUV lithography is required. Next-generation low-n / high-k absorber films used in EUV photomasks contain compositional elements that are notoriously difficult to etch due to their chemical inertness. During plasma etching, this inertness can lead to unwanted erosion of the hardmask (HM) above the absorber, ultimately degrading the absorber profile and preventing achieving required critical dimensions (CDs). To etch these advanced masks, obtaining a high absorber/HM etch selectivity is necessary. We have addressed this challenge with a novel hardware-enabled etch process that delivers high selectivity, and thus manageable HM budget to achieve the desirable optical requirements. The newly developed method can also extend to the etching of other new materials in the future. This new approach has two key components: (1) promote the balance between the chemical surface reaction and byproduct removal (2) tune plasma chemistries to the individual compositional elements in the absorber film. Together, this approach can open up the process window, enabling recipe adjustments that improve sidewall angle, CD control, uniformity, and linearity with enough HM remaining. The resulting improvements in profile and CD performance highlight the critical role of the hardware innovation and process development in enabling next-generation high-NA EUV photomasks.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: Scalable AXI4 Transaction Monitoring for Mixed-Criticality SoCs: From Phase-Level Precision to ID-Level Efficiency
items.abstract: Mixed-criticality Systems-on-Chip (SoCs) with on-chip interconnects based on the AXI4 open standard protocol lack a protocol-level timeout mechanism, exposing systems to deadlocks and missed real-time deadlines when subordinate devices or managers fail or stall due to hardware faults, radiation-induced upsets, or software errors. This work presents a configurable hardware intellectual property (IP), non-intrusive in fault-free operation, that detects AXI4 protocol violations and timing faults at runtime and restores interconnect liveness through a cut-and- drain isolation mechanism. To address the fundamental trade-off between monitoring granularity and area cost, we introduce three designs at decreasing monitoring granularity: Phase-Level Track-ing (PLT), which provides cycle-accurate fault localization across individual protocol phases; Channel-Level Tracking (CLT), which coalesces per-phase monitors into channel-level supervision; and ID-Level Tracking (ILT), which achieves sub-linear area scaling by monitoring only per-ID transaction boundaries. Synthesized in GlobalFoundries 12 nm technology, CLT reduces area by 36.7% relative to PLT while preserving worst-case detection bounds at a minimal detection latency overhead, whereas ILT achieves an 89.2% area reduction suitable for tightly constrained deployments at the cost of a 3.7x higher median detection latency with coarser fault localization. Fault injection campaigns on a RISC-V SoC across 1.2 million scenarios confirm that no fault manifesting as an AXI4 protocol or liveness violation escaped detection, with observed detection latencies consistently bounded by theoretical worst-case predictions.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems

items.title: Postgrowth Annealing Strategy for β -Ga 2 O 3 on Sapphire Solar Blind Photodetectors With High Detectivity and Fast Response
items.abstract: Despite extensive efforts toward$\beta $-Ga2O3-based solar-blind ultraviolet (UV) photodetectors, further performance improvement remains challenging due to intrinsic defect limitations and material-quality constraints. In this work, we demonstrate high-performance solar-blind photodetectors using heteroepitaxial$\beta $-Ga2O3films grown on sapphire and systematically elucidate the critical role of high-temperature annealing in overcoming these bottlenecks. Asignificant reduction in oxygen-vacancy-related defects within the$\beta $-Ga2O3heteroepitaxial layers was confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Photodetectors annealed at$1100~^{\circ }$C achieve a responsivity of 14 151A/W and a detectivity of$1.83\times 10^{{16}}$Jones at 10V under 254nm illumination, representing fivefold and sixfold enhancements relative to unannealed devices. The annealed films exhibit a carrier lifetime of 0.13s, much faster than the reported Ga2O3photodetectors with similar responsivity. This work demonstrates a viable approach to achieving both high gain and fast response in$\beta $-Ga2O3photodetectors, providing a reliable strategy and key insights into defect engineering for advancing wide bandgap optoelectronics.

items.title: Performance Enhancement of a-IGZO TFTs With Elevated Source/Drain Structure via Channel Trench Etching
items.abstract: We demonstrate an elevated source/drain (S/D) amorphous InGaZnO (a-IGZO) thin-film transistor (TFT) in which the channel is selectively recessed while the S/D access regions retain the original active-layer thickness. Despite sharing the same 10-nm channel thickness as a uniformly thinned device, this structure preserves thick S/D access regions, decoupling gate-control improvement from the access-resistance penalty of uniform active-layer thinning. Transmission-line method (TLM) measurements reveal that the width-normalized contact resistance (${R}_{\text {C}}~\cdot ~ W\text {)}$decreases to$1.04~\Omega \cdot $cm, a 60.2% reduction relative to the uniform 20-nm device. Technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations indicate that the decoupled channel-access geometry alleviates current crowding and redistributes the resistive voltage drop. This selective channel trench etching approach offers a simple, interlayer-free route to reducing parasitic resistance in scaled oxide TFTs.

items.title: Pattern contrast analysis through two-mirror projector: impact of central obscuration and scan mirror shadowing
items.abstract: We analyzed the pattern contrast of a two-mirror EUV projector proposed by Prof. Tsumoru Shintake of OIST through optical simulations. This work focuses on the impact of the central obscuration and the scan-mirror shadowing observed in the OIST EUV projector. While the central obscuration is also present in current high-NA EUV projectors, the shadowing caused by the scan mirror is unique to the OIST design and therefore requires careful evaluation. In this study, both effects were incorporated into the optical model, and the modulation transfer functions (MTFs) were computed for line-and-space (L/S) and staggered-hole patterns. In addition, contour simulations were performed for several device-like patterns to assess the impact on image formation.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: Multi-beam mask writer MBM 4000: enhancements and latest performance
items.abstract: The MBM™-4000, which targets the A14 technology node and beyond, has been designed to meet the requirements for High-NA EUV wafer lithography and has been released in 2025. Having concluded the development the MBM-4000, we are now working on new technologies for future MBM series and recently have developed the two new writing functions; Deflection Stripe Shift (DSS) and Stage speed Optimization scan (SO scan). The DSS function improves local position accuracy without throughput deterioration by introducing the new writing strategy of exposing two stripes in one pass writing using large deflection of beam array to switch stripes exposed. The SO scan optimizes stage speed per stripe by detecting pixel with maximum dose in a stripe to enhance writing speed. The SO scan has been enabled by applying the resist Thermal Effect Correction (TEC), which corrects Critical Dimension (CD) variability depending on pattern densities and stage speed; 16% writing speed improvement by the SO scan with accommodating CD variability from stage speed variation across stripes within 0.1 nm by TEC for a layout with 160% dose variation.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: Microwave Annealing Enables Low-Voltage Ferroelectric Switching and Enhanced TDDB Reliability in HfO 2 /ZrO 2 Superlattice-Based Capacitors
items.abstract: Low-temperature microwave annealing (MWA) was employed to activate 12-nm HfO2/ZrO2superlattice (SL-HZO)-based capacitors. Compared with conventional rapid thermal annealing (RTA), MWA treatment reduced the onset voltage (V${}_{\text {on}}\text {)}$for detectable ferroelectric (FE) switching from 1.5 to 1.25 V. The MWA-treated SL-HZO films exhibited a lower coercive voltage and a more symmetric piezoresponse amplitude (PRA), indicating improved polarization switching characteristics at reduced driving voltages. During endurance testing, the device exhibited wake-up-free behavior and an extrapolated retention capability of at least tenyears. Time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) measurements further demonstrated that the MWA-treated devices achieved improved breakdown lifetime and thermal stability, maintaining reliable operation at temperatures up to$85~^{\circ }$C. These results indicate that MWA treatment effectively lowers Vonfor detectable FE switching in SL-HZO-based metal–FE–metal (MFM) capacitors while enhancing device reliability, thereby offering a promising approach for low-power and highly reliable nonvolatile memory applications.

items.title: Leak-CIM: A PVT-Robust and Energy-Efficient SRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro Exploiting Transistor Leakage
items.abstract: The binarized neural networks (BNNs) significantly reduce arithmetic and storage costs for edge inference, but repeated bitwise accumulation and memory access still limit system energy efficiency. This article presents leak-computing-in-memory (CIM), a$256\times 64$static random access memory (SRAM)-based voltage-mode CIM macro that exploits the subthreshold leakage ofoff-state transistors as ultrahigh-impedance pseudo-resistors for low-energy analog accumulation. Unlike charge-sharing CIMs, the proposed scheme maintains a wide read-bitline (RBL) dynamic range while strongly suppressing the shoot-through current that typically limits voltage-mode operation. To compensate for the process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensitivity of leakage-based pull-up and pull-down paths, the leak-CIM employs a postfabrication N-well bias calibration scheme that restores their resistance balance. The postlayout simulations show that the calibrated macro maintains a normalized mean-squared error below$1.12\times 10^{-2}$across 40 global PVT conditions. Fabricated in a 22-nm bulk-CMOS process, the macro achieves up to 1799 TOPS/W and 31.67 TOPS/mm2across measured operating points. When the measured ADC characteristics are incorporated into a BNN inference model, leak-CIM attains 98.15% accuracy on MNIST and 86.04% on CIFAR-10.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems

items.title: Impact of Interface and Dielectric Defects on HKMG MOSFETs Down to Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: This study investigates the impact of interface and dielectric defects on high-$\boldsymbol {\kappa }$metal gate (HKMG) MOSFETs at cryogenic temperatures, focusing on key MOSFET metrics and their correlation with room temperature values. We use substrate injectors to induce a controlled generation of interface and dielectric defects on devices with a scaled CMOS gate dielectric stack with SiO2interlayer, HfO2, and gate metal. We evaluate how these defects affect subthreshold swing (SS), threshold voltage, gate leakage, transconductance, and 1/f noise down to cryogenic temperatures by comparing fresh devices and devices subjected to controlled substrate hot-carrier stress prior to cryogenic characterization. The findings are then validated on devices fabricated in commercial FDSOI MOSFETs, using test structures designed to induce varying plasma damage and dielectric defectivity, confirming the robustness of the observed trends across technologies.

items.title: High-NA in-line projector for EUV lithography
items.abstract: Four-mirror, in-line projector for high-NA EUV lithography is studied in this paper, which eliminates the most troublesome mask 3D effect. The light rays pass through the central aperture in each mirror with acceptable obscuration. The numerical aperture (NA) is 0.5 and 0.55. It has a circular exposure field with a diameter of 20 and 30 mm, respectively. The residual radial distortion is rather high at a few microns at the field rim, and the scan motion causes image blurring in the scanner. Thus, we need to revert to the stepper design, and the field becomes smaller, i.e. 14 mm x 14 mm square and 21 x 21 mm. It is important to note that both the wafer and the photomask remain stationary during the EUV exposure. Illumination will be provided through two rectangular scan-mirrors located in front of the mask, providing dual line scan field, which matches with off-axis illumination enhancing the resolution and bypassing the central obscurations. The impact of patterning due to shadowing of the scan mirrors and central obscuration should be examined carefully.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: HBF-Sim: An Extensible HBF Simulator for Large-scale GPU Memory Systems
items.abstract: High-bandwidth flash (HBF) is introduced to address the memory wall, which can co-package a dense NAND stack with the GPU, targeting the performance gap between near-accelerator bandwidth and flash density. HBF, however, is neither a large HBM nor a fast NVMe SSD. Its usable bandwidth depends on how GPU cache-line requests map onto NAND pages, how concurrency spreads across channel-affine die sets, and how media management interacts with the GPU memory pipeline. To our knowledge, existing GPU, SSD, or HBF simulators cannot faithfully model this behavior. We present HBF-Sim, an extensible, reusable, and faithful HBF simulator integrated with simulated GPUs. It closes the loop between GPU issue limits, device queuing, and NAND behavior in one end-to-end request path. HBF-Sim separates a GPU-HBF interaction controller from page-based parallel stack storage, and it models the full GPU-HBF request path. It provides an MSHR-based address mapping table that merges cache-line requests into page-based operations, as well as a page-based multi-stack flash manager for highly parallel reads and writes. Validation tests and device-level microbenchmarks expose performance bottlenecks caused by limited channel distribution and resource conflicts, offering concrete guidance for next-generation HBF architectures.

items.title: Grain-boundary scattering between chiral domains in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi
items.abstract: We evaluate the electron scattering properties in CoSi thin films having either twin (heterochiral) or non-twin (homochiral) grain boundaries using first-principles quantum transport calculations. We find that scattering across a twin grain boundary is more resistive than scattering across a non-twin grain boundary and that non-twin grain boundaries have a greater percentage of surface conduction than twin grain boundaries. This is corroborated by the transmission eigenstate profiles, which show that the surface Fermi-arc electrons can transmit past the non-twin grain boundaries between homochiral domains on the same surface without significant backscattering. In contrast, these surface electrons get scattered along the twin grain boundaries between heterochiral domains to the opposite surface, resulting in partial forward transmission and partial backscattering that yields higher grain-boundary resistivity. This work helps elucidate the complexities of electron transport in chiral topological semimetals for potential application in next-generation nano-interconnects.

items.title: Functionalization-Free Atomic Layer Deposition of Sub-1 nm EOT HfO2 Directly on MoS2 for Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Layered semiconductors offer a promising route beyond conventional silicon technology but face challenges in integrating high-k dielectrics due to their dangling-bond-free surfaces. Here, we report a direct atomic layer deposition approach, termed HALO (High-dose precursor immersion, Adsorption enhancement, and Low-temperature Oxide improvement) ALD, enabling uniform HfO2 growth on two-dimensional (2D) materials without surface functionalization. The HALO process improves nucleation and interface quality, yielding smooth high-k films (∼0.1 nm roughness). MoS2 dual-gate field-effect transistors (FETs) exhibit an equivalent oxide thickness of 0.83 nm, a subthreshold swing of 80 mV dec–1, and breakdown fields up to 9 MV cm–1. Reliability studies, including bias stress and thermal tests, confirm stable device operation. This approach further enables conformal high-k integration in gate-all-around structures, providing a scalable pathway for three-dimensional (3D) integration of 2D electronics.

items.title: From silicon to spikes: System-wide efficiency gains via exact event-driven training in neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) promise efficient inference because they communicate sparse spike events rather than dense numerical activations. Most training pipelines, however, still use surrogate gradients or dense time-step simulations. This creates a mismatch between the training state kept in software and the event-driven state processed by neuromorphic hardware. We introduce an analytical event-driven learning framework that differentiates spike times exactly in continuous time and jointly trains synaptic weights, programmable delays and adaptive threshold amplitudes. The derivation treats every emitted spike time as an implicit function of the neuro-synaptic parameters and evaluates gradients only at threshold crossings. The resulting implementation stores event records and local crossing slopes rather than full membrane traces. On five event-stream benchmarks, controlled simulations show a consistent accuracy gain of up to six percentage points over a matched surrogate-gradient baseline. Event-replay accounting further shows an approximately reduction in on-chip SRAM traffic and an approximately reduction in dynamic energy under the stated memory and device models. Besides these algorithmic outcomes, we report simulator-based traffic, energy, thermal, and reliability estimates, and provide ablations against weight-only, weight-delay, and weight-threshold reductions. The results support the central claim that exact event-local training improves temporal accuracy while making the training state better aligned with sparse neuromorphic execution.

items.title: Fabrication and Characterization of β -Ga 2 O 3 -Based MIS Structures by Mist-CVD-Deposited Al 2 O 3 Dielectric
items.abstract: Mist chemical vapor deposition (mist-CVD) is an emerging, low-cost, and scalable technique for depositing high-quality dielectric films on ultrawide bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors. In this work, aluminum oxide (Al2O${}_{{3}}\text {)}$thin films were deposited on beta-gallium oxide ($\beta $-Ga2O${}_{{3}}\text {)}$substrates by mist-CVD, and metal–insulator–semiconductors (MISs) capacitors were fabricated to evaluate their electrical properties and interface quality through capacitance–voltage ($C$–$V$) characterization. Optimal deposition and process conditions were established, including an assessment of post-deposition annealing (PDA) treatments in N2atmosphere. The dielectric constant of mist-CVD Al2O3was extracted by using Si MIS capacitors through$C$–$V$measurements combined with spectroscopic ellipsometry, yielding$\varepsilon _{\text {r}} \approx {6.4}$. Electrical characterization of$\beta $-Ga2O3/Al2O3MIS capacitors revealed low oxide fixed charge, reduced hysteresis after optimized PDA, and overall promising interface quality. These results demonstrate the viability of mist-CVD as a cost-effective deposition method for$\beta $-Ga2O3power devices and provide a foundation for further optimization of dielectric growth and interface engineering in UWBG electronics.

items.title: Development of low-n/mid-k EUV masks for high-NA lithography
items.abstract: Low‑n absorber materials are considered to be promising candidates for mitigating mask 3D effects in High‑NA EUV lithography. In this study, simulation‑based mask optimization was carried out for line-and-space (L/S) patterns with a 20‑nm pitch to compare Low‑n/Mid‑k and Low‑n/Low‑k absorber materials. As a result, it was found that the Low-n/Mid-k absorber exhibits superior normalized image log-slope (NILS) and a smaller best-focus shift compared with the other absorber candidates, suggesting improved imaging performance for High-NA horizontal L/S patterning. Process challenges related to etching of Low‑n/Mid‑k materials were also investigated. Through comprehensive process optimization, well‑controlled absorber profiles and stable critical dimension (CD) performance were achieved. Favorable CD uniformity, CD linearity, and resolution were obtained, indicating that Low‑n/Mid‑k absorbers have strong potential for High‑NA EUV lithography and that a viable mask fabrication process has been established.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: Defect‐Engineered N‐Doped ZnO as a Dual‐Functional Platform for PENG‐Driven Memristive Sensory Memory
items.abstract: Energy‐efficient computing is a critical challenge for artificial intelligence and edge applications. Although self‐powered memory systems that integrate sensing, energy harvesting, and storage are promising, they often suffer from high leakage currents, poor reproducibility, and material incompatibility. Here, we present a dual‐functional N‐doped ZnO (NZO) platform that electrically couples an interface‐type memristor with a piezoelectric nanogenerator (PENG), enabling self‐powered memory programming. Uniform N‐doping via low‐temperature atomic layer deposition passivates oxygen‐related defects, suppresses leakage currents, and stabilizes resistive switching. A thin TiO2‐x interfacial layer acts as an oxygen reservoir and enables precise barrier engineering for reversible, low‐power multilevel operation. At the same time, the reduced carrier concentration in NZO enhances PENG performance through suppression of electrostatic screening effects. Density functional theory (DFT+U) calculations further predict N‐induced changes in elastic stiffness and compliance, suggesting a possible secondary contribution to the electromechanical response through modified strain accommodation. As a result, the rectified PENG output directly programs the memristor without an external bias. The coupled system exhibits stable multilevel storage, robust endurance, and synaptic plasticity. By co‐designing energy harvesting, sensing, and memory on a unified oxide platform, this work establishes a practical pathway toward energy‐autonomous neuromorphic computing and intelligent tactile memory systems.

items.title: Current Status of Research on High‐Electron‐Mobility Transistor Devices on Gallium Nitride and Aluminum Nitride Substrates
items.abstract: Gallium nitride‐based high‐electron‐mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) are widely used in fields such as microwave communications and power electronics due to their excellent properties, including a wide bandgap, high critical breakdown field strength, and high electron mobility. Although commercial GaN HEMTs on foreign substrates (Si, SiC, and sapphire) are widely adopted, unavoidable heteroepitaxial mismatches in lattice and thermal expansion introduce high dislocation densities, exacerbating current collapse and leakage. This paper systematically reviews the material properties and structural advantages of free‐standing GaN and AlN single‐crystal substrates, detailing the latest research progress on GaN‐substrate HEMTs in terms of substrate doping engineering, buffer layer optimization, and enhancement‐mode device design. The key technological breakthroughs of AlN‐substrate HEMTs in GaN and high‐Al‐content AlGaN channel devices were also explored. It compares the application potential and core challenges of these two technical routes, outlines future development directions, and provides a systematic reference for the research and development of GaN‐based power and RF devices.

items.title: Bioinspired Multifunctional Optoelectronic Synaptic Transistors for Neuromorphic Visual Applications
items.abstract: Conventional artificial vision architectures typically suffer from physically separated sensing, memory, and processing modules, leading to high power consumption and limited integration. Herein, a bioinspired optoelectronic synaptic transistor is developed based on an IGZO channel and natural konjac glucomannan (KGM) polysaccharide electrolyte, enabling the fusion of optical perception, synaptic plasticity, and neuromorphic visual information processing in a single device. Benefiting from the persistent photoconductive (PPC) effect in IGZO and the proton-mediated electric-double-layer (EDL) behavior of the natural polysaccharide gate, the device can functionally emulate multiple core synaptic behaviors of biological synapses, including excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC), paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), short-/long-term plasticity (STP/LTP), and metaplasticity. Such versatile synaptic functions allow the device to realize wavelength-dependent color perception emulation, visual image preprocessing, and direction-selective visual receptive field emulation, mimicking key processing stages of biological vision. This work provides a promising device-level strategy toward the development of highly integrated neuromorphic visual systems.

items.title: Benefits of alternative reticles for high-NA EUV logic metal printing
items.abstract: The introduction of ASML’s EXE:5000 scanner has allowed to keep Moore’s law on track. It uses a Numerical Aperture (NA) of 0.55, which, compared to the 0.33NA of the NXE scanners, allows for a significant increase in resolution and enables the printing of unprecedently small pitches. However, to fully leverage the capabilities of High-NA EUV lithography in terms of contrast and Dose-to-Size reduction, alternative reticles are crucial. In this study, we explore the advantages that we obtained by the use of alternative absorbers, namely low-n low-k and low-n mid-k absorbers compared to a tantalum-based absorber, and by the use of an alternative multilayer mirror, namely a Ru/Si multilayer mirror compared to a Mo/Si multilayer mirror. We show how the low-n absorbers improve the Exposure Latitude vs. Dose-to-Size trade-off for horizontal dense line/space patterns with 20 nm pitch (P20) in Dark Field, in addition to an improvement in tip-to-tip printability. We also show how the alternative multilayer mirror brings considerable improvements for non-telecentricity related issues such as two-bar asymmetry through focus.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: Automated SRAF generation for 75-nm contact holes patterning using generative AI in 193-nm immersion lithography
items.abstract: Contact holes are essential patterns in semiconductor manufacturing but exhibit smaller process windows and lower image contrast than line-and-space features, making their lithography particularly challenging. To avoid costly mask rewrites after AIMS inspection, we investigate a machine-learning framework that automatically detects and repairs problematic contact-hole layouts early in the design flow. We present an automated framework for contact-hole mask optimization under 193-nm ArF immersion lithography using PROLITH™ simulations. Mask layouts are procedurally defined in Python as numerical coordinates, enabling hole- only masks pattern synthesis with reduced human bias. A total of 4,941 75-nm contact-hole masks were generated and labeled with a 4:6 ratio of compliant to non-compliant patterns, based on rule-based lithographic criteria. Using the latest YOLOv12 detector as a binary classifier, we achieved approximately 94% accuracy. When a layout is classified as non-compliant, we invoke the inpainting component of a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) trained only on compliant masks. Stage 1 optimizes a variational autoencoder (VAE) to learn a compact latent space, and Stage 2 trains a U-Net diffusion model in that space. After 1,000 epochs, conditioning on separately prepared hole-only masks, the model synthesizes high-fidelity SRAF-enhanced layouts, which are re-simulated in PROLITH™ to evaluate process window and confirm low MEEF. This combination of machine learning and generative inpainting enables efficient optimization of contact-hole assist features, reducing design time and mask-revision cost. The framework is extendable to high-NA EUV and multipatterning, and helps reduce human-induced mask errors while improving design-technology co-optimization and reliability in high-volume manufacturing.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: Automated Regulatory Compliance Question Answering in Financial Services with Domain-Adapted Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.abstract: Financial institutions operate under dense, frequently amended rulebooks, and answering a compliance question correctly requires not only fluency but verifiable grounding in the authoritative text. Large language models are attractive for this task, yet the models that firms can realistically deploy on-premise are compact ones, and compact models hallucinate obligations. We study whether a carefully domain-adapted retrieval-augmented generation pipeline closes that gap. Our retriever is built in three stages on top of LegalBERT: entailment tuning that recasts question--passage matching as premise--hypothesis reconstruction, contrastive tuning with in-batch negatives, and score-level fusion with BM25. Our generator is a compact model (2B--12B parameters) served under 4-bit quantization, either prompted or adapted with retrieval-aware fine-tuning (RAFT) through LoRA. On ObliQA, a question-answering benchmark built from the Abu Dhabi Global Market rulebooks, the staged retriever raises Recall@10 from 0.256 to 0.774 and outperforms BM25 (0.678) and E5-large-v2 (0.758), the strongest general-purpose dense encoder we tested. RAFT-LoRA then improves the composite RePASs answer-quality score for every model we could adapt, with the largest gain on the weakest one. However, the adapted models do not transfer to Australian case-law questions, and a closed-book model that receives no passages at all scores within 0.011 RePASs of the full pipeline while producing answers that cite nothing and misstate obligations. The retrieval gain is therefore measured directly, the generation gain is a gain in RePASs rather than demonstrated grounding, and grounding itself requires an evaluation protocol that RePASs does not provide.

items.title: An Open-Source Standard-Cell Library for IHP 130nm Developed by Students
items.abstract: Standard-cell libraries form the critical interface between transistor-level circuit design and automated digital design flows, yet their design and characterization are rarely covered in depth in digital VLSI courses. This paper presents VLSI 5, a graduate-level course at ETH Zurich in which students design, lay out, characterize, and integrate their own standard cells using IHP's open-source 130nm SG13G2 process design kit. In the first course offering, 19 students developed EZ130 8T, an open-source eight-track standard-cell library comprising 220 cells. We evaluate successive library versions using eight synthesis benchmarks, across which EZ130 8T achieves significant area reduction compared to the SG13G2 library at competitive timing. For a postlayout 8x8 matrix-vector multiplier, EZ130 8T reduces cell area by 35% and energy by 39% while maintaining virtually the same clock period. The library has already been adopted in other ETH Zurich VLSI courses, enabling the creation of chips entirely designed by students down to the transistor level.

items.title: A holistic approach to curvilinear enablement for advanced logic scaling: from design to patterning
items.abstract: Curvilinear design has emerged as a critical enabler for continued technology scaling, as conventional Manhattan design styles increasingly constrain pattern fidelity and process window. This work presents imec’s recent holistic approach to curvilinear enablement, spanning the full flow from design to patterning, including curvilinear design intent, mask manufacturing and metrology, lithography experiments, and patterning qualification. This integrated framework demonstrates a significant breakthrough on the logic scaling roadmap by leveraging the capabilities of advanced EUV lithography and patterning techniques. We also discuss the efficiency of curvilinear nano-interconnect-adapted logic standard cell designs from a design-technology co-optimization perspective.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: A Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network Compact Model for RF Transistors
items.abstract: Physics-informed artificial neural network (PI-ANN) compact models have attracted considerable attention owing to their physical interpretability. However, because physical knowledge is incorporated only into the loss function, the neural networks in conventional PI-ANNs are difficult to capture complex intrinsic physical relationships, resulting in strong dependence on training data and limited extrapolation capability. To address these limitations, this article proposes, for the first time, a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) that directly embeds physical knowledge into the network architecture for radio frequency (RF) transistor compact modeling. First, a Fermi-level graph node is introduced to obtain an accurate global analytical solution for the surface potential. Compared with conventional approaches, this node improves the prediction accuracy of the carrier concentration in the subthreshold region by up to 40%. Next, a graph neural network (GNN) is constructed by representing key physical quantities as graph nodes. Physical knowledge is embedded into the network by connecting these nodes through analytical physical equations and auxiliary artificial neural network (ANN) modules, enabling the model to effectively capture the underlying physical relationships. Finally, self-heating and trapping-effect models are incorporated into the proposed model. Validation results demonstrate that the proposed PI-GNN significantly outperforms the baseline model. Notably, even with an 87.5% reduction in the required S-parameter training data, the proposed model improves large-signal prediction accuracy under high-voltage operating conditions by 17%, owing to its superior extrapolation capability. These results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves strong extrapolation capability while substantially reducing dependence on training data.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques

items.title: A Low-Gm Programmable Transconductor Based on FVF Architecture in 180 nm CMOS Process
items.abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a programmable low-transconductance (Gm) operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) suitable for integrated analog filters. The proposed architecture is based on a Flipped Voltage Follower (FVF) core with a source degeneration path implemented using a voltage-controlled MOS pseudo-resistor. This configuration enables wide tunability of the transconductance while maintaining low power consumption and compact area. Designed in a 0.18 μm CMOS process and operating at a 1.8 V supply, the OTA achieves a tunable Gm range from 3.25 nS to 25 nS with a power consumption of only 9 μW. The circuit exhibits a bandwidth of 560 kHz and a total harmonic distortion

items.title: A Cryo-CMOS Electron- and Nuclear-Spin Controller for Color-Center Quantum Processors
items.abstract: Pursuing a scalable quantum processor based on color centers in diamond, this work presents a novel multi-qubit cryo-CMOS system-on-chip (SoC) with a class-DE radio frequency digital-to-analog converter (RFDAC) and a class-D pulse-density modulation (PDM) driver that controls both electron and nuclear spin qubits of a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center using a shared driving coil. The electron spin driver employs a polar-based architecture with programmable memory for amplitude control and a direct-digital-synthesis (DDS) phase modulation (PM) path for accurate phase and frequency control. The nuclear-spin driver adopts a digital loop filter with resonant feedback to shape quantization noise out of band, while ensuring improved supply rejection thanks to a feedback loop via an analog-to-digital converter (ADC). Fabricated in a 40-nm CMOS process and operating at 6 K, the chip can drive over 80 mA output current with a 52 dB signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) over 50 MHz bandwidth (BW) at the electron-spin target frequency (2.5 GHz), and 36 mA with SNR > 52 dB over 20 kHz BW and a spurious free dynamic range (SFDR)$= {\mathrm {47~\text {dB}}}$across the target nuclear-spin band (1.9 to 2.1 MHz), allowing for driving operations on multiple nuclear spins with high fidelity. Driving the qubits resulted in a Rabi frequency of 2.31 MHz (1.95 kHz) for the electron (nuclear) spins, while drawing 45 mW (17 mW) from the supply. The single-qubit operation on an electron (and a nuclear) spin, characterized using gate-set tomography (GST), achieves a fidelity of 99.3(1)% (99.5(1)%). These results advance the scalability of distributed quantum processors based on color centers in diamond.

items.title: A Compression Tree Generation Method for High Performance VLSI Datapaths
items.abstract: Compression trees have been historically a key component of several arithmetic units, most notably multipliers. The latter have been for the most part standalone units and in common situations synthesis tools can generate very close to optimal solutions. With large matrix multiply structures taking more of a central role in the compute industry, the need for a better understanding of these compression trees is apparent. Furthermore, the boundary of its usage needs to be redefined: dot products, polynomial fitting of non-linear operators, are all sums of products. And since products are sums of partial products, in the end, we are just adding many things together as bit heaps; i.e. the fundamental role of a compression tree. Therefore, we must see them as more than just a component of a multiplier. This paper presents a delay-aware compression-tree methodology based on a weighted bit heap. Each bit is described by its significance and relative arrival time, and the generator uses technology-independent normalized delay units to estimate Boolean logical pressure. By exploiting the commutativity of addition within each column, the method reorders bits across reduction stages and uses a Dadda-style maximum-bandwidth topology with flexible CSA3:2 operators. For Radix-4 Booth multipliers from 11 to 64 bits, the resulting trees show lower modeled delay and estimated logic volume than the evaluated Wallace-style maximum-compression trees. Fused four-way integer dot products further demonstrate how the same representation can evaluate the cost of microarchitectural constraints, such as preserving individual product redundant formats. These results show that weighted bit-heap generation provides a practical technology-independent basis for exploring compression trees beyond standalone multiplication.

items.title: 14th eBeam Initiative Annual Luminaries Survey predicts photomask market and equipment growth
items.abstract: The eBeam Initiative completed its 14th annual opinion survey in July 2025 with anonymous feedback from 86 industry luminaries representing 51 companies from across the semiconductor ecosystem – including photomasks, electronic design automation (EDA), chip design, equipment, materials, manufacturing and research. Started in 2012, the Luminaries Survey is used each year to gather predictions of industry trends. 64 percent of the luminaries who responded to the survey predict that mask revenues in 2025 will increase compared to 2024. In a new survey question, mask writing ranked as the top priority for investment at the leading edge for 2026, followed closely by mask inspection and repair, and optical proximity correction (OPC)/inverse lithography technology (ILT). In a related question, 88 percent of luminaries who responded predict that multi-beam mask writer purchases will increase over the next three years. EUV lithography and curvilinear masks are two significant technology trends impacting the photomask market. High-NA EUV lithography is targeted for the most advanced nodes and early adoption is underway. In a question about High- NA EUV’s impact on mask makers, 40 percent of luminaries surveyed now believe the minimum dimension of mask sub-resolution assist features (SRAFs) needed is 15nm or below, an increase from 29 percent who said that last year. Turning to curvilinear masks, confidence continues to remain high for manufacturing curvilinear mask features, with 77 percent of respondents indicating that leading-edge mask shops can manage at least a limited number of curvilinear masks in high-volume manufacturing (HVM) by the end of next year.
items.venue: Photomask and next-generation lithography mask technology. Conference

items.title: xTier: Intelligent Tiering for CXL-Enabled Memory
items.abstract: CXL-enabled memory expands server memory capacity, but introduces a page-placement problem: the operating system must decide which pages should reside in DRAM and which should reside on slower CXL memory. Existing systems make this tradeoff in one of two ways. Userspace controllers support flexible policies, but expose placement decisions to scheduler jitter and kernel-userspace crossing overhead. Kernel-space systems avoid this latency, but rely on fixed heuristics that must generalize across workloads. We present xTier, a kernel-resident learned memory-tiering system. xTier attaches eBPF programs to PEBS events and uses a compact quantized MLP to score sampled pages inside the kernel at microsecond-scale latency. Rather than reacting to every candidate, xTier converges to a low-churn placement for the current workload phase, reduces sampling cost after convergence, and returns to a higher sampling cadence when the workload shifts. We evaluate xTier on six memory-bound workloads at DRAM:CXL ratios from 1:5 to 1:25. The advantage grows as the DRAM budget tightens. At 1:15 and beyond, xTier is the fastest system in 14 of 18 configurations. Where it is not fastest, it trails the best baseline by 3.9% on average. It reaches this performance while moving 13% fewer pages in geometric mean, and 22% fewer at the tighter ratios. When a workload changes phase, xTier rebuilds its hot set in DRAM faster and more completely than any baseline.

items.title: X-ray inspection of glass substrates and through-glass vias using laminography, tilted radiography, and automated defect recognition
items.abstract: Glass substrates with through-glass vias (TGVs) are becoming increasingly important for advanced packaging and large-area panel-level manufacturing. However, their inspection remains challenging because relevant defects may occur both in the glass volume and inside metallized vias. Typical defect classes include missing holes, residual glass, micro-cracks, voids, incomplete metallization, and delamination. While optical inspection is highly effective for surface features and high-throughput screening, it is limited once the relevant information is buried in the glass or hidden by metal filling. This paper presents an application-oriented study of X-ray inspection of glass substrates and TGVs using 2D radiography, tilted radiography (2.5D), and computed laminography (3DCL). The focus is placed on practical system parameters and their influence on defect visibility, including beam energy, magnification, imaging geometry, and detector characteristics. Special attention is given to detector efficiency and contrast sensitivity, which are critical for identifying weakly absorbing features such as residual glass or subtle density fluctuations under realistic inspection-speed constraints. Representative case studies on etched and metallized TGV structures demonstrate how different acquisition modes reveal complementary information. In addition, segmentation in Dragonfly 3D World and automated defect recognition workflows are discussed as tools for scalable defect localization and quantification. The results support a hybrid inspection strategy in which fast radiographic methods are combined with volumetric laminography and AI-assisted analysis to address the inspection needs of emerging glass-based packaging technologies.

items.title: VisionPsy-Nano: Improving Accuracy, Efficiency, and Reliability in On-Device Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Sub-billion-parameter Vision-Language Models are increasingly viable for on-device deployment, yet compact model size alone does not guarantee usability. On a phone, such a model can still require more than two minutes to produce its first token. On-device usability depends on three axes: accuracy, efficiency, and behavioral reliability; standard benchmarks miss the third, with answers too short to expose doom loops and prompts too benign to probe adversarial safety. We introduce a diagnosis-driven post-training recipe in which a teacher VLM stress-tests the student, uncovers failure modes beyond human priors, and converts them into targeted supervision and preference alignment, supplementing generic data scaling with failure-driven optimization. Coupled with two visual-token policies, the recipe yields two accuracy-efficiency variants with improved behavioral reliability. \textbf{\NanoFull} attains a 62.3 normalized average over 17 benchmarks, the highest among openly released $\sim$0.5B models, +7.4 over its base at identical architecture and token budget, with doom-loop rates at or below the strongest baseline's. \textbf{\FlashFull} retains 61.4 while cutting warm time-to-first-token on a Pixel 9 from 138\,s to 6.1\,s (23$\times$). By jointly addressing all three axes, we move compact VLMs toward practical on-device usability.

items.title: Validation-Driven Capacity Planning for Chiplet-Based Flagship SoC Programs: An Economic and Architectural Framework
items.abstract: A chiplet strategy that reduces per-die fabrication cost can still lose much of that advantage at the validation stage, and this article argues that most chiplet economics literature simply does not account for that risk. Emulation and validation capacity for multi-die programs is typically forecast by extrapolating from a prior monolithic-SoC generation’s emulator footprint, an approach that appears to understate the capacity growth driven by cross-die interface count and protocol complexity. The framework proposed here treats validation capacity as a first-class capital and organizational commitment established at program inception, then revisited at three defined program milestones – an early architecture-gate sizing estimate, a subsystem-gate reforecast once per-die RTL stabilizes, and an integration-gate provisioning commitment ahead of multi-die bring-up. The argument draws on capacity-planning and capital-governance experience across four flagship SoC generations and a large emulation asset base exceeding a billion dollars in value, including program-level outcomes from capacity-doubling initiatives, system virtualization, and structured vendor negotiation. These outcomes suggest that staged, milestone-linked capacity governance can materially improve capital efficiency relative to linear extrapolation, though the comparison offered is qualitative rather than a controlled trial. Chiplet economics, as currently framed in the literature, appears incomplete without an explicit validation-capacity line item; without it, capacity shortfalls tend to surface only once multi-die bring-up is already underway – precisely the point where a program has the least room to absorb schedule risk. The three-gate model is proposed as a transferable planning discipline, independent of process node or specific die-partitioning choice.
items.venue: Global Journal of Computer Science and Technology

items.title: Ultra-Wide Bandgap AlGaN Heterostructure Field Effect Transistors With Current Gain Cutoff Frequency Above 85 GHz
items.abstract: We report the design and demonstration of ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) AlGaN polarization-graded field-effect transistors (PolFETs) that achieve a current-gain cutoff frequency above 85 GHz and a current density exceeding 1.3 A/mm. Ultra-thin channel and buffer layers were grown epitaxially on AlN substrates, and a reverse-graded AlGaN contact layer was incorporated to reduce the contact resistance to below 1 ohm.mm. With aggressively scaled device dimensions, the AlGaN PolFETs exhibit state-of-the-art high-frequency performance for UWBG transistors. Small-signal modeling reveals both parasitic and transit delays, confirming the benefits of reduced access resistance and enhanced intrinsic transconductance. These results establish a new performance benchmark for UWBG AlGaN devices and demonstrate their strong potential for next-generation millimeter-wave electronics.

items.title: Surface Acoustic Wave Transversal Filter With Fractional Bandwidth of 51.3%
items.abstract: This article presents a synthesized surface acoustic wave (SAW) transversal filter featuring a center frequency (${f}_{c}\text {)}$above 4 GHz and a record-high fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 51.3%. Unlike conventional filter topologies that rely on resonant or anti-resonant frequencies to create transmission zeros, the transversal architecture decouples achievable bandwidth (BW) from the electromechanical coupling coefficient (${k}_{t}^{{2}}\text {)}$to enable wide passbands, thereby shifting the primary design requirement to a resonator platform that supports a broad range of operating frequencies while maintaining a high-quality factor (${Q}\text {)}$. The demonstrated filter is based on shear-horizontal (SH) and longitudinal-leaky (LL) SAW resonators fabricated on a lithium niobate on silicon carbide (LiNbO3-on-SiC) hetero-substrate. Leveraging this platform, low-loss resonators with scalable resonant frequencies ranging from 3.2 to 5.6 GHz, and${k}_{t}^{{2}}$values from 10.1% to 20.4% are realized on a single substrate. Using these resonators, a transversal SAW filter targeting the 5G n77 band is successfully synthesized. Furthermore, an ultrawideband (UWB) transversal filter with a center frequency of 4.39 GHz and an FBW of 51.3% is demonstrated. The achieved BW covers a major portion of the 3–5-GHz spectrum, enabling carrier aggregation (CA) across multiple 5G FR1 mid-band allocations, including n77, n78, and n79. The proposed approach offers a promising solution for wideband radio frequency (RF) front ends, particularly for sub-6 GHz 5G/6G wireless communications, as well as UWB systems.

items.title: Stable Cellularity in Hopfological Algebra
items.abstract: Let $H$ be a nontrivial finite-dimensional nonnegatively graded connected Hopf algebra, with $\ell=\max\{d:H_d\ne0\}$, and let $A\ge0$ be a locally finite $H$-module algebra with finite-dimensional split semisimple, $H$-trivial $A_0$. Under the gap $A_d=0$ for $0<d<\ell$, the shifted standard cells $\{q^{-r}Ae_x:0\le r<\ell\}$ form a simple-minded collection. A socle estimate for positive syzygies proves negative-Hom vanishing, while the gap makes the degree-zero endomorphism algebra semisimple. A bounded $t$-structure on the compact derived category with these cells is constructed, with standard cells as its simple heart objects.
